articles.excerpt: Two-time Australian Hairdresser of the Year, working one-on-one from his Darlinghurst studio.
articles.body: Two-time Australian Hairdresser of the Year, Brad Ngata has spent more than two decades building one of Sydney's most respected independent salons. Tucked into the creative, Soho-like stretch of Darlinghurst Road, Brad Ngata Hair Direction operates as a one-on-one, single-operator studio, no production line, no battery-hen formula. Brad's editorial credentials span shoots for Sunday Times Magazine and Culture Magazine , plus advertising campaigns for Nokia, with named collections including Rebel, Tangeres , Breakage and Paper Cut showcasing his fashion-forward range. Inside, full-length mirrors, cascading greenery and gold-rimmed porcelain lend a sense of playful luxury that clients consistently describe as both stimulating and surprisingly peaceful. Recognised at Hair Expo and the Maybelline Australian Fashion Awards, Brad also holds back-to-back titles for Sydney's Best Hairdresser. Review by Sigourney Cantelo CONTACT 269A Darlinghurst Road Darlinghurst NSW 2010 0404 806 118 bradngata.com.au

articles.title: Delphine Sorel, Sydney
articles.author: Tess Schlink
articles.excerpt: With a 160-person waitlist and six months fully booked, French-born Delphine Sorel has become Sydney's most coveted brow stylist for effortlessly natural arches.
articles.body: French-Inspired Brow Styling in Sydney A slice of Gallic heaven tucked away in the heritage Dymocks Building overlooking Sydney’s George Street, Delphine Sorel has quickly cemented a reputation for excellent arches since opening in early 2020. In the short time since she opened her doors, Delphine’s salon has attracted a 160 person waitlist and is fully booked for the next six months, not a small achievement in Sydney’s surprisingly competitive brow styling scene. An Intimate Salon with Chicness in Spades The brainchild of the eponymous Delphine, who honed her craft at Kristin Fisher Eyebrows before heading off to create her own space, the salon is intimate but with chicness in spades. The room is decked in a muted palette of beiges and pale greys, with design by Laura Downie from Studio 1 Interiors ; a whimsical swirling wallpaper adds understated interest, as does an eye-catching half-moon mirror. Preserved floral bouquets adorn the back bar created by Delphine’s “flower wizard”, Myra Perez of My Violet. Enhancing Natural Beauty, Not Changing It Having grown up on the French Riviera, Delphine arrived in Australia in her early twenties but has continued to preserve the Gallic sensibilities she was raised with, and to imbue her salon and work with this sense of French refinement. The whole ‘less is more’ philosophy is not an invented cliché: it’s based in truth. “I believe the art of beauty lies in enhancing someone’s natural beauty,” explains Delphine. “My work is about making clients look their best without changing who they are.” “After falling victim to the 90’s skinny brow trend I resolved to find a better way of caring for my eyebrows. I discovered how a set of well-balanced brows can accentuate a face in the most incredible way. From that moment on I was obsessed with eyebrows and my passion has only increased over time.” The Eyebrow Style and Tint Experience Delphine is most renowned for her eyebrow style and tint, which is what I’m trying today (she also offers cosmetic tattooing and lash styling). I’m a little nervous as I’ve had some dodgy eyebrow tints in the past, while I like some definition, I’m not a fan of the ‘one-size-fits-all’ heavy dye and block shape that many salons dole out. But Delphine’s attention to detail immediately allays any latent fears I might have had: she quizzes me about how I’d like the intensity of the tint, how full I want my brows, whether I’d prefer them trimmed or not. She happily shares her expert opinion while adapting to each client’s preferences, and the individual style each face requires. I’m thrilled with my results: gently tinted, groomed but still fluffy and full. I need nothing more than a quick comb through and a slick of clear gel to look instantly put together in the morning. Curated Home Care Products For home care, Delphine offers a considered edit of products if you want to recreate her effortless style chez soi: she stocks brow pencils and gels from Le Sourcil by French MUA Angélik Iffennecker, and highlighter and brow brush duos from cult Perth salon Alison Jade. Timeless Brows That Transcend Trends Ultimately, Delphine is dedicated to bystepping trends to create a timeless brow look that won’t have you cringing at photos of yourself in 20 years’ time. “Beauty ideals can convince you that you have to change,” she shares. “The problem is that those ideals are constantly shifting with each new trend. I believe in bringing to life an ameliorated version of my clients without changing who they are. I work to enhance their natural beauty steering clear…

articles.title: Djurra Lifestyle Salon and Spa, Fremantle
articles.author: Lucy Searle
articles.excerpt: An Aveda salon and spa in a 100-year-old Fremantle building where every appointment begins with a complimentary stress-relieving massage.
articles.body: An Aveda Haven in Heritage Fremantle Located in an historic 100-year-old building in Fremantle's West End lies the uber cool Aveda salon and spa, Djurra. Owned by hair stylist powerhouse, Anita Sutton-Galloway, Djurra Salon and Spa offers hair and spa treatments for men and women, with a natural and nurturing focus. Their holistic approach to beauty is deep-rooted in Aveda's mission, which is 'to care for the world we live in, from the products we make to the ways in which we give back to society'. And it's evident that the team here practice what they preach. The stunning hair salon has an incredible sense of space, achieved through the rustic, pared-back, warehouse look complete with exposed brick walls, floor-length mirrors, wooden floorboards and stunning pendant lights. You can pass through the salon and past the double doors to arrive at the equally impressive sanctuary that is the spa, which I make note of to visit next time. Setting the Tone for Each Guest I arrive for my blow dry and, like any hair salon on a Saturday afternoon, the place is buzzing. What I sense immediately about this salon is that each guest has the opportunity to set the atmosphere and tone for their time here. Whether it's time to sit in silence and enjoy the treatment or chat excitedly with your hair stylist, it's completely up to the client. Client comfort is first and foremost The Signature Stress-Relieving Ritual I'm led to my chair and settle in with magazines and a cup of Aveda Tea; a deliciously calming infusion of peppermint and liquorice root. A therapist arrives to begin what is the ritual for all spa and salon appointments at Djurra, the stress-relieving massage. I close my eyes as I'm instructed to take three deep breaths of Aveda's signature Blue Oil. The calming blend of peppermint and blue chamomile clears my head instantly and, despite the hubbub around me, I completely switch off. Suspended somewhere between heaven and earth for five minutes, I am treated to a sublime head, neck and shoulder massage. All tension just melts away. We could drift away just looking at the inviting space Blow Dry and Beachy Waves As I gently come back to reality Jake, my stylist, appears. I have quite fine hair that lacks shape and style but Jake, a senior stylist at Djurra, assures me he can transform it into a voluminous mane, full of bounce and body. And, I secretly trust him. We talk through some styling ideas for my blow dry and I am then whisked away to the basin for a shampoo. The relaxation never ends here at Djurra: I lie back on the massaging chairs and inhale the aroma of the Aveda shampoo and conditioner. Ensconced back in my chair, Jake starts by applying Aveda Phomollient to my damp strands. This styling product is a personal favourite, I just about jumped for joy when I discovered a mousse that doesn't leave hair sticky and stiff. Phomollient is light and gives hair gorgeous texture, hold and longevity. We are going for a beachy, relaxed look so Jake starts to blow dry in sections, spritzing in Aveda Pure Abundance Style Prep. Another product that features regularly in my at-home hair routine, this gem provides all day weightless volume and really helps to hold the style. Jake creates relaxed, loose curls with a curling wand sprayed with Aveda Air Control Hair Spray, a new little trick I'll be keeping up my sleeve, and finishes by brushing out the curls, creating a very glam and bouncy look. At the end…

articles.title: Dr Anh Medispa, Perth
articles.author: Lucy Searle
articles.excerpt: A lavishly appointed CBD sanctuary where privacy is paramount, cosmetic enhancements, medifacials and wellness treatments under the care of Dr Anh Nguyen.
articles.body: Located in the heart of Perth’s bustling CBD lies the highly sought after medispa and wellness clinic, Dr Anh. Owner and plastic surgeon Dr Anh Nguyen has created a stylish inner city escape offering a range of cosmetic enhancements, wellness and medispa treatments, where clients are treated like royalty. Dr Anh Nyugen opened the doors to her Perth CBD luxury medispa and wellness clinic in October 2014 with a vision of creating a safe and private sanctuary for patients looking for less-invasive cosmetic enhancement. Dr Anh wants her clients to feel special, empowered and cared for and, with over a decade of experience under her belt as well as a dedicated team of nurses, dermal and beauty therapists, there is no one better for the job. Situated in a heritage building on William Street, Perth, Dr Anh’s clinic keeps a low profile on the street, with minimal signage, perfect for those after a little more privacy. I arrive by private elevator, more than happy to leave the busy city streets behind and stepped into the tranquil world. No details have been overlooked at the lavishly appointed clinic; from the luxurious waiting room with stylish wing back chairs to the gilded tables and chandeliers. Upon arriving I am whisked into the gorgeous waiting room where I sip on chilled water and enjoy the peaceful music floating through the room. Inspirational feel-good quotes adorn the clinic, a lovely reminder to clients that this is a place where they can feel truly beautiful. Dr Anh’s clinic features state-of-the-art equipment and treatment rooms with relaxing facial and massage spaces and private consultation rooms, a Body Boost Bed, makeup application room and a surgery theatre. Today I’m having the Mesoeclat Treatment (read my review on the treatment, coming soon) and I’m greeted by my therapist Charmaine, who leads me through to a treatment room. The deeply exfoliating medifacial leaves my skin sparkling and nourished. Dr Anh tells me that client comfort is the absolute number one focus for her here at the clinic and her team work tirelessly to ensure the wellbeing and privacy of all clients. Aside from the many private consultation rooms available, patients are offered the use of lockers, bathrooms as well as a private payment desk at the back of the clinic, away from the main reception. Elegantly appointed and client focused, Dr Anh’s clinic is the perfect place to have a bit of me time and escape from the daily grind. Her gentle and compassionate approach to each and every one of her clients is what makes this clinic so unique. Review by Sigourney Cantelo

articles.title: Edwards and Co, Melbourne
articles.author: Arianne Witt
articles.excerpt: Hidden away down Punch Lane in Melbourne's CBD, Edwards and Co is a collaborative open studio space where freelance stylists deliver sun-kissed balayage, signature waves and expert colour in a stunning industrial setting.
articles.body: Inside Melbourne's Most Coveted Hair Studio Hidden away down Punch Lane in the bustling CBD of Melbourne is a vastly beautiful industrial style space home to fashions favourite hair salon, Edwards and Co. Dreamed up by one of Sydney’s most celebrated hair colourists and stylists, Jaye Edwards, the salon is becoming one of the city’s most popular destinations for a colour, cut, blow dry and style. A collaborative open studio space houses some of the countries best talent, allowing freelance stylists to cut and colour as they please without all the unnecessary extras. Edwards obviously did something right as streams of fashion savvy professionals, models and influences push open the doors each day to get their shiny locks cared for by the fine array of expert hands before them. Being recently awarded the winner of the Salon Business of the Year Award at the 2017 Australian Hair Fashion Awards, It seemed like it was time for me to check it out and get my unruly hair tamed with a sun kissed glow and soft tousled waves, Edwards and Co’s signature look. Walking into the studio filled with soft natural light, whitewashed walls and sections of exposed brick its hard not to feel like your in another world away from the busy Melbourne streets. Being a business owner who frequently travels between all five of his salons I was lucky enough to catch Jaye while he was in town and get treated by the man himself! Sun-Kissed Balayage by Jaye Edwards After being seated at the huge communal table between foiled up beauties flicking through glossy magazines or tapping away on laptops, I was offered a pot of delicious fruity tea in a gorgeous ceramic teapot with a matching mug and saucer. Once settled, Jaye and I discussed how my glowy sun-kissed look will be achieved through a rich mahogany base paired with a chestnut honey balayage and an array of soft highlights. Gently and efficiently he paints it on as we chat about our weekly musings and thoughts. Soon Jaye leaves me at the table to get on with my work and I am relieved I don’t have to look at my headful of foils in a salon mirror as per the hair experiences I’m used to. Premium Products and Signature Waves Time flies by and soon I am lead past vibrant coloured artworks and teal blue ceiling-hung swings to the basin to be glossed and to be treated with what i must say was an amazing head massage. To finish up its time to sit myself in one of the gorgeous white tulip chairs positioned in front of a large metal-rimmed mirror. In terms of products, collaborating with the likes of Christophe Robin, Kevin Murphy and Oribe, there’s almost too much to choose from when it comes to styling mists, serums and volumisers. However, once blow dried and while brushing out my immaculate waves, Jaye opts for Kevin Murphy’s hair resort spray to give texture paired with the shimmer shine as a finishing mist to further revive my now glowing mop. Not only is the colour amazing but now my entire look is just to die for, as I attempt to remember all the steps so i can get this look everyday! A Salon Worth Returning To It’s obvious I will be returning. In six weeks to be exact, which is the required time period for a follow up, and you wouldn’t want to miss it. It’s almost dangerous to have my hair done by Jaye as I wouldn’t want to have it any other way. My hair has…

articles.title: Edwards & Co, Surry Hills
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: A converted warehouse salon where freelance creatives rent-a-chair and the city's most fashion-forward clientele come for balayage, colour and effortless lived-in hair.
articles.body: A Collaborative Warehouse Salon in Surry Hills Amid the rag trade HQs and hipster espresso bars in Kippax Street Surry Hills, is one of the fashion industry’s favourite salons, Edwards and Co. Sprawled across a first floor converted warehouse, the vast industrial-styled space is home to some of the country’s most celebrated styling talent. Brainchild of top colourist Jaye Edwards, the collaborative space allows freelance stylists to rent-a-chair and service clients, without needing to sign up to a hefty lease. And it works. Every day, a steady stream hip-haired models, professionals and influencers climb the stairs to have their tresses tended to by Jaye and his band of merry creatives. Despite hearing about Edwards and Co for years, I’ve never actually had my hair coloured here, but on my manager Marina’s insistence, I’m here to sample her go-to guy Joel Wallbank for myself. On entering, I’m immediately struck by the sense of space and light. The huge vaulted space is book-ended by majestic windows and carefully placed spotlights. Whitewashed floorboards, hanging foliage and bucketloads of natural light make this space feel more like a photo studio than a hair salon. It’s got a major communal thing going on, made evident by the complete lack of walls. Foil-laden clientele sit happily around a huge rough-hewn table sipping Pinot Grigio and thumbing fashion magazines. Rather than hiding out the back in a poky staff room, the staff sit at a side communal table eating their lunch or casually tapping at their laptops. Honey Balayage with Joel Wallbank After Joel and I decide on my colour direction (honey balayage with a warm chestnut base), he paints it on speedily and leaves me at the large table with my laptop and sipping my soy latte out of a beautiful Milly Dent marbled mug. Unlike the usual three-hour marathon, today the time actually zooms by as I write my stories. The lack of a mirror in front of me makes me feel much less conscious of the fact I have a headful of foils on, and much more able to get fully absorbed into my work. Styling Products for Lived-In Texture When it’s time for my gloss I’m led past a wall adorned with a brightly-coloured Brian Connolly artwork to the basin, where I’m treated to an excellent head massage by Paige. Next up, it’s over to the styling station where a line of white tulip chairs are positioned in front of huge metal-rimmed mirrors. Paige rubs a dab of Oribe Supershine Serum through my ends along with a generous misting each of Christophe Robin Instant Volumising Mist and Kevin Murphy Anti.Gravity Weightless Volume Spray. This cocktail not only smells amazing but, she assures me, it will give my hair the perfect lived-in grit and hold (minus the stickiness) and shine (minus the heaviness). I’m sold. True to word, half an hour later Paige brushes out perfectly-set, touchable waves while misting it with Oribe Anti Humidity Spray (to keep my baby hairs in check). It’s so pretty I can’t resist taking a selfie. Colour That Only Gets Better When Joel comes to check my colour, we’re both thrilled with the result. It’s shiny and rich with delicately-painted biscuit tones peeking through, giving it beautiful texture and movement. I’m thrilled and immediately book my six-week follow up. I don’t want to risk missing out on an appointment. Edwards and Co is so popular, it’s a very real threat. As the weeks draw on after my appointment my colour only seems to improve. At launches and photo shoots, people, even other hairstylists, comment on it. Proof that…

articles.title: Follow Hair Studio, Surfer's Paradise
articles.author: Gracie Clough
articles.excerpt: 4/19 River Dr, Surfers Paradise QLD 4217.
articles.body: From the moment you step into the Scandinavian designed hair studio, you feel instantly at ease and comforted by the wooden walls and surrounding greenery. One of my favourite elements to the salon's design is that there are designated sections for colouring and blow-drying. Mirrors are only located at the blow-dry bar, therefore you do not have to feel uncomfortable by staring at yourself looking like Medusa with a head of foils. The team at Follow Hair Studio are experienced and friendly, and always keep your hair on trend while respecting your requests. The team also have regular training sessions where they learn the latest techniques and hair trends, so you can count on them for your babylights and ecaille baylayage. Follow Hair Studio uses quality Kevin Murphy products that contain no parabens or sulphates, so you can guarantee your fresh hair colour will not fade in one wash. The salon now uses Olaplex so not only will you leave with a fresh new 'do, you will also leave with hair stronger than what you entered the salon with. Follow Hair Studio is located at Budds Beach on the Gold Coast, directly above Bumbles Café. Review by Gracie Clough

articles.title: Glow Haus, Potts Point
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Chanel Corban's grown-up beauty studio in Potts Point. Gray and Co interiors, custom-mixed spray tans, laminated brows and an infrared sauna out the back. Proof that a fake tan can be a luxury service.
articles.body: Chanel Corban has been perfecting the art of the spray tan for fifteen years, and Glow Haus is the grown-up home she built for it. Gray and Co designed the Potts Point studio in beige, cream, walnut and bronze, with travertine surfaces and heavy linen curtains dividing the zones, professional without a hint of clinical. The tan is the hero, custom-mixed with a choice of developers, airbrushed to whatever depth you dare. Beyond it there are laminated brows, lash lifts and an infrared sauna out the back. Grounded, refined and quietly glamorous. Proof that a fake tan can be a luxury service, in the right hands and the right light.

articles.title: Head Studio, Perth
articles.author: Beauticate Editorial
articles.excerpt: 64 King Street, Perth WA 6000.

articles.title: Herbario, Prahran
articles.author: Kath Karras
articles.excerpt: Forget meditative music and candles, Valli Shubere's signature 90-minute facial workout targets all 77 muscles in your face for visibly sculpted, glowing skin.
articles.body: A facial by Valli Shubere is anything but conventional; it’s a 90-minute vigorous workout for your face and neck. Valli and her husband Vito, botanical virtuosos, have been providing skin and body care at their Melbourne clinic, Herbario, for some 30 years. And while the clean living and organic lifestyle is no trend du jour , our skin care routines are getting progressively more complicated. When was the last time we detoxed our faces? I heard about Valli’s signature detox treatment through Sydney’s own skin whisperer, Jocelyn Petroni. What better endorsement? A visit to Herbario is unlike any other beauty room. In the absence of meditative music and candles, is a line up of herbal remedies, rich in natural, active ingredients. There is nothing artificial to be found here. Valli, who is dressed in a crisp white coat and whose nature is quite disarming, greets me. I’m intrigued. Upstairs from her shop of herbal concoctions, Valli examines my face, in a very matter-of-fact manner. I’m assured that once she works through the 77 muscles located in my face and neck, I will be transformed. There is pulling, stretching, thwacks and her famous adjustments to my jaw, where Valli claims the majority of my stress is housed. It hurts, but only a little. Valli claims that lymphatic, muscular and emotional blockages inflame the skin’s metabolism, distorting one’s natural features. It makes total holistic health sense. With my workout complete, a blend of herbs is softly brushed onto my face and neck, where I’m left to sleep. My treatment ends with Valli’s own blend of serums. The result. Glowing, smoother skin with more defined contours. It’s the ultimate facial workout. Review by Kath Karras

articles.title: Joey Scandizzo, South Yarra
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Three-time Australian Hairdresser of the Year Joey Scandizzo runs a celebrity-loved salon on Toorak Road where editorial edge meets five-star luxury service.
articles.body: Three times Australian Hairdresser of the Year in a row, Joey Scandizzo's busy and bright trendy Toorak Road salon sits in the fashionable and affluent area of Melbourne's South Yarra. Formerly known as the successful Rokk Ebony, Scandizzo shocked the hairdressing world when he changed the salon's name and decor (to a more modern and fresh look) four years ago and took over the business with two other partners. A bit of a family affair, brother John also works for the salon. Scandizzo, 35, who is married with a toddler son, is well-known in the glamorous world of celebrity, having styled top models and actresses for years. Regular clients include Ruby Rose, Kate Peck, Rebecca Maddern and Buddy Franklin. He is also proving a mentor to Australia's youth and enjoys an international TV ( Beauty and the Geek and Project Runway ) and radio reputation. More recently he launched his own set of luxury hair and body products, known as Eleven and which are PETA approved (ie they're not tested on animals) and are available to purchase in the salon. But you'll also find his salon stocks the upmarket brands Wella Professional, ONYX Face & Body and Kevin Murphy. Visit the salon and you'll find it has a rather trendy and edgy feel to it. In fact, you can be sure the Scandizzo team are well onto what's hot in the world of hair before even the magazines are (for a start, Joey is often drafted in to style those editorial shoots). Despite this time-consuming fashion focus, the Joey Scandizzo Salon persists with its five-star luxury appeal where all customers receive a signature hand massage and undivided attention, as well as the offer of tea or coffee the minute they sit down in one of the comfortable salon leather seats. The salon prides itself on its team of hair 'experts,' having also picked up the title Salon Team of the Year. Other accolades the team have won in recent times include HAIR EXPO New Creative Force Winner 2015 (Hermiz Daniel) and AHFA Victorian Hairdresser of the Year 2015 (Joseph Semaan). The team have also picked up a whole host of colouring accolades. Male friends and partners may be interested to know that the Kings Domain Barber Shop across the road from the Toorak Road salon is also part of the Joey Scandizzo empire. One regular client includes international footballer Cristiano Ronaldo, no less.

articles.title: Joh Bailey, Double Bay
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Four decades behind Australia's most iconic blowdries.
articles.body: Founded by Joh Bailey and Marilyn Koch in 1985, Joh Bailey in Double Bay is arguably Australia's most iconic hair destination. For four decades, this is where Sydney's elite, and visiting royalty, supermodels and celebrities including Diana Princess of Wales, Kylie Minogue, Elle Macpherson, Cate Blanchett and Olivia Newton-John, have come for the signature Bailey blowdry: voluminous, glossy and full of life. What began as a single salon on Cross Street became an institution of effortless glamour and impeccable service, where women walk in one version of themselves and leave luminous. The salon offers a full suite of services spanning precision cutting, bespoke colour, styling, hair extensions, makeup and treatments. A second outpost in Bowral extends the Bailey legacy beyond the city. Review by Sigourney Cantelo CONTACT 16-18 Cross Street Double Bay NSW 2028 (02) 9369 1144 johbailey.com.au

articles.title: Juliana Marcs, Double Bay
articles.author: Chrisanthi Kaliviotis
articles.excerpt: We find one of the best, not to mention cool, salons in Sydney, delivering on impressive hairstyles, even turning out in-house Bondi babe, Christanthi’s,…
articles.body: Opulent Salon Design and Decor Tucked away in Sydney’s Double Bay village, Juliana Marcs is a hair salon that’s a cut (and blow-dry) above the rest. With rich Rococo finishes and just a touch of glitz, the salon’s namesake has her hands full (literally) with the latte ladies of Sydney’s society scene. We present you a blow-by-blow of all this small, but swanky, salon has to offer. From the exterior, the façade of Juliana Marcs hair salon is simplistic and inviting, with black-trimmed white walls and a classic gold insignia. Stepping inside, the drama is raised a notch with the salon gilded in gold and burnished Baroque accents. The décor is tastefully opulent and reflective of Double Bay’s European character. In the centre sits a spherical counter in copper and each client chair has their own majestic mirror. Juliana Marcs knows how to make a great first impression It’s cool luxury from beginning to end Meeting Juliana and the Consultation Juliana greets me promptly. She is dressed stylishly in an all-black ensemble, offset with long, smooth flaxen hair, a note to self: a hairdresser with good hair is always trustworthy, and she shows me to my über -cool ghost chair. A warm herbal tea, glass of water and a cookie are placed beside me alongside some editorial entertainment for my perusal. I chat to Juliana about what I want hair wise, a bouncy blow-wave that will remain buoyant and big at a friend’s birthday on the wind-stricken harbour. I also apologise profusely for my wild, salty, Bondi mane. Luckily for me, Ms Marcs yields magical (hair) powers and begins to work her craft. The Aveda Hair Wash Experience I am moved to my chair by the simplistic, serene space at the basin in the back. I look up and see a cluster of low-hanging light bulbs and catch the scent of nature. As a salon that is monogamous to one brand, a rare feat these days, only Aveda products stack the shelves of the basin and salon. Due to the unruly and frizzy nature of my post-beach ‘do, Juliana advises me she is using the Aveda Smooth Infusion Shampoo and Conditioner and proceeds to lather away. The soothing scent of aloe and guar bean coupled with the oh-so-heavenly scalp massage has me drifting off into a halcyon slumber. After the deepest, most thorough hair washes of my life, my squeaky clean locks are now indulged in a Smooth Infusion Smoothing Masque and another scalp massage (read: yes, please). Juliana Marcs takes client comfort very seriously Aveda’s natural offerings are exclusively used in the salon Blow-Wave Styling and Finishing Touches As I return to my chair, slightly zonked from my state of sensory bliss, she tends to my locks with a Volumizing Tonic, just what the hair doctor ordered for my bouffant desires. With hairdryer in tow, she proceeds to dry off my now silky locks, blow-wave style, and we tête-à-tête like girls in salons do. For curls that last, and with such a long, heavy head of hair, the tong comes out, and adhering to my mantra of volume, she arms herself with a backcomb and slightly teases the crown of my hair for that extra oomph. Finally, the Aveda pièce de résistance : their revolutionary Shampure Dry Shampoo (an aerosol-free product that is pumped and poof’ed all over my hair for added grit and texture). Looking into the mirror, I have a bouncing mane of curls, ready to take on my Saturday afternoon soirée on the bay. A Natural Glamour Destination For those after a glamorous yet wholly natural…

articles.title: KAILO Wellness Medispa, Fortitude Valley
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Serious skin work above the Calile Hotel on James Street. KAILO runs from Biologique Recherche facials to Halo laser, IV drips and DMK in a room that reads like the hotel below it.
articles.body: Up on level one of the Calile, above the pool and the palms, KAILO does the serious skin work James Street is known for. This is a medispa, not a fluffy day spa, so the menu runs from Biologique Recherche facials to Halo and BBL laser, IV vitamin drips and DMK. The room reads like the hotel below it. Timber, stone, terrazzo, water moving somewhere just out of sight. You can book a facial or you can book a full reset. Either way you walk back out into the Valley looking like you slept for a week. That is the trick of the place.

articles.title: La Boutique by Belinda Jeffrey, Darlinghurst
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Home of "The Blonde Whisperer", unpretentious, high-energy and unapologetically luxe.
articles.body: Widely known as "The Blonde Whisperer," Belinda Jeffrey is one of Australia's most sought-after hair colourists, with a career spanning more than 30 years across film, fashion, editorial and advertising. Her client list reads like a who's who of Australian and international celebrity, Sarah Murdoch, Miranda Kerr, Russell Crowe, Leonardo DiCaprio and Carey Mulligan among them, while her editorial credits include campaigns for Vogue , Harper's Bazaar and Vanity Fair . La Boutique, her salon now located at 36 Kings Lane in Darlinghurst (having recently relocated from its longtime Double Bay address), is an extension of Belinda's philosophy: unpretentious, high-energy and unapologetically luxe. The interiors are finished in gold, rose gold, platinum and bronze, with a champagne cabinet on hand for good measure. Together with a handpicked team of senior colourists and stylists, La Boutique delivers colour without equal. Review by Sigourney Cantelo

articles.title: Lavada, Hobart
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: A polished skin clinic and spa on Hunter Street in Hobart's heritage waterfront, working both sides of the equation with cosmetic aesthetics, dermal therapies and spa treatments.
articles.body: The reception desk is a long slab of marble, product glowing on the wall behind it, and it tells you what kind of place you have walked into. Lavada sits on Hunter Street, in the heritage waterfront pocket of Hobart near the old wharves. It works both sides of the skin equation, cosmetic aesthetics and dermal therapies on one hand, spa treatments and massage on the other. So you can come for results or come to switch off, or book both and call it a morning well spent. The setting is polished without trying too hard. Old bricks, new skin.

articles.title: Lee Preston Hairdressing, South Perth
articles.author: Beauticate Editorial
articles.excerpt: 155 Angelo Street, South Perth WA 6151.

articles.title: Little Company, Collingwood
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: An anti-beauty skin studio down a Smith Street laneway, built by Studio Goss in a century-old furniture warehouse. Brushed linen, lime render, labyrinthine light. Skin as craft, not correction.
articles.body: Down a laneway off Smith Street, in a furniture warehouse that has stood for a century, Stacey Burt has made a skin studio that refuses to shout. Little Company calls its approach anti-beauty, which sounds like a pose until you are inside it. David Goss of Studio Goss dimmed the whole thing right down and built five treatment rooms from brushed linen, lime render, textured stone and reclaimed timber, the light kept low and labyrinthine so you lose your bearings pleasantly. Emerald artworks at the entrance riff on drops of chlorophyll. Every facial is treated as a one-off, informed by the face in front of it. Skin as craft, not correction. Cave-quiet, and better for it.

articles.title: Me Skin and Body, South Yarra
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Inside South Yarra's Me Skin & Body: a closer look at the cult Melbourne skin clinic known for its expert facials, Synergie treatments, and subtle, transformative results.
articles.body: Melbourne's Quietly Iconic Skin Clinic Tucked above the buzz of South Yarra’s Toorak Road sits one of Melbourne’s most quietly iconic skin clinics: Me Skin & Body If you climb the stairs of the elegant terrace that houses Joey Scandizzo’s salon you'll find this South Yarra staple that’s been quietly transforming skin for over 25 years. Owned by skincare expert Brooke Holmes (also known as Zoe Foster Blake’s go-to skin wizard) and experienced dermal clinician Rachael Hofer, Me Skin & Body offers a rare blend of cutting-edge treatments and soul-soothing care. Brooke’s philosophy is all about marrying serious skin science with a nurturing, intuitive touch, and that’s exactly what I experienced during my visit. I was lucky enough to be booked in with co-owner Rachael, whose magic hands gave me one of the most memorable facials I’ve had in a long time. Synergie Skindulgence Facial Treatment The Facial: Synergie Skindulgence in Expert Hands The moment I lay down on the treatment bed, I knew I was in expert hands. Rachael started with a thorough skin analysis using a wood’s lamp, then moved into the clinic’s Signature Synergie Skindulgence Facial. It’s a tailored treatment that pairs Synergie Skin’s high-performance cosmeceuticals with layered massage and gentle yet powerful actives. (As it happened, I’d just interviewed Synergie founder Terri Vinson the day before for the podcast, so it felt serendipitous to experience the products in a treatment setting so soon after. And yes, they absolutely delivered.) The facial began with a double cleanse and a Synergie lactic acid peel to gently exfoliate, followed by sonophoresis infusion with the brand’s B serum and Hylavive for deep, targeted hydration. But the real hero here? The massage. Why Expert Massage Transforms Your Facial Why Massage Makes All the Difference I’ve always believed that the difference between a good facial and a great one lies in the hands. You can have all the tools, lasers and serums in the world, but if the massage is lacklustre, it just doesn’t hit the same. Rachael’s hands? Pure alchemy. She strummed my facial muscles, released the tension in my jaw and neck, and worked lymphatic pathways in a way that lifted, sculpted and calmed me on every level. What Is Buccal Massage, And Why You Need It Then came the pièce de résistance: buccal massage. If you haven’t tried it, it’s where the therapist uses gloved hands inside your mouth to massage your jaw and cheeks. I know, it sounds a bit nuts. But it’s unbelievably effective for releasing tension and lifting the face. When Rachael removed her hands 10 minutes later, I felt a wave of release, it was as if my jaw had unclenched for the first time in months. My face felt… spacious. Acupressure Bliss and Glowing Results Post-Facial Glow and Acupressure Bliss She followed with a long, luxurious session of acupressure facial massage, and by the time I floated out, my skin was noticeably brighter and plumper, and I felt lighter, more grounded, and more than a little bit glowy from the inside out. I was so impressed with how much clinical know-how Rachael brought to the treatment, but also how nurturing the whole experience was. That’s the magic of Me Skin & Body: they’re able to deliver real, skin-changing results and hold space for your nervous system to rest and reset. Laser and Advanced Treatment Options What Else Is On Offer at Me Skin & Body? Next time, I’m planning to try some of their more intensive tech offerings: the Cutera Excel V (which uses Laser Genesis to target fine lines, redness and pore size)…

articles.title: Mineral Lifestyle Hair Spa, Paddington
articles.author: Isabella Ousby
articles.excerpt: 17 Oxford Street, Paddington, NSW 2021 (02) 9360 7311
articles.body: An Eco-Conscious Salon in Paddington \ \ \ Being perennially well groomed while being eco-aware is no mean feat. Most salons and spas unfortunately put the environment pretty low on their list. Mineral Lifestyle Hair Spa in Paddington is different. Tucked inside the retro chic Verona cinema complex in Paddington, the space is specifically designed to be carbon and gender neutral. Oh, and beautiful. With earthy wood tones throughout, mirrored walls and flattering lighting it’s the perfect backdrop to Aveda services for which they are a flagship Spa and Salon. Dedication to creating a calm ambiance throughout, with muted tones and zen lighting, sets this spa apart from the rest. Aveda Spa Facial and Foot Scrub Upon arrival I am offered a glass of Aveda tea; a refreshing mix of licorice root and peppermint, which I sip while filling out a chart of my skin’s needs. I’m shown to my room where I put on a luxe robe and then meet my therapist. She asks me to sit down and gently begins a soothing foot scrub before asking me to smell my way through an array of beautifully scented Aveda oils. I’m asked to chose the oil I find the most relaxing, this will be used in my treatment. After cleansing my skin, I’m ready for an Aveda Perfecting Plant Peel Facial. After years on Roacatane, I’ve always had quite sensitive skin and would ordinarily not sign myself up for a peel. However, the thought of a deep cleanse and rejuvenating my skin fresh for the weekend seems the perfect end to my week. The treatment begins with the Aveda Botanical Kinetics Cleanser and Aveda Botanical Kinetics Skin Firming/Toning Agent Mist they smell so heavenly I mentally add to cart. BRINGING THE OUTSIDE, IN WITH TIMBERS AND GREENERY TO GREET CLIENTS The Perfecting Plant Peel Treatment After my skin is prepped, the peel is applied and a hot towel is wrapped around my face. I can feel the requisite tingle of the peel doing its work while I’m treated to a foot massage. Just before I slip into sleep, the treatment finishes gently with the Aveda Botanical Kinetics Soft Creme. Coming back to the real world after such a relaxing treatment is no easy task. WHATEVER YOUR PAMPERING NEEDS, THE SPA HAS YOU SORTED FROM HEAD TO TOE Hair Styling With Aveda Damage Remedy Back in the salon, it’s time to move onto hair. I’ve recently cut all mine off in a bit of a ‘Bingle bob’, a blunt, no-fuss cut. In keeping with their attention to detail and environmentally conscious stance, all at the salon’s magazines are digitally available on iPads, which I flick through casually. My hairstylist and I discuss what she will be doing with my hair and we decide on some ‘effortless’ waves. Well they’re effortless on my behalf, at least! Before my wash, I’m treated to a shoulder massage with Aveda’s Blue Oil, a blend of peppermint and blue chamomile oil designed to help focus and relax. I have dyed blonde hair so I’m always looking for ways to rehydrate the drying effects of bleach, so take mental notes to start using the Aveda Damage Remedy Shampoo, Conditioner and Daily Hair Repair, a leave-in conditioner, they use on me. Final Results and Mineral Makeup Touch Once I’m in the chair it’s on to taming my thick tresses. When it’s finished I run my fingers through my hair and can instantly feel the softening effects of the treatment. To finish my pampering experience, I leave the salon with a light touch of Aveda mineral makeup and…

articles.title: Mr Burrows, Newtown
articles.author: Megan McGlinchey
articles.excerpt: An award-finalist salon on Enmore Road where organic, Australian-made products meet expert cuts designed to look just as good weeks after your appointment.
articles.body: Nestled in the eclectic inner west suburb of Newtown, Mr Burrows Hair is a kitschy-cool salon that is fitted out with a woody, inviting interior that feels somewhat like being at home, only more luxurious. Lush gardens make this space a haven in the hustle of the city, and combined with fabulous staff who pay the highest amount of attention to the finer details, Mr Burrows Hair is a heavenly salon experience. --- Located on Enmore Road right near Newtown Station, Mr Burrows was listed as 'Australian Hair Fashion Award Finalist' in 2014 for good reason. Upon arrival, I am greeted with a beverage of choice (my choice? A deliciously bubbly glass of organic champagne) and a gorgeous cheese platter. The staff definitely know how to host a beautiful experience from the get-go. The salon was created by Mr James Burrows himself, who has been working at the height of hair colour and styling for 10 years and working as a senior designer for six. The salon also boasts a line of staff James has clearly trained technically so there is little room for error. All cuts are created to ensure longevity of style (through a particular layering method). Their approach is to gift you with a style that ensures you look glamorous every day, and not just for the few days after you leave the salon. For this reason, they provide in-depth tips on how to recreate the look at home so you aren't left with that post-salon depression that comes after the next wash. Perfect for anyone who's far from being an expert with the blow dryer (like yours truly). Mr Burrows have an organic product philosophy which is evident from the shampoo right through to the colours. There's no harsh chemicals or toxic ingredients in any products, and on top of this, they're all Australian made. Leaving the salon I feel completely refreshed and confident. It's actually the first time I've walked out of a salon without that nail biting fear or horrible sense of regret. If you're ever in the inner west and want to stray from your usual, head straight to Mr Burrows. Review by Sigourney Cantelo

articles.title: Mukti Organics Beauty Rooms, Mullumbimby
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: The flagship treatment rooms behind Mukti's certified-organic skincare line. Natural facials, Healite LED and Buccal massage in Mullumbimby.
articles.body: Mukti spent twenty years building a certified-organic skincare house that people now speak about in slightly hushed tones. This is where it lives in the flesh. The Beauty Rooms in Mullumbimby are the flagship, soft and quiet, the treatment side of a brand you have probably seen on a bathroom shelf. The facials use nothing that is not natural and certified organic. There is Healite LED for the science, and a Buccal facial that works the muscles from inside your cheeks, which is stranger and better than it sounds. The founder wrote the book on this. Literally. It is called Truth in Beauty.

articles.title: Painted, Darlinghurst
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: The anti-strip-mall manicure. Sunlit, flower-filled, health-conscious and custom-furnished by Palomar Rowe. Waterless pedicures, non-toxic polish and a silent-service option.
articles.body: Sunlit, flower-filled, and a world away from the strip-mall bar. Nicole Doube-May left a career in software to open the nail salon she could not find, and Painted is the design-led, health-conscious result, its furniture custom-made by the Sydney fabricators Palomar Rowe. The point of difference is real. Waterless pedicures to cut infection risk, non-toxic polish, hospital-grade sterilisation. Dazzle Dry and CND Shellac on the trolley, builder gel for anyone who wants length, and nail art that runs from mirror chrome to intricate 3D. There is even a silent-service option for the overstimulated. Book ahead, because everyone wants in. The anti-strip-mall manicure, and the nicest room to have one in.

articles.title: Pamperina, Woollahra
articles.author: Tess Schlink
articles.excerpt: The European-inspired salon that caters to all your beauty needs.
articles.body: It’s a bright, clear winter’s morning in Sydney’s Woollahra when I slip off a bustling tree-lined street into Pamperina’s chic and cosy salon. The brainchild of Georgie Palamountain, the salon offers a full suite of beauty treatments all in one elegantly-appointed space. European-Inspired Treatments in Woollahra Since opening in early 2019, the salon has been treating Sydney’s well-heeled beauty lovers to European-inspired facials, manicures and pedicures, lash treatments, waxing, and more, and I’m excited to experience what it’s got on offer. Meeting Silvia the Classical Therapist I’m welcomed by the charming Silvia, my beauty therapist for today. Possessing that characteristically Italian warmth, she describes herself as a classical beauty therapist, favouring non-invasive, traditional facials for long-term skin health. She talks me through the Continental ranges and techniques she was trained with that she’s looking to introduce to Australia. In Italy, she shares, women invest in monthly facials (as, famously, French women also typically do), while in her experience Australian women tend to be less diligent with regular treatments, then try to correct things later with injectables. I like the sound of her gentler philosophy to skin health and make a mental note to be more disciplined with my facials. The Signature Deep Pore Cleansing Facial Today I’m experiencing Pamperina’s Signature Deep Pore Cleansing Facial, a comprehensive treatment that promises a purified and hydrated complexion, which I’ll never say no to. It involves a thorough cleanse and extractions, and a glow-giving enzyme peel from Dr Spiller, topped off with hydrating ampoules, masks, and serums to round out the treatment. The salon uses a select edit of brands, including Dermalogica, Dr Spiller, and Dr Alex, which they also have available to purchase to complement their treatment regimen. Anti-Cellulite Lymphatic Drainage Massage I’m then treated to their ‘Anti-Cellulite Lymphatic Drainage Leg and Tummy Massage’, a satisfyingly thorough massage that’s simultaneously quite intense and relaxing. For those unfamiliar, your lymphatic system transports fluids around the body but needs constant stimulation (through exercise or body brushing, both of which I’ve been guilty of neglecting) to keep things moving. This hardcore muscle manipulation allows your body to rid itself of fluid retention, and I’m left feeling lighter and energised. Silvia imparts that putting your legs up a wall for ten minutes a day is a simple way to care for your lymphatic system by letting gravity draw down excess fluids, and I vow to recommit to my body brushing practice and to up my daily step count, as well as scheduling in these massages regularly. Glowing Skin and Post-Facial Results At the end of the treatment, Silvia greets me with a beautiful cut crystal glass of water (the treatment lasted some two hours overall so I’m in need of a dose of rehydration) and I emerge from the treatment with majorly hydrated and glowy skin. I’m being treated to a surprise dinner out with my husband tonight (our first date night in months due to lockdown) and I think I need just a few licks of mascara and a brow brush to be ready to go, no base products required. Review by Tess de Vivie de Régie. Images from Pamperina.

articles.title: Polished Beauty Rooms, Byron Bay
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: A low-tox nail spa in Byron Bay built around the world's best considered brands. Nails, skin, brows, lashes and scalp under one soft roof.
articles.body: Polished is a nail spa that thinks about what it puts on you. The founder went looking for the world's best low-tox brands for nails, skin and scalp, and built the room around them. So a manicure here is not just colour. It is your nails treated as something attached to a person you would like to keep healthy. There is skin, there are brows and lashes, and there is scalp work, all under one soft considered roof in Byron. First timers get an LED session thrown in. Book a colour and stay for the calm. It earns the name.

articles.title: Que Colour, Darlinghurst
articles.author: Amanda Chan
articles.excerpt: A first-person review of QUE Colour in Darlinghurst, where balayage specialist Taylah delivers golden, sun-kissed highlights using Olaplex in an intimate exposed-brick salon.
articles.body: As I arrive and take a seat inside the salon, I’m immediately offered tea and coffee by the lovely staff. The salon itself is intimate and tucked away in the streets of Darlinghurst, allowing you to sit back, relax and let the professionals take care of you. Monique’s team have a plethora of experience under their wings, and many have jetsetted around the globe with a portfolio of star clients in tow. I’m greeted by Taylah, who listens attentively to my aspirations of going lighter and recommends balayage to ease into the lightening process. She starts by adding chocolate foils near the top of the roots, followed by baby blond and biscuity tones throughout the rest of my hair to lighten up around the face. The colourists at Que know how to seamlessly achieve colour that instantly rejuvenates and revives otherwise lacklustre hair. I watch in awe as Taylah does my foils with precision, and then with a freehand technique, sweeps on Olaplex’s Bond Multiplier to the lower sections of my hair. Olaplex is a revolutionary new active ingredient, which lightens and colours the hair without any breakage, perfect for aspiring blondes. We chat away about Fashion week and where she was part of the team backstage with Ginger and Smart this year. After a few minutes of waiting for the colour to lift, I’m sent to basin for it all to be washed out. The head massage instantly relaxes any stress and tension I’d brought with me. Taylah also uses Christophe Robin’s Regenerating Mask with Rare Prickly Pear Seed Oil on me, an amazing product which immediately softens and strengthens my hair with the addition of smelling divine! Back at my seat and Taylah starts blow drying my hair, I let out an involuntary gasp, my hair looks incredible. The afternoon light bounces off the new additions of golden hues and I leave the salon feeling like I’ve been transformed into an effortless Parisian It girl without a care in the world. I’ll definitely be coming back for my next colour. Review by Amanda Chan.

articles.title: Raw Anthony Nader, Surry Hills
articles.author: Jill Sandringham
articles.excerpt: Taking up residence in a hip pocket of Surry Hills in the area's busy Commonwealth Street, Anthony Nader's hair salon Raw is positively buzzing.
articles.body: Taking up residence in a hip pocket of Surry Hills in the area's busy Commonwealth Street, Anthony Nader's hair salon Raw is positively buzzing. A member of Australian hairdressing royalty, Nader and his salon have picked up numerous awards in recent years, including Australian Hairdresser of the Year. The salon is comfortable and resembles a smart loft-style apartment in Tribeca, New York where Nader himself lives six months of the year. This tress-tamer to the stars (he's looked after everyone from Gisele Bundchen to Nicole Richie) can also be found regularly taking up residence backstage in fashion catwalk shows in New York, London and Milan. The rustic and industrial look of the salon's smart interior is all dark wood panels and deliberately exposed wooden frames, brick walls and low-hanging pendants. There is an industrial, unfinished air about the place that makes a refreshing change from the glitz and bling of other top salons. And, well, it's an appropriate look for a salon named Raw, after all. Despite the relaxed look of the interior, don't be fooled into believing you will get anything less than an upmarket service here. For, after being charmingly greeted by the receptionist and ushered into a plush leather chair I was instantly offered tea (organic; and a variety of creeds and colours), coffee (latte, cappuccino, you name it) and even a glass of champagne. Half a glass of bubbly down and I came face-to-face (in the mirror) with the salon's lovely Stella. She's worked there seven years now and certainly knows her stuff. She took me to the "relaxation pod" for my wash, a soundproofed room at the back of the salon where an earthly form of heaven is located, they have full reclining massage chairs imported from Japan that take a simple wash to another level entirely. So, after a swift soaking of my naturally untameable tresses (with Anthony Nader shampoo and conditioner, of course) and a tip from the assistant to always make the last rinse cold-ish in order to close the cuticles and make the hair stack on my head more manageable) it was time to visit the loo (or rather the shrine to Madonna, Nader is a huge fan). So anyway, interiors aside, how was my hair? Well let's just say, the salon is now a set of GHD hair straighteners down and I've already booked my next appointment. Review by Jill Sandringham

articles.title: Rêve Skin + Beauty, Annandale
articles.author: Angie Vida
articles.excerpt: Inside Rêve Skin + Beauty in Annandale, a women-only skin clinic where science-led treatments meet calm, thoughtful care.
articles.body: Women-only sanctuary where science meets softness. Tucked into the heart of Annandale, Rêve Skin + Beauty is the kind of place you discover once - and immediately wonder how you ever lived without it. Occupying a beautiful corner position on Booth and View Street, Rêve Skin + Beauty Annandale announces itself quietly but confidently. My eye was instantly drawn to the warm burgundy exterior, rich, elegant and inviting. As I stepped through the front door, adorned with an oversized bow for the festive season, I felt an immediate sense of ease. Not rushed. Not clinical. Just calm. Founder Meghann Nikola and her team greeted me warmly at the door, and before I had even begun my tour, a loyal client followed closely behind me, happily sharing how devoted she is to Meghann and how regularly she books her appointments. It felt like the ultimate endorsement, the kind of loyalty that can’t be manufactured. Thoughtful Design, Inside and Out As I was guided through the space, it became clear that every detail at Rêve has been thoughtfully considered . Soft lighting that flatters rather than interrogates. Beautiful cabinetry that feels as practical as it is elegant. Even thoughtful touches like in-built charging cables during treatments, because yes, we’ve all been there. Meghann and I spoke briefly about her background in science and pharmaceutical marketing, which so clearly underpins everything she has created here. Rêve isn’t simply about indulgence, it’s about evidence-based treatments delivered with warmth, honesty and connection. A high-end experience, without the intimidation that sometimes accompanies clinical spaces. A high-end experience, without the intimidation that sometimes accompanies clinical spaces. Treatments That Prioritise Skin Health I was then whisked away for my very first lash lift with Samantha. I’ll admit I was slightly nervous, but her calm confidence immediately put me at ease. The results were genuinely impressive, and it was clear I was in expert hands. My lash lift and tint flowed seamlessly into a Hydrafacial , with a thoughtful handover between therapists to explain aftercare, a small detail, but one that speaks volumes about the level of care here. During the Hydrafacial, I chatted with Faireen about skin and her extensive experience in the beauty industry, spanning more than 15 years. As the treatment progressed, I could feel the gentle warmth on my skin as the glycolic and salicylic acids worked their magic. The treatment was finished with a decadent layer of Synergie Skincare and a generous application of UberZinc , leaving my skin calm, nourished and visibly refreshed. A Retreat Built on Trust From there, I headed downstairs to meet Sara for my manicure . Her work was beautifully precise, leaving me with soft pink nails that felt polished yet effortless. Exactly my style. What struck me most throughout my time at Rêve was the sense of trust that naturally develops when you’re being cared for by therapists who truly know their craft. There’s a particular touch that conveys confidence and expertise, something refined only through years in the industry. Every team member I met at Rêve seemed to possess it. A Moment of Calm in the Middle of the Week Founder Meghann Nikola’s mission is simple but powerful: to build confidence and connection through tailored treatments and compassionate care. She wants every client to feel seen, supported and celebrated, and it’s something you feel in every interaction. Spending time in a space where multiple treatments can be seamlessly delivered by highly skilled professionals, surrounded by such beautiful interiors, left me feeling genuinely uplifted, especially on what had otherwise been an ordinary weekday. My time at Rêve Skin…

articles.title: Robertson Kirkwood Salon, Rozelle
articles.author: Megan McGlinchey
articles.excerpt: A tranquil Aveda flagship salon on Darling Street where owner Terri Robertson Kirkwood, Hair Director for David Jones, delivers expert colour, cuts and botanical treatments.
articles.body: Situated in the inner west suburb of Rozelle, is flagship Aveda salon, Robertson Kirkwood. With minimalist lines and modern fittings, the space is flooded by an abundance of natural light. The friendly team ooze warmth and knowledge from the moment you walk in the door, making you never want to leave. As I walk through the doors off the busy Darling Street, I’m greeted by the most gorgeous light fitting I’ve ever seen. I’m ushered through to a streamlined bucket chair, and caped up before being offered an Aveda Stress Relieving Ritual with a head and neck oil massage, using the brand’s beautiful Blue Oil, a mix of blue chamomile and peppermint, which proves nothing short of magic. Suddenly the woes of Sydney’s nightmarish traffic and short-term parking schemes melt away. I’m then introduced to the salon owner and highly esteemed Aveda stylist, Terri Robertson Kirkwood. From a few minutes of chatting, I clock that this is a woman of serious hair know-how and capability. After a few leading questions about my personal hair habits and lifestyle, she has a game plan for my tortured strands, and I’m whisked away for a wash. THE SALON STAYS TRUE TO AVEDA'S FOCUS ON NATURE AND WELLBEING, AS WELL AS RESULTS. Given that I’m a bit hot-tong-happy at the best of times (and have the split ends to prove it) Terri prescribes the Aveda Dry Remedy hair range. After a wash with Aveda Dry Remedy Shampoo, followed by a generous lick of the leave in Dry Remedy Moisturizing Masque to intensely hydrate and lock in moisture, I can always hear my tresses singing with happiness. Next up, Terri applies the Aveda Dry Remedy Daily Moisturizing Oil to help nourish and coat the ends of my hair. I can safely say that this is a product I will treasure and re-purchase for many years to come as it gave my hair an undeniable gloss and softness. Later that evening, friends were commenting on my hair and asking if I’d had it coloured, when all I’d had was a wash and style. A ZEN HIDEAWAY FROM THE FRENETIC CITY SURROUNDINGS With the split ends addressed and my head feeling exceptionally refreshed, it was time for my blowdry, a skill I endeavour to hone before 2017. After discussing season trends (something the salon is clearly well versed in as Terri is the Hair Director for the David Jones National Fashion Launch) we settle on an effortless, fallen curl look that would accentuate the newly nourished tresses. As she expertly wound my strands around a big round brush, Terri chats through the process, giving me tips and tricks to make my own technique a little more professional. I love it when stylists take the time to explain what they’re doing. With Terri at the helm and an accomplished team of hairstylists working alongside her, there’s something truly special, tranquil and personable about this salon experience. I’ll definitely be heading back for a colour consult and cut.

articles.title: Roji, Canberra
articles.author: Katherine Ring
articles.excerpt: 25 Edinburgh Ave, Canberra ACT 2601.

articles.title: Salon x, Paddington

articles.excerpt: 86 William StreetPaddington NSW 2021

articles.title: Skin and Tonic, Armidale
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Thirty-four years of skin thinking on Rusden Street in Armidale. Bio-microneedling, infrared sauna, and considered lines like The Beauty Chef, Meder and Inika Organic.
articles.body: Maryann has been doing skin for thirty-four years, which means she has watched every trend arrive, peak and quietly disappear. Skin & Tonic, her room on Rusden Street, is built against all that. No chasing the new thing. Just the long game of skin that holds up over decades. She works with bio-microneedling and skin needling, has an infrared sauna, and stocks the good, considered lines. The Beauty Chef, Meder, Inika Organic. Armidale is not where you expect this level of skin thinking. That is precisely why it is worth the drive up. Experience you cannot fake. Only earn.

articles.title: Skin Temple, Melbourne
articles.author: Vickie Zarifopoulos
articles.excerpt: A Turkish-inspired medispa on St Kilda Road where hammam escapism meets serious clinical results, led by cosmetic physician Dr Alicia Teska.
articles.body: Tucked away on leafy St. Kilda Road in Melbourne is Skin Temple, a medispa in the purest sense of the word. With five treatment rooms, a stunning tiled hammam and a treatment list to rival exotic spas in Asia and the Middle East, the sizeable location is just the ticket when you want a seriously credible skin treatment combined with the escapism of a spa. Presided over by respected Cosmetic Physician Dr Alicia Teska, the team are experts at addressing even the most serious skin woes. ambience is the call of the day at the chic medispa Arriving at the Turkish-Inspired Medispa As I step through the entry from Arnold Street into the waiting area I clock a large armchair, fresh white walls and gilded mirrors. Tea light candles light the way, enticing me to reception. Today I’m booked in for a Pigment Regulating Facial and on arrival I’m warmly greeted and seated in the waiting area. I have to admit I’m feeling a little nervous. The treatment, by US Cosmeceutical brand Skinceuticals, contains a high concentration of glycolic and salicylic acids. Being so active, I wonder if I’ll still be able to drift off to my happy place. I’m introduced to my dermal therapist, Leanne, and shown to a large bathroom where I change into a soft waffle robe and slippers. Once in the facial treatment room, Leanne soaks my feet in a copper bowl of warm bubbles and asks me about my skin’s general condition and my pigmentation concerns. Despite wearing sunblock religiously, I’m starting to see the first patches of pigmentation on my cheeks and nose. Leanne tells me it’s actually very common for pigmentation to be predominately sitting under the surface of the skin. This sends me into a little bit of a panic, but I decide to wait until she looks at me properly under the magnifying mirror. The Pigment Regulating Facial Experience Once tucked into the heated bed, Leanne starts off with a good cleanse and exfoliation. With the day’s debris removed, she examines my skin under the lamp. I feel like I’m anxiously awaiting a score from the judges, but despite the beginnings of some pigmentation, Leanne compliments me on the overall health and condition of my complexion. Her gentle and kind manner helps put me at ease. I’m beginning to nestle further into my cosy blanket cocoon, as Leanne mixes my mask. She warns me that some tingling and tightness will be experienced while the mask is on. I brace myself for the worst. But Leanne is incredibly professional and attentive. While she massages my neck and arms, she keeps a dialogue going and checks in regularly to assess if I am experiencing any pain or discomfort. A few tingles and I can definitely feel it working; so far, so good. Post-Treatment Glow and Aftercare Despite trying to stay present and focused, I drift away. The massage comes to an end, the mask is washed off and a serum and moisturiser are applied. Leanne treats me to a cup of tea and a rose water Turkish delight while I sit up and regroup. I look in the mirror and, although I’m a little red and sensitive in places, I can already see my skin is looking brighter. instant calm, the moment you step through the door creature comforts while you wait After I’m dressed, Leanne talks me through an aftercare regime; staying out of the sun and using some specific products, so I take home a three day course of skincare. This includes sunscreen and a tinted moisturiser to cover any redness…

articles.title: Skinologie, Albert Park
articles.author: Rikki Hodge-Smith
articles.excerpt: Dr Ceylan Yilmaz and her dermal clinicians use Visia imaging, lactic peels and sonophoresis to deliver completely individualised skin treatments with zero downtime.
articles.body: In the leafy beach-side Melbourne suburb of Albert Park is skin clinic, Skinologie. Under Dr Ceylan Yilmaz and her team of dermal clinicians, Skinologie doesn’t believe in a one-size-fits-all approach to skin. Rather, they employ the latest technology, and the most thorough analysis to discover exactly what each skin needs. Our Beauticate Managing Editor, Rikki, visited Skinologie to find out some skin secrets that she didn’t know were hiding beneath the surface… Booking the Hero Facial Treatment Some time after my 28th birthday I started to notice the signs of (gulp) ageing. However, now in my 30s I have a new perspective; ageing is not end of days, but it does mean I need to take better care of my skin than I did at 21. Including, getting the right facials. So when I heard about Skinologie’s individualised approach to skin I was keen to try it out. I’ve booked for ‘The Hero’, a treatment developed by Dr Yilmaz that uses microdermabrasion, laser and a peel for maximum results with no downtime. Visia Skin Imaging and Consultation I walk into the medispa and notice the space is full of light and immaculate but not soulless, small touches like the fragrant floral arrangement at the entrance keep it inviting. I’m greeted by my facialist, Kate. She gives me a very detailed form to fill out in preparation for my consultation. I hesitate at being truthful, they’re very serious about skin and I haven’t abided by too many rules, do I tell them I don’t use serum?? Eek. We begin with a Visia (a facial imaging system), something I’ve always wanted to try. I pop my chin on to this futuristic imaging machine and it takes several 3D photos. Then come the home truths… My biggest concerns beforehand were pigmentation (intensified during pregnancy a little over a year ago) from my early-20s spent thinking my pale skin would tan if I just fried it at midday. Discovering Melasma and a Customised Plan The image is a bit startling, I won’t lie. The images emphasise each concern, so pigmentation, for example, appears several shades darker. The Visia confirms my concerns, although it’s melasma, rather than UV damage, that is causing most of my pigmentation. Melasma, Kate tells me, is type of pigmentation with a hormonal cause. Unfortunately, without proper skin-prepping homecare, this rules out ‘The Hero’. So we decide upon a lactic peel followed by an infusion of potent antioxidants. Kate tells me the lactic is a gentle, hydrating type of peel that will slough off my dead skin cells and plump up my dehydrated skin. Rather than just applying the antioxidant, Kate says she’ll use sonophoresis, an ultrasound instrument that will the amplify the penetration of the potent antioxidant cocktail. She’ll then finish with an extra-boosting peptide mask. Lactic Peel and Sonophoresis Treatment Kate leads me to one of the treatment rooms and I snuggle into the pre-warmed bed. She asks me if I’d prefer to be talked through each step or enjoy the quiet time, I go for the latter (mum to a little boy, quiet moments are few and far between). Relaxing into the bed, she gently applies the peel. As pre-warned, it is a bit tingling, but nothing unbearable. After this, the sonophoresis is like a warm massage on the skin. Speaking of massage, Kate gives me a shoulder massage, I could almost drift off to sleep. Tailored Skincare Regime and Fresh Results After an hour and a final application of hydrating serum and SPF, we’re done. I can already feel the renewed freshness on my skin. Kate goes…

articles.title: SURSKIN, West Leederville
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Skin care that behaves like a spa day. SURSKIN on Cambridge Street combines injectables and dermal therapies with a private sauna, cold plunge and the Wellness Ritual for Two.
articles.body: The name used to be SurFACEskin, which told you exactly where its attention stopped. SURSKIN dropped the FACE to make a point. The work here goes past the surface. On Cambridge Street in West Leederville the menu runs from injectables and dermal therapies to lymphatic drainage and something called the Crystal Energy Facial, which is more restful than the name suggests. There is a private sauna and a cold plunge on site, so skin and body get treated in the same visit. The Wellness Ritual for Two puts a couple through all of it in an afternoon. It is skin care that behaves like a spa day. Book the ritual. Bring someone.

articles.title: The Facialist Darwin, Darwin
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: A pared-back sage green studio working with dermaviduals, the bespoke system where products are mixed to your skin rather than pulled off a shelf.
articles.body: The whole studio is done in sage green, pared right back, nothing to compete with the reason you came. This is skin, taken seriously. The Facialist works with dermaviduals, the bespoke system where products are mixed to your skin rather than pulled off a shelf, and builds treatments around what your face actually needs on the day. No jargon thrown at you for effect. No upselling a ten-step routine you will never do. Just a considered facialist in a calm green room, reading your skin properly. Book once. You will understand the loyalty immediately.

articles.title: The Facialist Noosa, Noosa Heads
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Face sculpting and buccal massage from a world-trained facialist in a private Noosa Heads studio. Anna Walker works with Sodashi and Murad, and she knows exactly what she is doing.
articles.body: Anna Walker trained under some of the best facialists in the world and now works out of a small private studio at Noosa Heads. The Facialist is pared back on purpose. No noise, no upsell, just skin. Walker specialises in face sculpting and buccal massage, the inside-the-cheek work that lifts and drains, and she is Reiki trained on top of it. Skincare is healthcare is her line, and she means it. The shelves are Sodashi and Murad, botanical and clinical in equal measure. New clients get a proper consult first. Book the sculpting facial and watch your jaw reappear. She knows exactly what she is doing.

articles.title: The Parlour Room, Clovelly
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: This bright and poppy salon in Clovelly is fast becoming one of Sydney's best-loved neighbourhood beauty destinations, nails, brows, tanning and a house nail polish line called COAT.
articles.body: The Parlour Room is bright and poppy salon in Clovelly that is fast becoming the go-to nail, brow and tanning hotspot for Sydney’s social set. The boutique beauty destination, with its trademark tropical yellow wallpaper, is part of a new wave of highly visible, social-media-savvy salons that are gathering a loyal following on Instagram. Owner Natalie is at Home in the Salon Instagram-Powered Bookings and Buzz “Everything is through Instagram. We get so many bookings from it,” confirms The Parlour Room owner Natalie Papadopolous as she welcomes me in and introduces me to Heather who will be doing my pedicure. I take a seat on the banquette and watch as the busy salon welcomes a stream of upbeat customers. Testament to their social media prowess is the Instagram wall, which takes up pride of place alongside the communal manicure table. The wall is chock-a-block with selfies from the Parlour Room’s gorgeous clients, among which are many high profile models and bloggers, all posing proudly with their bright glossy manicures and flawless self tans. Meet the Founder Behind the Salon Natalie, a gorgeous redhead with a wealth of experience in the beauty industry, opened her salon three years ago after working for key players in the beauty industry. Nat, who used to do all her girlfriends makeup before they went out on a Saturday night, wanted to recreate that social, supportive atmosphere in a salon, and to create a place where clients felt comfortable and celebrated their beauty in a non-judgemental space. The Instagram Wall of Selfies The Instagram Wall of Selfies “I love bringing a group of girls together, to make them feel really beautiful and happy about themselves,” she says. A Social Salon Atmosphere That Keeps Clients Returning She’s definitely succeeded. On this particular day, I note several of the city’s most glamorous young things prepping for events they’re attending that evening, as they put important decisions like nail shades and tanning formulas up for discussion. Within minutes we’re rating the various merits of each as if we’re old friends. Nat believes it’s this buzz and atmosphere that keeps people coming back. “People don’t know each other but they say they feel so comfortable talking to each other,” she says. “We also treat every client like a celebrity. We take time to make sure the treatment’s perfect, that we get every hair during a wax or if it’s raining we escort them to their car with an umbrella.” Salon Tour and Spray Tan Setup With my punchy coral pedicure complete (and my feet looking about a thousand times better), I take a quick tour. The five room salon features fresh, colourful décor, a chic black bathroom, and gorgeous flowers from local florist Rheannon Lee. I note appreciatively that the two tanning rooms also have high-powered extractor fans (to protect your lungs from the fumes) and Nat tells me proudly that the spray tan machines are powered by the same system they use to spray cars. I also love that they use sticky feet to ensure you don’t get self tan on the bottom of your feet. Little details like this are essential for a good quality spray tan. The Salon is Always Buzzing Details Make the Treatment Rooms Feel Like Home COAT Nail Polish and Beauty Partnerships In addition to stocking Techno Tan, J Bronze & Sunescape for tanning, Curtis Collection for makeup and Skinstitut skincare, Natalie has also created her own line of nail polish called COAT and she and her staff were asked by Bec & Bridge to do nails for their Fashion Week Show. The range…

articles.title: Liberty Belle, Melbourne
articles.author: Zoe Briggs
articles.excerpt: Hidden behind tall hedges on Toorak Road, Liberty Belle is Melbourne's purpose-built aesthetics compound where bespoke Dermasweep facials and LED therapy deliver visible results for a discerning clientele.
articles.body: Tucked away behind tall hedges from the prying eyes of Toorak Road, in that most old money of Melbourne suburbs, lies Liberty Belle, a purpose-built compound devoted to all things aesthetics. Twin buildings in pale stone surrounded by well tended jasmine house staff with the ability to treat just about any skin concern you could think of, at whichever level you’re after. On the right hand side is the plastic surgery centre, run by Dr Chris Moss, and on the left is the skincare clinic, the destination for those who are a little less brave (that would be me) but who still want visible results. Skin Assessment and Double Cleanse Before we begin my bespoke Belle Dermasweep facial, my therapist Marnie asks me about my skin. I sheepishly explain that everything is a bit red and delicate, as I have recently been upping my prescription retinoid in the hope of putting an end to my persistent acne. So that she can see for herself exactly what she is dealing with, she performs a thorough double cleanse under bright lights, and reader, I may never have been so quickly put at ease so early on in a facial. Frankly, I think this should be the standard way all therapists begin treatments, rather than relying on the far less experienced client’s own assessment (or starting things off with whale song and aromatherapy oils). Before Photos and Inspiring Transformations Marnie then whisks me into a separate room where I, totally bare faced, am photographed from every angle. Skin tone mugshot complete, I do feel a little vulnerable, but she assures me the pictures won’t be seen by anyone but clinic staff. Some clients have loved their results enough to approve their before and after shots being featured on the walls, and it is certainly reassuring, if not downright inspiring, to see what can be achieved.
