Bespoke Dermasweep Facial Treatment We head back to the treatment room, where Marnie tells me that she will perform a bespoke treatment that will give me the results I am after, less red, more glow, please, while taking care of my poor, decimated skin barrier. She explains that Liberty Belle’s Dermasweep is gentler than standard dermabrasion, and their special tool has two heads and three functions: the tiny street sweeper head brushes off debris, the second suction head sucks it up away from the face, and then there’s also a smooth, cooling element, designed to push serum into the impeccably cleaned skin. Extractions and Yellow LED Light Therapy She the performs traditional, manual extractions (any skincare lover’s favourite part of a treatment, pain be damned), though left my active acne alone, as manipulating any spots not yet ready to come to the surface would only damage the skin further. After a special balm designed for sensitive skin is applied, I spend twenty minutes under the yellow LED light, which promotes wound healing and skin rejuvenation. For any fellow claustrophobes out there, know that Marnie first asked me outright how I felt about it, and not only took the time to show me the machine, but said that with all clients, nervous or not, she remains in the room the whole time. Liberty Belle RX Superhero Antioxidant Moisturiser The LED contains three panels, with one directly over your face and one at each side, but isn’t particularly close or confining, banish any thoughts of an MRI, and the experience itself was pleasant. I felt no anxiety at all; the light was so warm and relaxing that I was both snug and smug, knowing that such a cosy treatment was…

articles.title: The Youth Lab, Perth
articles.author: Lucy Searle
articles.excerpt: Perth’s latest offering in high-tech, paramedical treatments, led by Dr Kate Jameson in a beautifully appointed West Perth clinic.
articles.body: Youth Lab is Perth’s latest offering in high-tech, paramedical treatments, housed in a beautifully appointed clinic on a leafy street in West Perth. At the helm is Medical Director, Dr Kate Jameson, one of Perth’s most highly regarded medical aestheticians. Dr Kate leads a team of experienced and passionate dermal therapists to deliver advanced dermal therapies, injectables, dermal fillers and medical grade light based treatments in a luxurious setting. Arriving at the West Perth Clinic I arrive for my appointment on a chilly May evening and I’m thrilled to find complimentary parking out the front of Youth Lab’s gorgeous exterior. Lush greenery frames an inviting entrance which is almost Hamptons-esque. Polished floorboards, marble counters and hues of blue and white give the space a really fresh, elegant feel and I immediately sink into a plush armchair to complete my pre-appointment paperwork, iced tea in hand. The reception space feels like a boutique hotel, with stunning designer chairs, plush rugs and shelves lined with Ultraceuticals, Cosmedix and Mesoestetic products. Hydrafacial and Skin Analysis My therapist, Tash, greets me and takes me through to an equally elegant treatment room that could be mistaken for a day spa. But despite the luxury, I am not here for a scrub and massage. Today I’m having a Hydrafacial, followed by Healite II LED treatment. Tash commences with a quick cleanse before using Visia Skin Analysis imaging to have a good look at my skin and it’s needs. I’m surprised to learn my sun damage isn’t too bad and apart from one pesky pimple, redness isn’t much of an issue either. Keeping congestion levels at bay and brightening patches of pigmentation are my biggest bug bears, which is the goal for today’s treatment. How the Hydrafacial Works The ultimate multi-step treatment, the Hydrafacial promises to cleanse, evenly exfoliate and extract impurities. The treatment uses a Vortex-Fusion serum delivery system to deposit medical grade serum into the skin at each step which helps loosen up dead skin cells, while simultaneously vacuuming the skin and removing excess oil and other congestion. The treatment is completely painless (apart from a gentle sucking sensation on the skin) and requires virtually no down time, hello lunch time facial! The treatment commences with a thorough cleanse and exfoliation where excess skin cells are removed to reveal healthy, new skin. Step two involves an acid peel to help loosen dirt and debris from the pores without irritation and to make way for the next step, extractions where pores are cleaned out with vortex suction. Finally, skin is infused a potent dose of antioxidants and hyaluronic acid to nourish, protect, reduce the appearance of fine lines and provide deep hydration. Healite II LED Light Therapy After the Hydrafacial, Tash leads me into another stunning treatment room for 15 minutes of bliss under the Healite. The LED light enhances the body’s natural cellular recovery, including improving healing time, promoting skin rejuvenation and subsiding active acne if present. Glowing Results the Next Morning After the time has passed I reluctantly peel myself up off the bed and float out into the evening. My skin feels springy, super clean and I am sporting a noticeable glow, as my dinner date points out. I wake the next morning to incredibly soft and supple skin that actually seems both brighter and clearer. The blemish I went in with has faded completely within two days and makeup sits beautifully on my skin. It’s no surprise that Dr Kate and her team have a following of dedicated clientele at Youth Lab. The experience is second to none and the Hydrafacial delivered…

articles.title: Tognini's, Newstead
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: A three-time Australian Hairdresser of the Year dynasty, nearly four decades in the making.
articles.body: Founded in 1987 by Benni Tognini, a three-time Australian Hairdresser of the Year, five-time Educator of the Year and World Master Hairdresser, Tognini's is one of Brisbane's most storied salons and a genuine institution in Australian hairdressing. Now based in a purpose-built space in Newstead, the family-run salon is led by the next generation of Togninis alongside a team of award-winning stylists and Wella Colour Experts renowned for precision cutting, bespoke colour, blonding, balayage and seamless extensions. At the 2026 Australian Hair Industry Awards, Tognini's was named Australia's most nominated salon, taking home three wins. Nearly four decades on, the salon remains a creative powerhouse where mentorship, artistry and individuality sit at the heart of every appointment. Review by Sigourney Cantelo

articles.title: Vaia Beauty, Darlinghurst
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Herbalist and skin therapist Vaia Pappas brings 20 years of holistic expertise to this Darlinghurst clinic, where customised facials, infrared sauna and herbal formulas treat skin from the inside out.
articles.body: A calm and sleek oasis in the heart of East Sydney, Vaia Beauty offers a range of skin and wellness modalities under the one lofty terraced roof, from herbal health consults to infra red sauna sessions alongside customised facials and body treatments. The creation of experienced herbalist and skin sorceress Vaia Pappas, the clinic specialises in skin health and takes a uniquely holistic view of beauty therapy. A Warm Welcome in East Sydney Stepping into the fresh white space, I’m instantly greeted with a hug from Vaia. I haven’t seen her for a few years but I’ve never forgotten her facial massage. I first went to see Vaia in her tiny single-treatment roomed salon in Surry Hills over ten years ago. Her recent move into this stunning interior-designed building complete with marble bench tops, earthy finishes and Vaia’s own artworks, has clearly been a labour of love. There are even plans to open a crèche here so mums can squeeze some pampering in and keep bubs close by. Inside the Facial Treatment Room We head upstairs into Vaia’s facial room, which feels a little like being welcomed into her home. There are bunches of fresh spring blooms and crystals arranged in clusters. A writing desk looks out to a balcony heaving with potted plants and there’s a little bookcase packed with health and beauty tomes. Today I’m booked in for the Ultraceuticals Signature Facial with a side of LED light. I nestle into the cushy treatment bed and we catch up on the last ten years while Vaia cleanses and massages my skin with expert strokes. “The goal is pure relaxation today,” she says soothingly when I ask about her philosophy, as she takes the massage down to my neck and shoulders. “But I guess it’s just about really understanding and hearing a client’s needs, understanding and guiding them. And delivering targeted skin results in the most natural way possible.” Treating Skin From the Inside Out Vaia has developed a loyal customer base over 20 years in the industry thanks to an ability to diagnose and treat skin conditions from the inside out. Some of her best work has been treating acne, psoriasis, and rosacea, “I’ve even helped people fall pregnant who haven’t been able to before,” she adds mysteriously. Active Skincare and Deep Relaxation She orders pathology and analyses it to address underlying health issues then hand mixes liquid herbal formulas and prescribes appropriate skincare. She stocks her own products alongside active Australian range Ultraceuticals. “I love that they use high-grade cosmetic ingredients and create potent formulations,” she says as she applies a mask then massages my hands and feet with the Ultraceuticals Body Retexturising Complex. I start to drift off, time stands still and the minutes slip by in a haze. When the sublime facial is finished, Vaia positions the LED light over my skin then kindly offers to repaint my chipped nails for me. There’s a hilarious moment when we realise my nails are still wet and she will have to dress me. I feel like I’m five again but somehow it’s not embarrassing. A Holistic Beauty Experience There’s something very nurturing about Vaia, part Greek mama, part witchdoctor, she has that ancient gift of the healer, which is a rare thing these days. I love that you can have a wellness consult with Vaia, but also get your beauty maintenance seen to at the same time, the salon also offers waxing, tinting, nails and tans. I vow to return soon to try a course of infrared sauna sessions, just sitting in it for forty minutes apparently…

articles.title: Wieselmann, South Yarra
articles.author: Beauticate Editorial
articles.excerpt: Over 40 years on Toorak Road and still Melbourne's go-to for the perfect blonde, sophisticated colour, precision cuts and Kerastase care.
articles.body: An award-winning, sophisticated hair salon on South Yarra's cosmopolitan Toorak Road, Wieselmann is known for doing the best blondes in Melbourne. Having been in business for over 40 years and still going strong, Wieselmann definitely know a thing or two about how to create the perfect hair salon experience that will have you coming back time and time again. Stepping Inside the Toorak Road Salon Stepping inside the bustling salon at 9:30am on a Saturday morning, the first thing you notice about Wieselmann is their stylish clientele; the local fashion set with the perfect shades of blonde for their complexion, each matched with a killer blow dry. The interior is sleek, with modern black leather chairs, polished chrome finishes and floor-to-ceiling mirrored walls. It's light, bright and radiates sophistication. As I'm ushered to my seat by the warm and approachable reception staff, I order a (much needed) latté and some biscotti . I'm handed the salon's little black book of hair inspo to peruse; it's page after page of what can only be described as the ultimate edit of 'cool girl' hair -- the latest hairstyles from the likes of It-Girls Margot Robbie, Lara Bingle, and Blake Lively, to name a few. Expert Colour and Cut Consultation Dee, one of the salon owners and expert hair stylists, warmly greets me. Feeling inspired, we talk through possible cut options and decide on a short and sharp, 'of the moment' cut. Next up is my colour consultation with Di, the salon owner and my colourist, who specialises in blondes. I must confess, I always get a bit nervous having my colour done by someone who hasn't done it before because, as many blondes know, it can be tricky to get it right. After speaking to Di though, I have no doubt I'm in very safe (and highly skilled) hands. The Raw Collection by Dee Parker-Atwood -- 2015 Hair Expo Emerging Hairdresser of the Year Finalist. A Polished, Textured Blowdry Finish The staff are attentive and often come around to offer further refreshments (I order another latté while my colour develops). After my colour, comes my cut with Dee -- her precision and attention to detail is impressive. She finishes with a modern, polished but textured blow-dry, leaving me ready to start the weekend. Professional Hair Services and Products Wieselmann offers a full range of professional hair services from colouring and cutting to styling and treatments. The salon also stocks expert hair care and styling lines by Schwarzkopf and Kérastase to keep your hair feeling and looking its best between salon visits. Review by Beauticate Editorial

articles.title: Wildlife Origin, Milson's Point
articles.author: Beauticate Editorial
articles.excerpt: A one-stop hair and beauty destination with jaw-dropping Harbour Bridge views, led by three-time Australian Hairdresser of the Year Jane Wild and a full beauty treatment menu.
articles.body: With one of the most gobsmacking views in Sydney, Wildlife occupies some seriously prime Kirribilli real estate. Each chair and mirror in the salon is privy to a sprawling perspective that takes in the majestic arc of the Harbour Bridge, the grassy knolls of Bradfield park and the stunning expanse of Sydney’s most famous waterway. Award-Winning Team Led by Jane Wild This blue ribbon location also boasts service to match with a team of highly skilled stylists led by multi-award winning director Jane Wild (she’s won Australian Hairdresser of the Year, not once, but three times). Wildlife Origin is one of three salons in the business, the others being Sogo in Surry Hills and Studio in Milson’s Point. A Renovation With Harbour Views A recent renovation to the Origin salon sees the front windows turned into sliding doors, which cantilever, bringing the incredible vista, literally, right into the salon. The street-side entry has also been opened up and features a new café that tempts the locals with Single Origin and Vietnamese Coffee, fresh zesty salads and devilishly innovative desserts (Violet Crumble Muffins anyone?). Luxe Shu Uemura Colour Treatment Today I’m booked in for a luxe Shu Uemura Colour Lustre treatment followed by a style with Jayne ahead of a function I have this evening. After a quick chat with the beautiful Jayne (who is one of the loveliest women in hairdressing) about the style I want, a chignon or up-do that will work with my black Zimmermann seventies style dress, and I’m introduced to Eve, who will be doing my treatment. Kaija begins my treatment with a paddle brush in each hand and gently brushes my scalp to stimulate the blood supply, it’s sensorial and shiver inducing. I sip a delicate mint tea and close my eyes. When I open them I’m again struck by the beauty of Sydney harbour. With the delicate afternoon breeze wafting through the space, it feels like I’m having my hair done on someone’s private waterfront balcony. I step through to the basin area for my wash and it’s all subdued lighting and chilled music. Kaija tells me that the salon uses specially purified water to wash clients’ hair, this prevents any toxic build up and gives extra doses of shine. Full Beauty Menu Beyond Hair In addition to the hair service, you can also choose from a full beauty treatment menu to enjoy either in chair or next door in one of the four treatment rooms. Daniella, who runs the beauty salon, offers incredible Cosmedix and Payot facials, gel manis, waxing, massage, makeup and even injectables (her father cosmetic doctor who does special visits). Wildlife also also make their own candles so that you can take a little piece of the relaxation home with you. Jane Wild on the Wildlife Experience “It’s not just about the hair,” explains Jane Wild a few minutes later, as she expertly winds my hair around a brush while blasting it with a ghd aura hairdryer “It’s about having a whole Wildlife experience. My dream when we first built the salon was to have a one-stop shop. A destination where clients can have hair, beauty, they can have something to eat… Most of my clients are time poor and running to get the kids, or get back to work, and they forget to eat, so it’s important they can get everything done at once, because it’s precious time that you get to yourself.” And within minutes, my hair has been folded into an elegant chignon and I do exactly that, swoop out of the salon to face the daycare…

articles.title: Wildlife Studio, McMahon’s Point
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: A cosy, art-filled terrace salon on the lower north shore where the Wildlife team deliver expert Goldwell colour and Davines styling in an atmosphere that feels more like visiting a friend than a hair appointment.
articles.body: The third salon in the esteemed Wildlife group, Wildlife Studio, is a fun and friendly beauty bolthole in Sydney’s McMahon’s Point. Housed in a cosy terraced building on busy Blues Point Road, it has a completely different feel to sleek and glossy Wildlife Origin salon, with its famous view of Sydney harbour and bustling energy. The studio, on the other hand, is more local and low key, with pale wood floors, ornate pressed tin ceilings and lashings of natural light from the street. A Rainy Friday at Blues Point Road I arrive for my colour appointment with salon owner Monica on a rainy Friday and am immediately welcomed by the lovely Craig, with his charming lilting Scottish accent. He cloaks me up and offers me a drink before Monica introduces herself, and her new rescue dog, Tink, a Maltese x Chihuahua who bounds over to say hello. She only adopted him yesterday, and everyone is clearly thrilled with the salon’s new mascot. During my appointment several clients bring their own dogs in to meet him. Local Art and Handmade Touches I comment on a stylish, spindly wooden sculpture that adorns the wall dramatically. “One of my clients made that, Catriona Pollard, she’s in PR but she also makes these wooden sculptures. We get a lot of comments on it, and we sell them for her.” As for the handmade colourful pompom hanging in the window? The team made it themselves. “We’re very into craft. We made a Christmas tree, too. Clients kept asking where they could buy one!” she says mirthfully, adjusting her Tom Ford glasses. Beneath the pompoms is a row of cute knitted cactuses in pots, another client’s artsy business. The colourful Davines products on the shelves above the desk, with their stylish folksy packaging, compliment the artsy vibe of the salon beautifully. Goldwell Colour by a Seasoned Stylist After a quick chat about my colour, we decide on a chestnut demi-permanent by Goldwell, which will cover my grays and tone my now-brassy highlights, yet will be easy to maintain. Monica mixes the colour and starts painting it on swiftly, as she tells me about her background. She has worked with Wildlife owners Jayne Wild and husband Gary for 17 years, she started as an apprentice at age 16. “They gave me such wonderful opportunities, I’m so grateful to them,” she says earnestly. From Apprentice to Salon Partner After several years at Wildlife, Monica took a sabbatical in London for two years and honed her craft before returning to Sydney and back into the Wildlife fold. She was ready for new challenges when Jayne and Gary acquired the nearby Rocket Salon and the trio went into a partnership, renaming it Wildlife Studio. As my colour develops, I watch Monica interact with all the clients the salon, who clearly adore her. Coincidently, her next client is Janet, one of my best friends’ mothers. She confides that she comes here every week for her blowdry, which explains why she is always immaculately turned out. The Wash, Blowdry and Final Result When the buzzer goes, Kaija takes me to the basin for my wash before giving me an excellent blowdry, which is spritzed generously with Davines Volu Spray so it will last me until my event, the next day. As I pack up handbag and de-robe, I tell Monica I’m thrilled with the colour. It’s glossy and rich, and the highlights are toned so subtly you can’t see any regrowth. I step out of the warmth into the blizzardly Sydney day reluctantly. Wildlife Studio has a lovely, personal vibe. I love…

articles.title: Yots Hair, North Adelaide
articles.author: Beauticate Editorial
articles.excerpt: 17 O'Connell Street, North Adelaide SA 5006

articles.title: Olive & July, WA
articles.author: Tess Schlink
articles.excerpt: Chloe Sherrell opened Olive & July at 23 and quickly built a cult following for signature lash lifts, bespoke facials and a beautifully Instagrammable Subiaco space.
articles.body: In the two years since its opening, Olive & July have quickly switched up the beauty space in Perth, offering a new kind of beauty destination to the city: a myriad of different highly-sought after treatments in the one (very Instagrammable) space. A Beautifully Designed Subiaco Salon I arrive at the salon on a typical blistering Perth summer’s day and stepping inside is blissful, it’s airy and bright, with a blush pink sofa, and chic houseplants dotted around the space. Oh, and a swing, the place is pretty much begging to be photographed, which I swiftly to do to file away for future interiors inspiration. The salon is flanked by cult hairdresser, Paris Rose, a KX Pilates studio and a F45 gym; it’s quickly evolved into the focal point of Subi’s wellness and beauty offerings. Meet Founder Chloe Sherrell At the helm is Chloe Sherrell, who is a bit of a beauty wunderkind, after honing her craft at some of Perth’s most prestigious beauty locations, she started her own salon aged 23, sharing a space with a friend’s clothing store in Leederville before moving to her current location. The salon is named in honour of Chloe’s beloved dogs, which is a small detail I love (I’m obsessed with dogs). The Cult Lash Lift Treatment I’d never had a lash lift before, but Chloe suggests I try it as it’s their signature treatment, and it has many devotees. I’m told many of the city’s beauty aficionados refuse to let anyone but the clever Olive & July team touch their lashes, travelling from all over Perth for the cult treatment. I’m led into a very chic and zen treatment room (think more houseplants, blush and white linens and elegantly minimal art), where Chloe proceeds to examine my lashes. My lashes (which I’ve always considered quite rubbish) make me an ideal candidate for the treatment, they’re very straight and practically point downwards, but they’re long and have apparently great curling potential. Perming, Tinting and Keratin Finish She pops on some gingko-infused eye patches for an added beauty boost, and puts the perming solution on my lashes to curl them into place. It’s followed with setting solution, and then by a much-need tint for my mousy lashes. At the end of the lash lift, Chloe applies a nourishing keratin lash treatment to keep them in good nick post-treatment. They look amazing, managing to mimic falsies while also being natural enough for everyday. I look forward to waking up everyday with Bambi-esque lashes without having to pick up my mascara or Shu Uemuras. What sets the Olive & July team apart is their perfectionism and attention to detail. Case in point: Chloe surveys my lashes and notices one rogue lash that had managed to stay poker straight. It’s probably barely noticeable to most people, but she insists on reapplying the perming solution on just that one lash to perfect the whole lash lift. Bespoke Facials and Skincare Range At Olive & July, it’s not all about lash lifts, though. They’re also known for their bespoke facials, the salon currently uses Dr. Spiller and Herbal Aktive products, but Chloe shares that they are soon launching Olive & July skincare, based on the specialist knowledge she has accrued over her years working in skin, so watch this space. There’s a whole suite of other beautifying treatments on offer for the whole body, brows, tanning, and massages are all also covered. It’s a total mecca for the time-poor beauty lover who needs to get all her or his treatments done in the one spot. Spend a few hours…

articles.title: Youth Lab, Claremont
articles.author: Tess Schlink
articles.excerpt: Dr Kate Jameson's Claremont outpost pairs advanced Hydrafacials, LED therapy and injectables with Nickolas Gurtler's Upper East Side-inspired design in a heritage building.
articles.body: After opening their well-loved West Perth clinic in 2018, Youth Lab are now extending their reach into the city’s western suburbs with their elegantly designed Claremont outpost. A stone’s throw from the heart of Claremont, it’s a chic urban oasis where modern design perfectly and respectfully complements the heritage of the building that houses the clinic. Upper East Side-Inspired Clinic Design Their new space was conceived by Melbourne-based designer Nickolas Gurtler, who was also behind the design of cult furniture purveyor James Said’s Nedlands showroom. Taking inspiration from the understated luxury of New York’s Upper East Side, Gurtler has done an exquisite job in highlighting the building’s framework (think lofty ceilings with intricate plasterwork) and blending it with more modern elements. As I enter I spy a table laden with interesting vases by Jonathan Adler, illuminated by an eye-catching angular light fitting. A striking artpiece by artist Dina Broadhurst serves as the focal point of the waiting room, while Calacatta Viola marble fixtures and brass fittings dot the various treatment rooms. Advanced Dermal Therapy by Dr Kate Dr Kate Jameson and the team behind Youth Lab have established a solid reputation for their state of the art advanced clinical dermal therapy and injectable treatments: some of their most popular offerings include their Hydrafacial ( which I enjoyed before my wedding and rate highly). Today I’m opting for their Signature Facial to give my skin a total reset: the treatment combines select elements of their most popular offerings for a comprehensive and totally customised experience. The Signature Facial Experience After a brief consultation about what I want to get out of my skin, Sarah thoroughly cleanses my skin with a clever ultrasonophoresis device. She follows with a bespoke enzymatic peel to exfoliate and rejuvenate, carefully monitoring my skin to see if it could manage an extra layer. Next Sarah performs a beautifully thorough massage, it’s so deeply relaxing, although I fight the urge to sleep in order to take mental notes of the whole experience, followed by a nourishing layer of Mesoestetic’s Radiance DNA Crystal Fibre Mask. Healite II LED Light Therapy And then, my favourite part of the facial: the Healite II LED. I’d previously enjoyed this light energy treatment on two occasions, and rated it highly for its skin repairing qualities, as well as imparting that ethereal ‘lit from within’ glow to the skin. It’s a soothing experience for body and mind too, with the warm light lulling you into serenity and calm. A Glowing Post-Treatment Complexion After emerging blissfully from my treatment room, Sarah presents me with a glass of water spiked with The Beauty Chef’s Hydration Booster, a delicious refreshment that highlights their ‘beauty from the inside out’ philosophy. My skin, which before the treatment was annoyingly temperamental and sensitised, is glowing and soft, and I decide to switch out my low-key weekend plans for something more social just to make the most of my beautified complexion.

articles.title: Youth Lab, Joondalup
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: The latest in Dr Kate Jameson's Youth Lab empire brings Hydrafacials, laser pigmentation correction and LED therapy to Perth's northern suburbs in a Gurtler-designed space.
articles.body: Perth’s Growing Appetite for Skin Treatments With a sunny, moisture-sapping climate, it’s no wonder Perth dwellers are avid consumers of skin treatments. Since she opened her cutting edge medical skin clinic Youth Lab in Perth in 2018, Dr Kate Jameson has seen a steady rise in the adoption of cosmetic procedures. “The demand for cosmetic procedures is steadily growing here in Perth, especially energy and laser-based procedures focused at treating pigmentation and sun damage. Here in sunny Perth we are seeing ageing skin at a higher and more severe rate, with signs including wrinkles, volume loss, skin sagging, vascular and pigmentation disorders,” explains Dr Kate Jameson. “Much of this can be attributed to our harsh climate, proximity to the equator, clear skies and our outdoor lifestyle. We have significant UV exposure which in turn is increasing our appetite for skin treatments to combat the effects of sun damage and premature ageing.” A Gurtler-Designed Space in Joondalup Her second clinic in Claremont in 2020 was a runaway success (despite COVID lockdowns) and now she brings her unique expertise and flair to the Perth’s North with Youth Lab Joondalup. Sprawling throughout a sleek sunlit space in Joondalup’s CBD, the latest Youth Lab is every bit as gorgeous as its predecessors, thanks to a stylish interior design by Nickolas Gurtler. With hued slate walls, gold hardware, Dina Broadhurst art, and the clinic’s statement reception desk, fashioned from polished Venetian plaster with Arabescato Vagli marble, there’s no question you’re in for a luxurious experience when you arrive. The First Visit Experience In the waiting area, I nestle into a curved bouclé chair and fill out my info on an ipad. There’s barely time to peruse the Slim Aarons coffee table books before I’m whisked into a treatment room by my therapist Corina. All first-timers begin with a full consult including photographs and a skincare plan, one of the most valuable aspects of a clinical skin treatment: expert skincare supervision and a treatments plan of attack. Youth Lab already has my data so I relax straight onto the bed. Corina expertly assesses my skin before explaining that today’s Advanced Facial is an indulgent and pampering yet results driven affair. Since I’m already on some pretty major actives, she tweaks the exfoliation and uses an enzyme rather than a peel. She uses a sonophoresis machine to help the mesoesthetic products penetrate more deeply and does some expert massage that almost lulls me off to sleep. LED Light Therapy and Hydrafacial Treatments Then it’s time to bliss out under the LED. At Youth Lab they use the Lutronic Healite which is an 830 nanometre yellow light that stimulates collagen and the healing function in the skin. It feels like lying in the sun but with a host of benefits and zero sun damage. Corina tells me that the most popular treatment at Youth Lab is the Hydrafacial and a great starting point for anyone wanting to get serious about their skin. Results Worth Coming Back For And with that, it’s a quick application of sunscreen and moisturizer and I’m unveiled as a Brand. New. Woman. My skin is all dewy and sparkly and I feel 100% better than when I walked in. I vow to come back soon so I can try a few more of the fabulous lasers on offer at Youth Lab: a veritable wonderland of good skin trickery.

articles.title: Brad Ngata Hair Direction, Darlinghurst
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Two-time Australian Hairdresser of the Year, working one-on-one from his Darlinghurst studio.
articles.body: Two-time Australian Hairdresser of the Year, Brad Ngata has spent more than two decades building one of Sydney's most respected independent salons. Tucked into the creative, Soho-like stretch of Darlinghurst Road, Brad Ngata Hair Direction operates as a one-on-one, single-operator studio, no production line, no battery-hen formula. Brad's editorial credentials span shoots for Sunday Times Magazine and Culture Magazine , plus advertising campaigns for Nokia, with named collections including Rebel, Tangeres , Breakage and Paper Cut showcasing his fashion-forward range. Inside, full-length mirrors, cascading greenery and gold-rimmed porcelain lend a sense of playful luxury that clients consistently describe as both stimulating and surprisingly peaceful. Recognised at Hair Expo and the Maybelline Australian Fashion Awards, Brad also holds back-to-back titles for Sydney's Best Hairdresser. Review by Sigourney Cantelo

articles.title: De Stijl Hair, Hobart
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Half hair salon, half designer fashion boutique. An Aveda concept salon on Elizabeth Street in Hobart where vegan colour and curated racks share the same considered light.
articles.body: Half the space is a hair salon. The other half is a designer fashion boutique, and the line between them is deliberately blurred. De Stijl runs as an Aveda concept salon on Elizabeth Street, which means the colour is vegan and the ethics come standard. It hangs like a gallery, clothes and styling stations sharing the same considered light. Owner Tracy Snow has been named a state hairdresser of the year finalist more than once, so the work behind the aesthetic holds up. Get your colour done, then browse the racks while it develops. Two good reasons to go, under one roof.

articles.title: EdwardsAndCo, Byron Bay
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Jaye Edwards' Byron Bay salon on Centennial Circuit. Master stylists with fashion-week credentials, open Tuesday through Saturday.
articles.body: Jaye Edwards built a salon group that turned hairdressers into names people follow. The Byron outpost keeps that up. On the floor you might find Clayton Truefitt, a master stylist with fashion-week and editorial runs in Melbourne and London behind him, or Stephanie Clifford Hosking on colour. It sits in Centennial Circuit, in the industrial pocket of town, open Tuesday through Saturday. This is the kind of place you book before a wedding or a big birthday, or simply when you want your hair to look like it belongs to a slightly more organised version of you. Byron gloss. Big-city hands.

articles.title: Fön Salon, Goodwood
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Heritage stone walls, gender-neutral pricing and a considered wine list inside one of Adelaide's most design-awarded salons on King William Road.
articles.body: The stone walls date to the 1800s. They belonged to Spats Café once, and Fön kept them, then spent a year building a salon around them on King William Road. It paid off. The interior landed on a list of the world's top 100 for design, which is not a sentence you write about many Adelaide hairdressers. Inside there are warm lavender towels, a considered list of wine and gin, and a WFS station for anyone who cannot switch off. Pricing is gender-neutral. You can book a silent appointment or talk the whole way through. Heritage and colour, under one very old roof.

articles.title: Headcase Hair, Paddington
articles.author: Isabella Ousby
articles.excerpt: Run by Fashion Week veterans Jon Pulitano and Vincent Nobile, this Paddington icon has been delivering impeccable cuts and colour since 1997.
articles.body: A Paddington Icon Since 1997 Paddington’s Oxford Street has seen many iconic stores come and go during its time, however for the past 18 years, one has remained constant. Headcase Hair, which occupies the full length of a landmark Paddo terraced building a few doors up from the post office, opened its doors in 1997. The much-loved salon was created after super stylist Jon Pulitano and colour extraordinaire Vincent Nobile came together to realise their mutual passion for and expertise in hairdressing. When Jon and Vincent aren’t in the salon they’re backstage at New York, Milan and Paris Fashion week working with some of the top hair directors in the world. So it’s safe to say, I feel pretty confident letting Jon cut my hair. Walking in to the salon it’s not hard to see why clients return appointment after appointment. The sound of John Legend crooning in the background, crisp monochrome tones along with beautiful mirrored walls that stretch for the entire length of the salon, gives it a sophisticated appeal. All the reflection and some cleverly placed lights make the salon give it a Manhattanesque feel, clearly influenced by the pair’s jetsetting schedules. Champagne, T2 Teas and Expert Consultation When I arrive I’m offered a champagne or my choice from a selection of T2 teas (with an impending deadline tonight, I resist the bubbles and go for a green tea) before chatting to Jon about what we were doing with my hair. I’ve got really thick unruly hair so I’m usually nervous when people cut my hair, but after chatting to Jon I know I’m in good hands. Vincent is a Redken colour ambassador so the salon is filled with the beautiful scent of fresh blowdries and Redken products. Jon uses Pureology (a product line distributed by Redken) shampoo and conditioner on my hair as its great for strengthening dyed hair, especially bleached hair like mine. Precision Cutting and Olaplex Treatments After a wash and a light blowdry it’s time to cut. I tell Jon that I don’t like having noticeable layers in my hair, which is lucky, really, as Jon cuts hair in a way that gives you ‘unnoticeable layering’ while still giving the hair movement. For all those tortured blondes out there like me, Headcase Hair is also a registered Olaplex salon. Olaplex is a miracle product that stops your hair feeling like straw after its been dyed, which, as Jon tells me, is because the product works at reforming and strengthening the bonds of the hair. After my cut, Jon blowdries my hair into beautiful unstructured curls and I’m event-ready. Too bad I’m going back to the office. It’s a good thing though that my blowdry lasts for several days. A few extra spritzes of dry shampoo and I reckon I can stretch it for the week. Makeup in the Chair for Events One clever point of difference for the time-poor and socially-stretched, Headcase Hair also offer makeup in the chair, an aspect Jon and Vincent pride themselves on (having seen the full extent of hair and makeup stress backstage). And on that note, I know exactly where I’ll be coming before my next event. Review by Sigourney Cantelo

articles.title: Hues Hair, Richmond
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: A Memphis-inspired hair salon on Swan Street designed by architect Adriana Hanna. Bold flat colour, geometric forms, and colour work at the basins as considered as the colour on the walls.
articles.body: Ettore Sottsass never designed a hair salon, but Hues on Swan Street is what it might have looked like. Architect Adriana Hanna built the Richmond space as a love letter to Memphis, blocking it out in bold flat colour and geometric forms that Dezeen and Wallpaper both came running to photograph. Pinks meet primaries meet clean hard edges. It should read as a gimmick and somehow does not, because the colour work at the basins is as considered as the colour on the walls. You go for a cut and end up sitting inside a piece of design history. Loud, precise, unrepeatable. Richmond's most photographed salon, and it has earned every frame.

articles.title: Joh Bailey, Double Bay
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Four decades behind Australia's most iconic blowdries.
articles.body: Founded by Joh Bailey and Marilyn Koch in 1985, Joh Bailey in Double Bay is arguably Australia's most iconic hair destination. For four decades, this is where Sydney's elite, and visiting royalty, supermodels and celebrities including Diana Princess of Wales, Kylie Minogue, Elle Macpherson, Cate Blanchett and Olivia Newton-John, have come for the signature Bailey blowdry: voluminous, glossy and full of life. What began as a single salon on Cross Street became an institution of effortless glamour and impeccable service, where women walk in one version of themselves and leave luminous. The salon offers a full suite of services spanning precision cutting, bespoke colour, styling, hair extensions, makeup and treatments. A second outpost in Bowral extends the Bailey legacy beyond the city. Review by Sigourney Cantelo

articles.title: KODA Cutters, Bondi
articles.author: Tess Schlink
articles.excerpt: Founded by award-winning session stylist Diane Gorgievski, this Bondi Beach salon draws a celebrity clientele for its masterful colour and customised cuts.
articles.body: A Hair Mecca Near Bondi Beach Nestled under the chic QT Hotel just a stone's throw from the heart of bustling Bondi Beach is KODA Cutters, a veritable hair mecca for Sydney's social set and in-the-know hair lovers alike. Walk a block back from the throngs of sunseekers around Bondi Pavilion, and you will discover the salon, a sanctuary from the hustle and bustle of the busy beachside suburb. Since opening four years ago, KODA Cutters has quickly cemented itself as a go-to destination for those seeking highly customised and personalised treatments and colour. Founder Diane Gorgievski and Celebrity Clients The salon was founded by Diane Gorgievski, a veteran of the international fashion week circuit, lauded editorial stylist, and 2019 AFHA Session Stylist of the year. She also tends to the tresses of Rose Byrne and Elizabeth Debicki. Given that we are hosting an event with Armani this evening, I'm thrilled that Diane makes a space in her schedule to zhoosh my hair. She expertly whips around my head with a hot tong, then carefully finger styles it at the end, finishing with mistings of Oribe hairspray. I love that this salon has all the trimmings of a luxury high-end salon without any of the attitude. The team genuinely love to look after their clients and you can feel this as soon as you enter. The salon tends to the tresses of many other well-known faces. WHO profile alumnae Hayley Bonham, Kate Fowler, Lucy Folk, and Saskia Havekes all cite KODA Cutters as their go-to for all things hair. (Visit their website to watch an edgy film of Jesinta Franklin modelling an array of achingly cool hair looks.) Designer Interiors and Philippe Starck Mirrors Enter the salon and you're immediately greeted by an elegant reception desk of blue-grey cut onyx, overhung with architectural pendant lighting from Lee Broom. There are a series of asymmetrical windows cut artfully into the wall, displaying the salon's products of choice. A stunning light installation (the Big O Suspension from Moooi) illuminates the next room. The space is adorned with custom mirrors by designer Philippe Starck, chic Italian chairs, and European oak flooring. The predominant palette is of creams and neutrals punctuated by bold accents of black. It's a serene and intimate space, perfect for whiling away a few hours getting pampered. Freestyle Colour and Premium Haircare They're renowned for their personalised and relaxed approach to hairdressing, including their masterful use of freestyle colour for a natural yet perfected finish (and as Saskia Havekes attests, 'Diane at KODA Cutters in Bondi does the best blow-dry, she really knows hair, and is a wonderful cutter and colourist'). They also stock a well-selected edit of high-end haircare from Oribe, Redken, and Olaplex, to name a few. All in all, it's a chic salon with a fiercely loyal set of customers. Book in for a treatment, and you may well expect to become one, too. Review by Sigourney Cantelo

articles.title: Paloma, Paddington
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Paloma Rose Garcia's fashion-world eye turned salon. Polished wood, Beauty Chef elixirs in Maison Balzac carafes and a lived-in cut worth its two-month wait.
articles.body: Paloma Rose Garcia spent sixteen years in fashion, including a stint with Hermes and fifteen Australian Fashion Weeks, before turning the old Oscar Oscar space on Oxford Street into something closer to a curated hotel. Polished wood floors, muted tones, fresh flowers and copies of Monocle and The Gentlewoman set the tone. The welcome ritual runs to Beauty Chef elixirs and matcha, served in Maison Balzac carafes, because the details are the point. The signature is the lived-in cut, worth its reported two-month wait, and Kevin Murphy colour led by the blonde whisperer Ash Croker. Undone yet elevated. You will think about the scalp massage for days.

articles.title: Paloma Roan, West End
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Sustainable colour work in a sun-filled West End salon. Paloma Roan specialises in lived-in blondes, warm coppers and balayage that grows out like it was always meant to.
articles.body: Paloma Roan moved out of its Woolloongabba flagship in 2020 and set up on Montague Road in West End, where the light does half the work. The salon is all plants and sun, botanical and a little bohemian, and it has the sustainability credentials to back the aesthetic. A Sustainable Salon partner. Named by Harper's Bazaar as one of Australia's best sustainable salons. The specialty is lived-in colour. Soft blondes, warm coppers, balayage that grows out like it was always meant to. Ethical extensions too. It is a creative space as much as a salon. Go for the colour. Stay for the calm.

articles.title: Roji, Canberra
articles.author: Katherine Ring
articles.excerpt: 25 Edinburgh Ave Canberra, ACT 2601 (02) 6257 7559
articles.body: Nestled snugly in the raw wooden panelling of NewActon’s now-famous Nishi building is a lovely little hair salon called Roji. Owned by renowned Canberran hair stylist Jason Hartwig, Roji has been sharing floor space with the award-winning Hotel Hotel for almost a year and has recently taken out an award of its own: Best Salon Design at the 2015 Hair Expo Awards. Roji is an Aveda concept store, designed by Melbourne-based Craig Tan Architects, and offers an intimate and considered salon experience for a discerning (and loyal) clientele. Nestled snugly in the raw wooden panelling of NewActon’s now-famous Nishi building is a lovely little hair salon called Roji. Owned by renowned Canberran hair stylist Jason Hartwig, Roji has been sharing floor space with the award-winning Hotel Hotel for almost a year and has recently taken out an award of its own: Best Salon Design at the 2015 Hair Expo Awards. Roji is an Aveda concept store, designed by Melbourne-based Craig Tan Architects, and offers an intimate and considered salon experience for a discerning (and loyal) clientele. Roji Uses Lush Natural Aveda Products on All Clientele The Japanese Tea Ceremony Philosophy A roji is a small garden that separates the teahouse from the main house; a “transitional zone between the outermost spaces of everyday life and the innermost sanctum of the sacred tea ceremony”. This nod to the traditional Japanese ritual is carried through into the smaller details of the considered in-salon experience at Roji Salon; starting with a freshly brewed pot of herbal Aveda tea upon arrival. A complimentary scalp and shoulder massage with Aveda aromatherapy oils is offered prior to the service to ensure a truly relaxing experience. The seats are wide and plush, and the black salon gowns feature niftily-positioned arm holes to allow for easy magazine flipping and phone-scrolling. Intimate Service and Natural Ingredients It is this attention to detail that makes the salon experience at Roji so unique. With a tiny staff of five regular stylists, the interactions are intimate and the treatments feel calm and luxurious. The decision to partner with Aveda came down to a mutual appreciation for naturally derived ingredients and environmental responsibility. For this reason the choice of location, in Canberra’s most sustainable mixed-use building complex, makes complete sense. The Zen Space is Reflective of the Holistic and Calming In-salon Experience Customer Comfort is a Paramount Priority for Roji, Upholding the Aveda-salon Reputation A Zen Wash Area and Signature Treatments Separate to the main salon floor, facing onto Canberra’s Edinburgh Avenue, is a zen oasis with a row of generously proportioned sinks for a genuinely relaxing wash. Aveda shampoo and conditioner seem to be selected with care and tailored to the individual client, and controls for reclining the seat are embedded in the armrest. Elect to enjoy one of Aveda’s signature treatments and the room can be completely closed off from the noise of the main salon for a quiet moment of repose. It seems this holistic consideration of the salon experience at Roji has struck a chord with Canberran locals; the overwhelming majority of the salon’s clientele are regular customers, which is no mean feat for a space that has barely been open a year. It appears that Roji understands very clearly a need, and a demand, to transform what can otherwise be simply haircare maintenance into a spa-like salon experience; to turn the modern woman’s (and man’s) bi-monthly chore in a brief respite from the demands of the day. Booking and Dining at Roji Roji opens Tuesday through Saturday, though appointments are limited. As well as tea served on arrival,…

articles.title: Saint Louie Hair, Melbourne CBD
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: A lofty hair studio on Russell Place, a bluestone laneway most people walk past. Mezzanine, gallery light, and cuts as considered as the room they happen in.
articles.body: Russell Place is a bluestone laneway most people walk straight past, which makes finding Saint Louie feel like being let in on something. The salon runs tall and lofty, a mezzanine folded into the volume so the room reads more like a gallery or an atelier than a place you get your hair done. Light pours down through the height of it. Downstairs the work happens, upstairs the space just breathes. It is the kind of considered, art-leaning interior that tells you the cut is going to be considered too. A hair studio that treats the room as part of the craft. Find the laneway. The rest takes care of itself.

articles.title: The Best Sydney Beauty Treatments for Post-Lockdown Preening
articles.author: Tess Schlink
articles.excerpt: The most enjoyable way to slip back into normal life.
articles.body: As our social diaries starts to fill up again as lockdown lifts, it would be wise to schedule in a few beauty appointments to help feel prepped to greet the outside world again. (This is especially the case if you’ve tried your hand at cutting your own fringe or executed a dodgy at-home brow tint during the haziest, darkest days of lockdown.) To help make your re-entry into civilised society that much chicer, here’s our edit of the treatments we suggest you schedule in as we head back into some sort of normality. For Groomed Brows: A Wax and Tint at Delphine Sorel Formerly working at renowned salon Kristin Fisher Eyebrows, French-born Delphine opened her own space earlier this year in Sydney’s CBD. Located in the elegant Dymocks Building, Delphine offers a suite of beautifying treatments for natural-looking brows and lashes, all executed with typically Gallic refinement and chic. I went for her eyebrow styling and tint, and my brows were full, fluffy, and tinted just enough, not so much as too look weird with my fair hair, but enough to make me feel groomed just by simply brushing up my arches. For Chic and Low-Key Hair: A Cut and Blowdry at RAW Anthony Nader “I want you to look like you haven’t been to see me,” says Anthony Nader, the iconic hairstylist behind cult salon RAW in Sydney’s Surry Hills. In other words, a salon visit that leaves you looking like you, only better; a refreshing attitude if you’re not one for overly preened and stiff pageant queen blowdries. The industrial cool, pared-back space could be situated in any number of big cities that Nader’s illustrious career has taken him to, complete with a ‘relaxation room’ for hair washing modelled off a first class aeroplane cabin (for the luxurious experience “without the jetlag”). Expect an off-duty model blowout, and low-maintenance haircut that looks good with minimum fuss, perfect for feeling polished on a Zoom call if you’ve just rolled out of bed. For A Pampering Manicure: The Ultraceuticals Anti-Ageing Manicure at Jocelyn Petroni Not unlike a facial but for your hands, this beautiful treatment uses a customised cocktail of exfoliating lactic acid and actives from Ultraceuticals to rejuvenate and beautify. This is then followed with an exquisite manicure using Jocelyn Petroni’s elegant selection of Chanel nail polishes. The ideal treatment to help lighten sun spots, or to deal with keratosis pilaris (otherwise known as ‘chicken skin’).

articles.title: Three New Sydney Beauty Destinations We Love
articles.author: Tess Schlink
articles.excerpt: You need to visit these ones ASAP.
articles.body: Those mid-winter blues got you feeling a little, well, blah? Then there's no better excuse to schedule in a rejuvenating facial, luxurious massage, or whatever you desire for a much needed spot of indulgence. Here, our edit of three of the best new beauty destinations that Sydney has got to offer. Time to get pampering... For Head-To-Toe Solutions As its name suggests, Combined Clinics Australia houses a collective of beauty and health professionals, all in one very chic space, designed by Graham Simmonds of Gray & Co. It's headed by chiropractor Dr. Cody Hanish (we recommend you check out his Instagram, by the way, where he adjusts his patients; it makes for very satisfying and addictive viewing). There's also light therapy facials, kinesiology, waxing and yoga classes available. Schedule in a whole day of treatments here and emerge feeling totally refreshed. For An Urban Getaway Located in Sydney's bustling Eastern Suburbs is the lush and luxurious Sol Spa. Once settled into the gorgeous space (think pretty blush chaise-longues, cosy fur rugs and zen water features), it's easy to imagine you're miles away from the city's chaos. The dense, leafy garden surrounding the spa certainly helps in this respect. Sol Spa offers a suite of dreamy treatments, from organic facials to full body massages and Ayurvedic rituals. Our advice? Book in at the gorgeous Botanica restaurant after your treatment for even more indulgence, post-spa. For Holistic Help To Wonderland Spa champions "a beauty from the inside, out" philosophy, and they very much practice what they preach with their portfolio of wellness therapies on offer. Providing naturopathy, colonic hydrotherapy and energy healing (as well as beautiful facials and massages), the focus here is on improving internal health for glowing results on the outside.

articles.title: Valonz, Paddington
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: The name whispered among Sydney's social set, where Cate Blanchett, Nicole Kidman and Naomi Watts trust their hair to Renya Xydis and her team.
articles.body: It's the name whispered among Sydney's social set and a crop of particularly well-coiffed A-listers, whispered because true luxury never shouts. Since its opening in 1987, the stylish salon has done a roaring trade among the most elite of clientele. Its success is in no small part due to the energy and artistry of its founder, Renya Xydis (who also owns four other thriving salons). With her trademark shock of fairy-floss-pink hair and exuberant nature, Renya has become one of Australia's best-loved beauty professionals. She's the one that Cate Blanchett trusts with her immaculate mane, and Nicole Kidman and Naomi Watts call on when they're in town. In a quiet and leafy sidestreet of Paddington, the salon allows clientele to duck in surreptitiously, and emerge only hours later, as if they were just born with such fabulous hair. The cutting room is fresh and bright with blonde wood parquetry floors. White, old-school white barber-style chairs are positioned in front of elegant Venetian mirrors and cutting stations, and you walk through to the hair-washing area above which hangs a vintage French barber sign announcing the "Coiffure Messieurs" . Upstairs is a rich and luxurious colour room where customers can while away the processing hours in private. There's an adjacent nail bar, Miss Frou Frou, so that clients may have their talons tended to at the same time as their hair, maximising treatment time. Review by Sigourney Cantelo

articles.title: Alba Thermal Springs & Spa, Fingal
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Sculptural concrete forms set into a Fingal hillside by Hayball architects, with geothermal pools following the fall of the land across fifteen hectares of the Mornington Peninsula.
articles.body: The concrete arrives before the water does. At Alba, architects Hayball set a run of sculptural concrete forms into a Fingal hillside and let the geothermal pools follow the fall of the land, so you move downhill through the bathing as the Mornington Peninsula opens out around you. Fifteen hectares of it. The material is raw and grey and deliberate, softened by MALA's planting, warmed by mineral water that has done its own slow work underground. There is a spa built into the same architecture. It reads as landscape first and building second, which is the point. Concrete, steam and a long view south. Very few places get this balance right.

articles.title: Auriga Spa at Capella Sydney, Sydney CBD
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Amber light, warm timber and walls of greenery on the sixth floor of Sydney's restored Department of Lands. Auriga is one of the most beautiful spa spaces in the country.
articles.body: Sydney's grandest sandstone lady, the old Department of Lands and Education building, spent a century as a place you visited for paperwork. Now Make Architects has restored her and BAR Studio has dressed the interiors, and the sixth floor holds one of the most beautiful spa spaces in the country. Auriga is amber light, warm timber and walls of greenery, with a steam room, sauna, experiential showers and an ice fountain to move between. The signature is Connect to Country, worked with heated stones gathered from across Australia with the permission of Elders. Or the two-hour Fluidform Rebalance, developed with Kirsten King. The skincare is Byron Bay's Synthesis Organics, all clean botanicals. You arrive frazzled by the city ten floors below. You leave recalibrated, and quietly smug about it.

articles.title: Aurora Spa & Bathhouse, Sorrento
articles.author: Beauticate Editorial
articles.excerpt: Inside the subterranean bathhouse at InterContinental Sorrento, 1,000 square metres of hydrotherapy pools, thermal experiences and ASPAR treatments on the Mornington Peninsula.
articles.body: Tucked beneath the sandstone facade of the InterContinental Sorrento, the reimagined Continental Hotel that has anchored this stretch of the Mornington Peninsula since 1875, Aurora Spa & Bathhouse is the kind of place that makes you want to cancel whatever you had planned for the rest of the day. Part of the hotel's sweeping AU$120 million redevelopment, the spa occupies a vast 1,000 square metres of subterranean space that feels both grand and intimate at once. Descend the stairs and the temperature shifts, the light softens, and the outside world, the limestone cliffs, the bustling village, the car park squabble, simply ceases to exist. The bathhouse is the centrepiece, and it is worth arriving early to give it the time it deserves. Four hydrotherapy pools sit at varying temperatures, designed to be moved through in sequence: warm to hot, cold plunge, then back again. The circuit is meditative and quietly addictive, each transition sharpens the senses before the next pool lulls them back into submission. Between dips, there are steam rooms and thermal experiences to explore, and a relaxation lounge where you can stretch out with a cup of tea and stare at nothing in particular, which is rather the point. The circuit is meditative and quietly addictive, each transition sharpens the senses before the next pool lulls them back into submission. The treatment rooms, eight in total, are hushed, beautifully appointed spaces. Facials, massage and body treatments all draw on the house ASPAR product line, Aurora's own range of botanically-led formulations that smell like a very expensive garden. The products are elegant without being fussy, and the therapists apply them with the kind of unhurried confidence that tells you they genuinely believe in what they are using. For something more immersive, the float room offers a sensory deprivation experience that strips away every last thread of tension, not for the claustrophobic, perhaps, but deeply restorative for everyone else. What elevates Aurora beyond a hotel day spa is the sense that every detail has been considered with real intention. The architecture honours the heritage of The Continental while the interiors feel unmistakably contemporary. There is no muzak. No synthetic lavender assault on entry. Just clean lines, warm stone, and the gentle echo of water moving through the pools below. The setting helps, of course. Sorrento is one of the Peninsula's most charming villages, and the InterContinental has positioned itself as its anchor, a place where a weekend away can pivot effortlessly between long lunches at the local restaurants, coastal walks, and an afternoon dissolving into the bathhouse. Aurora Spa is rated number one in Sorrento on TripAdvisor, which feels deserved. It is the rare spa where you leave feeling not just pampered but genuinely recalibrated. ASPAR products are available to purchase at the spa and online, so there is no excuse not to extend the ritual at home. Though frankly, a jar of body oil in your bathroom will never quite replicate the experience of floating weightless in a subterranean pool while someone else worries about dinner. Aurora Spa & Bathhouse 23 Constitution Hill Road, Sorrento, VIC 3943 auroraspa.com.au @auroraspaandbathhouse

articles.title: Aurora Spa, Palazzo Versace, Gold Coast
articles.author: Beauticate Editorial
articles.excerpt: Sea World Drive, Main Beach QLD 4217.

articles.title: Aurora Spa, St Kilda
articles.author: Beauticate Editorial
articles.excerpt: 2 Acland Street, St. Kilda VIC 3182 (03) 9536 1130. One of Australia’s most adored dayspas, Aurora…
articles.body: One of Australia’s most adored dayspas, Aurora, originally opened in 1997 but moved to its current St. Kilda location in 2000. Located in the hip Prince Of Wales Hotel, the spa has managed to keep up its flawless reputation and even with minimal updates to the décor, it has kept its sense of fresh, cutting-edge cool that was a drawcard when it first opened. THE DAYSPA IS LIGHT AND BRIGHT Walking through the dark and broody lobby of the Price and up a black cement staircase, I have a sense of shedding the urban doldrums. The day outside is typically bleak for Melbourne, and I can’t wait to step into the cloistered confines of the spa. The reception area is hidden behind a glass wall of rushing water that advertises Aurora Spa, and again, I get the feeling of transformation, a moving through the elements, as I step inside the brightly lit space. My therapist, Penelope, leads me into a change room where I’m given a white waffle cotton robe and some slippers to change into. I note the cute little locker key rings are duck-shaped nailbrushes, a quirky element to keep your keys close by. Once changed, it’s into the chill out lounge, which enjoys views over St. Kilda towards Melbourne’s CBD. Carved wooden shutters add a sculptural artsy vibe to the view. Sleek leather chairs invite sleepy pre and post-treatment lingering and inspirational books scattered on the tables leave you feeling uplifted and ready to face the world again. I sip an Aurora signature blend tea, a mix of chamomile, spearmint and lemon balm, and count down the seconds to my treatment. THE SPA USES ITS OWN RANGE ASPAR SHOWERS LOOK OUT TO THE DECK Once inside the treatment room and nestled into the cushy bed, Penelope begins the massage, her hands moving around my body rhythmically. I soon zone out completely and actually fall asleep, which happens rarely for me, during a beauty treatment. What must be an hour later she gently squeezes my arm to tell me that she’ll wait for me outside. Apart from my neck and back feeling much better than when I walked in, I have vague memories of sensorial deliciousness and a complete and overwhelming sense of calm and wellbeing. I levitate back out to the chill out room and spend a good twenty minutes sipping tea and radiating happiness. Aurora is the perfect spot to escape the grind and completely check out of life for a while. The treatments range from the sublime (The famous Kitya Karnu Signature treatment takes place in the steam room and involves a full body scrub, a hair mask and cold stone rebalancing ritual) to the ridiculously relaxing (manicures and pedicures are given in lazy boy chairs that recline fully so you can doze and wake up with fresh tips). They also offer popular cosmeceutical facials with Kerstin Florian as well as incredible body treatments using their own range of products, ASPAR, that utilises delectable-smelling Australian Native ingredients. As I leave, I’m told that there’s actually another Aurora Spa located in the Palazzo Versace Hotel on The Gold Coast, and as I head out, fully revived, into the grey Melbourne Day, I mentally add it to my ever-growing beauty bucket list. The Aurora experience is definitely one worth seeking out. COUNTLESS OPTIONS FOR REST AND REFLECTION

articles.title: Authenticity Health and Wellness Retreat, Port Elliot
