articles.excerpt: 74 Mt Lofty Summit Road, Crafers SA 5152

articles.title: Stephanie’s Vintage Spa, Cleveland
articles.author: Beauticate Editorial
articles.excerpt: Situated in a timeless and charming Victorian cottage in Cleveland Stephanies Vintage Day Spa is a chic space that covers all bases from massage to…
articles.body: Situated in a timeless and charming Victorian cottage in Cleveland, a short 30-minute drive from Brisbane, is Stephanie’s Vintage Spa. This is not your average beauty destination. With eight suites, a guest lounge and an enchanting entrance, the heritage home, which was originally built in 1852, has been restored with love, thought and purpose. Beauticater, Elyse Goyan, experienced the hidden utopian spa’s Stephanie’s Signature Skin Treatment for herself. Having frequented Stephanie’s Urban Spa and Spa Retreat, I had an idea of what to expect from this renowned Queensland brand; but when I arrived at Stephanie’s Vintage Day Spa I couldn’t have anticipated the calm that instantly washed over me. From the minute you’re greeted by the lovely Heather at reception to the fluffy almond coloured robe that softly comforts like a childhood toy, every detail of this spa is considered. My therapist, Stacey made me feel right at home, offering me rose water in a quaint Turkish glass while she shared the history of the spa with me. Each room has its own unique design and a distinctive ambience to suit your treatment. With a scattering of candles throwing off a soft light and the scent of lavender wafting through the air, it’s the perfect environment for one of Stephanie’s soul-pleasing signature treatments. I am booked in for Stephanie’s Signature Treatment, 100 minutes of pure bliss with a rose petal foot exfoliation, heated stone massage and Stephanie’s classic facial. From the moment my toes touch the warm petal-infused liquid, I feel rejuvenated. The little things make the biggest difference: from the way the heated stones are placed on my back, to the orange, lavender and ylang-ylang oil used to soothe my tense shoulders. I drift into a euphoric state, despite my best efforts to stay awake and note every detail of the experience for this review. Beyond the serene setting and exceptional treatments, Stephanie has developed a collection of beautiful products including a Lapis Body Crème and Macadamia Exfoliator which I trial before I wander through the lush grounds on my way to the guest lounge. Once ensconced there, I enjoy a cup of soothing herbal tea. Stephanie’s philosophy is to “embrace new technologies, respect ancient rituals, step away from the ordinary and create breathtaking treatments,” and the Vintage Spa certainly delivers on this sentiment, with one of the most magnificent spa treatments I’ve had to date. I depart feeling still and, despite heading straight back to the hustle and bustle of every day life, I drive home feeling peaceful in complete silence. Review by Elyse Goyan

articles.title: Sofitel Spa, Darling Harbour
articles.author: Beauticate Editorial
articles.excerpt: A $4 million wellness sanctuary elevated above Darling Harbour, Sofitel Spa delivers half-day wellness journeys, Waterlily facials and eco-conscious luxury.
articles.body: A New Standard for Sydney’s Spa Scene Frankly, it’s high time that a new hotel spa arrived on the scene to shake things up. Sydney’s spa scene has been, well, a little lackluster in recent years. So, when the team at The Sofitel Darling Harbour contacted me to discuss becoming their Spa Ambassador you can bet I was excited. I was weary of recommending the same handful of day spas, many of which haven’t been updated for several years. It was a great day for the beauty industry when the internationally renowned Sofitel Sydney Darling Harbour unveiled its pièce de résistance, the Sofitel Spa, a $4 million, two-storey magnifique wellness spa that sets a new standard for luxury retreats in the city. Sigourney checks in to Sydney's Newest Luxury Wellness Destination Since the launch I’ve had the pleasure of visiting several times to report on their latest offerings, usually after a staycation at the hotel. Each time, I’m further impressed by the level of care and detail at the spa. Elevated above Sydney’s iconic Darling Harbour, the urban oasis offers a holistic and indulgent experience that targets all facets of the body, mind, and soul. It’s a sophisticated approach to wellness and perfectly in line with what’s happening on a global scale in the industry. I also love the way the spa effortlessly blends French indulgence with Australian authenticity, redefining the concept of wellbeing within the hotel market. Inside the Sofitel Spa Sanctuary Stepping foot into Sofitel’s sanctuary, I’m greeted by thecalming palette of soft timbers, sandstone, and marble finishes. The space has been meticulously designed by award-winning firm PikeWithers, ensuring that every detail contributes to the overall sense of understated luxury. Seven spacious treatment rooms, including two exquisitely designed suites, await guests, with one featuring a bespoke bath overlooking the picturesque Darling Harbour. At reception is a stunning and elaborate dried floral arrangement that the hotel florist constructs seasonally, currently it is a warming mix of oranges slices, cinnamon sticks, dried blooms and branches for Winter. Design Inspired by Sydney's Harbour Evoking the spirit of Sydney, the spa draws aesthetic inspiration from its surroundings. Spa Manager Cecilia Ferreyra points out that the gorgeous aquamarine marble tops represent the waters of Darling Harbour and the sandstone walls are reminiscent of Sydney's coastal cliff faces. “The linens in the Spa are all custom made by an Australian upholsterer, who was briefed on the seasonal concept and sourced beautiful Warwick fabrics to align with the seasonal theme,” she says. “The Spa changes its decor and treatment room linens in the warmer and cooler seasons.”I’m also impressed to note that the spa actively engages in eco-friendly practices, utilizing digital forms, providing fully compostable linen slippers, and offering bamboo-based amenities. The jewel in the crown of Sofitel Spa Darling Harbour, however, is its signature half-day Wellness Journeys that harmoniously blend the elements of Movement, Nourishment, Care, and Rest. Today, I embark on the Winter Wellness Journey, a five-hour holistic spa experience that promises to be an exquisite sensory adventure. The Winter Wellness Journey Experience The journey commences with an invigorating Peloton spin session, designed to activate circulation and awaken the senses. Following this exhilarating start, I decompress in the infrared sauna before wilfully surrender to the expert care of my therapist for a three-hour full-body treatment and facial using delicious products from Waterlily that contain winter-themed sensory delights like spiced maple, cardamom, cinnamon, star anise, pumpkin enzymes and maple syrup. The massage employs custom blended oil blend by the Spa Sofitel and Waterlily that is gifted to me in a body set at the…

articles.title: Tama Wellness, Dunsborough
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: A small, deliberate wellness studio tucked behind Bungalow Social in Dunsborough. Infrared sauna, treatment rituals and meditation for the quieter end of wine country.
articles.body: You will find it behind Bungalow Social, tucked off Naturaliste Terrace in the middle of Dunsborough. Tama is small and deliberate. The heat comes from an infrared sauna rather than the usual hot rocks, a gentler kind of warmth that lets you stay in longer and think less. Around it sit treatment rituals and meditation, the slow end of wellness rather than the athletic one. This is not a plunge-and-post-about-it operation. It is a place to go quiet for an hour on your way through wine country. Open Tuesday to Saturday, late morning to mid-afternoon. Book ahead. The room is intimate by design.

articles.title: Tank Farm, Bli Bli
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Two guests at a time. Tank Farm on Bli Bli Road is a Hamptons-spirited private bathing property with magnesium floats, hot pools, cold plunge and a licensed restaurant, all utterly yours for the afternoon.
articles.body: Tank Farm takes only two guests at a time. That is not a typo. Out on Bli Bli Road, twenty-five minutes from Noosa, the property is Hamptons in spirit and rural in setting, so stepping onto it feels like the world has gone quiet. There are magnesium float tanks, hot pools, a cold plunge, saunas, steam rooms and outdoor showers, plus a licensed restaurant for after. Because it is just the two of you, the whole place is effectively private. Book it with someone you actually like. Thursday to Saturday only, strictly by appointment. This is the antidote to the crowded bathhouse. Utterly yours for the afternoon.

articles.title: The Darling Spa, Pyrmont
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: One of Sydney’s most palatial spa retreats, hidden inside The Star’s boutique hotel, think La Prairie facials, Moroccan Hammam rituals and a saltwater Jacuzzi you won’t want to leave.
articles.body: Sydney’s Most Palatial Spa Retreat One of Sydney’s newest and most palatial retreats, The Darling Spa is sprawled over the entire second floor of luxury boutique hotel The Darling, located at premium entertainment destination The Star in Pyrmont. Although it was opened only four years ago, it has recently undergone a stunning renovation, which includes the addition of a steam room, a saltwater Jacuzzi and state-of-the-art gym, complete with a Kinesis wall. Five-Star Facilities and Pool Access If you want to spend the day luxuriating, spa treatments grant you five star access to all the rock star facilities including full use of the spa and gym, as well as access to the pool on level five (where you can order drinks, food and enjoy the attentions of the ‘tanning butler’ who supplies guests with sunscreen.) Parking is also complimentary for spa guests. I’m booked in for a massage today, but I have had the La Prairie Skin Caviar facial before, which was superbly luxurious. The Darling is also the only spa in Sydney to stock the prestigious, holistic European brand Espa. A Meditative Space with 13 Treatment Rooms Although the place is huge (there are 13 treatment rooms including two incredible couples rooms), it doesn’t feel it, due to the design. Architects Cox Richardson and interior designers DBI Design and Stack Studio have created a peaceful and meditative space, with softly lit hallways in tones of burnished gold, charcoal and chocolate. After changing and sipping a ginger tea in the luxurious taupe-toned waiting room, I’m led to my treatment room. Through hushed geometric hallways and past grand mosaics, each turn leads me deeper into the magical rabbit hole. It’s so deliciously quiet and a million miles away from the frenetic activity of The Star next door. I disrobe and stretch out, ready to begin my hour of escape. It’s an indulgent and satisfying massage and my therapist, Anna, is attentive and responsive. Kneading out niggly knots and willing my worn out body into a state of meditative bliss. The Moroccan Hammam Ritual I wish I didn’t have to go back to work, as on the way back to the change room I’m invited to use the glamorous hammam . Anna tells me that they do a Moroccan hammam ritual on the huge marble slab in the middle of the room. After a full body scrub with black soap, you’re covered in warm rhassoul clay and rose water imported from the Moroccan Atlas Mountains. The heat from the room infuses all the goodness into your skin and leaves you baby-soft and delightfully fragranced. There are also some pretty amazing couples treatments on the menu, too, including “Date Night”, a version of the hammam ritual where you apply a mud wrap to each other (ooh er!) followed by a 90-minute massage and hour long Espa facial in the VIP suite. Review by Sigourney Cantelo

articles.title: Chuan Spa at The Langham, Sydney
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Chinese medicine meets five-star indulgence at The Langham Sydney. Element-matched massages, bespoke oil blends and a starlit pool that makes Millers Point feel a long way from the office.
articles.body: Chuan means flowing water, which is the first clue. This is the wellness arm of The Langham, tucked away from the marble grandeur upstairs, and it runs on Chinese medicine rather than a standard treatment list. You start by finding your element. A short consultation, then a bespoke oil blended to whichever of wood, fire, earth, metal or water you turn out to be. The massage follows your element. A pot of matching tea closes it. There is a sleep programme for the truly frayed. And the hotel's pool waits under a ceiling pricked with fibre-optic stars. The starlit swim is the part you will tell people about. Millers Point has never felt so far from the office.

articles.title: Bells at Killcare Day Spa, Killcare NSW
articles.author: Beauticate Editorial
articles.excerpt: Nestled in the iconic beachside property Bells at Killcare, the eponymous Day Spa is a little haven of serene on the Central Coast.
articles.body: A Coastal Spa Retreat at Killcare Nestled in the iconic beachside property Bells at Killcare, the eponymous Day Spa is a little haven of serene on the Central Coast. In keeping with the boutique resort’s crisp Hamptonsesque styling, the spa is housed in a little building off to the side of the car park. While it mostly caters to guests of Bells, it’s also open to the public and they offer a variety of packages in conjunction with the award-winning restaurant. Stepping into the warmly lit space of the spa out of the blustery winters day is a welcome relief. Inside, it’s all blue and white linen with tasteful coastal accents. Natural Beauty Products and Coastal Style French doors lead out onto a patio (much more inviting on a summer’s day). On offer for purchase are a plethora of natural beauty options from the locally made Bouddi beauty range (named after nearby Bouddi National Park) to Australian cosmeceuticals Aspect and the beautiful organic Aboriginal-inspired L’itya range. There’s also Eco-Tan and the vegan non-toxic Sienna Nailpolish from Byron Bay. After a quick change into a terry robe and slippers I fill out my treatment form swiftly. I’ve booked in for the Li’Tya Kodo Melody Massage, a rhythmic sequence aimed at bringing the body back into balance and inspired by traditional techniques. My therapist Jennifer collects me from reception and leads me through to the massage room. My room is cocoon-like, lit with just the rosy glow from a salt lamp… The Indigenous Smoking Ceremony Opening Jennifer passes three oils under my nose and I select the Detox blend, a zesty mix of native mint, lemon myrtle and juniper that I hope will kickstart my sluggish winter system. Then, face down and eyes closed I inhale the delicious aroma of burning gum leaves, paperbark and oakmoss in a Coolamon Dish, a smoking ceremony that opens the treatment. This is a micro version of the welcoming ritual they do at Bell’s sister property Pretty Beach House and it pays respects to the original owners of the land. The incense-like effect puts me into a sleepy reverie and I succumb to the rhythmic wave of massage… There are circular and figure-of-eight movements done with a flat hand, which Jennifer later tells me are designed to move excess energy (like stress, depression and anxiety) away from the heart. I’m soothed into a delicious state of bliss, to a soundtrack of didgeridoo and tribal song… Rhythmic Massage and Facial Sequence barely registering when I roll over to treat the top side of my body. The massage concludes with a lovely facial sequence, Jennifer’s fingers butterflying over my long-clenched jaw muscles and deeply furrowed brow, expertly easing out the tension. A final scalp massage brings me back gently from a precipice of sleep and I float into the bathroom to dress. The Spa at Bells is both beautifully designed and run. What it lacks in size (there are just four treatment rooms) it makes up for in soul and service. A Central Coast Weekend Escape There’s a lovely atmosphere and the therapists are clearly skilled and very knowledgeable. If you’re anywhere near the Central Coast it’s the perfect pit stop, even better, make a weekend of it and check into a villa at Bells for a total respite from the city.

articles.title: Halcyon House, Cabarita Beach, NSW
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: A former 1960s surf motel reimagined as a Hamptons-meets-St-Barths boutique hotel, with a six-room spa, custom aromatherapy oils and Sodashi treatments steps from the sand.
articles.body: A Boutique Beach Hotel Reimagined A short walk from the shore of Cabarita Beach lies Halcyon House, a superbly designed boutique beach hotel with an inspired spa to match. The former 1960s surf motel has retained its classic beachside feel with a spectacular overhaul by interior designer Anna Spiro and architect Virginia Kerridge. Not one detail seems out of place. Crisp blue and white is the order of the day, echoing through the hotel via striped awnings and daybeds, geometric tiled floors and a mélange of mismatched but harmoniously toned textiles. Every available wall is decorated with expertly curated artworks and oversized clam shells are filled with fresh fruit. The effect is that, rather than checking into a hotel, you are visiting someone's very tastefully decorated beach house. The spa is a natural extension of the resort's Hamptons-meets-St-Barths style, housed in an airy white building off to the side of the property. Although it overlooks a car park, the minute you step in you are transported somewhere much more sophisticated. The Spa Boutique and Sodashi Products As I enter and check in for my massage I am distracted by an enticing wall of Lucy Folk sunglasses and the Spa Boutique, stocked with linen separates from Sarah J Curtis, Bassike and Thierry Coulson. Down one wall is a range of Sodashi products ripe for smelling and taking home. As I thumb through a Slim Aarons tome, it takes me a minute to find the source of the room fragrance. On the coffee table before me, an oversized clam shell holds half a dozen pineapples. It is an unexpected but delightful twist on the typical oil burners you find in a spa. The ripe fruity aroma is perfectly at home with the terracotta tiles (imported from Mexico, no less) and the white wood-panelled walls. Custom Aromatherapy and Treatment Rooms Before I get changed for the steam room, Prashanti gives me a tour of the six treatment rooms, which she tells me are named affectionately by the staff as Pinkie, Mr Mustard, Miss Green, Grandma Blue and so on. Prashanti is also a clinical aromatherapist and has formulated three custom oils for the Halcyon spa, of which I will select one for my massage. They all smell like heaven. They are also nut free but light and do not leave you feeling greasy. After a quick spin around the gorgeous blue tiled steam room, my therapist Leone collects me from the Relax Lounge and leads me through to my treatment room, Miss Green. I stretch out between crisp white sheets, surrendering to her expert strokes. I am lulled off to near sleep but vaguely remember an excellent pressure point head massage, some very impressive neck work and a foot massage that is definitely worth writing home about. Room Service and Evenings by the Shore Halcyon House certainly lives up to its name. A peaceful and stylish place that dreams are made of. The spa experience stays with me all the way into my cavernous bed that night, the memory of those massage strokes mingling with the sound of the ocean lapping just beyond our balcony. I float back to my room in a near stupor, grateful for a short break until my husband arrives toting two tired children. We bundle them into bed and order room service from Paper Daisy. We sit out on the terrace under a blanket of stars, listening to the nearby surf against the shore. The meal arrives on beautiful ceramics with Frette linen, taking room service to the next level with locally sourced, organic produce and a complimentary…

articles.title: The Louise, Marananga
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: A Baillie Lodges address on Seppeltsfield Road. In-suite massage, private yoga on the lawn, an outdoor pool facing the vines and hot and cold sauna.
articles.body: The massage comes to you. At The Louise the treatment happens in your suite, which means you can walk ten steps and fall into bed afterwards rather than driving home through the Barossa dusk. The lodge sits on Seppeltsfield Road in Marananga, vines running to the edge of the property and an outdoor pool that looks straight out over them. It is a Baillie Lodges address, so the standard is high and quietly held. Private yoga on the lawn, Indian head massage, a fitness room with hot and cold sauna. Wine country tends to undo people. This is where you get put back together.

articles.title: Eleme Day Spa at Crystalbrook Byron
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: A wellness sanctuary nestled within 45 acres of subtropical rainforest on the outskirts of Byron Bay.
articles.body: Nestled within 45 acres of subtropical rainforest on the outskirts of Byron Bay, Eléme Day Spa is the wellness sanctuary at Crystalbrook Byron, a responsible luxury resort near Tallow Beach. Formerly part of the Byron at Byron Resort, the property is now under the Crystalbrook Collection, whose sustainability-first ethos extends to the spa's approach: treatments are built around natural botanicals and the healing energy of the surrounding rainforest. The menu is designed to flex, allowing therapists to personalise each session, from deep-tissue massage and infrared sauna to bespoke facials using plant-based formulations. Guests can extend the experience with complimentary morning yoga, heated infinity pool access and rainforest boardwalk walks. Open Monday to Saturday, Eléme is both a resort amenity and a destination day spa for visitors to the Byron hinterland. Review by Sigourney Cantelo

articles.title: The Spa at Park Hyatt Sydney, The Rocks
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: A rooftop spa across the water from the Opera House, with a pool, cabanas and iKou organics. The best view in Sydney, earned by anyone who books ninety minutes or more.
articles.body: Location is the whole argument here, and what an argument. The spa sits on the roof of the Park Hyatt, across the water from the Opera House, with a pool, cabanas and a jacuzzi arranged around the best view in Sydney. Inside it is ivory and beige, timber and limestone, five treatment rooms and two aromatherapy steam rooms in warm quiet tones. The skincare is iKou, organic and Australian. Book anything over ninety minutes and the rooftop is yours, or try the Native Clay and Hot Oil massage that works the length of your spine. The city showing off, gently, to anyone who has earned an afternoon off. The sails are right there. Let them be your view.

articles.title: The Spa, Rae’s on Watego’s, Byron Bay
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: A shimmering Aladdin’s Cave of indulgence tucked into the ground floor of Byron Bay’s most iconic boutique hotel, where bespoke facials and Reiki healing meet mother-of-pearl walls.
articles.body: Byron Bay’s Most Iconic Boutique Spa A shimmering Aladdin’s Cave of indulgence, tucked in the ground floor of a boutique luxury hotel Rae’s Spa, is where to come in Byron Bay if you’re serious about your skin. While the stunning, petite, two-roomed spa offers a range of treatments, it’s really all about the facials, thanks to the Hotel and Spa Manager Marionne De Candia, who administers them. An industry doyenne, with over 30 years in the business and a knowledge of skin and ingredients to match, Marionne tailors the treatment to your complexion, utilising her own skincare range, a pure, highly-active range of cosmeceuticals along with the healing magic of Reiki. Access to the spa is via a staircase from the front driveway and up white, windy stone path that leads you past the pool. I’m lucky enough to be staying upstairs so I don’t have to travel far, but the spa is open to non-guests, as well. Rae’s has played host to almost every visiting celebrity to Byron Bay over the years, such is it’s privacy and sense of understated luxe. As a result, Marionne has tended to the delicate dermis of everyone from Elle Macpherson to Kate Hudson. Mother-of-Pearl Walls and Moroccan Charm Stepping inside the spa, you do get the impression that you are entering a magical golden cave, the walls are curved and tiled with beautiful champagne-hued Italian mother-of-pearl tiles that glisten iridescent, like fish scales. Ornate fretwork adorns the arched doorways giving the spa an exotic, Moroccan vibe, the marble floors glisten and cleverly placed lighting gives everything a gilded glow. Rae’s signature blend of oil (gardenia, geranium and patchouli) is burning and the place smells gorgeous. I shed the Tigerlily silk robe that I’ve wearing (it feels appropriate to waft around in seventies caftans and kimonos at Rae’s, such is the luxe I’m-with-the-band-vibe of the place) and slip between the cool crisp cotton sheets as Marionne begins her magic. Reiki Healing and Bespoke Facial Treatment She does a double cleanse and then during a deep, satisfying steam I feel her hands on my forehead and I know she’s doing Reiki on me, I can feel the warmth of her hands even she’s barely touching me. Suddenly I feel incredibly calm and cared for. An energy that stays with me for the entire treatment. After the steam, Marionne applies a 100% strength hyaluronic serum, its jelly consistency is sucked up by my skin almost immediately. She addresses some pregnancy-pigmentation with a vitamin C and vitamin B actives, before beginning a heavenly facial massage. Her touch is light and delicate, with gentle tapping motions that Marionne tells me later was lymphatic drainage. Once the mask is on, she does an incredibly relaxing arm massage with a warm collagen massage cream. A few times I feel myself balancing on the edge of sleep, catching myself as my breathing tips into its heaviest. An hour whizzes by in what seems like seconds and then Marionne speaks quietly, telling me she’s going to get me some water. I sit up slowly and go to examine my skin in the mirror. It’s all juiced up and plump, the dim-light reflects off my cheekbones satisfyingly. It’s just what my starved skin was craving. I head back to my room and leave the products on my skin for the rest of the day, the beauty of a facial with Marionne is that she doesn’t use any oil, so you don’t have to wash your hair afterwards. My skin feels hydrated but not greasy. Staying at the Ocean View Penthouse We are staying…

articles.title: Venustus, Paddington
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Behind white portal doors on Oxford Street, a hush closer to a monastery than a spa. Sculptural pods, four-handed massages and thirty years of quiet excellence.
articles.body: There is nowhere else like it. Behind the white portal doors on Oxford Street is a hush closer to a monastery than a spa, with sculptural egg-shaped pods you climb inside to be reborn and a spiral staircase that belongs in a gallery. Jeannie Bourke has run it for the better part of thirty years, and her people stay for twenty. That tells you most of what you need to know. Each day opens with sage and palo santo. The massages are the thing. Four hands, sometimes six, moving at once. Lymphatic drainage, intuitive work, packages named 11 11 and 777 for anyone who wants to disappear for an afternoon. The skincare is Venustus's own, made in-house. It has a following that reportedly includes Nicole Kidman, though the staff are far too discreet to say. You go in wound tight. You come out rearranged.

articles.title: Waldheim Spa, Cradle Mountain Lodge
articles.author: Beauticate Editorial
articles.excerpt: Deep in Tasmania's alpine wilderness, Waldheim Spa pairs Elemis and Sodashi treatments with hydrotherapy, King Billy Pine views and the kind of silence only a national park can offer.
articles.body: Nestling in amongst bush and native trees in the rugged Alpine forests in Tasmania's Highlands, the Waldheim Spa is part of the Cradle Mountain Lodge hotel complex and sits at the edge of Lake St Clair National Park. This spa has six treatment rooms boasting sensational views of the tall King Billy Pines and the Pencil Pine River, thanks to its large and roomy glass windows. The Spa Sanctuary is available for private bookings, and includes a sauna, steam room, relaxation beds and both a hydrotherapy and cold plunge pool. Rather minimalist-looking, the setting is all white walls, light wood and glass and has been designed to reflect the colours of nature's growth outside. The lodges are stone and timber with cosy roaring open fires, perfect for relaxing in front of with a drink after a long day of walking. If you choose to book the Spa Sanctuary with a partner or friend ($130 for 60 minutes) then we recommend adding in the upgrade ($270 for 75 mins) because then you'll find a member of staff arriving with a bottle of sparkling wine and a plate of chocolate-covered strawberries. A happy indulgence indeed and well worth the extra money, since when is the next time you plan to be back here? Treatments at the Waldheim Spa are all carried out with a choice of Elemis or natural Australian Sodashi products. But the real plus is the hot and cold water therapies on offer. This ancient form of circulation-boosting treatment is included in both the 'muscle melting' Waldheim Signature aromatic bath and the refreshing Blue Gum Eucalyptus Bath. Review by Sigourney Cantelo

articles.title: Wellness Spa, Daintree EcoLodge
articles.author: Beauticate Editorial
articles.excerpt: 20 Daintree Road, Daintree QLD 4873.

articles.title: GROUNDUP Wellness, Dickson
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: A treetop recovery floor at DKSN in Dickson with infrared and traditional saunas, ice baths, a red-light bed and the full contrast circuit under one roof.
articles.body: Take the lift at DKSN, past the IGA, and you land in a recovery floor sitting up in the treetops. The views are all leaves. Inside there are infrared and traditional saunas, ice baths and a red-light bed, the full contrast circuit under one roof. It sits directly above GROUNDUP's reformer studio, so a class and a cold plunge can be the same trip. You can come once, buy a pack or join. This is the only GROUNDUP wellness space in the city, which makes it something of a first for Canberra. Sweat, plunge, repeat. Then go back down to the street a different person.

articles.title: One Hot Yoga & Pilates, South Yarra
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: A dim and deliberately sensory hot yoga studio on River Street. Natural materials, heavy linen curtains and controlled lighting that turns the attention inward. Elegant, hushed, a little cinematic.
articles.body: Most hot yoga studios are lit like a car park. One Hot Yoga on River Street is the opposite, a dim and deliberately sensory room where the heat, the finely controlled lighting and the tone-on-tone palette are all part of the practice. Natural materials throughout, heavy linen curtains, a courtyard of greenery to land in afterwards. The darkness is the point. It turns the attention inward and keeps it there, which is what the good studios understand and the fluorescent ones never will. Hot yoga and reformer, run with the same quiet rigour as the design. Elegant, hushed, a little cinematic. You sweat, then you exhale into something that actually feels calm.

articles.title: Power Moves, Newstead
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Brisbane's best pilates instructor, as voted by the Courier Mail. Power Moves runs athletic reformer, hot mat and yoga classes from a boutique Newstead studio on Helen Street.
articles.body: Morgan was voted Brisbane's best pilates instructor by the Courier Mail in 2021, so Power Moves comes with a pedigree. The Newstead studio on Helen Street holds two spaces and the classes are the athletic kind. Reformer, hot mat, yoga, fifty minutes of proper work. There is a West End studio too, for the south-side crowd. The fit-out is boutique and considered rather than clinical, which matters when you are face down on the carriage at 6am. This is pilates with intent, built for people who want to feel it the next day. Turn up. Push through. Book the earlier class than you think you can manage.

articles.title: Reju, Braddon
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: A minimalist recovery clinic on Lonsdale Street in Braddon offering cryotherapy, hyperbaric oxygen, infrared saunas, IV infusion and more.
articles.body: Everything at Reju is glass and light. The rooms are walled in it, the tables are made of it, and the effect is meant to leave you feeling grounded rather than clinical. Tucked into Lonsdale Street, it gathers the whole modern recovery arsenal in one place. Cryotherapy, hyperbaric oxygen, infrared saunas, IV infusion, compression, remedial massage. It opened as one of the more serious recovery clinics in the country, and the minimalism is the point. Nothing here distracts from the work. You come in tired. You leave with your edges sanded off. Longevity, done without a single scented candle in sight.

articles.title: Saint Haven, Collingwood
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: A hundred-and-fifty-million-dollar wellness club in Collingwood. Candlelit grotto bathhouse, cedar sauna, Himalayan-salt pool, cryotherapy and a membership capped at five hundred.
articles.body: Tim Gurner spent a hundred and fifty million dollars to make wellness feel like membership, and Saint Haven is the result. The Collingwood club takes its cues from Soho House, soft curves and beige calm and a marble bar you would happily drink at, then loads recovery technology behind the design. A candlelit grotto bathhouse, a two-tier cedar sauna, a Himalayan-salt mineral pool held at thirty-five degrees and an ice plunge that bites at six. Hyperbaric chambers, cryotherapy, a meditation cave for breathwork. The restaurant bans seed oils and refined sugar. Membership is capped at five hundred, and members wear Oura rings to prove the point. Extravagant, yes. Also seriously equipped. There is nothing else like it in Melbourne.

articles.title: The Commons Health Club, South Yarra
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Five thousand square metres of South Yarra designed by DesignOffice. A magnesium bathhouse, sauna, reformer, strength and two hundred classes a week under one very considered roof.
articles.body: The Commons made its name on beautiful co-working, then asked why the gym could not look as good. Its first health club answers the question across five thousand square metres of South Yarra, designed by DesignOffice with the same restraint that made the desks worth sitting at. There is a magnesium bathhouse and a sauna for the recovery end. Reformer, strength and around two hundred classes a week for the effort end. The idea is that you step out of a morning meeting and into an evening soak without changing postcodes. Movement, recovery, work and a social life stacked under one very considered roof. Fitness that finally understands design. It should not have taken this long.

articles.title: The Movement Society, Cottesloe
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Low-impact mat Pilates before Cottesloe is properly awake. Forty-five minutes at quarter past six in a small white room inside the Civic Centre, all levels welcome.
articles.body: Two mornings a week, before Cottesloe is properly awake, a small white room inside the Civic Centre fills with mats and props. The Movement Society runs its signature class here at quarter past six, forty-five minutes of low-impact mat Pilates built to strengthen and lengthen rather than exhaust. Bring your own mat and toolkit, or borrow one. All levels welcome, which in practice means nobody at the back feeling out of place. There is an online platform too for the mornings you cannot make it in. Three classes for forty-nine dollars to start. Set an alarm. The early ones tend to be the ones that stick.

articles.title: Wellness and Recovery Haus, Kiama
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: A tight, well-chosen recovery circuit on Manning Street in Kiama. Float tank, cold plunge, infrared sauna, compression boots and Dermalux LED in one small room.
articles.body: You find it by the sign. A black board hung out over Manning Street with a single decorative ampersand doing all the work. Inside, Kiama's recovery crowd move through a tight, well-chosen circuit. A float tank loaded with Epsom salt until your body forgets it has weight. A cold plunge kept honest by a proper chiller, so the temperature never wavers. An infrared sauna for thirty or forty minutes when you want the slow burn instead. Add compression boots and Dermalux LED and you have a full contrast day in one small room. The ocean is right there. This works better.

articles.title: Guy Sebastian on Identity, Inner Circles and Rebuilding Self-Worth
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: I've known Guy Sebastian for over two decades, and yet this conversation felt different. We didn't talk about success. We talked about survival, self-trust and the courage it takes to live a balanced life in an unbalanced world.
articles.body: Listen to the full episode here I've known Guy Sebastian for more than two decades. I've watched him go from the kid who won the very first season of Australian Idol to one of the most enduring artists this country has ever produced. And yet this conversation felt different. We didn't sit down to talk about the records or the longevity. We sat down to talk about the quieter things. Survival. Self-trust. The courage it takes to live a balanced life in a world that never switches off. What follows is one of the most open conversations I've had on Beautiful Inside, and I left it thinking about my own life differently. On the Pressure to Be Everything "Trying to be everything to everyone is just a fast road to being unwell." Guy is clear-eyed about the cost of people-pleasing. He talks about how early fame magnified a feeling he'd carried since childhood, that he was different, and how the instinct to keep everyone happy quietly became unsustainable. As he puts it, "I can't be everything to everyone and be a good friend." It's a line I keep coming back to. On Being Manipulated, and the Fallout "I felt like I was a monkey on a treadmill. I was constantly working, constantly away and very heavily manipulated." This is the hardest chapter, and Guy doesn't dress it up. He describes a period of being manipulated at a deeply vulnerable point in his career, and the depression that followed. What struck me most was where the pain actually sat for him. "The biggest thing that made me really blue and really sad was my opinion of myself, to be able to be that manipulated." It wasn't the betrayal that floored him. It was what the betrayal made him believe about himself. Rebuilding from there, he says, had to happen from the inside out. On Mental Health and Asking for Help "I ask for help when I feel like I can't help myself." For a man of his generation and profile to say that so plainly matters. Guy is honest about the version of masculinity that tells you to push through, and about learning the opposite the hard way. "I learned the hard way that if I'm rendered useless, I can't help anybody." He frames looking after himself not as indulgence but as the thing that lets him show up for everyone else. On Protecting Your Inner Circle "Life's about balance and doing what's good for you." We talk about the noise of the digital age, the endless external input, and why shrinking your world down to a few trusted people can be an act of protection rather than withdrawal. Guy has clearly thought hard about who gets his energy, and why guarding it is non-negotiable now. On Parenting in a Digital World "I don't care if the other kids have it." Becoming a father reordered everything. Guy is thoughtful about screens and boundaries, and refreshingly unbothered by the social pressure to give his boys what everyone else has. Much of this thinking flows into the youth mental health programs he and his wife Jules fund, work he speaks about with real purpose, having reached, in his words, "200 and something thousand kids." Why It Stayed With Me This is a grounded, generous conversation about identity, responsibility and choosing a life that actually holds you up. Not perfection. Not having it all. Just balance, and the people who matter. I left it lighter. I think you will too. Interview by Sigourney Cantelo. Sponsor Thank you to our sponsor, Aestheticá Byron Bay, the…

articles.title: What to watch and listen to over the break – conversations from Beautiful Inside by Beauticate
articles.author: Beauticate Editorial
articles.excerpt: What to watch and listen to – thoughtful podcast and vodcast conversations from Beautiful Inside by Beauticate, curated for different moods.
articles.body: The end of the year is a time to slow down and make space for meaningful conversations. This edit brings together Beautiful Inside by Beauticate podcast and vodcast episodes to watch and listen to over the break, curated for different moods and moments. Curated for different moods and ways of listening, this is an easy edit of podcast and vodcast episodes to watch or listen to at your own pace. Whether you’re travelling, staying close to home, or easing into January at your own pace, these episodes were made to keep you company in those quieter moments. Sigourney Cantelo Founder & Host, Beautiful Inside by Beauticate For the Long Drive Long stretches of road, solo time, and the kind of listening that makes the journey feel shorter. Celeste Barber on ADHD, Bullying, Boundaries & Social Media Funny, honest and deeply relatable – a conversation that keeps you company mile after mile. Watch or Listen Here Trinny Woodall on Confidence, Ageing & Owning Who You Are Sharp, energising and full of perspective on reinvention and self-belief. Watch or Listen Here Jane Wurwand on Resilience & Building a Billion-Dollar Brand A quietly powerful story about longevity, purpose and building something meaningful. Watch or Listen Here For the Staycation Slow mornings, skincare on, nowhere to be. Sacred Six: The Rituals Helping Me Heal From Burnout Short, grounding episodes designed for calm moments at home. Watch or Listen Here Dimitri Weber on Fragrance & Making Australia His Muse An atmospheric conversation about scent, place and creative intuition. Watch or Listen Here Terri Vinson Jones on Body Image, Anxiety & Self-Worth An honest, generous conversation that rewards unhurried listening. Watch or Listen Here For the Nights with no Schedule When you have time – and want to use it well. Sigourney Cantelo Episode Two and Three Our most-loved episodes to date. A deeply personal conversation about life, loss, healing and finding meaning, shared across two parts and still the most listened-to episodes of Beautiful Inside by Beauticate . Watch or Listen Here Pip Edwards on Identity, Motherhood & Reinvention Candid, thoughtful and compelling – a conversation about evolution and staying true to yourself. Watch or Listen Here Jess Sepel on OCD, Grief & Building JSHealth With Heart A powerful, restorative listen about healing, resilience and building with intention. articles.title: The Calm, Last-Minute Christmas Guide
articles.author: Jayde Balderston
articles.excerpt: A calm, last-minute Christmas guide curated by the Beauticate team – thoughtful gifts that feel considered, not rushed.
articles.body: December gets busy quickly. Plans stack up, deadlines blur, and suddenly Christmas is closer than you’d like to admit. This guide is for that moment - when you still want to give well, just without the panic. Gifts That Feel Considered, Even If You’re Buying Them This Week Curated by the Beauticate team, this is a calm edit of last-minute Christmas gifts chosen for their quality, thoughtfulness and ease. Nothing frantic. Nothing obvious. Just pieces that feel considered, even if they’re bought at the last minute. Because good taste isn’t about timing – it’s about intention. Sigourney's edit For me, the best gifts are the ones that create a feeling the moment you unwrap them. Goldfield & Banks’ Silky Woods is exactly that – rich, enveloping and unmistakably Australian, with a depth that feels luxurious without ever being overpowering. I love pairing it with Maison Louis Marie’s Fleur de Vanille Hair & Body Mist , a softer, comforting scent that works beautifully for everyday wear and quiet moments at home. And for a little extra glow, Gisou’s Glow All The Way Set delivers exactly what it promises – luminous hair and skin that feel polished, joyful and effortlessly put together. Quietly luxurious, beautifully considered. Jayde's edit My edit is all about comfort that feels intentional , not thrown together. Saarde’s Saint-Raphaël Room Spray turns any space into a calm, welcoming place – because good ambience never goes out of style. I love the Frank Green Lip & Sip Bundle , which keeps hydration and a little shine close at hand wherever you go (hydrated lips + water = holiday survival). Useful, lovely, and a little luxe – the best kind of present. Zoe's edit My Christmas wish list leans towards pieces that feel timeless and genuinely well made. Considered, reliable, and the kind of gifts you know will actually be used. Kristina's edit My holiday edit is all about thoughtful touches that make everyday feel a little more radiant. Lancôme’s Juicy Tubes in Lavender Latte is my go-to lip gloss – soft, wearable and effortlessly chic for any occasion. When my skin feels tired or stressed (which, let’s be honest, it often does), Kate Somerville’s Goat Milk Stressed Skin Saviors is my calm-down hero – soothing, rich and genuinely comforting. And for eyes that feel polished with minimal effort, Clé de Peau Beauté’s Eye Color Quad Holiday Collection delivers luxe, blendable shades that elevate any look without fuss. Polish without pressure – my holiday beauty mantra. Written by Jayde Balderston

articles.title: Home Alone, but Never Boring: My Nightly Beauty Rituals in December
articles.author: Jayde Balderston
articles.excerpt: December is loud. Being home alone is the counter-luxury. These are the nightly beauty rituals I come back to when everything else ramps up.
articles.body: December is busy in a very specific way. This nightly beauty routine is the one constant I protect, even when everything else ramps up. End-of-year deadlines stack up, invitations overlap, work kicks into a whole other gear, and suddenly every night feels spoken for. I go out, I work late, I say yes — which is exactly why being home, on my own terms, feels like a luxury rather than a default. By the time I get home, I don't want silence. I want movement. Familiar chaos. Hello, ADHD. I want a clean face, no bra, a glass poured, emails half-checked, and Bravo on loud enough that I can hear women yelling while I move around the apartment. Candles lit because — why not? It's not about switching off — it's about switching gears. Especially now, with a kitten called Blueberry Muffin supervising proceedings and a month full of obligations already behind me. These nights aren't about pretending I don't love things. They're about ritual, routine, and using products properly — many I've relied on for years, some newer, all genuinely part of my life. I won't lie: I love products. I love experiencing the scents, textures, and most of all… the packaging. I am a marketer's dream. The Arrival Ritual: How the Night Actually Starts I don't rip my makeup off the second I walk through the door. I like a buffer. I wind down first. Shoes off. Bag hung. My new Steven Khalil x Black Blaze candle lit. A glass of wine poured — one of my longest friends has a vineyard in Victoria's King Valley Wine Region, founded and run by women — and my varietal of choice, the Symphonia Arneis 2022. I check emails and messages while setting up my watchlist. This is the decompression window — the slow shift from public-facing to private. These nights aren't about pretending I don't love things. They're about ritual, routine, and using products properly. Only then do I cleanse. I double cleanse every night. Always have. I've tried all the oil cleansers, and the holy grail is the MECCA Cosmetica Nourishing Cleansing Oil. I work it into dry skin (pro tip from the very talented James Vivian : cleanse for at least 60 seconds) before removing it with a Retreatment Botanics muslin cloth soaked in water that's slightly warmer than warm. Followed by the Rejuvaus Deep Exfoliating AHA Cleanser. I am the least active person you will meet, but this cleanser walked so everything else could run. It includes 15 intelligent acids — including lactic, malic, citric and tartaric acids — plus activated charcoal, prebiotics and a lipid complex. It's lightweight and leaves my skin feeling clean and nourished, never dry or squeaky. About ten years ago, I was seeing an incredible facialist who introduced me to Sesderma, a Spanish skincare brand that genuinely changed my life. After my hysterectomy at 30 (cervical cancer survivor over here), my skin went into chaos thanks to no natural hormones and the introduction of multiple medications, including HRT. The Azelac Lotion Spray is a staple in my beauty cupboard and always will be. A few squirts onto a cotton pad and gentle swipes across the face soothe the skin, diminish redness, and help regulate sebum. If you have folliculitis, this is the product. I finish with Jurlique Calendula Toner, pressed in with my hands. It's grounding, uncomplicated, and exactly what my skin wants at the end of a long day. If I want extra hydration, I'll dot the Calendula Cream onto my cheeks, chin, nose and forehead, then gently massage it in.…

articles.title: The New Pool Rules: 7 Trends in Luxury Pool Design for Australian Homes
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: From resort-style wet decks to magnesium water and sculptural curves, these seven luxury pool design trends are redefining Australian homes – and turning backyards into…
articles.body: Aussies have always had a thing for pools. But lately, the backyard watering hole has evolved into something far more elevated - a scene-stealing centrepiece that speaks to design, lifestyle, and a deep desire for connection. Once a place for perfunctory barbecues and a modest patch of grass, it's now the heart of the home - a sanctuary for escape, play, and wellness. And at the centre of this evolution? The swimming pool. But not just any pool. These aren’t just places to cool off - they’re extensions of the home’s architecture, reflections of personal style, and increasingly, the setting for some of life’s best memories (and let’s be honest, the occasional epic tantrum or Aperol spill). Working with Blue Haven on our own dream pool gave me a front-row seat to the new era of aquatic luxury – think sculptural curves, textural tiles, magnesium water, and sunken lounges that wouldn’t look out of place at a five-star resort. “We’re seeing a big shift towards curves, minimalism, and spaces that feel like luxury resorts at home,” says Remonda Martinez , CEO of Blue Haven Pools. “Think built-in lounges, seamless edges, smart lighting, and that indoor-outdoor flow. People are over the standard rectangle and want a pool that feels like a vibe. It’s all about integration.” Whether you’re planning a knockdown rebuild or revamping your existing space, here are the seven design-led trends redefining Australian luxury pool design in 2026 – many of which featured in our very own pool collaboration with Blue Haven. 1\. Wet Decks and Built-In Sunken Lounges Nothing says ‘ holiday at home ‘ quite like a sunken lounge or a shallow wet deck built into your pool. These resort-style features offer a space to socialise, sip something cold, and feel completely immersed – without ever needing to ruin your hair. “Tanning ledges are massive right now,” says Remonda. “Especially for young families who want splash zones for the kids and chillax zones for the adults.” These shallow, submerged platforms double as safe play zones and sleek relaxation areas. 2\. Curved and Organic Pool Shapes Forget rigid right angles. The most design-forward pools for 2026 favour soft, organic forms that mirror nature and architecture alike. “People want pools that reflect their lifestyle and personal aesthetic,” Remonda explains. “There’s significant planning going on.” Curves complement both classic and contemporary homes, and when paired with the right tiling and landscaping, they become sculptural showpieces. Our own Blue Haven build embraced this ethos with a gracefully curved concrete shell that invites movement and flow. 3\. Why Tiled Pool Interiors Are Worth the Investment Step aside, fibreglass blue. Today’s high-end pools are all about tactile, tonal tiling. “Fully tiled pools are having a major moment,” says Remonda. “Textured glass, natural stone, Moroccan mosaics – there’s a hunger for texture and tone. People want pools that glow and blend with their outdoor palette.” Beyond aesthetics, tiled interiors offer superior durability and a luxe finish that ages beautifully. Personally I love a larger format tile, I think it looks more modern than the traditional mosaics. 4\. Mineral and Magnesium Pool Systems Wellness is now integral to pool design. Homeowners are prioritising health-conscious water systems that support skin and eye sensitivity. “ Magnesium pools are softer on the skin, gentler on the eyes, and packed with healing properties,” says Remonda. “You step out feeling like you’ve had a spa treatment – not a chemical rinse.” For our pool, we opted for a magnesium mineral system that delivers both silky water and beauty benefits. Not only is it seriously beautiful to swim in. It feels…

articles.title: Tanya Ali Jalani on Awakening, Mental Health, and the Human Side of Healing
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: I sit down with breathwork facilitator and Soulchemy founder Tanya Ali Jalani on spiritual awakening, depression, cultural conditioning and the human side of healing.
articles.body: Listen to the full episode here This week, I sit down with the luminous Tanya Ali Jalani, breathwork facilitator, sound healer and the founder of Soulchemy. Tanya's story is one of profound inner awakening, cultural reinvention, and the courage it takes to dismantle the conditioning we inherit. It is a conversation for anyone who has ever felt wired differently, struggled in silence, or longed for a deeper connection to themselves. Cultural conditioning and the weight we inherit Tanya grew up in Iran before migrating to Australia at age six, carrying the weight of cultural expectation, displacement, and early mental health struggles. We talk about how the conditioning we inherit, from family and from culture, quietly shapes our identity long before we have the words for it. For Tanya, that included the hidden emotional load so often carried by immigrant and Middle Eastern families, the things that go unspoken and unprocessed across generations. At twelve, she knew something inside her felt different, but did not yet have the language for depression, trauma, or the emotional storms that shaped her early life. It is a tender, honest place to begin, and it sets up everything that follows. The awakening that changed everything Tanya's life changed dramatically six years ago during a deep meditation retreat, where she experienced a spiritual awakening so powerful it rewired the way she thought, felt and moved in the world. We talk about that profound before and after, what it felt like to come back into ordinary life changed, and how an experience like that becomes the foundation for the work she does now. Soulchemy, breath and sound healing Through her Soulchemy method, Tanya combines breathwork and sound frequencies to shift the body into deep relaxation and release. But she is just as interested in what happens afterwards. We explore why breathwork can activate dormant energies, and why responsible aftercare and integration matter so much. A practice this powerful asks for care, not just intensity. Depression, mental health and staying human Tanya speaks openly about the days she still has to work hard not to dip. We get into the difference between everyday sadness and clinical depression, and why she approaches her work through a lens of responsibility, integration and emotional safety rather than chasing peak experiences. As she puts it, spiritual highs mean nothing without staying grounded and human. We close on the rituals and practices that help her stay steady, the unglamorous, daily work of actually feeling well. A special thank you to our sponsor, Aestheticá Byron Bay, the female-founded, nurse-led medi-spa redefining natural, ethical cosmetic treatments. Created by registered nurse Alexa Roetger, Aestheticá is built on education, safety, and subtle, confidence-led results, staffed by highly trained medical and wellness professionals and grounded in Alexa's "less is more" philosophy. The clinic specialises in anti-wrinkle treatments, dermal fillers, bioremodelling, regenerative therapies like PRP, medical boosters and advanced dermal treatments, with a strong focus on peri- and menopausal skin support. Nurse Lex is kindly offering our audience a 20% discount: head to aestheticabyronbay.com to book and use the code BEAUTICATE2026. Hosted by Sigourney Cantelo.

articles.title: Why I Swapped My Whoop for an Ultrahuman Ring (and What It's Taught Me About Stress, Sleep, and Bio-Age)
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: I swapped my Whoop for the Ultrahuman Ring AIR – a chic wearable that tracks sleep, stress, HRV and bio-age without the pressure. Here's what…
articles.body: It all started with a book. Specifically, Why We Sleep by Matthew Walker, which I read on a plane, probably while drinking champagne and committing every circadian sin in the book. I stayed up late multiple nights reading it (ironic) and by the time I finished it, I was fully converted: sleep wasn’t just “important,” it was EVERYTHING. The foundation of your health, your hormones, your glow, your patience with your kids. Your whole damn life. Naturally, the next step was to start tracking it. That's how I fell into the world of wearable tech – and why, for a long time, I wore the Whoop band. I even went full Gwyneth and got the champagne-coloured strap with gold hardware, which looked chic until it started looking a bit… grotty. Foundation, sweat and God knows what else. Let's just say if it were a handbag, it would've been demoted to "school run only." Why I Broke Up with Whoop (Mostly) To be fair, there were things I really liked about it. The weight training function was excellent – you can add exercises in and it even counts your reps and you can find out how much strain you're under. It made me feel like a bit like an athlete. (An athlete who only works out when she hasn't washed her hair.) But then the monthly subscription fee started to annoy me. I don't like renting things I've already worn in the bath. Plus, it became a bit… intense. Like it was constantly judging me for staying up past 10pm trawling the internet for aesthetic massage chairs (spoiler: they don't exist). I started to get what my mum – in her infinite wisdom – called "sleep anxiety". She gently suggested that maybe I didn't need another device telling me I'd failed at resting. Touché, Mum. The Switch: Ultrahuman Ring AIR Eventually, I started hearing buzz about the Ultrahuman Ring AIR . Sleek. Sexy. Designed in titanium and blessedly strapless. It promised to track my sleep, stress, HRV and recovery – but in a way that felt less sweaty sports bra and more elevated wellness tech. So I ordered one. And honestly? I love it. It gives me the data I want – like how stressful that spicy that podcast tech meltdown really was on my nervous system, or how well I recovered after three glasses of pinot and a late-night episode of Selling Sunset. But it doesn't yell at me. It feels more like a gentle nudge than a coach screaming in my face. What I Use It For (and How You Can Too) Here's what I've learned – and how I actually use it in real life, in case you're considering the switch or wondering how wearable tech can be useful without driving you mad. 1. Sleep Quality Check I still track my sleep most days – but I no longer spiral if I don't hit 8 hours. I use it more like a weather report: am I running on reserves or fully charged? It's especially helpful to see how: • Alcohol affects me (spoiler: always worse sleep) • Whether red light before bed improves my HRV (so far so YES!) • If magnesium or journalling helps my deep sleep increase (jury out, still tracking) 2. Stress Awareness (a.k.a. NSI / "You Might Want to Chill") Ultrahuman calls it your Stress Score, but it's really just your nervous system in numbers. When it's high, I know I need a bath, a walk, or a moment without children climbing on me. Sometimes it reminds me to: • Meditate (even if it's…

articles.title: The Only Christmas Hint I'm Leaving Out This Year: Better Skin (Not More Stuff)
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: This Christmas, I'm leaving one clear hint: better skin, not more stuff. Here's why LED light therapy is the smartest, most intentional beauty gift -…
articles.body: There are two kinds of gifts at Christmas. The kind you smile politely at and quietly re-gift by February. And the kind you use, love, and thank someone for every single time you look in the mirror. This year, I'm campaigning for fewer novelty mugs, panic candles and vaguely passive-aggressive Secret Santa gifts, and more presents that actually do something. Preferably for your skin. Preferably while you're lying down. Enter: LED. If you've been anywhere near a dermatologist's office, a medi-spa, or the skincare-obsessed corner of the internet lately, you'll know LED light therapy has well and truly crossed over from "nice clinic add-on" to serious at-home skincare investment. And for good reason. I've been testing Qure's LED tech for months now, and quietly loving the ritual, the results, and the fact that it requires absolutely zero effort beyond putting a mask on and existing. Which is my favourite kind of skincare. But here's the part that made me do a double take: Qure is still running one of the most generous offers I've seen this year. Buy the LED face mask and they're literally giving you the neck device for free. Two LED devices for the price of one. Yes. Really. Why LED Is One of the Smartest Gifts You Can Give LED light therapy works by delivering specific wavelengths of light into the skin, triggering cellular repair and regeneration. Red light, in particular, has been shown to stimulate collagen production, reduce inflammation, improve skin tone and texture, and support overall skin health. But the benefits don't stop at aesthetics. From a wellness and biohacking perspective, red and near-infrared light therapy has also been linked to improved circulation, muscle recovery, reduced joint pain, and faster tissue repair – which is why athletes use it, longevity enthusiasts swear by it, and increasingly, women are integrating it into their evening wind-down rituals . Think of it as skincare that quietly multitasks. Why the Neck Matters (And Why Most of Us Ignore It) We're meticulous about our faces and strangely negligent about our necks. And yet the neck is often where ageing shows first – thinner skin, less collagen, more sun exposure, fewer oil glands. LED works best when you treat the face and neck consistently, which is why this particular Qure offer is so smart. It actually supports a full routine rather than pretending the neck doesn't exist. And here's the bonus detail I love: the neck LED device isn't just for your neck. You can use it on your shoulders, upper back, lower back, stomach – you want to support circulation, recovery, or inflammation reduction. Tight shoulders from desk life? Post-Pilates soreness? That weird spot in your lower back that flares up when you least expect it? LED doesn't care where it goes . It just gets to work. From a biohacking lens, that versatility makes it far more than a beauty device. It's a low-effort, high-return longevity and wellness tool, which, frankly, is exactly what most of us need. A Better Way to Do Christmas Gifting Here's my Christmas suggestion: rethink meaningful gifts – the ones you buy for partners, parents, or yourself. Instead of another candle, voucher or "I panicked" present, consider something that becomes part of a real ritual. Something that actually supports skin, wellbeing, and rest. The kind of gift that keeps giving long after the wrapping paper's gone and the tree's come down. This is the category LED sits in: not impulse gifting, but intentional, long-game care . And if you're hoping someone special might be reading between the lines? This is an excellent "accidentally…

articles.title: The Mondrian Gold Coast is the Luxe Coastal Escape You Deserve
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: A chic and joy-filled escape with Celeste Barber at the Mondrian Gold Coast ,  ocean views, quiet luxury, beauty moments and golden-hour glamour. The kind…
articles.body: It’s not often that work and pleasure collide quite so stylishly. But when you’re invited to film an interview for our video podcast Beautiful Inside with none other than Celeste Barber - Australian icon, comedian, and all-round legend - near her home on the Gold Coast, you lean all the way in. She wasn’t able to shoot in her home this time, so I had to come up with the PERFECT setting. Somewhere achingly cool and visually delightful; somewhere fitting of a comedy queen. A chic and joy-filled escape with Celeste Barber at the Mondrian Gold Coast – ocean views, quiet luxury, beauty moments and golden-hour glamour. First Impressions: Chic Meets Chill You know that moment when you arrive somewhere and immediately decide that now you live here? That was me, stepping into the Mondrian's all-white, marble-drenched lobby – majestic arches soaring above like some sort of luxe Roman holiday fantasy. It's perched right on Burleigh Beach, which has all the beauty of the Gold Coast without the chaos. Think less Surfers Paradise, more Saint Tropez (if Saint Tropez served flat whites and had friendly tradies). The lobby alone is worth the trip – bronze accents, soft leather banquettes, avant garde art, and marble for days. It whispers quiet luxury, but with an Aussie accent. Jayde and I immediately started scouting corners for impromptu fashion moments. Spoiler: we found many. The Suite Life (a.k.a. My Fake Apartment) Our suite was, in a word, ridiculous . In the best way. You know that moment when you arrive somewhere and immediately decide that now you live here? That was me, stepping into the Mondrian's all-white, marble-drenched lobby. Separate living and dining zones, a full kitchenette (for making tea and storing snacks I had no intention of cooking), an enormous balcony overlooking the ocean, and a bathroom so beautiful I briefly considered forwarding my mail. We got to work straight away rearranging the furniture for the vodcast interview, and when she arrived, I gave Celeste a tour as though it were my actual apartment. She played along, graciously admiring the BOOIE beauty stash I'd artfully arranged by the bath – the purple, aqua and gold tones looked like it was purpose built to showcase her brand. All part of the plan. Celeste was everything you'd hope she'd be: warm, grounded, unfiltered in the best way – check out our episode here. We chatted on the pod about beauty standards, bullying, social media, and why the world needs more belly laughs. It was real. She was real. And I had to keep pinching myself that this was, in fact, my job. Fashion Moments (and Jayde's Testino Era) I brought along a few pieces from Camilla's new collection – flowing silks, earthy tones, divine details – and proceeded to drape myself around the suite very casually , as if I were an extra in La Piscine meets Boogie Nights (but make it Burleigh). Jayde , who is now basically Mario Testino with a side hustle in Reels, captured various outfits reclining on curved velvet lounges and "wistfully" staring into the distance. We timed our golden hour shoot on the balcony just right – sunlight bouncing off the ocean, everything bathed in that soft, cinematic glow that makes you look well-rested even when you're running on a flight and three coffees. Food, Flow and the Scene The downstairs restaurant was a delightful surprise – modern Italian, all white linen and soft curves. Breakfast here felt vaguely like we'd stumbled into a Vogue editorial: avocado toast, yes, but elevated . Upstairs, Haven Pool Club serves up incredible…

articles.title: Rae Morris on Beauty, Mistakes and the Happy Accident That Changed Her Life
articles.author: Zoe Briggs
articles.excerpt: In an intimate conversation, Rae Morris opens up about the childhood that shaped her, the challenges that forged her resilience, and the accidental moment that…
articles.body: Long one of the most globally recognisable names in makeup artistry , and renowned for her exquisitely refined eye for detail, it would be easy to presume perfection was Rae Morris’ entire way of life. Not so. Rae gets honest and frank with us about her simple tomboy childhood, her physical and mental health challenges, and the sparkling career that she insists happened quite by accident — a glamorous one involving none other than Naomi Campbell. Following mentorship by David Bowie’s makeup artist, a healthy dose of innate creativity and talent was unleashed. Three decades on, her no-nonsense yet warm approach makes it clear why A-listers insist she be wielding the brush. Her exacting taste and balance are part of the reason one of the world’s oldest brush makers (180 years and counting) chose her for their only collaboration. Her willingness to make mistakes and work through them, whether on set or in life, explains why she remains a stalwart in the fickle world of fashion. On Growing Up, Dyslexia, and Early Inspiration “My childhood was quite simple, and I was very much a tomboy. My younger brother and I grew up on acreage in Brisbane with typical working parents. School wasn’t easy for me – I struggled academically, partly because of dyslexia and partly because of my health, and eventually failed. Looking back though, I’m grateful to have grown up in the ‘80s, because that era was filled with such bold influences in hair, makeup, and fashion. Being exposed to icons like Boy George, Duran Duran, and Kiss really planted the seed for what would become my lifelong passion for those worlds.” Physical and Mental Health Challenges “I’ve had a few really tough chapters in my life of physical and mental health struggles. As a kid and teenager I had a rare neuropathy that affected my peripheral nerves. It meant having many surgeries, and I spent a lot of high school in hospital because of that. In my early twenties, I struggled with depression so severely that I was hospitalized. The turning point for me in finding my way through that was meeting the right therapist. I had tried medication, seen many doctors, and struggled for years, but eventually I found someone who really understood the severity of my depression.” Postnatal Depression and Finding Support “The hardest time of all came after the birth of my beautiful daughter. When I became pregnant with her, my therapist helped to prepare me for what may come next. I wasn’t truly ready for what followed, but I can see therapy did help guide me through it all. I went through extreme postnatal depression; I had never imagined things could feel so dark. I think what made it even harder was the social expectation that this was supposed to be the happiest time of my life. Thankfully, I reached out for help and received this amazing therapy, which pulled me through. Now, when I reflect back on that period, I can see it was absolutely the darkest time of my life, but also one that gave me the resilience and empathy that I carry with me today. I also learned that I shouldn’t have suffered in silence. Shame kept me from reaching out to the people around me, but when I finally opened up, I discovered so many other women had been through the same thing. Now, whenever I meet a new mum, the first thing I ask her is, “are you okay?” I was never asked that, and I think it could have made a big difference. I think it’s also important…

articles.title: David the Medium on Intuition, Healing and Life After Death
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: What comes to mind when you picture a psychic medium? Incense, crystal balls, whispery voices? David is none of those things. The former counter-terrorism analyst turned medium joins me to talk intuition, grief and his beautiful philosophy that life on earth is a classroom for the soul.
articles.body: Listen to the full episode here What comes to mind when you picture a psychic medium? Incense? Crystal balls? Whispery voices? David is none of those things, and that is exactly what makes this conversation so disarming. Before becoming one of Australia's most sought-after mediums, he was a corporate counter-terrorism analyst. Logical, sceptical and deeply uninterested in anything that smelled of woo woo. Then a single reading in suburban Melbourne changed everything. From counter-terrorism to mediumship David's story is not the one you would expect. He spent his early career in a world of evidence, risk and cold analysis, the furthest thing from crystals and tarot. He had no intention of becoming a medium, and even less interest in being one publicly. That all shifted after one reading he booked almost on a whim. What he heard in that little Melbourne lounge room was so specific, so undeniable, that the analyst in him could not explain it away. It cracked something open, and slowly he began to follow the thread. How trauma sharpened his intuition One of the most moving parts of our conversation is how honest David is about the hard stuff. He talks about growing up as a highly intuitive child without realising it, coming out as a teenager in a more conservative Melbourne, and his parents' separation. His view is that grief, heartbreak and ordinary real life were not obstacles to his gift. They were the training ground for it. He believes trauma often unlocks or sharpens psychic and intuitive abilities, because pain forces us to feel more, notice more and pay closer attention to what is unspoken. Why everyone has intuition If there is one message I want you to take from this episode, it is this. David is adamant that intuition is not reserved for a chosen few. We all have it. Most of us have simply been taught to ignore it. He shares practical, grounded ways to start strengthening your own intuition, and how to tell the difference between a true inner knowing and the noise of anxiety. It is far less mystical, and far more useful, than you might assume. Life as a classroom for the soul We also go deep on the big questions. David describes what it feels like to receive messages from spirit, why he believes nothing is a coincidence, and his beautiful philosophy that life on earth is a classroom for the soul. He talks about reincarnation, soul contracts and what he calls the waiting room of heaven, and how to recognise the signs, synchronicities and moments of deja vu that he believes are quietly guiding us all the time. There is also a surprising overlap, he says, between spirituality and good old self-development. A grounded look at grief and what comes next It is a thoughtful, surprisingly practical look at intuition, energy, grief and what it means to be alive. Whether you are deeply spiritual or gently sceptical, this episode might just change the way you see the world, and yourself. If you enjoyed this episode, please leave a review or share it with a friend. It truly helps the show grow.
