articles.title: Wellness Water: Why Magnesium Pools, Plunges and Shower Design Matter More Than Ever
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Magnesium pools by Blue Haven Pools. Cold plunges. Rain showers that reset your nervous system. Water is wellness-and your home is the new retreat.
articles.body: Some people meditate. Others ice bath. And some people (like me) sit under the shower with jets aimed at their shoulders and pretend no one else in the house exists—for exactly three minutes. No matter the method, one thing is clear: water is having a moment. From magnesium-rich plunge pools to steam-filled bathrooms that double as day spas, the way we design our homes is shifting. More than ever, we’re favouring calm, recovery, and a little bit of everyday indulgence. With help from the team at Blue Haven Pools (and having tested more than a few of these features myself), here’s how water is becoming the new wellness frontier-and why now is the time to design with flow in mind. In a world where self-care has finally moved beyond bath bombs and face masks, water is quietly becoming the unsung hero of modern wellness design. Whether it’s magnesium-rich pools, mood-shifting showers, or plunge pools made for endorphin-chasing cold dips, our homes are transforming into personal sanctuaries-and water is leading the charge. “To me, wellness pools are about creating a space that rejuvenates your body and mind,” says Remonda Martinez, CEO of Blue Haven Pools. “Whether that’s through mineral water, heat therapy, or just the ability to unplug from the world while floating under the stars.” Water as the Ultimate Wellness Tool The benefits of water on the body and mind are well documented. It lowers cortisol, supports circulation, soothes joints, and promotes mental clarity. But beyond the physical, water invites pause. A deep breath. A moment of stillness. “There’s a growing conversation around wellness pools,” says Remonda. “We’re seeing more women driving the decision-making-mums, professionals, wellness warriors. In particular, they’re prioritising health over hype.” Designing with water in mind means thinking beyond simple aesthetics. Instead, it’s about how you want to feel: calm, energised, refreshed. The Rise of Magnesium Pools One of the most powerful-and popular-upgrades in wellness pool design is magnesium water. Unlike traditional chlorine, magnesium is gentle on the skin, eyes, and respiratory system. In addition, it offers a slew of therapeutic benefits, from stress relief to muscle recovery. “You step out of a magnesium pool feeling like you’ve had a spa treatment-not a chemical rinse,” says Remonda. “Magnesium pools are softer on the skin, packed with healing properties, and better for kids or people with sensitivities.” She likens the experience to floating in a mineral spring-but in your own backyard. No car required. When it came to building our pool, it was a no-brainer to go for magnesium. I’m a nightly magnesium bather, so the idea of having that en masse was just irresistible. In terms of upkeep, it’s not too different from adding chlorine to the pool. You simply pour in large bags of magnesium on a regular basis. Yes, it’s pricier than chlorine or salt, but the beauty and health benefits are worth it. Cold Plunges Beyond Elite Athletes What was once the domain of elite athletes has now gone mainstream. Cold plunges and compact ice baths are cropping up in luxury home designs everywhere-and for good reason. After all, a short, sharp immersion in cold water has been linked to reduced inflammation, better sleep, improved mood, and increased stress resilience. “There’s been a significant increase in plunge pool requests,” says Remonda. “And importantly, they’re not just functional-they can be absolutely beautiful. We design them with curves, integrated steps, or even spa-style glass panels for a high-end look.” Whether you use it as a pre-gym ritual or an evening wind-down, a plunge pool is fast becoming a must-have in wellness-oriented homes. Shower Rituals for Daily…

articles.title: This Isn’t Really Me, but It’s What AI Thinks I Should Be
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: I Let AI Turn Me Into a Desert Princess, Yacht Babe and Heiress, And Now I Have Questions
articles.body: What happens when a beauty editor stops directing the shoot and starts starring in it: thanks to the internet’s most viral AI beauty app? I trialled Glam AI to see what one of most powerful digital image generator could dream up. The results? A surreal scroll of high-glam digital avatars: me in diamonds, on yachts, wrapped in furs, and flanked by designer pets. The dopamine hit was instant. But so was the identity crisis. In this honest exploration, I unpack the emotional rollercoaster of seeing yourself reimagined by artificial intelligence, from fantasy fulfilment to body image angst: and the bigger questions this technology raises for the beauty industry. We also invited our audience to weigh in, and their responses reveal just how divided (and deeply affected) we all are by AI’s growing role in beauty. It's a question that's trending on Google right now: Q: Should I try AI-generated portraits? The answer in a nutshell? A: They’re fun, fantastical and hyper-flattering , but they also reveal what tech really thinks beauty looks like. And that’s where things get complicated. I fell down a rabbit hole. Not the kind involving late white rabbits or existential crises about time (although, sure, those too), but the kind paved with perfect skin, ballgowns, desert sunsets and very implausible poodles. It started with a casual test of an image generator app that lets you upload a few photos and choose your fantasy shoot settings: think Vogue Arabia meets Upper East Side old money meets Disney-on-a-desert-safari. And honestly? I was hooked. Leopard print, power suits, and surreal glamour: what AI thinks I should look like. What is Glam AI and how does it work? In a matter of minutes, I was suddenly starring in a luxury yacht editorial, posing in a fantastical ski resort, and swanning through desert dunes in couture, flanked by leopards and flamingos. Furs draped across shoulders, diamonds glitter under desert light, and wild animals posed-eerily still-as if they knew their mark. I was even tempted to see what I’d look like as a muscle-bound body builder (because it’s the closest I’ll ever come!) It was like being the protagonist of a highly aspirational fever dream. The kind of grand scale shoot we poured thousands into when I was working at Vogue, but never starred in ourselves. There’s a rush to seeing yourself this way. As someone who’s worked on beauty shoots for decades, I’ve spent years behind the camera. Now, Glam AI (here's a special code) was putting me in front of it: styled, polished and lit in ways that would normally cost tens of thousands and a team of ten. And yet… no crew, no effort, no makeup chair time. Just… me, in a fantasy land. But then came the gut punch. Looking back at the images, once the initial dopamine hit wore off, I started to notice things. Arms, long and impossibly lean. A waist, cinched to fairytale proportions. Posture that could belong to a ballerina. None of it was me. “And with that the glamour curdled. Because what AI thinks I should look like… isn’t me.” When you see yourself represented in these heightened, idealised ways, it raises some uncomfortable questions. Why does AI default to a single aesthetic version of beauty? Where are the wrinkles? The freckles? The crooked smiles, the soft stomachs, the strong thighs? The human bits? Flamingos, feathers, fitness-because AI has range. Is AI Beauty Reinforcing Unrealistic Standards? From snow queen to yacht goddess-all in a single AI swipe. It reminded me of Dove’s recent campaign, “Beauty in the AI Age” where they showed what…

articles.title: Mukti Organics Founder on Trauma, Truth and Building a Beauty Brand with Purpose
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Mukti is the founder of one of Australia's most respected organic skincare brands and the author of Truth in Beauty. In this raw and honest episode she opens up about trauma, healing and building a beauty brand with purpose.
articles.body: Listen to the full episode here She is the founder of one of Australia's most respected organic skincare brands, a true trailblazer in green beauty and the author of Truth in Beauty. But Mukti's path to purpose was anything but picture perfect, and that is exactly what made this conversation so moving to record. In this raw and radically honest episode of Beautiful Inside, Mukti opens up to me about the defining moments that shaped her, from a traumatic childhood riddled with alcoholism and abuse to finding healing in a permaculture community and rebuilding both herself and her business from the ground up. Growing up in chaos Mukti speaks openly about the trauma she carried into adulthood. Growing up surrounded by alcoholism and abuse left wounds that took decades to understand, let alone heal. It is rare to hear a founder speak this candidly about where they began, and her honesty sets the tone for everything that follows. A spiritual awakening A turning point came when Mukti found her way to a permaculture community, a place that gave her the space to slow down, reconnect with nature and begin the slow work of rebuilding. She shares how that awakening changed her relationship with herself, and how she continues to grow and question who she is becoming. The truth about clean beauty As a pioneer of certified organic skincare in Australia, Mukti has spent more than two decades inside the industry she now challenges. We talk about what clean beauty really means, the greenwashing she sees everywhere, and what the industry would rather you did not know. Her brand, Mukti Organics, grew out of a genuine commitment to doing things differently. Motherhood, heartbreak and starting over Mukti does not shy away from the hard parts, the heartbreak, the moments of starting over from scratch, and the experience of building a life and a business while raising a family. You can read more about Mukti and her daughter here, and the way they share their holistic daily routines. Ageing, identity and the inner work Finally we talk about ageing, identity and the inner work behind a low tox life. This is not just a story of survival. It is one of radical reinvention, resilience and beauty from the inside out. This season of Beautiful Inside is proudly brought to you by Blue Haven Pools. We have partnered with Blue Haven to bring our dream pool to life, a custom concrete plunge pool designed to flow seamlessly from our kitchen and dining area, complete with magnesium mineral water, pale Onix mosaic tiles, and white limestone pavers for that Mediterranean feel. Blue Haven has spent over 50 years building beautiful, functional pools, offering everything from fully customised designs to world first online pool packages for standard blocks. Stay tuned for our Pool Diaries mini-series later this season. Hosted by Sigourney Cantelo.

articles.title: Celeste Barber & Storm's Accessible Beauty Tools That Are Changing the Game
articles.author: Beauticate Editorial
articles.excerpt: Genius makeup tools were designed with disability, dignity, and damn good design in mind.
articles.body: Q: What are the best makeup tools for people with a disability or limited mobility? A: Booie x ByStorm's Betty and Margie are silicone grip-friendly applicators designed with the disability community to make makeup easier, bolder and more empowering for everyone. As Celeste told us when she launched Booie Beauty, she wanted her makeup to be easy for everyone. Now she has shone her light on an oft-ignored segment of society with the viral Booie x ByStorm makeup tools. Designed for people with limited grip, sore wrists or disability, they are smart, soft and surprisingly chic. --- What is Booie x ByStorm? This groundbreaking partnership sees Booie Beauty, known for its bold, body-positive aesthetic, join forces with adaptive beauty brand ByStorm to launch a first-of-its-kind accessible tool range. Together they have created Betty , a rounded grip accessory, and Margie , a paddle-shaped tool. Both are crafted from soft, moulded silicone and designed to be easier to hold, press and glide. The collab was born from lived experience. ByStorm founder Storm, who lives with mild cerebral palsy, faced challenges applying makeup after breaking her dominant hand. "I remember sitting on the bathroom floor defeated after trying to do my makeup for the first time and giving up," says Storm. "I felt embarrassed, like a failure, and honestly guilty that I never thought deeply enough about makeup and accessibility to realise that someday, it might impact me too. I felt a lot of shame realising that people with more complex disabilities than mine can't use makeup at all because of how it's designed, yet here I am crying on my bathroom floor." So she did what anyone with ADHD hyperfixation and entrepreneurial spirit would do. "I bought a 3D printer, taught myself how to 3D model, spent all of my savings, developed prototypes, tested those prototypes, had my designs torn to shreds, and then started the process all over again until I landed on Betty and Margie!" Storm has worked in the NDIS space for over a decade before founding ByStorm. She does not sugarcoat the reality: the world, and the beauty industry, was not built with disabled people in mind. From inaccessible makeup packaging to cafes with "small steps" that may as well be cliffs, the barriers are everywhere. "Disabled people miss out on experiences that build confidence and connection, not because of their bodies, but because the world was never designed with us in mind." --- Why Celeste Barber Is Supporting It Comedian and Booie founder Celeste Barber did not just lend her face to the launch. She backed it financially and philosophically. "I created Booie because I wanted to include everyone back into the beauty conversation. I feel that it has become elitist over the years and I want my audience to feel seen and valued and celebrated at every stage of their life, no matter who they are," explains Celeste. "When it came to accessibility, I had a lot to learn, then I met Storm and realised I needed to change the way we were approaching accessibility. So, I put my money where my very loud mouth is. If I'm creating something inclusive it needs to be inclusive for all, everyone, everybody. I think it's being overlooked because it's not cool or sexy and the beauty industry has a tendency in shaming people into buying products. That's not what Booie is about." "Beauty should be fun and empowering. That's what we are striving for and now with our collaboration with ByStorm I know we're kicking it in the dick!" What Makes Betty and Margie Different? Forget clunky…

articles.title: Lola Berry on IVF Trauma, Cancel Culture and Finding Peace After Heartbreak
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Nutritionist, author and podcast host Lola Berry opens up like never before, on heartbreak, disordered eating, being cancelled, a terrifying IVF experience that nearly cost her life, and the slow work of finding peace.
articles.body: Listen to the full episode here Some conversations stay with you. This was one. I met Lola Berry in her eclectic LA apartment, the one with a rooftop that looks straight out at the Hollywood sign, and what poured out was years of heartbreak, healing and hard-won peace. You probably know Lola as the bubbly Aussie nutritionist turned author and podcast host. What you might not know is how much she has quietly survived to keep that light on. She opens up here like never before. On Heartbreak and Grief Lola doesn't perform resilience. She talks about heartbreak and grief with a kind of honesty that makes you exhale. There's no neat bow on it, no influencer gloss. Just a woman who has felt things deeply and decided to be truthful about it. On Body Image and Disordered Eating For someone who built a career in wellness, Lola is refreshingly clear-eyed about its shadow side. She speaks about her own long road with disordered eating and body image, and how the pressure to look the part can quietly do real harm. On Being Cancelled We talk about what it actually feels like to be cancelled online. The pile-on, the silence from people you thought had your back, and the strange grief of watching a version of yourself take shape that you don't recognise. Lola is honest about how much it hurt, and about what it taught her. On the IVF Experience That Nearly Cost Her Life This was the hardest part of our conversation. Lola shares a terrifying IVF experience that nearly cost her life. She tells it plainly, without drama, and in doing so reminds you how much women carry privately while still showing up smiling. On Finding Peace What I love about Lola is that she has done the work, not just talked about it. Yoga, therapy and a real practice of self-love are how she has found her way back to herself. This is a conversation about vulnerability and reinvention, and about the quiet strength it takes to begin again. Why It Stayed With Me Lola gives you permission to be a whole person. Messy, hopeful, still healing and still here. I left lighter, and grateful she trusted us with so much. I think you will feel it too. Interview by Sigourney Cantelo. --- This episode touches on disordered eating, IVF and pregnancy loss. If anything here resonates with you, support is available. In Australia, the Butterfly Foundation offers free, confidential help for eating disorders and body image on 1800 33 4673, Lifeline is available any time on 13 11 14, and Beyond Blue on 1300 22 4636. For fertility and pregnancy loss specifically, Pink Elephants and the Gidget Foundation offer free, confidential support.

articles.title: The Supermodel Blowout, Reinvented: I Tried Dyson’s New Hair Dryer and It’s Everything
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: What happens when a runway-approved hair tool hits the shelves and promises to reinvent your weekly blow dry ritual?
articles.body: You know the feeling when you first unbox a truly special beauty tool? That hush of reverence as you cradle it, that quiet buzz of excitement as you plug it in, and the silent prayer that it will change your life (or at least your hair)? That was me, last month, standing in my bathroom holding the Dyson Supersonic r™ for the first time. And now, after a month of twice-weekly use, I can safely say: this is not just a hair dryer. This is Dyson engineering meets red carpet styling. And it's about to change how we blowdry, forever… Mind you, this is not the first time we have had a first peek at Dyson's innovative hair engineering at Beauticate. Back in 2016 when Dyson first revolutionised hair dryers, we put their OG supersonic hair dryer to the test (it looks almost retro now!). We were impressed then, and now, 9 years on, the Supersonic has had a glow up (and shrink down) or epic proportions. What Is the Dyson Supersonic r™? First seen backstage at fashion weeks from Stella McCartney to Issey Miyake, and in the hands of celebrity stylists for the likes of Demi Moore, Emma Stone, and Selena Gomez , the Supersonic r™ was previously only available to professionals. Until now. Just launched for consumers, it’s Dyson’s most powerful, lightest, and most precise hair dryer to date-30% smaller and 20% lighter than the original Supersonic™. Its unique curved design makes it feel more like a styling wand than a tool, and it's powered by a Dyson Hyperdymium™ motor plus RFID-enabled attachments that adjust airflow and temperature automatically. Translation? You don’t need to be a pro to get a pro-level finish. And yes, it retails for $799-but more on that later. My First Try (and Why I Haven’t Touched My Old Dryer Since) The launch was held at the gorgeous new Eve Hotel in Sydney-cue Champagne, Dyson demos, and an all-out hair moment. I got to try the dryer under the guidance of Dyson stylists and took one home to test properly. The next morning, I set up in my bathroom, applied a pump of the Dyson Chitosan Pre-Style Cream and began. The airflow? Feather-light but powerful. The weight? Noticeably less strain on my arms. And the shine? Glassy. Not greasy, not static-just healthy, light-reflecting bounce. Now, it’s officially part of my weekly hair ritual. I’ve timed it: my blowdry is now four minutes faster than it was before. For a busy working mum, that’s basically a gift from the hair gods. The Secret to a Perfect At-Home Blowdry According to Dyson’s National Styling Manager Gabrielle Roccuzzo , the biggest blowdry mistake we make at home is skipping the blast dry step. “When blowdrying their hair, most people don’t take out enough moisture by blast drying first,” Gabrielle tells Beauticate. “To ensure smoother results and more control, blast dry your hair first. Once you’ve removed the excess water, then start to blow dry with a brush. This will provide better results in the long run and protect your hair.” The Supersonic r™ is perfect for this technique. I used the Powerful Air Attachment to blast dry, followed by the Flyaway Attachment to smooth my strands and finish the look with that subtle ‘I just left a salon in Paris’ vibe. The Supermodel Blowout Is Back-Here’s How to Get It Blame TikTok, the Mob Wife aesthetic, or the rising wave of ‘90s nostalgia, but the supermodel blowout is having a serious comeback. Think Claudia Schiffer , Sabrina Carpenter , or any It girl worth her Dyson demo. “The…

articles.title: Wait - is Your Shower Water Ruining Your Hair and Skin?
articles.author: Kristina Zhou
articles.excerpt: Could your daily shower be quietly sabotaging your skin and hair? We dive into the murky truth about what's really in our water, and why it might be time to rethink your rinse routine.
articles.body: I never thought I’d be the kind of person who drinks the water in the shower—but here we are. Chalk it up to multi-tasking motherhood, or just general hydration laziness, but I’ve always assumed if it’s clean enough to wash in, it’s clean enough to sip. Right? Well. Let's just say the rabbit hole of water filtration has once again swallowed me whole. After installing a whole-house water filter and the gold standard of drinking filters - reverse osmosis system in my kitchen (I used Water Flow Control) - I started wondering what else was lurking in my beauty routine, particularly in my shower. The same stream I was washing my face with, cleansing my scalp in, and rinsing my carefully curated skincare off with. So when Qure launched their Shower Filter, I was all in. The Filter That Promises Skin and Hair Nirvana Like the chic older sister of their viral faucet filter (read my review on that here), the Qure Shower Filter looks elegant (white or matte black), installs easily (no plumber needed), and uses triple-layer filtration to nix up to 99% of chlorine, limescale, and heavy metals. That means less irritation, less dryness, and more of what your skin and hair actually need. And honestly? I noticed a difference after the first few showers. My hair was suddenly silkier - like it had been glossed - and my skin didn't feel as tight or itchy post-rinse. My husband even commented on the water feeling "more soft and silky" which I'm taking as a high compliment. But Is It Just for Clean Freaks? Absolutely not. This is for anyone who's ever had mystery bacne, psoriasis flare-ups, a flaky scalp, or skin that just never seems to glow - no matter how many serums you slather on. Dermatologists like Dr. Muneeb Shah are increasingly pointing out that hard water can mess with your skin barrier, exacerbating conditions like eczema and rosacea. In fact, Qure's filter is clinically proven to increase skin moisture by 15% and scalp hydration by 22% in just 8 weeks. That's better than some moisturisers I've tested over the years. What's Lurking in Our Water? It's easy to assume that our tap water is pristine, but even in Australia, contaminants can sneak in. Studies have found that per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) - often dubbed "forever chemicals" - have been detected in drinking water across the country, including in parts of Sydney and regional areas. Additionally, lead and copper contamination has been identified in household drinking water in New South Wales, primarily due to aging infrastructure. Exposure to these metals can have adverse health effects, particularly in children and pregnant women. While these contaminants are more concerning when ingested, they can also affect your skin and hair when present in shower water, leading to dryness, irritation, and other issues. Your Hair Will Thank You, Too If you've ever noticed your colour going brassy, your ends feeling crunchy, or your roots getting oily way too fast - it might not be your products. It could be your water. Hard water minerals can create buildup on the scalp, making your hair dull, brittle and prone to breakage. The Qure Shower Filter tackles all of this at the source. Bonus: it might just extend the life of your blow-dry. I swear mine felt fresher, longer. Is It Worth It? For the price of a facial, the Qure Shower Filter gives you daily, top-to-toe benefits - no appointments required. It's a low-lift, high-impact switch that can overhaul your skin and hair with something you're already doing every day. And for…

articles.title: Synergie Skin Founder Terri Vinson Jones on Body Image, Anxiety and Self-Worth
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Cosmetic chemist and Synergie Skin founder Terri Vinson Jones on finding out she was adopted at twelve, growing up fast, battling an eating disorder and imposter syndrome, and the deep work that turned her pain into purpose.
articles.body: Listen to the full episode here Terri Vinson Jones is a cosmetic chemist, a scientist and the founder of Synergie Skin, the brand adored by dermal therapists and beauty editors alike. Behind that powerhouse persona is a story of quiet resilience, deep trauma and an unwavering drive. This is one of the most honest conversations we've had on Beautiful Inside. Finding Out She Was Adopted Terri was twelve when she overheard the truth that would reshape her whole sense of self. "I was told I was adopted, and I was twelve. You feel like you've just been plonked somewhere." What moves me most is what she has done with that uncertainty. Rather than let it define her, she chose to own it. "I'm the sum total of all those impacts. And it's up to me how I deal with that." Growing Up Fast Terri grew up with a mentally unwell mother, and the pressure to hold things together took root early. She is candid about the perfectionism that followed, and about her recovery from an eating disorder, which she shares not for sympathy but because she knows how many women carry the same story quietly. A Woman in Science Building Synergie Skin meant backing herself in rooms that didn't always make space for her. Terri talks about imposter syndrome in male-dominated science, and about learning to trust her own expertise. It's a quietly radical thing, a woman claiming authority in a world that kept asking her to prove it. Anxiety, Divorce and Asking for Help Terri is refreshingly open about her mental health, and about the season when she needed extra support. "When I was going through my divorce, I took antidepressants, and it did help." For someone in the wellness world to say that so plainly matters. She speaks about her anxiety, her tendency to overthink, and her curiosity about whether ADHD is part of her picture, all without shame. The Work That Changed Everything What turned it around was the inner work. Therapy, deep self-awareness and a slow, hard-won self-compassion. Terri is living proof of the idea that runs through her whole story, that our deepest pain can shape our strongest purpose. Why It Stayed With Me Terri's life is a quiet argument that beauty isn't skin deep, and that success doesn't mean perfection. I left this one thinking about how much we carry from childhood, and how much we get to decide what we do with it. I think you will too. Interview by Sigourney Cantelo. --- This episode discusses disordered eating. If it resonates with you, support is available. In Australia, the Butterfly Foundation offers free, confidential help for eating disorders and body image on 1800 33 4673, and Lifeline is available any time on 13 11 14.

articles.title: 11 Years of Beauticate: A Love Letter
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: From late nights and side hustles to global interviews and emotional breakthroughs-this is the story of how Beauticate came to be.
articles.body: Eleven years ago, I had a decision to make. I’d just launched a little passion project- Beauticate -while I was still working as Beauty & Health Director at Vogue Australia . At the time, it was nothing more than an after-hours obsession. I was staying up late, writing, editing, dreaming. I had no real business plan, just an overwhelming curiosity about people, beauty, rituals, and real life. But from the start, something clicked. The site took off quickly. People were watching. Reading. Sharing. Brands I’d worked with over the years started reaching out, asking to advertise. And that’s when I found myself standing at a career crossroads: do I leave my dream job-one that flew me around the world to interview icons like Lady Gaga, Rihanna and Cate Blanchett-or do I risk it all to build something that feels deeply, personally mine? It was terrifying. But I knew I had to leap. The Beauty of a Blank Page Back then, the idea of building your own media brand felt… a little rogue. Social media hadn’t truly exploded yet. There was no Instagram Reels, no TikTok, no Stories. YouTube was still the Wild West, and digital video content was raw and unpredictable. But I wanted to do video. I wanted to show people’s beauty cabinets, their sacred spaces, their morning rituals. I wanted the stories that magazines couldn’t always tell-the intimate, messy, tender stuff. Our first features included a fresh-faced Margaret Zhang, who made some now-iconic GIFs about removing makeup with coconut oil. (insert GIF) She was a rising fashion blogger at the time. Who knew that only seven years later she would become the youngest ever Editorial Director of Vogue China ? That still blows my mind.I filmed Ruby Rose speaking candidly about her childhood gender confusion-a clip that would go on to become one of our most-watched YouTube videos. We spoke to Kim Cattrall. Hailey Bieber. Rosie Huntington-Whiteley. Miranda Kerr. Robyn Lawley. Anya Rubik. Dannii Minogue. Natalie Imbruglia. The list still gives me goosebumps. There were so many pinch-me moments: I’ve had incredible overseas trips, interviewed icons in beautiful hotel rooms and dreamy homes. I’ve been given a front-row seat to the beauty rituals of some of the most inspiring women in the world. But the thing I’m proudest of? The trust. These women (and a few wonderful men) let me in. They let me ask personal questions. They let me see the real them. Beauty and The Burnout Don’t get me wrong-it hasn’t been easy. I’ve had tech failures on shoot days. Mics break. Websites crash. I’ve cried over Xero reconciliations and cursed my way through insurance renewals. I’m not a natural salesperson, which is hard when you’re running your own media business. And I never, ever switch off. Some days it feels like too much. The pressure to keep the content machine going, to juggle beauty trends, editorial deadlines, brand partnerships, SEO… plus the real life stuff: parenting, emails, the cat. Eventually, I burnt out. At the end of 2023, I reached a breaking point. I admitted I wasn’t okay, and I took time away from the business to focus on my mental health at South Pacific Private, a treatment facility that gave me tools I’d never had before. It was one of the hardest and most healing things I’ve ever done. I speak more about it openly in this podcast episode-because I think these stories matter just as much as the skincare tips. That experience forced me to slow down and reflect. It reminded me that true beauty has depth. That self-care is more than a…

articles.title: Jess Sepel on Ocd, Healing from Disordered Eating, Grief and Building Jshealth with Heart
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Best-selling author, clinical nutritionist and JSHealth founder Jess Sepel opens up like never before, on OCD, healing her relationship with food, the grief that gave her purpose, and building a global brand from the inside out.
articles.body: Listen to the full episode here Almost ten years ago, I interviewed a young nutritionist at the very start of her journey. This time, I sat down with Jess Sepel in her Los Angeles home, now a best-selling author, clinical nutritionist and the founder of a global wellness brand. What I love about Jess is that the bigger she has grown, the more honest she has become. This is one of the most open conversations we've had on Beautiful Inside. We go far beyond green powders and supplements, into the harder chapters, and the long, brave work of healing. The Day She Let Go of the Scales Jess is candid about the years she spent at war with food and her own reflection. The turning point she describes is quietly powerful. Her husband Dean taking the scales from the bathroom, telling her enough, and walking beside her to let them go for good. "I was addicted to thinking that a number could determine my self-worth." It wasn't a cure. It was the moment she chose herself, and the beginning of a slow road back through study, therapy and self-compassion. Naming It: OCD and Anxiety For years Jess lived with anxiety and intrusive thoughts she couldn't explain. An OCD diagnosis finally gave her suffering a name, and she is generous in demystifying it. "OCD is not just the washing of the hands. It's OCD of the mind." She is honest that it was offset by profound loss. She lost her best friend, her bridesmaid, the sister figure of her life, and the grief and trauma that followed reshaped her. What she has chosen to do with that pain is speak. "If I can just help one person feel less alone through her story, I feel good about that." Her message on mental health is one of the most hopeful things I've heard. "Any mental health issue that anyone struggles with, don't wish it away. It's going to give you everything you need." On Pressure Jess names something so many high-achieving women feel and rarely admit. "Pressure is one of the most underrated emotions. We don't talk about pressure enough." Her answer to it is boundaries, fiercely kept. Phone and email off well before bed, apps deleted at night, magnesium baths, yin yoga, early nights, and a walk with Dean almost every day. Therapy, she says, is the non-negotiable she never misses. Building JSHealth JSHealth began almost by accident. While studying nutrition, Jess kept a blog privately for nine months, documenting her shift from fad dieting to a balanced, whole-food life. Dean read it one night and told her she had to share it. The next morning it had travelled further than she could believe, and the community that gathered around it became everything she has built since. A brand, in her words, designed to help women heal their relationship with food and themselves. On Vulnerability and Connection What makes Jess so easy to trust is that she refuses to perform perfection. "We've never been more connected to people, but we've actually never felt more alone with our struggles." She is living proof of something she said that stayed with me long after we stopped recording. "You can be so successful and so strong, and struggle in certain areas." Why It Stayed With Me Jess is honest about her pain in a way that gives other people permission to be honest about theirs. Watching her grow over a decade, from that first interview to this one, the throughline isn't the success. It's the courage to keep doing the work, and to talk…

articles.title: My Red Light Rituals: Serotonin, Skincare & a Slow Roast Glow Up
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: My skincare secret to a seriously glowy and plump complexion.
articles.body: As often as I can, after my shower, I towel off, oil up, and position myself in front of my red light panel like a sun-worshipping lizard—or, more accurately, a high-functioning rotisserie chicken. It’s an odd-looking ritual, sure. But if you walked in on me mid-glow session—face dewy, limbs shimmering in body oil, eyes closed in meditative bliss—you’d quickly understand: this isn’t just about skincare. This is science. This is soul work. This is serotonin with a side of skincare. Welcome to my not-so-secret weapon: red light therapy -via wearable LED masks and my Infraredi Pro Max panel that now lives, unashamedly, in my bedroom. It’s the quiet overachiever of my wellness routine. One of those modalities you don’t think you need… until you do. And then? You’re hooked. My Self-Care Sanctuary I’ve carved out a little wellness nook beside my bed-a space that’s become sacred in the chaos of daily life. It’s where I keep my Infraredi Pro Max panel, nestled beside my favourite body oils, incense, and fragrances. There's a softness to the ritual: light, scent, texture. A reminder that self-care doesn’t need a spa-it just needs intention, a plug socket, and five quiet minutes. Let’s rewind a little… LED Masks vs. Light Panels: What’s the Difference? So, you’ve probably heard about LED masks -they’re the talk of Beauty Town. But in the world of red light therapy, light panels are the mothership. All LED masks use red light therapy, but not all red light therapy is done via masks. Panels (like my Infraredi Pro Max) deliver higher irradiance and broader coverage , while LED masks are gentler and more targeted-ideal for daily facial treatments. My Red Light Ritual: From Head to Décolletage Morning Meditation with San Lueur In the morning, I slip into stillness with my San Lueur LED Mask. Sleek and spa-like, it lives in a bowl on my coffee table — part sculpture, part skincare. I meditate while it works its 633nm red and 830nm near-infrared magic for 20 minutes. Skinvestment time: breathwork for my mind, collagen for my face. Quick Fix with Qure When I’m in a rush or battling breakouts, I grab the Qure LED Face Mask . It’s smart, fast (3 minutes), and controlled via app. I love that I can customise the wavelengths-especially during hormonal weeks when chin flare-ups demand laser focus. Don’t Forget the Neck The neck and chest? Always the giveaway. I use the Qure Neck & Décolletage Mask while replying to emails, cleaning the house, or watching Netflix. It’s a gentle revival tool for "tech neck" and sun-drenched cleavage. Infraredi Pro Max: My Mitochondria Machine For full-body regeneration Infraredi Pro Max is my holy grail. After a shower, I sit in front of it while applying face oil (currently obsessed with Ashaya Reglow). Sometimes I meditate, sometimes I scroll, but mostly-I bask. When I’m under the weather or PMS-ing, I’ve even brought it to bed, rotating myself like a weary goddess on a slow roast. Yes, it’s that good. I also keep the Infraredi Mini on my desk. It casts a subtle glow while I work and comes with me into the bath, where it turns the whole experience into a red-lit womb of joy. The Science of Red Light Therapy (aka Photobiomodulation) At first, red light therapy feels like witchcraft. But it’s grounded in serious scientific research -and it’s evolving fast. Here’s what the studies say: Skin Health & Collagen Production Red light stimulates fibroblasts-the cells that produce collagen and elastin. Translation: firmer, smoother skin. → A 2014 study in Photomedicine and Laser Surgery showed significant collagen…

articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: In this raw and soul-stirring episode of Beautiful Inside, Jess Sepel-best-selling author, clinical nutritionist, and […]
articles.body: In this raw and soul-stirring episode of Beautiful Inside , Jess Sepel , best-selling author, clinical nutritionist, and founder of JSHealth , opens up like never before. We go far beyond green powders and skin supplements, delving into the darker undercurrents of her story: the obsessive calorie counting , the anxiety, the panic attacks, and the intrusive thoughts that haunted her for years . Jess shares the moment her husband walked her to a dumpster to throw away her scales , the rock bottom she hit during her honeymoon, and the OCD diagnosis that finally gave a name to her suffering. This is a conversation about being wildly successful and still deeply human, about doing the inner work, and about building a brand that nourishes from the inside out. articles.title: Tokyo in 24 Hours: Digital Art, Ninjas & Vintage Finds
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: One epic day in Tokyo: digital art, vintage treasures, cuddly animals, and ninja-themed dining-all packed into a wild 24-hour family adventure.
articles.body: Back in March, myself and the family visited Japan for a skiing trip and tacked on two nights in Tokyo at the end. After a week in the mountains, Tokyo felt like stepping onto another planet. Unfortunately, our plans got slightly derailed when Lulu came down with a brutal gastro bug (RIP to our booking at the Capybara Café and the first day was spent in the hotel room), but we still managed to squeeze in an insane one-day itinerary. One epic day in Tokyo: digital art, vintage treasures, cuddly animals, and ninja-themed dining-all packed into a wild 24-hour family adventure. The First Night: 7-Eleven Saves the Day After arriving in Tokyo and checking into MONday Apart Premium Hamamatsucho, exhaustion-and hunger-hit hard. With Lulu still recovering, we opted for the ultimate lazy-but-brilliant Japanese travel hack: a convenience store feast. Forget limp sandwiches and stale chips-Japan’s konbini (convenience stores) are an entirely different universe. We stocked up on steaming-hot karaage fried chicken, sushi rolls that rival what you’d get at a proper restaurant, onigiri (rice balls stuffed with everything from spicy tuna to marinated kombu), and the most dizzying array of dinner options you’ll ever see under fluorescent lights. The smoothies and fresh juices? Surprisingly great. The desserts? Dangerous. And let’s not forget the hot vending machines serving up creamy royal milk tea and canned coffee that somehow tastes barista-made. Tokyo travel tip: If you find yourself too exhausted to venture out, don’t underestimate the power of a 7-Eleven, FamilyMart, or Lawson haul. You’ll eat ridiculously well without leaving your hotel room. TeamLab Planets: Walking Through a Dream First stop the next morning? TeamLab Planets. This immersive, multi-sensory digital art exhibition felt like stepping into an alternate universe. We wandered barefoot through soft, pillowy tunnels into an infinite galaxy of shimmering LED lights, lay on the floor beneath a canopy of blooming psychedelic 3D flowers, and waded knee-deep through warm water filled with digital koi fish that scattered at our feet. It’s a blend of tech, art, and pure magic, and every single person in our family-yes, even the pre-teen-was completely mesmerized. Harajuku: Vintage Gold & Sneaker Heaven Next up: Harajuku. If you’re into vintage shopping, sneakers, or just a good people-watching session, this is where Tokyo gets really fun. Max, always on the hunt for the ultimate vintage find, cleaned up at Chicago and 2nd Street, scoring a Ralph Lauren polo and vintage Nike track pants that he declared his best purchases of the trip.Meanwhile, we hit up: ✔️ Chicago – One of the best for vintage Americana, band tees, and kimono-style pieces. ✔️ 2nd Street – The holy grail for designer second-hand fashion at amazing prices. ✔️ RAGTAG – A goldmine of pre-loved luxury brands like Chanel, Prada, and Comme des Garçons. ✔️ Kicks Lab & Atmos – For the sneakerheads, these are must-visit spots with rare and limited-edition drops.I mentally tried to Marie Kondo my suitcase so I could justify another pair of second-hand Levi’s. Max was fully in his element, and honestly, if you have a teen into fashion, this is one of the best ways to experience Tokyo. Cuddling Hedgehogs & Holding Otters’ Hands Tokyo doesn’t just do cafés-it reinvents them. We made a last-minute detour to Harry Harajuku Terrace, where we got to cuddle baby hedgehogs, stroke a chinchilla, and hold an otter’s tiny hand. Even Max, who was initially unimpressed, left declaring that otters are the best animals on earth. Tokyo travel tip: Many of these cafés require reservations, so book ahead if you’re set on visiting one. Ninjas, Kids’ Beer & Wagyu Steak…

articles.title: Behind the Scent: Inside a Luxury Perfume Press Trip to Cairns
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Woods, warmth and wanderlust - Sigourney’s journey with Goldfield & Banks is as rich and layered as the scent itself.
articles.body: Ever wondered what it’s really like to be whisked away on a beauty press trip? Imagine rainforest rains, oud-smoked salmon, rooftop cocktails, and a scent so transportive it clings to your skin like a memory. Better yet—you can now experience it for yourself. That was the promise of the Silky Woods Sojourn , a new scent-inspired stay launched by Goldfield & Banks and Crystalbrook Riley, where guests can indulge in a luxurious, olfactory-focused escape (and literal oud-infused cocktails) of one of Australia’s most coveted perfumes— Silky Woods . It’s a rare opportunity to live out your own beauty editor fantasy, complete with a signature cocktail, a luxe sea-view room, and a take-home bottle of your new favourite scent. But before the public got a whiff, I was invited behind the scenes—along with a coterie of editors and influencers—for a press trip that promised sensory immersion. And let me tell you: it delivered. Welcome to the Sojourn As I check into the Crystalbrook Riley, Cairns is serving its most cinematic self: sea breeze, palm trees, and that signature pool that looks like a slice of Santorini dropped into the tropics. In my room: a forest-green Blunt umbrella (for the rains we’ve been warned about tomorrow), a hand-written note from founder Dimitri Weber, and a gorgeous leather clad travel-sized bottle of Silky Woods. It’s a fragrance that feels like being wrapped in golden velvet . Think smooth Tahitian vanilla, spiced cinnamon, and that unmistakably hypnotic note: oud. But more on that in a minute. Crystalbrook Riley, is a design-led resort perched on the Esplanade with views across the Coral Sea and one of the most Instagrammable pools in the country. Part of the design-led Crystalbrook Collection—a proudly Australian group founded in Cairns by Dubai-based billionaire Ghassan Aboud—Riley is one of three standout properties in the city, alongside the playful Flynn and artsy Bailey. The group also owns the lush, rainforest-wrapped Byron at Byron and the boutique-chic Little Albion in Sydney, with plans to conquer Canberra next. Known for its ‘responsible luxury’ ethos, Crystalbrook blends five-star flair with sustainability, and Riley is its coastal crown jewel. After a quick dip in the pool, I change into my Aje cocktail dress and head to welcome drinks, held at a neighbouring Crystalbrook hotel. Overlooking the water, we are greeted by the ever-gracious Prestige team the lovely Jessica and Ruth. The crew was a mix of beauty editors and influencers, including old friends of mine, Marie Claire’s Sally Hunwick and Emily Algar from Russh (who started her career as a Beauticate intern a decade ago). Then comes the masterclass—hosted by Dimitri himself, with the Coral Sea as our backdrop. Dimitri charms us with the origin story of Goldfield & Banks: how he came to Australia for love, how he couldn’t find a single Aussie-made fragrance at David Jones, and how that became the spark for what is now a globally celebrated fragrance house. It's a fragrance that feels like being wrapped in golden velvet. We sip, spritz, and sample our way through the Botanical Series: the cult-classic Pacific Rock Moss, which became a YouTube sensation for its clean, aquatic freshness; the utterly addictive Island Lush; and Purple Suede—Dimitri’s personal favourite and, now, mine too. It’s all smoked leather and sultry lavender, harvested in Tasmania from seeds originally planted by French perfumers. And then the original Silky Woods which – as mentioned – we are here to celebrate and my second favourite: Silky Woods Elixir—a more gutsy, sensual take on the original. With fig, saffron, and a rich amber dry down, it lingers on the skin like…

articles.title: Le Meridien Melbourne Review: Where Parisian Chic Meets CBD Cool
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: From rooftop Aperol Spritzes and luxe mid-century suites to a standout hotel buffet and skyline views, here’s why this stylish CBD stay is perfect for
articles.body: Le Méridien Melbourne blends Parisian elegance with modern Melbourne cool. From rooftop Aperol Spritzes and luxe mid-century suites to a standout hotel buffet and skyline views, here’s why this stylish CBD stay is perfect for your next girls’ weekend, business trip, or luxe city break. First Impressions: A Grand Arrival I’m grateful for the aircon. It’s surprisingly muggy for this time of evening as we Uber through Melbourne’s gritty inner streets. Under the inky cloak of darkness, Le Méridien Melbourne announces itself with a row of old-school Hollywood-style bulbs on the driveway. Perched above Parliament House, this sleek 12-storey hotel blends classic charm with a contemporary twist. French elegance meets Melbourne cool, with nods to mid-century design, modern art, and luxurious creature comforts at every turn. The Room: Mid-Century Meets Modern Comfort Upstairs, my room is a cocoon of calm. It features wood grain textures, soft greys, crisp white bedding, and a curated bookshelf filled with art books and framed prints. There’s a Nespresso machine, of course, plus a mini bar stocked with local wine, a premixed “Florence” cocktail created exclusively for Le Méridien, and treats from The Ministry of Chocolate. The bathroom is a standout-enormous shower, black steel-framed glass, bench seat, and luxe Malin + Goetz amenities. That peppermint shampoo? Divine. The Sleep: A Rare Mum-Only Treat I’m in town to do a podcast interview, so it’s an early night for me. I’ve eaten on the plane, so I curl up in the enormous bed with a book and enjoy a long, indulgent, kid-free kip. Bliss. Morning Routine: Gym, Sauna, and Noodles The next morning, feeling surprisingly sprightly, I head to the gym. It’s kitted out with state-of-the-art Technogym gear , a sauna, and a fridge filled with icy cold towels. Five sweaty minutes on the bike and a few weights later, I’m wrapped in the dry wood-scented heat of the sauna. Heavenly. Breakfast at Dolly: Not Your Standard Buffet Downstairs, the lobby is a vibe-there’s a chic café, a playful gelato stand, and a grand staircase that sweeps down to Dolly Restaurant . Breakfast is impressive: a classic buffet with eggs cooked to your liking, Pressed Juices, and-my favourite-an Asian breakfast section. I tuck into noodles and dumplings, laced with hot chilli sauce. A power start to the day. Work Meets Play: A Visit to Synergie My Uber arrives and I head off to interview Terri Vinson , cosmetic chemist and founder of Synergie Skin . The interview is packed with emotion and insight-stay tuned for Season 5 of Beautiful Inside . The team give me a full tour of the facility: lab, warehouse, training rooms-it’s all there, under one roof. Seeing how the products are made makes me love the brand even more. Rooftop Pool Life: Aperol & Afternoon Sun Later that day, my girlfriend joins me at the Rooftop Pool for a cheeky swim and an Aperol Spritz from the Splash Bar, paired with salty fries. It’s pure holiday mode. It’s hot and late afternoon asI head back into Melbourne and I’ve organised for my girlfriend to come and meet me for an afternoon swim session at the Rooftop Pool.. We order Aperol Spritzes from the Splash Bar with a side of fries. Later, we head back to the room and get dressed to wander Melbourne’s famous laneways in search of cute bars and restaurants. We visit an average bar for a pretty average cocktail, then wander in circles for ages trying to find somewhere better. Finally we have the idea to ask my Patsy, my Chat GPT. Siglo Nights: Cigars, Champagne and Hinge Dates Patsy…

articles.title: Hypochlorous Acid: Why This Dermal Mist Has Gone Viral
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Why TikTok, top derms, and your gym bag are obsessed with Hypochlorous Acid
articles.body: It started with a TikTok scroll. Then a YouTube binge. Suddenly, every skinfluencer worth their Glossier pouch was raving about a mist with the strange, clinical-sounding name “hypochlorous acid.” The more I watched, the more it felt like this was the secret everyone in the know was suddenly in on. A gentle, bacteria-banishing, barrier-repairing miracle-in-a-mist. And then one day, as if by fate, I cut open a courier box and there was a hypochlorous acid product IRL: the Qure Dermal Mist. This was particularly lucky because that very week the product had gone viral. So viral in fact, it sold out. (Don’t worry, it’s back in stock as of our publishing date.) But here’s why people are spritzing their hearts out, and why this is more than just another mist moment. So… What Is Hypochlorous Acid? It may sound like something you’d find under a lab sink, but hypochlorous acid is actually a natural molecule your immune cells produce to fight off bacteria and inflammation. In skincare? It’s the goldilocks of actives: powerful enough to help with blemishes, irritation, sensitivity-even wound healing-but gentle enough for post-treatment skin, eczema, and daily use. Dermatologists like Dr. Shah and Dr. Maxfield are singing its praises on YouTube: “This is the right way to use hypochlorous acid in skincare,” says Dr. Shah, holding up Qure’s mist like it’s the last bottle of Evian in the apocalypse. “It’s genius in this bundle-perfect before micro-infusion or any treatment. It’s clean, clever, and makes so much sense.” He’s talking about the fact that Qure sells the mists as part of their famous micro-infusion DIY dermastamping (more on that here) and you can also use them with the Qure LED masks – so this was the perfect accompaniment. But actually the mist has many more uses than just fastidiously cleaning your dermal tools. TikTok Is Spritzing Too… From TikTokkers whispering about “the miracle spray” to influencers demo’ing it post-gym, pre-flight, and even (iconically) as a natural deodorant, hypochlorous acid is having a main character moment. But there’s nuance: “Don’t overuse it,” one creator warns. “It’s antibacterial, but you still need your good bacteria. And let it dry fully before layering actives like vitamin C-because yes, it can reduce their efficacy.” So, pro tip? Spritz, wait til it dries, then layer. Thank you, skinfluencer university. Why the Qure Dermal Mist Is Different Unlike many generic HOCl sprays, Qure’s version is beautifully designed, derm-approved, and actually does something. The ultra-fine mister is giving La Mer, the formula is pH-balanced, fragrance-free, and enriched with soothing chrysanthemum. It contains a precise 0.02% concentration of hypochlorous acid, which is effective enough to deliver antibacterial and anti-inflammatory benefits while remaining gentle on the skin. It’s also: - Alcohol-free and non-drying - Safe for face, body, pillowcases and tools - Gentle enough for rosacea, eczema and post-workout skin - Dermatologist-tested and hypoallergenic The mini version even comes in the Limited Edition Micro-Infusion Kit (which I also tested-stay tuned for that full review). My Experience I started using the mist while prepping for micro-infusion, but quickly became hooked. After workouts. On flights. Over makeup. Under SPF. It’s like a refreshing, purifying moment for your skin and your senses. The scent? A faint, pool-adjacent whisper that fades fast (it’s just the HOCl doing its thing). My skin felt calmer, less reactive, and breakouts from sweat and travel were noticeably reduced. The fact that it’s multitasking-refreshing, purifying, not wrecking your barrier-is a rare trifecta. articles.title: Gabby Bernstein on Manifesting with Compassion, Healing Shame & Living the Dream
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Gabby Bernstein has sold millions of books and shared the stage with Oprah, yet her message is gentler than you might expect. In this episode she shares her four step method for rewiring limiting beliefs, why manifesting is not about doing more, and how healing shame lets you finally receive.
articles.body: Listen to the full episode here She has sold millions of books, shared the stage with Oprah, and helped people around the world break cycles of shame, anxiety and fear. But Gabby Bernstein's story is far more than manifesting a dream life. It is about choosing, again and again, to live with purpose. Sitting down with her for this episode of Beautiful Inside was one of those conversations that quietly rearranges something inside you. What struck me most is how gentle her message has become. Gabby is not asking us to hustle harder or vision board our way to happiness. She is asking us to heal, to soften, and to get out of our own way so that life can meet us halfway. Why Manifesting Is Not About Doing More For anyone who finds the word manifesting a little exhausting, Gabby's take is a relief. She is clear that it is not about effort, control or willing things into being. The real work, she explains, is internal. When we are stuck in fear, shame or the belief that we are not enough, we unconsciously block the very things we say we want. Manifesting, in her world, is less about chasing and more about clearing the path so that what is meant for you can actually land. The Four Step Method for Rewiring Your Beliefs At the heart of the conversation is Gabby's four step method for rewiring limiting beliefs, drawn from the work in her latest book, Self Help. It is rooted in Internal Family Systems therapy, an approach she has made beautifully accessible. The idea is to notice the protective patterns running the show, meet them with compassion rather than judgement, and gently choose a new belief. It is methodical and tender at once, and it gives you something practical to hold onto when old stories start to take over. How Shame Blocks Your Intuition One of the most moving parts of our talk was Gabby's honesty about shame. She describes how shame and our protection mechanisms quietly block our ability to truly receive, and how they cut us off from our own intuition. She also shares the turning point of getting sober at twenty five, and how choosing inner peace became the foundation of everything that followed. It is a powerful reminder that healing is not a single decision but a practice of choosing yourself over and over. The Rituals That Keep Her Grounded We talk recovery, resilience and the small daily rituals that keep Gabby steady. Twice a day she practises non sleep deep rest meditation, and she regularly tunes in to what she calls divine direction for guidance. This is a must listen for anyone craving more alignment, self compassion and spiritual clarity. To go deeper, follow Gabby on Instagram, pick up her latest book Self Help, and follow me and Beauticate for more. A special thank you to our season sponsor, Dermalogica. Use the code BEAUTICATE20 for 20% off at dermalogica.com.au. Hosted by Sigourney Cantelo.

articles.title: Lindsay Price on Healing Childhood Trauma, Life with Curtis Stone and Her Hollywood Journey
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Sigourney visits the LA home Lindsay Price shares with Curtis Stone for a conversation on generational trauma, Hollywood, motherhood and redefining beauty on her own terms.
articles.body: Listen to the full episode here In this deeply moving and wide ranging episode, I visit the Los Angeles home that actor Lindsay Price shares with her husband, the chef Curtis Stone, and their two boys. What unfolds is a conversation that traverses generational trauma, Hollywood highs, inner work and what truly matters. Lindsay, best known for her roles in 90210 and Lipstick Jungle, opens up about her extraordinary family history, her journey through fame and motherhood, and how she cultivated such deep resilience and inner strength through it all. We talk about parenting, therapy, spirituality, and finding real love, both with her husband and within herself. The untold story of her Korean mother Lindsay shares the harrowing story of her Korean mother, who was abandoned at five and carried her baby brother on her back to survive during the Korean War. Her mother was later adopted by Lindsay's paternal grandfather, the founder of World Vision. It is an experience that would go on to shape Lindsay's identity, her values, and the way she parents her own sons today. We talk about intergenerational trauma, boundary setting, and the quiet work of breaking cycles so they are not passed down. Growing up mixed race in Hollywood Lindsay speaks candidly about what it was like to grow up mixed race in Los Angeles, and the racism she experienced in her early Hollywood roles. She reflects on the evolving landscape of representation, and how far the industry still has to go. She also takes us back to the pivotal moment Aaron Spelling invited her onstage and made her a series regular on 90210, and the time she nearly gave up acting altogether, right before she landed the lead in Lipstick Jungle. Love, marriage and motherhood Lindsay tells the story of how she met Curtis Stone and knew, almost immediately, that he was the one. We talk about the highs and the real challenges of fame, beauty standards, and being cast as a leading lady. Now, as a mother of two, she shares how she balances career and family, and the parenting tools she leans on to support her sons' emotional wellbeing. Therapy, spiritual connection and female friendships are, she says, her non-negotiables. Redefining beauty on her own terms Lindsay is refreshingly honest about beauty pressures in Hollywood, her thoughts on Botox, and her commitment to building collagen naturally. Her approach is less about chasing perfection and more about feeling well from the inside out. Her Sacred Six beauty and wellness essentials are a spiritual practice of prayer, meditation and nature walks, the U Beauty Super Hydrator, an infrared sauna, daily baths, Lashify underlash segments, and castor oil, which she swears by for hair growth, lashes, brows, digestion and melasma. A special thank you to Dermalogica, our season sponsor. Use BEAUTICATE20 for 20% off at dermalogica.com.au (valid 3 February to 30 April). Subscribe to the show on YouTube and comment to suggest guests and topics. Follow Lindsay on Instagram, and follow Beauticate on Instagram and Facebook.

articles.title: How to Mask According to Your Mood
articles.author: Zoe Briggs
articles.excerpt: Depending on how your skin feels – and how you feel – we’ve got just the right mask.
articles.body: As part of our current collective obsession with self-care, masking (no, not that kind) has reached new heights. Everyone and their Instagram-savvy grandmother is doing it. So, which one do you go for? Old school clay, painted on with a brush, or the latest serum, wrapped up in a face-shaped sheet? Well, it depends on how you feel, and even more importantly, on how your skin is feeling at that particular moment. And that’s part of the joy of masking right there: the focus is on immediate results, not the long term. Remember, a mask is a quick boost, not a replacement for a good routine; it’s a jewel-toned satin sandal, not your favourite perfectly cut tee. So just as one always needs a few shoe options, let us present your new curated masking wardrobe, with an option for every mood. Best Masks for Maximum Glow When you want glow, and your skin feels up to the challenge Oskia Renaissance Mask or Go-To Transformazing Sheet Mask The brightening capabilities of Oskia's rose-scented, peach-hued mask, which contains both enzymes and AHAs for serious chemical exfoliation, have to be seen to be believed. It works well enough as intended, but I share with you now a pro-tip for application derived from UK skincare guru Caroline Hirons: instead of gently patting it on, instead apply it like you would a cleanser, rubbing it in vigorously. In doing so, the product will transform from peach to opaque white, which, when removed, will reveal a newly soft, high wattage visage. Once upon a time, SK-II made us all want to use sheet masks any time, anywhere. (Remember back to the distant past when you used to fly, and would give your poor seatmate a heart attack thinking they’d sat next to Michael Myers? Ah, memories…) For a while there, it seemed they were taking over. But do they actually outperform traditional masks? And what about the environmental concerns they raise (most masks, along with the individual sachets they are housed in, are neither readily recyclable nor biodegradable), fit issues (there is truly no such thing as one size fits all when it comes to our faces), and general gripes that they’re too fiddly, too messy, too wet, and don’t really allow for talking or eating (my two favourite past times). I am ultimately a much bigger fan of traditional masks, but will acquiesce that sheet masks do allow a large dose of serum to stay in contact with the skin, where it would otherwise just drip off without the sheet holding it in place. One of the most impressive in the category is Go-To’s Transformazing sheet mask, which contains plant and fruit extracts high in vitamin C. These ingredients mean it gives great glow, and as part of your prep before a wedding or other major daytime event where you want to be truly luminous, it is an excellent option. However, it may prove too much for those with easily upset skin, so if that sounds like you, read on. Gentle Glow Masks for Sensitive Skin When you want glow, but your skin is sensitive Sisley Express Flower Gel or Neutrogena Hydro Boost Mask If your skin is in need of a little boost but is feeling tetchy, this Sisley mask is a great option. It’s particularly incredible, if not also a little upsetting, to you use this when your skin is particularly dehydrated: you can actually see your face drink it in, before rather rudely demanding reapplication. The creamy gel texture is fairly unusual in a mask and one I’d like to see more…

articles.title: Where to Stay, Eat & Heal in Kerala: A First-Timer’s Guide
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Sigourney visits Kerala in India: the birthplace of Ayurveda
articles.body: It’s 5 AM, and I’m sitting on the veranda of my traditional wooden cottage in an Ayurvedic retreat in Kerala, a cane chair creaking beneath me as I watch the fishing boats pull in their nets below. The black expanse of the Arabian Sea crashes on the distant shore, a hypnotic lullaby, while a chorus of night insects hums around me. Somewhere in the distance, fishermen shout to each other, their voices rising above the waves as they haul in their catch. The retreat is still asleep. Except for me. The night air is thick—soupy, fragrant, alive with a heady blend of damp earth, salt, and distant spices. The scent of burning incense and ghee-fried dosa drifts up from the village below my clifftop vantage point. I take a sip of warm ginger tea and swat away a mozzie from my leg, still scented with sesame oil. This is Somatheeram, one of Kerala’s oldest Ayurvedic health resorts, and for the next few days, I will submit myself to an ancient healing tradition that has existed for over 5,000 years. I expect serenity. What I hadn’t vouched for is an all out assault on the senses . Getting to Kerala: The Route Less Traveled It’s a fair hike from Sydney to reach Kerala and I’m invited to try the new Malaysia Airlines route to Trivandrum. I break up the journey with a layover in Kuala Lumpur, which is a deliciously indulgent pause—if you do this, make time for the laksa and curries in the lounge (Malaysia Airlines has mastered the art of inflight dining). The final four-hour flight into Trivandrum lands around midnight. By the time we disembark into the humid embrace of Kerala’s night air, I am sleep-deprived but buzzing with anticipation. My mum—who has joined me on this trip—jokes that I look l look like Eat, Pray, Love just swallowed me whole. She’s not wrong. I may have even brushed up on some Elizabeth Gilbert in preparation… Because this isn’t just a wellness retreat. This is a full-body reset—two hours of treatments a day, a strict Ayurvedic diet, and medicinal herbs prescribed by my doctor that taste like soil and tree bark but promise transformation. The Real Ayurveda: Not Just a Spa Treatment At Somatheeram Ayurvedic Hospital & Research Centre, Ayurveda is medical, not cosmetic. The consultation with my doctor is thorough, almost forensic—she examines my tongue, checks my pulse, and diagnoses my dosha imbalance within minutes. “You are Vata-Pitta,” she tells me. “Too much fire, too much air. Anxiety, digestion issues, dryness in your skin. We will bring you back into balance.” You are Vata-Pitta. Too much fire, too much air. Anxiety, digestion issues, dryness in your skin. We will bring you back into balance. The treatments are intense and immersive, set against the backdrop of an authentic, rustic resort—not a glossy five-star retreat, but a place deeply rooted in tradition. If you’re after something a little more luxe with uninterrupted ocean views, its sister resort, Manaltheeram, might be a better choice. Two hours of pampering a day is deliciously, dare I say, sometimes even restlessly long. (I never thought I’d say that.) That said, I think I could submit to Shirodhara all day. The ancient practice, where warm herbal oil is poured onto my forehead in a steady stream, induces a meditative, near-psychedelic state. Abhyanga, a synchronized four-hand massage, is both deeply relaxing and slightly a lot like a baggy nappy and, after derobing and donning them, you sit on a little wooden stool. Yep… with everything just… hangin’ out. My lovely therapist Suji has seen it…

articles.title: The Exact Products a Beauty Editor Packs for Europe
articles.author: Zoe Briggs
articles.excerpt: One month of simple yet great hair and makeup
articles.body: My husband and I were recently lucky enough to spend an entire month in Paris and the UK. Being the obsessive beauty editor I am, I spent months whittling down which products would make the cut. The right edit would ensure I'd feel as fabulous at a fancy Left Bank dinner as I would feel neat and put together in the Scottish highlands. And, no matter the location or occasion, that I could get ready in as close to five minutes flat as possible. After all, no one wants to waste glorious travel time in a tiny bathroom. Behold – a list of some of the very best hair and makeup items that got me through all of that wonderful travel in style. The Best Transparent Cosmetics Case for Travel My bag of choice was the completely transparent CEE CLEAR cosmetics case, which was smart, durable and made seeing what I had so easy. Note the size I took, 'small', was deemed too large by a very humourless man at Heathrow. To be fair, it did fit a truly enormous amount of product. My husband's 'mini' size still fit plenty and is what I'd recommend any non-beauty-obsessive person take. @cee clear The right edit would ensure I'd feel as fabulous at a fancy Left Bank dinner as I would feel neat and put together in the Scottish highlands. In-Flight Skincare for Glowing Skin Do you absolutely need to use high-end products to ensure happy skin while travelling? No. Might they make the unbearable moments (a never-ending flight, say, or travel plans going awry) more pleasant? Certainly, if you choose wisely. On the plane itself, the Sisley Floral Spray Mist felt like a skin-and-mood saviour. Dry skin? Headachey? Generally irritated and a bit nauseous and desperate-to-get-out-of-this-tin-can-this-instant? Spritz yourself. The gentle floral scent is fresh and revitalising; 'softly glamorous', if you will. Many brands don't pay enough attention to the misting mechanism, seemingly not caring if we are drenched or left yearning for more. This one hits that perfect Goldilocks mark. My skin actually felt quenched afterwards, though not like I had hosed myself down. Otherwise, my skincare heroes were Tatcha The Dewy Skin Cream, topped off with the immaculate Sisley Black Rose Precious Face Oil. This combination ensured tired, dry and dehydrated skin was instantly lifted back to life. During the day I had a wonderful, glowing base for makeup, and at night my skin could repair itself from the cold, dry northern hemisphere weather in utter luxury. Travel Makeup for a Five-Minute Face @cee clear I can neither confirm nor deny whether I also packed a large separate bag of cosmetic wonders like false lashes and sparkly red lipstick, but what I want to focus on here is my 'main' makeup items. I really did try to keep this pared back to true basics, especially for what I took on the plane and what I had easy access to in our hire car. For complexion, that amounted to Trinny London Just A Touch Foundation + Concealer, a handy little item housed in a neat pot that can be blended out to act as foundation if need be, and two blush options depending on my mood and location – Rare Beauty's Stay Vulnerable Melting Blush in Nearly Berry, a soft wine hue for moody Paris, and Violette's Bisou Blush in Ines, an enlivening pink for a flush of health when tramping about the countryside. The latter comes in a stick format with a brush on the end, which really comes into its own when you're travelling and don't want to stick…

articles.title: Struggling to Sleep? This Mattress Changed Everything for Me
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: The bed that fixed my sleep - plus the rituals that made it stick.
articles.body: Struggling to sleep? I’ve tried everything —blue light glasses, magnesium baths, even banning my phone from the bedroom. But nothing made as much of a difference as upgrading to the customisable King Living Sleep+ Mattress and Promenade Storage Bed. Here’s how transforming my sleep setup (and a luxe Byron retreat) helped me reset sleep routine—and finally fall in love with bedtime. My Journey to Better Sleep Why I Became Obsessed With Better Sleep It’s no secret that I’ve become a bit of a sleep obsessive lately. After reading Why We Sleep by Matthew Walker, I swapped my bright white bulbs for amber ones, cut down on alcohol and caffeine, and started to actually think about how I sleep. But after a whirlwind overseas trip and a serious case of jetlag, I fell back into bad habits. Enter: The King Living Sleep Collection, my new bedtime obsession. The Byron Sleep Retreat That Changed My Routine Last year, I was lucky enough to join The King Living Sleep Retreat at the breathtaking Bunker Byron house. It was the kind of getaway sleep dreams are made of: a night away in Byron Bay with a curated mattress menu, personalised sleep consultations with Dr. Carmel Harrington, and the chance to trial King Living’s ultra-luxe bedding. (Cue: B-roll of impossibly chic interiors and fabulous food by Three Blue Ducks.) Transforming my sleep routine has been about more than just upgrading my bed — it's been about creating a space and habits that genuinely support rest and recovery. Dr. Harrington shared some pearls of wisdom during the retreat, like how to reset your sleep routine; the importance of a consistent bedtime routine and how light exposure impacts melatonin levels. These tips couldn’t have come at a better time—my own routine had been sidelined by long-haul flights and frantic nights working in bed (it’s just SO much more comfortable than the desk). When the team offered me a chance to trial one of their bed and mattress combos, I decided it was time to reset my sleep game. The King Living Sleep Collection The King Living Mattress That Transformed My Sleep I’m not kidding when I say this bed is a game-changer. See it in action here. I chose the Promenade Storage Bed because they are the bomb for storing off-season coats and bedding. With its low-line profile and padded edges, the Promenade design itself isn’t just stylish —it’s practical . I immediately stashed all our winter quilts in the easy-to-access gas lift hidey-hole and discovered its other function: ‘bed making mode”. With a simple pull towards you, it changes to a chest height position that makes bed-making a breeze (my back thanks you, King Living!). I opted for Sorrento Whitewash fabric to complement my grey and white interior palette beautifully—the best part? They’re fully removable and washable, so no more panicking over an accidental breakfast in bed coffee-spill (been there, had that heart attack). How I Personalised My Mattress for Summer (and Jetlag) The pièce de résistance though? My customised Sleep+ 8000 Mattress. This isn’t your average mattress—it’s a multi-layered feat of design brilliance. At its core is the King Cell Base which contains individually wrapped and zoned KingCell pocket coil springs to minimise partner disturbance.
