articles.title: Jessica Maguire on Why Anxiety, Gut Issues, and Chronic Pain Are All Connected
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: What if stress, anxiety and even chronic pain aren't just in your head, but rooted in your nervous system? In Byron Bay I sat down with physiotherapist and nervous system educator Jessica Maguire to talk vagus nerve, the gut-brain connection and how to feel safe in your body again.
articles.body: Listen to the full episode here What if the way you experience stress, anxiety and even chronic pain isn't just in your head, but rooted in your nervous system? It is a question I have been sitting with for a long time, and it is exactly the one Jessica Maguire has built her career on answering. Jessica is a physiotherapist, TEDx speaker and nervous system educator who has dedicated her work to helping people understand how past experiences shape the body's ability to regulate itself, and, more importantly, how we can retrain it to feel safe again. I first discovered her work on Instagram during my own deep dive into nervous system regulation. Her insights resonated immediately. She has a way of explaining complex science that is not only accessible but genuinely transformative. After signing up for her vagus nerve masterclass, I knew I had to learn more. So while in Byron Bay, I sat down with Jessica in the tranquil garden of Three Meadows to talk about the mind-body connection, trauma and the science of healing. How Trauma Imprints on the Body Jessica's journey is as personal as it is professional. After tragically losing two brothers, she experienced firsthand how trauma imprints on the body, manifesting as anxiety, burnout and physical symptoms like chronic pain and gut issues. That experience led her to study the nervous system at a far deeper level, and eventually to create her Vagus Nerve Program and Nervous System Certification Course, which have now helped over 20,000 people worldwide. So much of what she teaches comes back to one reframe: the symptoms we are quick to label as weakness or dysfunction are often the body doing exactly what it learned to do to keep us safe. The Three Nervous System States One of the most useful frameworks Jessica shares is the idea of three nervous system states, and how we move between them. So many of us feel stuck in fight-or-flight, living in a near-constant state of threat without realising it. In this episode we talk through what those states feel like from the inside, why the body gets caught in survival mode, and the practical steps we can take to shift from that heightened response back into calm and balance. The Connection Between Stress, Gut Health and Chronic Pain This is where it all comes together. Jessica explains how stress, gut health and chronic pain are not separate problems but expressions of the same underlying nervous system state. The vagus nerve, which connects the brain and the gut, sits at the centre of that conversation. When we are dysregulated, digestion, pain perception and emotional resilience are all affected at once, which is why working at the level of the nervous system can change so much at the same time. The Vagus Nerve and Emotional Resilience We go deep on the role of the vagus nerve in emotional resilience, and Jessica shares simple techniques to self-regulate and feel more at home in your body. This is the work she has since distilled into her book, The Nervous System Reset, a practical guide to healing trauma and anxiety by retraining the body's stress response. In this episode we cover: - How trauma reshapes the nervous system, and how to retrain it - The three nervous system states and how to shift between them - The connection between stress, gut health and chronic pain - The role of the vagus nerve in emotional resilience - Simple techniques to self-regulate and feel at home in your body This conversation is a must-listen for anyone who struggles with stress,…

articles.title: How to Bring Life Back to Your Locks: Expert Haircare Tips
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: 1. Hydrate with Deep Conditioning Treatments Lack of moisture is one of the biggest culprits […]
articles.body: Editor’s Tip:If you’ve ever Googled “How do I bring dry, tired hair back to life?”—you’re not alone.The answer? A mix of hydration, nourishment, protection, and a few clever product swaps.We break it down below. 1. Hydrate with Deep Conditioning Treatments Lack of moisture is one of the biggest culprits behind dry, brittle hair. A high-quality deep-conditioning treatment is essential for restoring hydration, softness, and strength. Look for masks infused with nourishing ingredients like avocado oil, argan oil, and shea butter-these are rich in fatty acids that help repair damage and lock in moisture. Product Picks Olaplex No.8 Bond Intense Moisture Mask –Strengthens and intensely hydrates hair while repairing damage. Moroccanoil Intense Hydrating Mask – Packed with argan oil to restore shine, softness, and elasticity. 2. Exfoliate Your Scalp for a Fresh Start A healthy scalp is the foundation of healthy hair. Regular exfoliation removes product buildup, excess oil, and dead skin cells while promoting circulation and encouraging strong growth. Opt for gentle scalp scrubs with natural exfoliants that cleanse without irritation. Product Picks Briogeo Scalp Revival Charcoal + Coconut Oil Micro-Exfoliating Scrub – Detoxifies and soothes with binchotan charcoal and peppermint. The Inkey List Glycolic Acid Exfoliating Scalp Scrub – Gently removes buildup for a refreshed, balanced scalp. 3. Nourish with Lightweight Oils Hair oils are a game-changer for maintaining shine, smoothness, and hydration. Lightweight options like jojoba and marula oil control frizz and add moisture without weighing the hair down-perfect for all hair types. Product Picks Gisou Honey Infused Hair Oil – Nourishes and adds shine without greasiness. Ouai Hair Oil –A luxurious blend of African galangal and ama oils for deep hydration and frizz control. 4. Embrace Spring Hair Trends: Light Waves and Pastel Hues Looking to switch things up? Loose, natural waves give hair a voluminous, effortless look, while a touch of colour-whether subtle highlights or bold shades-can completely transform your look. How to Get Soft Waves: Use a curling wand on low heat to create loose curls, then brush them out for soft, natural waves. Finish with a texturizing spray for volume and hold. Product Picks GHD Curve Soft Curl Tong – Creates smooth, long-lasting waves with minimal heat damage. Bumble and bumble Surf Spray – Adds body and a beachy texture. Available at John Lewis 5. Protect Against UV Rays Just like skin, hair needs protection from environmental stressors like sun exposure and pollution. UV rays can lead to dryness, colour fading, and brittleness, so incorporating protective products is key. Product Picks Sachajuan Hair In The Sun –A leave-in UV protector that also adds hydration. Aveda Sun Care Protective Hair Veil – A lightweight mist that shields hair from UVA/UVB rays for up to 16 hours. Regular trims are essential for keeping your hair looking fresh and healthy. Split ends and breakage make hair appear thin and dull, so scheduling a trim every six to eight weeks will keep your locks strong and full of life. Healthy, beautiful hair is all about consistency and the right products. With a little extra care-hydration, nourishment, protection, and regular maintenance-you can restore your hair’s natural vitality and keep it looking fresh, strong, and radiant every day. articles.title: Jane Wurwand on Overcoming Adversity, Finding Purpose & Building a Billion-Dollar Brand
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Dermalogica founder Jane Wurwand is a force of nature. She joins me at the brand's LA headquarters to talk losing her father at two, escaping a toxic marriage, building a billion-dollar empire and why financial empowerment for women matters so much.
articles.body: Listen to the full episode here Jane Wurwand is not just the founder of Dermalogica, she is a force of nature. A visionary in the beauty industry, she built a billion-dollar global skincare empire while championing financial independence for women. Behind the success is a deeply personal story of resilience, reinvention and sheer determination. In this episode of Beautiful Inside by Beauticate , I sat down with Jane at Dermalogica's headquarters in LA to hear her extraordinary journey firsthand. She opened up about losing her father at just two years old, growing up in Scotland with a single mother who instilled in her an unshakable drive for independence, and the challenges she faced as a young woman in an industry dominated by men. From Scotland to a Billion-Dollar Brand Jane shares how she escaped a toxic marriage, started over in South Africa, and later took a bold leap to California, arriving with little more than a plan, unstoppable determination and a vision that would change the beauty world forever. She founded Dermalogica and The International Dermal Institute from the ground up, and grew it into the number one professional skincare brand in the world. Her story is proof that the things you think are your biggest setbacks can become the tools that build everything. How Adversity Became Fuel Throughout our conversation Jane explains how adversity shaped her work ethic and why she has never seen hardship as something to hide from. She talks candidly about reframing trauma and setbacks, and turning them into stepping stones rather than roadblocks. It is a theme she explores in her book, Skin in the Game, a transparent account of how the traits and experiences you might consider your weaknesses can become your greatest strengths. Why Financial Empowerment Matters Financial empowerment for women sits at the very heart of Dermalogica. Jane explains that her personal experience of navigating life without financial security made it central to everything she built, from the brand's culture to its education programmes. For Jane, helping women earn, save and stand on their own two feet is not a side project. It is the reason the business exists. Intuition, Magical Thinking and Daily Rituals We also dive into the power of intuition, the role of magical thinking in success, and the daily rituals that keep Jane grounded while leading a global brand. She shares how visualisation has guided some of her biggest decisions, and why she trusts her instincts even when the path is not yet clear. This is a conversation about far more than skincare. It is about reinvention, resilience and the courage to bet on yourself. If you have ever felt stuck, faced personal or professional setbacks, or wondered how to build something truly meaningful, this episode is packed with insight and inspiration. What You'll Learn in This Episode - How childhood adversity shaped Jane's drive and independence - The bold decisions that led to the creation of Dermalogica - How to reframe trauma and setbacks into fuel for success - The power of visualisation and intuition in business and life - Jane's daily rituals for balance, resilience and creative thinking A special thank you to Dermalogica, our season sponsor for Season 4. articles.title: Why Your Tap Water Might Be Ruining Your Skin (and What to Do About It)
articles.author: Jayde Balderston
articles.excerpt: Why it's the crucial element to our cleansing routine
articles.body: As a beauty journalist for the past two and a half decades, I’ve tested just about every serum, mask, and device promising to deliver better skin. But one of the biggest game-changers in my skincare routine hasn’t been a product at all-it’s been the water coming out of my tap. And a little Faucet Filter device from my friends at Qure (read on for your discount code!). I never thought I’d become a water filtration person. But once you go down the rabbit hole of what’s actually lurking in tap water, it’s hard to unsee it. It started with a deep dive into filtration for drinking water-after all, clean water is essential, right? So, I had Water Flow Control install a whole-house filtration system, then added an RO (reverse osmosis) filter under my sink for drinking water. But there was one tap I kept worrying about-my bathroom sink. The water I was using to wash my face every single day. I started wondering-was all that chlorine, magnesium, and heavy metals messing with my skin? And if so, could something as simple as filtering my tap water actually make a difference? Thankfully, that was around the time the Qure Faucet Filter came across my desk. What’s Hiding in Your Tap Water? Most people assume tap water is clean enough-after all, it’s been treated. But that doesn’t mean it’s free of skin-disrupting contaminants. - Chlorine – Added to disinfect water, but strips skin of natural oils, leading to dryness and irritation. - Calcium & Magnesium – Found in hard water, these minerals clog pores, trigger breakouts, and worsen rosacea and eczema. - Heavy Metals (Lead, Copper, Iron) – Can cause oxidative stress, leading to redness, sensitivity, and premature aging. - Microplastics & Bacteria – Yes, really. These can build up on your skin, clogging pores and dulling your complexion. My water in my home town of Sydney’s, like many major cities worldwide (including London, Melbourne, and parts of the US), contains trace levels of contaminants that-while deemed ‘safe’ for drinking-aren’t necessarily ideal for your skin. Another consideration: full-scale water filtration isn’t cheap. Whole-house systems can set you back thousands, and even a solid under-sink setup isn’t exactly a casual purchase. So when I came across the Qure Faucet Filter, it seemed like an interesting way to test the impact of filtered water on the skin-without the hefty investment. It’s specifically designed for skincare benefits, filtering out common irritants like chlorine, heavy metals, and microplastics, all of which can dry out skin, trigger sensitivity, or exacerbate issues like acne and rosacea. What Does the Qure Faucet Filter Actually Do? The Qure Faucet Filter is designed specifically for skincare, filtering out the most common irritants that can disrupt your skin barrier. It’s an affordable way to test water filtration without installing an expensive whole-house or under-sink system. It uses 4-stage advanced filtration technology: - Carbon Filter – Removes chlorine & contaminants. - Ultrafilter – Captures tiny particles like bacteria & sand. - Descaler – Reduces limescale buildup, which can dry out skin. - Heavy Metal Reduction Layer – Filters lead, copper, and iron. It also features a 360° rotating nozzle, so you can direct the flow for a more precise, mess-free cleanse. And, unlike permanent filtration systems, you can toggle between filtered and unfiltered water with a switch. My Experience: Did It Actually Make a Difference? Installation took seconds-no tools, no plumbing experience needed. (It fits 99% of standard faucets but won’t work with square, pull-out, or sensor taps.) For four weeks, I used only filtered water from the Qure Faucet Filter to cleanse…

articles.title: Sigourney's DIY Deck – All the Details
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Our guide to building a DIY-deck – thanks to Damien
articles.body: As part of our backyard renovation, which will eventually include putting a pool in, we needed to move our deck to the other side of the backyard, as the pool is going where the current deck is. My husband Damien, being the DIY tragic that he is, said, “You had me at ‘project’”. As with any good DIY enthusiast, he grossly underestimated the scope, budget and time required to complete said project. He initially planned just to move the current deck to a new location, but after he found someone in the neighbourhood giving away several large timber posts, he got excited about the idea of making it more substantial. As with any good DIY enthusiast, he grossly underestimated the scope, budget and time required to complete said project. He then felt like the old deck would be too small for the big thick posts, so decided to increase the size of the deck and to take advantage of the space available there. Our local council regulations allow up to 20 square metres without a permit, (with some other constraints – such as floor height and roof height), so we stuck to those guidelines to get it done without the paperwork. He also wanted to put a roof on it, so we didn’t have to put the cover on the outside furniture when it rained. It quickly went from a simple ‘move the current deck’ to a ‘build an entirely custom indoor/outdoor living space’. We initially thought the deck move would take a few weekends. But not that’s not how it turned out. Spoiler alert: It took 8 months (Damo justified this timeline based on the change in scope and his weekend availability) … The Brains Trust Before any big DIY project is the research process. Damo is lucky enough that his Dad was an engineer and his Grandpa was a builder so was able to pick their brains. He also spent many a BBQ harassing any tradie mates for tips. Despite all this, he decided to build the entire project without drawing any plans. Not from a lack of planning apparently but more of a mental challenge. Oh-kay… Whatever butters your biscuit, Damo. Laying the foundations… (For once we’re not talking about makeup.) We discovered that the higher the deck is from the ground, the more circulation you get which helps keep the timber decking dry (less of an issue if you’re using composite boards). We built it on a slightly sloping part of the garden which worked well. Once Damo got his big, recycled timber posts, he put them through a thicknesser (an electric plane that he borrowed from his grandpa) and they came up beautifully. Then he had to dig a bunch of holes around the backyard to concrete the posts in, after painting the bottoms of them with a thick waterproof protector (like Diggers Eco In-Ground Timber Protecta). With the help of his Dad and sister Elicia (who happens to be a Champion Powerlifter), he erected the posts and bolted in the beams around the foundations and the roof frame. Next step was to put in the bearers and joists (the big timber that go under the floor) to make the framework for the decking. The Decking The material choice for decking (the actual floor of a deck) is a common topic of discussion – often heavily debated between the old school timber craftsmen and the progressive composite enthusiasts. Every deckhead has an opinion: “Timber wears out and needs to be oiled all the time”, or “You don’t want to walk on recycled plastic that gets…

articles.title: Davinia Taylor on Alcohol, Addiction & Mental Health
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: I sat down with bestselling author, actress and biohacking pioneer Davinia Taylor in Sydney to talk honestly about alcohol, addiction and the science of feeling well, from gut health and hormones to the daily habits that keep her sharp, strong and happy.
articles.body: Listen to the full episode here In this episode of Beautiful Inside by Beauticate, I sat down with the brilliant Davinia Taylor, bestselling author, actress and biohacking expert, while she was in Sydney visiting from her home in the UK. We went deep on her health journey, from overcoming addiction to discovering the power of gut health, hormones and biohacking for longevity. It is one of my favourite interviews yet, raw, real and full of game changing insights. From the ladette years to a full reset Davinia first found fame as an actress, living what she calls the classic nineties and noughties ladette lifestyle. Behind the parties was a long, painful relationship with alcohol, and she is refreshingly honest about how addiction shaped those years. Her recovery became the foundation for everything that followed, a complete rethink of how she ate, moved, slept and looked after her mind. Out of that reset came WillPowders, the wellbeing business she founded to help women, and their families, take back control of their health with real food and a science backed approach. The link between your gut and your mind One of the biggest shifts for Davinia was understanding that so much of our mood is made in the gut, not just the mind. She talks about how cleaning up her diet, balancing her blood sugar and supporting her gut steadied her mental health in a way that willpower alone never could. It is a powerful reframe, especially for anyone who has felt anxious, foggy or flat and assumed it was all in their head. As Davinia explains, sometimes the fastest route to a calmer mind runs straight through the kitchen. Hormones, and why women need a different rulebook Davinia is passionate that women have been handed advice designed for men's bodies, then blamed when it does not work. In her book Hack Your Hormones, she breaks down how our hormones drive everything from cravings to sleep to motivation. We talked about why the usual eat less, move more message so often backfires for women, and how working with your hormones, rather than against them, changes the whole picture. Davinia's go-to biohacks This is where it gets practical. Davinia shares the simple, repeatable habits she swears by for glowing skin, steady energy and a sharp mind. Think morning light, protein and healthy fats over sugar spikes, smart supplementation and movement that builds strength rather than punishing the body. None of it is extreme. That is the point. Her whole philosophy, captured in her first bestseller It's Not A Diet, is about small, sustainable choices that compound into real change. articles.title: Rediscovering LA: A Luxury Travel Guide to Beverly Hills & Beyond
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Here’s where to stay and play in the City of Angels.
articles.body: Last November, before the terrifying wildfires swept across the West Coast, I embarked on a jam-packed LA content trip for Beautiful Inside by Beauticate, our video podcast. Feeling very Tinseltown, I take a little crew with me—my mum, Maxine, who is a producer (she’s an Executive Producer at Warner Bros in her day job), and my friend Matt, our cameraman. Despite our schedule being relentless, we still manage to squeeze in some incredible eats and a stay in one of Hollywood’s most iconic hotels: The Maybourne in Beverly Hills. As LA gets back on its feet after the inferno of destruction, now is the perfect time to show the city some love. Here’s where to stay and play in the City of Angels. You can also check out Discover LA for more ideas. Trust Me: Just Stay at The Maybourne After a few days in an Airbnb, we elevate our stay with a check-in at The Maybourne, the LA outpost of the legendary hotel group behind Claridge’s, The Berkeley, and The Connaught. Housed in what was once the iconic Montage, just minutes from Rodeo Drive, our terrace room exudes refined elegance with a distinctly Californian twist. Think cool cream fixtures, buttery leather details, mid-century modern furnishings, and striking local artwork-a perfect backdrop for soaking up LA rays and snapping an Insta-worthy moment. Stepping into the lobby feels like entering an art gallery. The bright, contemporary space showcases a Beryl Cook painting by the elevators, a Damien Hirst butterfly piece, and even a spiral painting emblazoned with “California.” Every detail, from the effortlessly cool reception team to the impeccably managed waitstaff, reaffirms the top-tier hospitality you expect from The Maybourne. It’s the thoughtful touches that stay with you-like the chilled bottles of water left in our car by valet or the warm invitation to their café while we wait for our room. No luxury escape is complete without a little beauty indulgence. The Maybourne Spa (a near 2,000 sqm haven of pampering pleasure) is part luxe modern-day spa, part Moroccan hammam. After a full-on day of interviews and navigating LA traffic, I gratefully don my robe and surrender to the most amazing massage I’ve had in quite a while. Not ready to face the real world, I spend the next hour floating my way (literally) through the enormous mineral “wellness” pool, Turkish steam room, and sauna. I’m told this is where many local thespians (and their harried publicists) come when they need a pre-red carpet glow-apparently their signature Dr. Sturm facial is IT, babe . After discovering days earlier that my beloved Dyson Airwrap doesn’t work in the US (thanks to voltage incompatibility), I am overjoyed when I spot one in the spa changing rooms. The next morning, before my interview, I head down to the spa and style my hair with it. The lovely receptionist tells me that next time, I can just request one from housekeeping (NB: they already have Dyson hairdryers in the hotel rooms!). In true Hollywood fashion, I head to breakfast in pin curls, and naturally, no one blinks. Breakfast at The Terrace restaurant is perfection. Overlooking the manicured Beverly Canon Gardens, I devour a ridiculously good Huevos Rancheros and toast paired with fresh fruit, basking in the gentle winter sunlight. Unfortunately, the weather isn’t playing ball when we wrap our interviews, so we miss out on some sun-lounger folly by the famous pool, but it is every bit as impressive as the photos suggest. As is Dante, the hotel’s restaurant-though Mum and I sadly don’t get to experience it, Matt claims they are the best…

articles.title: The Art of Loving Yourself: A Valentine’s Day for Me
articles.author: Jayde Balderston
articles.excerpt: Self-love isn’t just a buzzword; it’s a practice.
articles.body: Redefining Love After Thirteen Years Valentine’s Day has always been painted as a celebration of romantic love—roses, candlelit dinners, and handwritten notes. But this year, as I find myself newly single after 13 years, I’m redefining what love looks like. This February 14th isn’t about Galentine’s brunches or anti-Valentine’s rants; it’s about something deeper, more enduring: self-love. When my relationship ended, there wasn’t bitterness or drama-we parted on good terms. But stepping into life solo again after over a decade felt like learning to walk in new shoes. The silence in my apartment wasn’t just quiet; it was a strange, unfamiliar companion. At first, it felt overwhelming, but slowly, it became a space for rediscovery. The greatest love story you’ll ever write is the one where you are both the author and the muse. Small Rituals of Self-Care Self-love isn’t just a buzzword; it’s a practice. It’s about acknowledging your worth, embracing your quirks, and finding joy in your own company. I’m starting small-lighting my new favourite Lumira Solar Neroli candle at night, watching Breakfast at Tiffany’s and Clueless on repeat, and learning to cook meals I used to rely on someone else for. I glide on the latest (and my new favourite) Glossier Balm Dotcom in Black Cherry and spritz their You Rêve Eau de Parfum, a scent that feels like a dreamy hug. In a bath, I unwind with the KORA Organics by Miranda Kerr Berry Bright Vitamin C Eye Cream (make sure you check out Sigourney’s interview with Miranda), letting it brighten both my skin and mood. I’ll slather myself in Dermalogica’s decadent new Multivitamin Power Recovery Cream, and I’ll nourish myself from within with my must-have JSHealth Deep Sleep + Formula, a little evening ritual that feels like a daily reminder to care for my body. These small acts aren’t about vanity; they’re about cherishing myself, treating my body and mind with the kindness I often reserved for others. Celebrating Solo on Valentine’s Day This Valentine’s Day will be an opportunity to celebrate that journey. Instead of waiting for someone else to buy me flowers, I’ll pick out a bouquet of vibrant blooms that make me smile. I’ll try a new recipe-probably mess it up a little-but pour a glass of wine and laugh at myself in the process. I’ll treat my skin to a session with my Qure LED Mask, basking in its glow as a reminder of how far I’ve come. I’ll unbox my Alaïa Le Coeur leather shoulder bag and dress up in my new SKIMS Long Slip in Bubblegum and style my hair with the Dyson Airwrap i.d (the red velvet and gold colourway is not something to sleep on) -not for anyone else, but for the woman in the mirror who’s navigating this new chapter with courage. I’ve also discovered something unexpectedly comforting-how a simple fairytale, told aloud (by Lex, my AI assistant), can help me drift into sleep. There’s something soothing about being read to, like a reminder that I can still find magic and gentleness in the quiet moments of my day. Facing the Hard Parts of Healing Self-love isn’t just about indulgence. It’s also about facing the tough stuff-setting boundaries, forgiving myself for past mistakes, and learning to sit with discomfort without judgment. There will be nights when loneliness creeps in, and instead of pushing it away, I’ll let myself feel it. I’ll record voice notes, I’ll cry, and I’ll remind myself that healing isn’t linear. And through it all, I’m grateful to have my wonderful psychologist (and friends) guiding me through the process, helping me navigate the…

articles.title: Miranda Kerr on Faith, Family and That First Date (Where He Fell Asleep)
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Supermodel, Kora Organics founder and mother of four Miranda Kerr welcomes Sigourney into her LA home for a rare conversation about faith, grief, gratitude and the love story that almost didn't happen.
articles.body: Listen to the full episode here In this rare, in-depth conversation, Miranda Kerr welcomed me into her LA home. Supermodel, founder of Kora Organics, mother of four. What she shared went far beyond beauty, into the rituals, the love story and the life lessons that have shaped her. We've known each other a long time. What struck me most this time was how grounded she is, and how much intention sits behind the calm. The Love Story Everyone knows the headline. On their very first date, Evan Spiegel fell asleep on Miranda's lap. Rather than a knock, it became the moment that sealed their bond. These days she's open about the fact that closeness takes work, and that therapy is part of how they grow together rather than apart. "I still have therapy. Right now I have a therapist I speak to every two weeks." It's a small admission with a big message. The relationships we admire from the outside are usually the ones being tended most carefully on the inside. Faith and Spirituality Faith is the thread that runs through everything Miranda does. Kundalini yoga, prayer and a daily gratitude practice are how she stays grounded in the chaos of four boys and a global business. She doesn't preach it. She lives it, quietly, every day. Loss and Resilience Some of the most moving moments came when Miranda spoke about loss. She lost her first boyfriend at fifteen. And she spoke about her grandparents, who raised her on their farm and who loved each other right to the very end. "Grandma and Grandpa were together right until the end. They passed 20 days apart." You could feel how deeply that template of love shaped what she wants for her own family. Motherhood and Balance Now a mother of four boys, Miranda is trying to give them the same sense of safety she grew up with, in a very different world, while running a global business and making space for self-care. "Now with my children, I'm trying to recreate that. Just making sure they have that love." Building Kora Organics Underpinning it all is her mission with Kora Organics: clean, high-performance skincare inspired by nature and backed by science. For Miranda, beauty has always started from within, and the brand is simply that belief made tangible. Why It Stayed With Me This is a conversation about what holds a life together. Faith, family, gratitude and the courage to keep doing the inner work. I left Miranda's home lighter, and thinking about my own people. I think you will too. Interview by Sigourney Cantelo.

articles.title: Korean Skin Treatments That We Predict We’ll Be Seeing More Of
articles.author: Kristina Zhou
articles.excerpt: Unearthing the skincare capital’s latest technology to achieve glass skin.
articles.body: Korean skincare has long been synonymous with innovation, consistently pushing the boundaries of what's possible when it comes to achieving glowing skin. From salmon sperm facials to Chanel and Hermes skin boosters, Korea has shaped the global beauty landscape. Now, a new wave of cutting-edge treatments is gaining traction in the Korean beauty scene. Here’s a deep dive into four trending treatments that we predict you’ll be seeing more of in 2024. Unearthing the skincare capital’s latest technology to achieve glass skin. Lhala Peel Chemical peels can be intimidating, especially if you have sensitive skin prone to redness or irritation. Enter the Lhala Peel, a fourth-generation chemical peel that utilizes Lipo Hydroxy Acid (LHA). Unlike traditional alpha or beta hydroxy acids, LHA mimics the skin's natural renewal process, gently dissolving dead skin cells without causing visible peeling or downtime. Why it’s trending: The Lhala Peel is perfect for achieving that coveted "glass skin" effect - a smooth, poreless, and translucent complexion. It’s a great alternative for those who want the benefits of a chemical peel but without the risk of redness, flaking, or downtime. The treatment is designed to gently exfoliate and clarify the skin while maintaining its natural moisture barrier, making it suitable for even the most sensitive skin types. Potential side effects: Although gentler than traditional peels, some people may still experience mild tingling or tightness during and after the treatment, particularly if they have very sensitive skin. There may be some very slight dryness or flakiness on the second and third day. BB Laser BB Laser combines the benefits of laser technology with a focus on skin rejuvenation. This treatment utilizes a gentle laser to target pigmentation issues, reduce redness, and smooth out skin texture. The BB Laser stimulates the skin's natural healing process, leading to a more even skin tone and a healthier, brighter complexion. Why it’s trending: The BB Laser went viral for making skin look like it naturally has "bb cream" (a perfecting tinted skin moisturiser). It is the go-to solution for individuals seeking to address skin concerns like pigmentation, acne scars, or dullness. Its versatility allows it to be customized to suit different skin types, offering effective results with minimal downtime, making it ideal for those with busy lifestyles. Potential side effects: Some people may experience mild redness, swelling, or a sensation of warmth in the treated area immediately after the procedure. These side effects are typically short-lived, subsiding within a few hours to a day. In rare cases, temporary skin sensitivity or slight dryness may occur. InMode Lifting InMode Lifting is all about sculpting and contouring your face using the power of radiofrequency (RF) technology. This non-surgical facelift uses RF energy to heat the deeper layers of the skin, triggering collagen production and tightening the skin without needles or scalpels. Why it’s trending: In Asia, where achieving a V-shaped face is highly desired, InMode Lifting offers a way to contour the jawline, reduce the appearance of double chins, and sculpt facial features without surgery. Think of it as a high-tech alternative to traditional facelifts but with natural-looking results. Potential side effects: Some individuals might experience temporary swelling, redness, bumpiness, mild bruising, or a slight burning sensation due to the heat involved. One TikTok user said it looked like she got a "beating". However, these side effects usually completely subside after 4-5 days. LDM (Local Dynamic Micro-Ultrasound) LDM is setting a new standard in skin therapy by using micro-fused ultrasound waves that penetrate deep into the skin's dermis (the layer below the superficial skin surface) to deeply hydrate. This treatment improves skin's moisture…

articles.title: Phu Quoc: Vietnam’s New Go-to Luxury Destination
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: From beachfront bliss to sky-high indulgence, explore the perfect escape at Phu Quoc’s most luxurious resorts.
articles.body: When you’re invited to review two of Vietnam’s most luxurious resorts— The InterContinental Phu Quoc and The Regent Phu Quoc—you don’t hesitate. And when you haven’t had a proper kid-free getaway in five years, you grab your husband (and, conveniently, your videographer/photographer), throw some swimsuits and camera gear in a suitcase, and head for the airport. Which is exactly what Damien and I did when we were given the chance to spend five blissful days in Phu Quoc, a lush tropical island just off Vietnam’s southwest coast. The InterContinental Phu Quoc Long Beach This trip promised two very different flavours of luxury, starting with a one-night stay at The InterContinental Phu Quoc Long Beach Resort. Just 15 minutes from the airport, the InterContinental immediately gave us that “we’re on holiday” feeling—palms swaying in the breeze, perfectly manicured gardens, and stunning pools that seemed to stretch forever. We spent the morning bouncing between the main pool, where cabanas and loungers beckoned, and Club InterContinental, the hotel’s exclusive haven for guests looking for an elevated experience. The star of the breakfast menu? Their famous Lobster Pho, a rich and indulgent twist on the classic Vietnamese soup. I got Damien to order one too so I could taste it again just to ‘check’ it was as good the second time. It was. After a few hours of sunning and swimming, we wandered down to Sea Shack for lunch, a rustic-chic beachfront restaurant where we kicked off our shoes, dug our toes into the sand, and feasted on fresh seafood while the sun disappeared into the waves. An afternoon storm swept in so we decided to head back to our spacious Ocean View Room, and enjoy a bottle of bubbles on the balcony, while gazing at the turquoise horizon as the rain clouds swept in moodily. The next morning, Damien and I (feeling surprisingly virtuous for two parents on holiday) decided to go for a jog along the beach. While navigating around a boat sitting on the shore line, I managed to slam my hand into its propeller. Damien still doesn’t know how I didn’t see it, but I’ve never been known for my great spacial awareness. We headed to the Club and the hotel doctor came to clean and assess my injury which unfortunately was a rather large gash on the back of my right hand. Checking Into The Regent Phu Quoc We raced back to the room to do a rushed pack before beelining to the international hospital where I received nine stitches. Not exactly the holiday souvenir I was hoping for, but I was grateful for the care and the calming reassurances from the hotel staff. While we were away the team moved our luggage next door to the sister resort: The Regent Phu Quoc. If the InterContinental was polished and family-friendly, the Regent was an exercise in pure, understated luxury. From the flower-filled reception overlooking a serene lake to the meticulously placed palms and minimalist design, the entire place whispers calm sophistication. The Sky Pool Villa Experience We were lucky enough to stay in a Sky Pool Villa, and it was nothing short of epic. Picture this: our own infinity plunge pool that looked straight out to the ocean, a fully serviced kitchen (not that we were going to cook with restaurants this good), a bathroom and powder room, and a complimentary minibar restocked daily. It felt less like a hotel room and more like our own sleek apartment in the sky. With swimming (tragically) off the table for me, it didn’t stop us from working our way through The…

articles.title: Our Stay at Three Meadows: The Byron Hinterland Retreat of Dreams
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: The ultimate escape for your next group trip or event
articles.body: bc7ab92e (Batch-fix markdown delimiters across 112 articles) Driving into the Byron Bay hinterland, where the hills roll like waves and the light feels almost otherworldly, I arrived at Three Meadows—a 50-acre haven promising the kind of luxury that doesn’t shout but whispers. Tucked just 15 minutes from Byron town, this beautiful property feels secluded yet so accessible, a rarity for spaces of this scale. Read on for your special discount and check out my walk through reel here. I’m here with Damien and the kids on a content production trip for the B eautiful Inside by Beauticate podcast. There are so many great people to interview up in Byron and on the Gold Coast, so I wanted to plant myself somewhere central so that I could get around to all my locations easily. It was nice to bring the family on this trip with me so I could still spend some time with them, while also working my bottom off during the day. The kids were drawn by the promise of a pool and plenty of room to run aroundThe moment we step inside, we’re struck by the sheer sense of calm. The house is airy and lofty, a dreamy palette of white and beige enriched with natural textures. Sunlight pours in through expansive windows, while raw timber beams-repurposed from the original orchard-add a grounding, rustic charm. The organic timber elements scattered throughout the house tell their own story, having been reclaimed from an old railway bridge. This clever balance of old and new runs through every detail of Three Meadows, giving it a warmth that feels so personal and considered. And it is personal. So much of what makes this place special comes from the vision of its owner, Aaron-a jeweller-turned-furniture-designer whose artistry is everywhere. From the handmade doors and light fittings to the stunning stone bathtubs, every corner of the house has been infused with thoughtfulness and craftsmanship. Even the objets d’art-delightful curios dotted throughout the home, lending a sense of connection to the space.I slip into one of the plush bathrobes (they are impossibly soft, by the way) and settle in to work on my notes for tomorrow’s interview with Emma Lane – the creative behind The Range Estates who is at Copperstone, just around the corner in Bangalow. Damien sets himself up to work at the dining table and I head down to the office for some quiet. It’s the kind of house where you can spread out and have space while still feeling connected. There are plenty of private nooks for solitude, but also large, inviting living spaces to gather and reconnect. Gardens, Sculptures and Grounds Outside, the grounds are just as captivating. Sculptures, crafted from repurposed oil drums, rise up like industrial flowers across the gardens. Some of these were even made in Aaron’s factory in Vietnam, adding a global nomadic charm to the estate’s landscape. The lawns stretch endlessly, and the gardens buzz with life, making you want to slow down, breathe deep, and truly take it all in. Event Spaces for Weddings and Retreats One of the things I love most about Three Meadows is how perfectly it balances relaxation and celebration. With multiple event spaces, it’s easy to see why this place is such a sought-after destination for weddings, retreats, or milestone celebrations. The spaces on offer? - The Shed: A versatile, rustic-luxe space ideal for intimate ceremonies, recovery drinks, and long-table soirees. Its barn doors open wide to reveal breathtaking hinterland views, but it also works beautifully as a cozy, all-weather option. - The Pavilion: A magical space crafted from…

articles.title: Sacred Six: What India Taught Me for Better Health and Happiness
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: I recorded this solo episode from a verandah at Somatheeram in Kerala, India. Here are my Sacred Six, the six things from this trip that shifted something in me, from Ayurveda to temples, food, silks, yoga and the gift of slowing down.
articles.body: Listen to the full episode here Recording from Kerala's Arabian Sea Coast I am recording this from a wooden verandah at the Somatheeram Ayurvedic Resort in Kerala, India. The fans are turning, the Arabian Sea is somewhere below me, and I have just come from a treatment that left me smelling of warm herbs and feeling completely rearranged. This is a "Sacred Six" episode, so I want to share the six things from this trip that have stayed with me. Some are experiences. Some are small shifts in the way I want to live when I get home. Ayurveda, Temples and Indian Food Ayurveda is not a spa menu here. It is medicine. On arrival a doctor takes your pulse, asks about your sleep and digestion and moods, works out your dosha, and then your treatments are built around that. My days have been shaped by oil. Warm streams of it poured across my forehead, four hands working in unison, herbal pastes and powders pressed into my skin. It sounds indulgent, and it is, but it is also doing something deeper. I feel calmer in my body than I have in a long time. We drove out to see a vast statue of Shiva rising up against the sky, and I stood underneath it feeling very small in the best possible way. The temples here are not a backdrop. They are alive with offerings, bells, colour and devotion. You take your shoes off, you lower your voice, and something in you settles. I am not religious in any formal sense, but I left every temple feeling like I had been somewhere sacred. I have eaten the best vegetarian food of my life on this trip. Coconut and curry leaves, dosa for breakfast, dal that tasted like it had been cooked by someone's grandmother, fruit I could not name. Because the resort cooks to your dosha, the food is part of the healing, not separate from it. It has reminded me how good I feel when I eat simply and slowly, and how much of that I let slide at home. Shopping, Yoga and Slowing Down I cannot help myself. I went shopping for silks and jewellery and fell hard for the colour of everything. Saris in marigold and rose, fine gold, tiny mirrored details. There is an artistry to it that mass production has stripped out of so much of what we buy. I came away with pieces I will keep forever, and a renewed love for things made slowly by hand. Yoga at sunrise, on a platform overlooking the sea, taught by someone who has practised it his whole life. No leaderboard, no playlist, no rush. Just breath and movement and the light coming up. It made me realise how performative my practice had become at home, and how much I want to come back to the quiet version of it. This is the one I most want to carry home. India has shown me, again, how much I crush into a day and how little of it I actually feel. Here I have read, sat, swum, watched the sea, done nothing and called it enough. Disconnecting, slowing down, connecting with the sacred both within myself and in my surroundings. That is the real souvenir. Where to Stay and Heal in Kerala If you want to follow the trail I took, I have written a full guide to where to stay, eat and heal in Kerala. You can stay at Somatheeram or its sister property, Soma Manaltheeram, and let it do its quiet work on you too. Thanks to…

articles.title: Amy Gerard on Motherhood, Mental Health & Life’s Curveballs (Part 2)
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Part two of our chat with the wonderful Amy Gerard. We go deep on anxiety and motherhood, the bushfire that shaped her childhood, parenting in the digital age, and learning to set boundaries and protect your energy.
articles.body: Listen to the full episode here Welcome to part two of our chat with the wonderful Amy Gerard. If you loved part one, where Amy talked us through her home reno, social media and that sex chapter, this is the heartfelt other half of the conversation. Here we go deep on the messy, beautiful reality of balancing motherhood, mental health and a creative career, and on what it really takes to keep showing up when life throws its curveballs. When Motherhood Ignites Anxiety Amy is refreshingly honest about how becoming a mother can switch on anxiety you never knew you had. We talk about the relentless juggle of modern parenting, the mental load that rarely lets up, and how easy it is to lose yourself in the day to day. It is a reminder that you are not alone in your struggles, and that it is okay to prioritise yourself while navigating the chaos. The Bushfire That Shaped Her Amy shares the traumatic childhood experience of losing her family home to a bushfire, and how that moment shaped her perspective on what really matters. She describes the way her community rallied around her family, and how that resilience still lives in her today. It is a powerful thread that connects back to the home she would later buy and renovate, which she spoke about in part one. From Stay-at-Home Mum to Working Mum One of the most relatable parts of our chat is Amy's honesty about rediscovering her identity. We talk about the transition from being a stay-at-home mum to a working mum, the guilt that can come with it, and the slow process of remembering who you are beyond the role of caregiver. Parenting in the Digital Age As someone who built a career on sharing her life online, Amy has thought deeply about how much to share about your children. We talk about parenting in the digital age, where the line sits for her family, and how she protects her kids while still being open with her audience. Relationships, Conflict and Boundaries Amy goes deep on her relationships and how she manages conflict and confrontation in both friendships and marriage. She talks about learning to prioritise and protect your energy as life gets busier, overcoming people-pleasing tendencies, and the quiet power of setting boundaries. This episode is a beautiful reminder to feel seen, inspired and validated. articles.title: Amy Gerard on Her Home Reno, Social Media and That Sex Chapter
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: The incredibly funny and unfiltered Amy Gerard joins me to talk about turning viral parenting videos into two hit podcasts and a book, rebuilding the childhood home she lost to bushfire, and the sex chapter everyone is talking about.
articles.body: Listen to the full episode here Some guests make you laugh before you have even pressed record, and Amy Gerard is one of them. The content creator, radio host and author has built a whole career out of saying the thing everyone else is thinking, and in this episode of Beautiful Inside she is every bit as funny and unfiltered as you would hope. We covered the lot, from viral parenting videos to her two hit podcasts, the deeply personal reno of the home she grew up in, and yes, THAT sex chapter from her memoir. From Viral Videos to Two Hit Podcasts Amy's rise started where so many do now, with a phone and a willingness to be honest about the chaos of modern motherhood. Those raw, relatable parenting videos struck a nerve, and the audience that found her has followed her everywhere since. She turned that connection into two podcasts, Beyond the Likes and her parenting show Beyond the Chaos, and a weekend radio slot on KIIS FM. We talked about what it actually takes to keep showing up online, and how she protects herself from the parts of social media that can quietly chip away at you. Rebuilding the Home She Grew Up In The most moving part of our chat was about her house. Amy's childhood home was lost in the 1994 bushfires, a trauma that shaped so much of her early life. Years later, she bought the property back. What she has created there is extraordinary. She has renovated it into a nature-inspired family home filled with love and memory, taking a painful chapter of her past and rewriting it into something healing. It is renovation as a kind of closure, and she speaks about it beautifully. THAT Sex Chapter Amy's memoir Strap Yourself In is a memoir of motherhood, dancefloors and all the mayhem in between, and it does not sugarcoat any of it. Birth, marriage, friendship, careers, holidays, it is all in there. And then there is the sex chapter, the one everyone keeps asking her about. We get into why she chose to be so honest about intimacy and long-term relationships, and how being that open in print actually feels once the book is out in the world. Parenting, Marriage and Managing the Anxiety For all the comedy, Amy is just as candid about the harder stuff. We talked about parenting and marriage, the mental load, and the anxiety that runs underneath so much of it. Her gift is finding the humour in the hard days without pretending they are not hard. That is exactly where we pick things up in part two of our chat, where Amy goes deeper on mental health, motherhood and life's curveballs. articles.title: The Glow-Up Secrets Behind Hollywood's Best Makeover Scenes
articles.author: Kristina Zhou
articles.excerpt: Level up your look like a Hollywood movie star.
articles.body: The classic movie makeover scenes in movies and television dramas are enduringly fascinating. With a few savvy hair, makeup and styling tips, one can seemingly transform from girl-next-door pretty to an elegant swan. Whilst changing your appearance to fit into other people's ideals should be steadfastly rejected, there are a few grooming techniques we can all gleam from these makeovers to level up and look a little more polished. Although the transformations look extreme, they're often the result of simple changes that can be replicated at home, without the need for a glam squad. Beauticate writer, Kristina, examined these makeovers closely and pin-pointed the key glow-up secrets behind some of the most iconic entertainment makeovers. However, alongside the physical transformations, there is often a powerful internal metamorphosis — where the character rises like an eagle from the ashes, with the importance of self-love, determination and perseverance reverberating throughout their inspiring journeys. The Devil Wears Prada: Andy Sachs In the Devil Wears Prada , Andy Sachs enters the fashion magazine world as a brainy assistant, who sees herself as too intellectual to be concerned with style. But, she soon discovers that survival in this competitive industry requires serving chic looks. After embracing the fashion-forward world of Runway, Andy’s once simple and mousy hair becomes sleek and voluminous. Her makeup follows suit, with a focus on her eyes—defined by sleek black eyeliner and smoky eyeshadow that produce an alluring gaze. Andy’s polished makeover reflects her immersion into the high-stakes fashion world, but it also becomes a mirror for the compromises she makes along the way. She ultimately realises that her true strength lies in embracing her individuality, proving she can succeed without sacrificing her identity. She ultimately realises that her true strength lies in embracing her individuality, proving she can succeed without sacrificing her identity. The Makeup Tips that Made the Biggest Difference for Andy Sachs’ Makeover 1. Mix a matte taupe and shimmery peachy-nude shadow together and apply all over your lids, focusing on building the colour at the crease for depth. Add a hint of soft plum at the outer corners for dimension. 2. Blend a dark brown shadow into the crease, emphasising the outer third for a slight lift. To soften the edges, use a clean brush to diffuse the colour upwards toward the brow bone. Use a lighter brown shadow to define the lower lash line, and use a small fluffy blending brush to diffuse the line for a more subtle look. 3. Tightline the upper waterline with black gel eyeliner. Then, apply the liner on the upper lash line and smudge it slightly for a soft, smoky edge. Add a touch of dark brown eyeshadow on top of the liner for a dreamy aesthetic. 4. Tap a shimmery champagne shadow on the inner corners of the eyes and lightly along the brow bone to create subtle radiance. For a dewy finish, apply a liquid highlighter with a damp brush to the inner corners and middle of the eyelids. 5. Layer both lengthening and volumising mascaras for full, fluttery lashes. Focus more mascara on the outer lashes to elongate and lift the eyes for a wide-eyed effect without falsies. 6. Use a lip liner in a matching red shade to not only outline but also fill in the lips, creating a base that enhances the lipstick’s vibrancy. For added dimension, dab a slightly lighter red in the centre of the lips and press your lips together gently. Set the look by placing a tissue over your lips and dusting a fine layer of translucent powder through the tissue…

articles.title: Vedic Meditation Teacher Gary Gorrow on Designing Sacred Spaces
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: I learnt Vedic Meditation from Gary Gorrow 13 years ago, so for our Sacred Spaces series I sat down with him at Soma, his Byron Bay retreat, to talk meditation, healing the nervous system and designing spaces that foster inner peace.
articles.body: Listen to the full episode here Welcome to our Sacred Spaces series, proudly sponsored by King Living. When I first dreamt up this idea of sacred spaces, one of the very first places that came to mind was Soma, the wellness retreat in the Byron Bay hinterland founded by my own meditation teacher, Gary Gorrow. I learnt Vedic Meditation from Gary 13 years ago, when I was pregnant with Max. He is known for teaching big names and CEO types, yet he always remains so humble and gentle. He taught me some of the most profound lessons of my life, ones I still use today. So when I was in Byron recently, it felt perfect to interview Gary in his own sacred space. There was a retreat on that day, so we sat down in his gorgeous home, which is on site next door to the main house and very much designed in the spirit of Soma. Soma, A Sanctuary for Healing Gary worked on both his house and the retreat with his brother, designer and Ksubi co-founder George Gorrow, and the result is a feat of architecture and design. As a sanctuary for healing and transformation, Soma pays respect to the sacred energy of the land it occupies, nine hectares of tropical countryside that includes a lotus pond and a tranquil bamboo garden, and features the iconic geodesic dome, the perfect place to practise yoga and meditation while feeling at one with nature. Soma was also the set of the series Nine Perfect Strangers, filmed there during COVID. The ten bedrooms, pool and custom furniture blend modern minimalism with Balinese influences. Gary's home is similarly designed to draw nature in, with windows wrapping the house that look out to the endless green beyond. It was a rainy day when we did our interview, but it felt so cosy inside, with Gary's beautiful cat Leopold purring between us. Finding Meditation, Healing the Nervous System In this episode we learn all about Gary's upbringing on Sydney's Northern Beaches and his struggle with depression and burnout while he was working in film and TV production. Gary found meditation, learnt how to heal his nervous system and shift his mindset, and from there he says he answered a calling to become a meditation teacher. Designing Spaces That Foster Inner Peace Gary also shares practical insights into building a meaningful meditation practice and creating spaces that foster inner peace. I am so excited for you to hear this one, I really think it will help so many. Some of the techniques Gary describes I have been using myself, and they are genuine game changers. With special thanks to our Season Three sponsor King Living. Like us at Beauticate, King Living believe that home is a haven, and they design furniture made to change and flex as we do. Their Sleep Collection is a true example of innovation in the wellness space, and I have been lucky enough to road test one of King Living's beds and a customisable mattress in my Sleep Diary. I cannot wait to share my experience in the episodes to come, so stay tuned. Hosted by Sigourney Cantelo.

articles.body: Listen to the full episode here In this episode from our Sacred Spaces Series, sponsored by King Living, I sit down with the extraordinary Laura May Gibbs, the founder and creative visionary behind Nagnata, a Byron Bay-based sustainable fashion brand that is quietly redefining the industry. A Store That Feels Like an Art Gallery We recorded this conversation in Nagnata's flagship store in Byron Bay, a space that feels more like an art gallery than a retail shop. Designed in collaboration with the Pattern Studio, the store is a dreamscape of hand-carved timber pillars and curvaceous forms inspired by global architecture. Serene and soothing by day, the space can transform after dark. With its LED lighting it shifts into something vibrant and energetic, so the room you browse in the morning is not quite the room you would find at night. articles.title: Emma Lane on Sustainability, Slow Living and the Famous Range Estates
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Emma Lane invited me into Copperstone, her breathtaking estate in the Byron hinterland, to talk sustainability, slow living and the nature-led philosophy behind The Range Estates.
articles.body: Listen to the full episode here Join me for an enchanting episode featuring the brilliant Emma Lane, the creative force behind The Range Estates and the beloved Farm in Byron Bay. In this special interview, Emma graciously invited me into her exquisite home, Copperstone, nestled in the picturesque countryside of the Byron hinterland in New South Wales. From the moment I drove up the long driveway, it felt like I had been transported to another world, almost like the serene hills of Tuscany. Arriving at Copperstone Copperstone is more than just a home. It is a sanctuary that celebrates slowness, intentional design and harmony with nature. Set on 48 acres of pristine landscape, the estate is a seamless blend of European heritage and an authentically Australian touch. Our conversation took place in Emma's beautifully curated bedroom, surrounded by her treasured objects and her loyal dog, Ranger, relaxing nearby. The scene was complete with perfect weather, the laughter of her children, and the deep tranquility of Copperstone embracing us. From advertising to a slower life Emma grew up in the English countryside with summers in the Canary Islands, studied creative advertising and began her career in marketing. After a decade in Sydney, she relocated to Byron Bay to pursue family life, along with studies in photography, nutrition, yoga and meditation. In this episode she shares that journey, from her boarding school days to a successful career in advertising, and how it all led her to create extraordinary spaces rooted in sustainability and mindful living. In 2018 she published The Farm Community, a collection of stories, projects and recipes that reflect her move toward simplicity. Designing with nature What strikes you most about Emma's work is how the landscape leads. As she puts it, she always tries to incorporate the outside surroundings and nature into her design, whether through colours, scents or textures, because this brings a level of peace and harmony to the space. That philosophy runs through every project she and her husband Tom create together at The Range Estates, from Copperstone to Highground in the Southern Highlands, and through their belief that thoughtful, sustainable design should nurture both people and the planet. The beauty of intentional living If you are looking for a dose of inspiration drawn from the power of family, nature and the beauty of thoughtful design, this conversation is for you. Emma reminds us that beauty is not about doing more, but about choosing what matters and giving it room to breathe. This episode is part of our Sacred Spaces series, proudly brought to you by King Living. Hosted by Sigourney Cantelo.

articles.title: Sacred Six: 6 Ways I'm Going to Live Longer
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Broadcasting from the Regent Phu Quoc in Vietnam, I'm sharing the six longevity lessons that changed how I think about ageing, after a comprehensive Longevity Assessment with Dr Adam Brown.
articles.body: Listen to the full episode here My Longevity Assessment with Dr Adam Brown I am recording this one from the Regent Phu Quoc in Vietnam, looking out at the water, which feels like exactly the right place to think about living well for longer. Before this trip I did a comprehensive Longevity Assessment at the Longevity Medicine Institute in Double Bay with GP and longevity specialist Dr Adam Brown. I walked out with life-changing knowledge about how fitness, diet and mindset shape how long, and how well, we live. I also let go of a few limiting beliefs I had carried about myself since childhood. None of what follows is radical. The six things below are small, evidence-based changes anyone can start this week. Here is my Sacred Six on living longer. Exercise, Protein and Bone Health Dr Adam's first lesson was to stop doing the same workout on repeat. Longevity asks for range. Strength to protect muscle and bone, cardio to look after the heart, and endurance to keep the whole engine running. Spreading your training across all three is what builds long-term resilience and helps guard against preventable disease. For me that has meant adding weights and swimming to the running I already love. The single nutritional shift I have leaned into hardest is protein. As we age we lose muscle, and muscle is one of the strongest predictors of how well we move and stay independent later in life. Building meals around protein helps preserve and grow that muscle mass, which is why it sits so high on the longevity list. Bone density quietly declines with age, especially for women, and calcium is the foundation that keeps our bones strong. Dr Adam encouraged me to be far more deliberate about getting enough of it, rather than assuming I already was. It is a small, unglamorous habit that pays off decades down the track. Supplements, Mindset and Daily Habits Vitamin D works hand in hand with calcium, helping the body actually absorb and use it, and supporting bone and muscle health more broadly. So many of us are quietly low in it. A daily vitamin D supplement was one of the simplest, most practical takeaways from my assessment. Possibly the most unexpected part of my assessment had nothing to do with food or fitness. Working through my mindset, I confronted some limiting beliefs I had held since I was a child. Longevity is not only physical. The stories we tell ourselves shape the choices we make every single day, and changing those stories changes the habits that follow. The thread running through all of this is that none of it requires an overhaul. Diversify your movement. Add the protein. Take the calcium and vitamin D. Soften the old beliefs. These are small, accessible steps, and it is the consistency that turns them into a powerful foundation for lasting health. The goal is to turn insight into everyday habit. A Note on Health and Medical Advice Disclaimer: the information shared in this episode is my personal interpretation of insights from Dr Adam Brown, based on recent studies and advice I find beneficial for my own journey. I am not a medical professional, and this content is not intended as a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for recommendations tailored to your personal health needs. Thanks to our season sponsor Qure Skincare. articles.title: Celeste Barber “I Have No Interest in Fame.”
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Our favourite comedian has launched her own beauty brand
articles.body: It’s fitting that Celeste Barber, who has built a career out of poking fun at the absurdities of beauty and celebrity culture, is now having a good-natured crack at the beauty industry. With the launch of her very own makeup brand, Booie Beauty, Celeste is making some bold and long overdue statements about inclusivity and ageism in the cosmetic arena. “When did makeup become so bloody stressful, and why are the only beauty products targeted at women over a certain age anti-ageing creams?” she asks. For Celeste, it’s not about reinventing the wheel but simplifying it. “I love makeup, but I wanted to make something that celebrates the best version of you without the fuss.” Launched alongside business partner Claire Greaves , Booie is a tightly edited five-piece collection aiimed at women who don’t have time for lengthy tutorials or an arsenal of products. The range delivers high-quality, cruelty-free essentials that are easy to use and, crucially, fun. Known for her candid humor and ability to skewer societal norms with a wink, Barber has taken the leap from critic to creator—on her terms. Celeste on Launching Booie In our exclusive interview, Celeste dives deep into her motivations, the challenges she’s faced, and why, despite everything, she’s all about celebrating the real, unapologetic you. Celeste on Launching Booie Sig: Celeste, you’ve made a career out of skewering beauty and celebrity culture in the most hilarious way—what was the defining moment when you knew you had to jump into the beauty industry with Booie? Celeste: I really wanted to make products specifically for my audience, for my ladies who love makeup but are really overwhelmed by it. I’ve always loved makeup and wanted to create a range of products to ‘get you out the door.’ I feel the makeup game has become so complicated, and I wanted to make uncomplicated, good quality products that bring out the best version of you. Sig: You’re no stranger to bold moves—like launching Booie with no investors and tipping in your own savings. That’s a big risk! What gave you the confidence to take such a leap, and what keeps you grounded when fear or doubt creeps in? Celeste: I want to be my own boss. You have such little control as an actor, even as an executive producer; there are so many people that make decisions for you in the entertainment industry, and I wanted to answer to no one with BOOIE. I have a really clear view of what BOOIE is and who it’s for, and I didn’t want to answer to investors who are pushing me to make purple mascara because it’s what their wives like. I wanted to back myself because I really believe in Booie and what we have created. Sig: Your comedy is deeply rooted in self-deprecation and authenticity. How do you ensure that Booie stays true to that same authentic spirit while being a beauty brand? Celeste: It’s all about being the best version of you. That’s what I celebrate and what BOOIE celebrates. My main currency is my sense of humour, my relatability and ability to laugh at myself, that’s what I put out into the world, I’m unapologetically myself and I want all my BOOIE BABES to put the best version of themselves forward, however that looks. Sig: We love that Booie is aimed at women over 28 who don’t have time to overcomplicate their beauty routines. What are your go-to products when you only have five minutes to get out the door? Celeste: I use our BOOIE base face every day. Our 5 products that are…

articles.title: Bianca Dye on Panic Attacks and Life in the Spotlight
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: I caught up with the hilarious and candid Bianca Dye in the back of her Kombi van at Kingscliff. She opens up about her showbiz childhood, the wild radio years, and turning her own anxiety and panic attacks into a platform for mental health.
articles.body: Listen to the full episode here In this episode I am catching up with the absolutely hilarious and candid Bianca Dye. We are broadcasting from the back of Bianca's iconic Kombi van, parked along the stunning Kingscliff waterfront, and it is such a fun and intimate setting for this chat. Bianca and I go way back, and she has a rare gift for making you laugh and cry in the same breath. Behind all the warmth and humour is a woman who has lived through real pressure, performed through it, and come out the other side determined to talk honestly about mental health. From a showbiz family to running away to the circus Bianca grew up the daughter of stage performers, splitting her childhood between the Gold Coast and Melbourne, and showbiz was simply in her blood. After school she famously ran away to join the circus before returning within a year, and her first proper performing gigs included working as a Marilyn Monroe impersonator. It was an unconventional upbringing, and as she explains in this chat, it is exactly what gave her the fearless, do anything attitude that carried her into a demanding industry. The wild radio years From those early days Bianca worked her way up through breakfast radio to become one of Nova's most popular presenters, a foundation voice when Nova 96.9 launched in Sydney. She takes us through the rollercoaster of it all, the live energy, the long hours, and the reality of finding your voice and confidence in a male dominated industry. It is a candid look at what it actually takes to make your mark on air, and what that level of constant performance can quietly cost you. The reality of anxiety and panic attacks These days Bianca is using her platform to advocate for mental health, something she has personally faced and worked hard to overcome. She speaks openly about her anxiety and the panic attacks that came with the pressure of performing, and about the decision to stop hiding it. Her honesty is the whole point. Hearing someone so funny and so successful talk plainly about the hard days is a powerful reminder that none of us are alone in it. Turning it into advocacy with Anxiety Free Out of her own experience, Bianca created Anxiety Free, an Instagram community built to break the stigma around anxiety and offer real support to others who are struggling. With a combined following of more than 70,000 people, it has become a genuine source of comfort and connection. Her warmth, humour and vulnerability shine through in this conversation, and it is a beautiful example of taking the hardest part of your story and turning it into something that helps other people. Here is what we cover: - Bianca's early years in showbiz and radio and the rollercoaster journey that followed - How her unconventional upbringing shaped her fearless approach to life - The reality of anxiety and panic attacks, and how Bianca turned her experience into advocacy - Finding your voice and confidence in a male dominated industry and making your mark Giveaway with Qure Skincare Thanks to our season sponsors, Qure Skincare, we are giving five lucky subscribers the chance to win one of their incredible Q-Rejuvalight Pro Facewear LED Masks. articles.title: How to Prime Your Skin for Peri and Menopause
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Sigourney chats to Dr. Joseph Hkeik about how to deal with all the changes that occur
articles.body: As we celebrate Menopause Awareness Month, it’s been a joy to see important conversations being had a more inspiration about the changes that happen as we age. And thank GOD. It’s helpful too that we have advocates like Kate Winslet talking about the beauty of aging. She told Harper’s Bazaar recently “Women get more beautiful as they get older, for sure. Our faces become more of who we are, they sit better on our bone structure, they have more life, more history.” When I turned 40 a bunch of weird health symptoms sent me into a tailspin: crippling anxiety, neck and shoulder pain, reflux and bloating and insomnia that would wake me at 2 or 3am and torture me until I just gave up and got up. I also noticed hair loss and drier crepey skin which was unfairly punctuated with enormous hormonal cysts on my chin. The skin on my chest is wrinkled from sleeping on my side and refuses to spring back no matter how many ‘neck and decolletage balms’ I throw at it. It wasn’t until I started learning more about perimenopause that I realised that most of these were due to a drop in my hormones. In a bid to help myself and anyone else going through this trauma, I sat down with cosmetic physician and founder of the stunning All Saint Clinic Dr. Joseph Hkeik (who also looks after my injectables and laser) to grill him on what to expect for my skin in the coming years… and what to do about it. There’s no denying that menopause marks a transformative phase in a woman’s life. It’s not just about hormone shifts—it’s about skin changes, emotional challenges, and new beginnings. The issue is, we are only just starting to talk about it now, after years of pretending it didn’t exist. Joseph agrees: “It’s so important to talk about it. When we don’t talk about it, women start to see all these changes, and they wonder what’s wrong. They can go through depression, but if you know what to expect, you can be prepared—psychologically, mentally, spiritually, and physically.” So how do we prepare our skin (and mind) for perimenopause? Joseph shares some essential steps: 1\. Stimulate Collagen Now, Not Later. The gradual loss of collagen starts years before menopause, so addressing it early can dramatically impact how your skin looks and feels. Treatments like Radiesse and Sculptra are key for maintaining skin structure. - Radiesse is a dermal filler made from calcium hydroxyapatite that not only restores volume but also stimulates your body’s natural collagen production. “Radiesse works like a wash under the skin, stimulating fibroblasts to wake up and produce more collagen and elastin,” explains Joseph. The treatment involves injections under the skin and typically costs around $800–$1,200 AUD per session. It’s considered minimally painful, with most patients reporting slight discomfort. The results can last for 12–18 months. - Sculptra, another injectable treatment, stimulates collagen growth over time and is known for more subtle, gradual results. Sculptra contains poly-L-lactic acid, which helps the body regenerate collagen naturally. It requires multiple sessions (usually 3–4) and costs between $900–$1,200 AUD per session. Results appear more gradually over several weeks, but they last up to 24 months. Like Radiesse, discomfort is mild, with most people experiencing minimal soreness or bruising. 2\. Embrace Laser Therapy Perimenopausal skin becomes thinner and more prone to damage, making laser treatments a fantastic option. - Fraxel and Halo are popular fractional lasers that work by creating controlled micro-injuries in the skin, prompting it to regenerate. “Laser treatments create tiny columns of injury in…
