articles.title: How to Choose the Right Products for Your Skin
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Revealing best ingredients and products for every skin type.
articles.body: It's all well and good to drop hundreds on the bakuchiol, PHA or peptide-pumped super cream that we saw on Instagram, but how often does it not have the life-changing skin transformation that we were hoping for? That's because (surprise, surprise!) not everyone's skin needs the same kind of treatment. Half the battle of finding skin equilibrium is knowing what skin type you have and what your unique needs are. Here, a very straight forward guide to the basics of choosing skincare according to your skin type and concerns. Understanding Your Skin: Identifying Your Needs The first step in selecting the perfect skincare products is understanding your skin type and its specific concern s. Whether you have oily, dry, combination, or sensitive skin, there’s a routine out there tailored to your needs. One helpful method for determining your skin type is the Paper method. Simply blot your face with a clean tissue in the morning and observe the results: - If the tissue has oil from your forehead, nose, and chin (the T-zone), you likely have combination or oily skin. - If the tissue shows oil from all areas of your face, you likely have oily skin. - If there is little to no oil on the tissue, you likely have normal or dry skin. Choosing the Right Cleanser Choosing the formulation to keep your skin clean is crucial for maintaining a healthy complexion. If you wear makeup regularly, opt for an oil or balm cleanser as they effectively dissolve makeup and impurities without stripping the skin’s natural oils. For those who enjoy the squeaky-clean sensation, or you have oily or teen skin, a gel, mousse or foam cleanser is great, as it provides a thorough cleanse without leaving a residue. If you have sensitive or dry skin, a cream cleanser offers gentle cleansing while providing hydration and comfort. Additionally, if you’re always on the go or prefer a low-maintenance routine, a micellar water cleanser is a convenient option as it effectively removes dirt and makeup with just a few swipes, no rinsing required. By considering your skin type and personal preferences, you can choose a cleanser that meets your specific needs and leaves your skin feeling fresh and radiant. For makeup/sunscreen wearers here’s a cleansing oil we rate: Aesthetics Rx Anti Pollution Cleansing Oil: Ideal for those in their thirties, this decadent oil melts away makeup and pollutants, leaving the skin clean and hydrated. For clean girls here’s a gel cleanser we like: Cerave Blemish Control Cleanser: Ideal for battling pesky blemishes, this clarifying cleanser contains salicylic acid and purifying clay to target oil and impurities. For the busy/lazy among us try a micellar water: Bioderma Sensibio H2O Micellar Water Makeup Remover: this gentle micellar water effortlessly removes makeup and impurities without stripping the skin’s natural moisture barrier. Saintlouve Facial Cleansing Oil Cerave Blemish Control Cleanser Bioderma Sensibio H2O Micellar Water Makeup Remover For those who like a creamier option: The Ordinary Squalane Cleanser is a hydrating cleanser formulated with squalane to nourish and replenish dry or sensitive skins. For a decadent balm cleanser try: Eve Lom, elevate your skincare routine with this luxurious cream cleanser infused with aromatic oils to cleanse and nourish the skin. Once you’ve identified your skin type and cleansed accordingly, it’s time to address specific concerns through targeted serums and exfoliating treatments. Whether you’re dealing with sensitized skin, dehydration, or breakouts, there’s a product to suit your needs. The Ordinary Squalane Cleanser Dull Skin? Achieve luminous skin with this skincare/makeup hybrid, suitable for all ages and skin types: try Glow Recipe Watermelon Glow Niacinamide…

articles.title: The Exact Products Melanie Grant Uses to Look Flawless
articles.author: Zoe Briggs
articles.excerpt: The celebrity facialist invites us into her bathroom
articles.body: Melanie Grant represents the crème de la crème of the beauty world in a myriad of ways. From her A-list clientele, to her chic salons in Sydney, Melbourne, LA, and soon, London (as well as a biannual residence in Paris, naturellement ), to her professional partnerships with CHANEL and Augustinus Bader, she is a skin expert well-versed in luxury. In winter 2022, she adds author to her list of accomplishments, with the much-anticipated release of her beauty tome, The Modern Guide to Skin Health. Despite a hectic schedule that involves constant skin-disrupting travel, she consistently looks utterly flawless, so we asked Melanie to open up her bathroom cabinet and makeup bag and share exactly which products she uses to get her glow. As to how to create your own personalised version of her routine? Speaking with us from the south of France, Melanie tells us that being able to share her advice with a wider audience than is possible for her to personally see in-studio is exactly what drove her to writing her book in the first place. She says, "I'm so lucky to belong to an industry that champions constant innovation, but often the amount of information presented to us on a daily basis can be overwhelming. I hope that by sharing what I have learned over the past two decades of my career, I can give others the tools to prioritise their own skin health in a way that's enjoyable, easy to reference and easy to return to as we navigate the many ebbs and flows of our skin throughout our lifetimes. Taking care of the skin doesn’t need to be complicated, complex or even expensive. Great results are achievable for all of us, just by using a handful of the right products in the right way." Melanie's Morning Skincare Routine I am a bit of a purist when it comes to what goes in the hands of my clients, and I try absolutely everything on myself before it ever gets into the studios. So while I keep abreast of what’s available, I know what’s good for my skin, and find myself remaining loyal to certain products. I have a core routine that is quite streamlined, and not complicated. In the mornings, I always cleanse any residual product and sweat from overnight, usually with one quick sweep of Bioderma Sensibio H2O Micelle Solution, or for extra nourishment in winter, I’ll use a balm cleanser. Then it’s always an antioxidant, perhaps Augustinus Bader The Serum, No. 1 de Chanel Revitalising Serum, or SkinCeuticals C E Ferulic Serum. When it comes to ageing, free radicals and environmental aggressors are just as bad as UV, so it must be a serum with antioxidants which provide that protection. Next, a quick dab of eye cream, as I have really fine skin around the eyes and can get quite dark under the eyes. My final step is moisturiser and SPF, which I like to find combined in one product. I listen to my skin as to which particular products to choose for each step – for instance, if it’s winter or I am a little drier I might go for the C E Ferulic, whereas if I want something lightweight or to go under makeup, I might choose the Bader or Chanel. It’s useful to have a little skincare wardrobe, so that you can gauge your skin, and adjust your products each day or by season. For example, I will switch between a rich, occlusive crème when it’s cooler, and gel crème or lotion when warmer, but I am not just constantly bouncing…

articles.title: How to Achieve Glass Hair at Home
articles.author: Kristina Zhou
articles.excerpt: Hair that looks like a permanent ring light is cast on your hair with mirror shine.
articles.body: Glass hair demands more than just shiny locks, but rather, hair so luminous it resembles the light-reflecting sheen of glass. Think: the liquidy-smooth locks of A-listers sashaying down an elite red carpet. Whilst glass hair is highly coveted, it is also considered the most elusive to achieve. But the truth is, you don’t need a personal hair-stylist at your beck and call, or a 10-step hair routine to achieve mega-watt glossiness. Read on, as we unveil tried-and-trusted techniques to attain glass hair in the comfort of your own home, without breaking the bank. Hair that looks like a permanent ring light is cast on your hair with mirror shine. Glass Hair Ingredients The key to achieving glass hair lies in using products that are specifically designed to nourish the hair. However, don’t just believe the marketing materials – examine the ingredients list to make sure the active ingredients are backed by science. Superstar ingredients to look out for include hyaluronic acid, hydrolysed soy protein, argan oil and rosemary extract. - Hyaluronic acid is a powerful humectant that helps attract and retain water. It hydrates the deeper layers of the hair shaft - meaning it targets the root cause of damage and can provide long-lasting nourishment, as opposed to superficial hydration. - Argan oil is rich in essential fatty acids, vitamin e and powerful antioxidants such as COQ10 – making it an excellent shield to protect your hair against environmental damage. Known as a deeply nourishing oil, it helps smooth texture, tame frizz and impart a soft gleam. - Hydrolysed soy protein contains an amino acid that boosts the production of keratin in the hair shaft - this helps enhance shine, strengthen locks and boost elasticity. Keratin (a protein) is the building block for healthy hair. Locks that are low in keratin becomes dull, brittle and prone to damage. This protein helps minimise future breakage and boost the thickness and volume of hair strands. - Rosemary is a green shrub that stimulates blood flow to the hair follicles and cultivates a healthy environment for hair growth. It also has anti-fungal and anti-bacterial properties which decreases inflammation and potential hair irritation that can cause dandruff and general hair brittleness. Holy-grail product recommendation I put these scientific claims to the test and trialed a shampoo and treatment duo infused with the above ingredients: DesignME GlossME Hydrating Shampoo and DesignMe PuffME Volumising Hair Treatment. From the first wash, I immediately noticed my hair had a more luminous sheen, and previously dehydrated areas looked silkier – with static and baby hairs significantly tamed. After a solid month of trialing these products together, my hair actually looked significantly sleeker and more lustrous, even with minimal styling. I also noticed that my hair had more body and bounce, but unlike many products that add volume, my hair looked thoroughly cleansed, with a mirror-like sheen. DesignME GlossME Hydrating Shampoo DesignMe PuffME Volumising Hair Treatment Diy Hair Masks For Glass Hair Whilst there are excellent products available in store, sometimes the secret to glass hair can also be found in your pantry. I trialed several viral glass hair techniques that people swore transformed their hair from dehydrated and damaged, to glossy and gleaming - the flaxseed hair masque was the standout that actually made my hair visibly luminous. Flaxseed gel mask Benefits: Flaxseed oil contains a powerhouse concoction of nutrients and essential fatty acids such as vitamin b, magnesium, selenium and copper. Topical application helps fight frizz, increase moisture and boost hair growth. The gel also imparts a physical sheen and helps tame unruly locks giving a subtle straightening…

articles.title: Valentina Ferrer, the Powerhouse Influencer Turned Wellness Entrepreneur
articles.author: Zoe Briggs
articles.excerpt: The model, mother and former Miss Argentina prioritising health
articles.body: How to best sum up Valentina Ferrer? Miss Argentina 2014. Major model and influencer (1M Instagram followers). Along with her partner, Colombian singer J Balvin (a cool 51M Instagram followers), parents to two-year-old son Rio… oh, and the latest Tiffany & Co brand ambassadors. You know, the usual for a woman who has only just turned thirty. In amongst her whirlwind existence, Valentina was diagnosed with coeliacs disease. This diagnosis renewed her focus on her health to such an extent that she went on to co-found Kapowder, a wellness brand made right here in Australia. Here, she tells us about her blissful childhood in Argentina, why her family’s support was what gave her the confidence to travel the world, and her secret happy place (hint: its not as glamorous as you might think!). Valentina's Argentine Childhood ”I grew up in Argentina, and had a very fun childhood that revolved around nature, sports and, most of all, spending time with family. I believe my early years shaped my life in a tremendous way and helped me develop into the person I am today. That is especially true when it comes to the importance I place on wellness, staying active, and my loved ones. Valentina's Move to America Leaving my family behind in Argentina and travelling the world was a very challenging time for me. That eventually meant moving to the US to work on my dreams, which was scary as I knew absolutely no one. However, it was ultimately an amazing experience I would never take for granted. Knowing I had my family’s support made an enormous difference in my outlook. I think some key factors in how we move through challenges are the passage of time, gratitude for the good and the bad, and having patience and perseverance. Valentina's Path to Wellness I never had a specific career goal, but thought my work would ultimately involve entrepreneurship. I think landing in the world of wellness was very much shaped by all my travels, and learning from different people and different cultures. I feel so glad that my job allows for me to learn, create and innovate. The worst part about what is otherwise a wonderful career and life is that I am still based so far away from my beloved family. I start every morning with my maté, the traditional South American herbal drink, and have breakfast with my baby Rio before he goes to school. Then I do my skincare routine, take my Enlighten from Kapowder and then off to the gym I go! Valentina's Skincare Routine My skin regime varies a bit depending on the amount of time I have. I usually start with Tatcha The Rice Polish, then apply a hydrating mask, Vital Hydra Solution, from Dr. Jart. I like to keep these in the fridge for a cooling effect. Once that’s removed, I spray my face with Mario Badescu Facial Spray With Aloe, Herbs & Rosewater, and pop on some Auteur Definitive Eye Cream, which is one of my ultimate favourite products. I love when my face glows and looks very glazed, so I like to use the C.E.O. Glow Vitamin C + Turmeric Oil from Sunday Riley. Then I move on to my Definitive Restoration Cream from Auteur, which is another great product of theirs. It locks in all the hydration. When it comes to face creams, what is key for me is ‘the thicker the better’! Last but most important is SPF – I like a tinted one, and alternate between Heliocare 360 Color Gel Oil-Free SPF50+ and ISDIN Fotoprotector Fusion Water Magic SPF50.…

articles.title: I Got an Under-Eye Concealer Tattoo!
articles.author: Kristina Zhou
articles.excerpt: Did the under-eye concealer tattoo work to conceal my under eyes? Discover the process, risk, side-effects and final result.
articles.body: An aesthetic doctor once told me that "only plastic surgery" could significantly reduce dark circles. Whilst my dark circles weren't tragic, they were visible enough to make me feel uncomfortable. However, I did not want to go under the knife, so I resumed my hunt for a non-surgical treatment that could visibly brighten my sleep-deprived eyed. A few years ago I wrote an article about under-eye concealer tattoo, but at the time it was not available in Australia. Fast forward to 2023, the procedure finally landed in Australia and I immediately booked an appointment. The under-eye concealer tattoo intrigued me, because the pigment is injected into an area that "shields" the darkness from being visible underneath the skin. Although the procedure sounds effective in theory, I was sceptical as to whether it would significantly soften my dark circles. Read on, as I unearth my personal experience — from the entire process, to my final results, after-care tips and potential risks. What is an under-eye concealer tattoo? Dark circles are not located on the surface of the skin, instead the darkness is caused by visible blood vessels underneath the top layer of the skin (epidermis). Think of it like this: the blood vessels are more opaque than the skin, so the darkness can show through to the epidermis. The under-eye concealer tattoo injects nude pigment between the blood vessels (area causing darkness) and the epidermis; this essentially creates a barrier that shields the darkness from showing through to the surface of the skin. The general procedure. Tattoo Artist: Princess Lash and Brows Academy The pigment creates a barrier that shields the darkness from showing through to the surface of the skin. Before the procedure I went to New Me Sydney for this procedure. My tattoo artist (Katerina) was realistic about what the procedure could achieve — informing me that it would not completely eradicate dark circles, but rather reduce the darkness by 80 – 90%, and impart a soft-focus glow, akin to applying brightening powder. Prior to starting the procedure, Katerina marked the area where the pigment will be deposited. After examining my skin tone, she created a custom pigment that was closest to my natural skin colour. Katerina mixed a white pigment with a nude pigment; the nude pigment helps conceal the dark circles, whilst the white tone adds radiance and prevents the colour from oxidising over time. A nude pigment is mixed with a white pigment to create a custom colour. The tattooing process The first step of the actual procedure involved Katerina using needle to create micro holes under my eyes, to open up the skin in preparation for the pigment to be injected. This mechanism is similar to microneedling and helps stimulate collagen production. The pigment is injected approximately 0.3mm under my epidermis using both gentle patting motions and short strokes. Katerina recommends using one fine needle to inject the pigment, because it allows for more control and precision. Some tattoo artists use a multi-needle tool (e.g. 4 needles are inserted into the skin in one go), but this can cause an unnatural patch of colour to appear under the eyes. In many under-eye concealer tattoo videos I often saw excessive pigment spill onto the client's skin, like splattered paint. However, Katerina ensured that just the right amount of pigment was injected beneath my skin. Katerina prefers to apply numbing cream right after the first round of injecting pigment underneath the skin, because the pigment is more evenly distributed through this method. The reason? The numbing cream makes it more difficult for the pigment to be injected,…

articles.title: 8 Scents That Will Make You Feel Good
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Stunning fragrances that ooze sophistication, vibrancy and joy.
articles.body: As we embrace the transition into the cozier months ahead, it's not just our wardrobes that undergo a transformation. Often our olfactory preferences change, too. Rather than gravitating towards the traditional leafy, warm and woody scents often associated with Autumn, add one of these innovative fragrances to bring an injection of vibrance and fun into your morning. Studies have shown that the aroma of fruits and summery scents can have a profound impact on our emotions, eliciting feelings of happiness and nostalgia. There are also studies that link the spicy fragrances to improved energy. The New Fruits The fruity fragrance category used to be reminiscent of cloying teen body sprays with naff names like “Wild Berry” and “Tropical Sunset”, but no longer. Some of the most covetable perfume houses are offering much more creative interpretations of fruit. Tom Ford Bitter Peach EDP Tom Ford’s creation combines the sweetness of ripe peaches with unexpected bitter notes, resulting in a fragrance that exudes confidence and sophistication. A symphony of sophistication, it marries the sweetness of ripe peaches with as statement-making piquance that’s as bold as it is refined. Goldfield and Banks Sunset Hour Inspired by the vibrant allure of Broome, Sunset Hour is a tropical paradise that blends fruity notes with creamy coconut. There’s the lively dance of crisp pear, mandarin, and a desert peach accord with jasmine’s rich white floralcy, green mango, ginger, and coconut cream. Australian sandalwood, a close relative of the Quandong, provides a spiced-green-woodsy springboard for the fruity decadence. It’s not just a fragrance; it’s a sensory journey. Vilhelm Parfumerie Mango Skin This fragrance captures that moment when you break open a mango and lift it to your nose, inhaling the insouciance of summer, the carefree feeling of holidays. Pairing juicy mango with subtle skin musk, crafts a seriously captivating fragrance. Departing from typical fruity blends, it offers an nuanced and unique twist that will be well received on a dreary day. Pulp Byredo A true classic in the fruity fragrance domain, Pulp Byredo defies conventions with a burst of ripe fruits like blackcurrant and fig. There’s a burst of blousy ripe fruits like blackcurrant and fig, it’s juicy, mouth-watering and utterly addictive. This fragrance is a statement-maker, perfect for those who want to stand out. Si By Armani Eau De Parfum Intense This is more down the traditional cool-weather route. It begins with the succulent sweetness of blackcurrant nectar before floral tones of Rose Damascena and Davana essential oil emerge,all over a rich base of bourbon vanilla. Opulent and sensual this fragrance is perfect for those days when you want to cocoon in a cashmere wrap-like fragrance. It’s definitely noticeable, expect compliments. Ellis Brooklyn Sun Fruit This cruelty-free, vegan, and sulphate-free fragrance is an addictive daydream inducer combining a creamy blend of fresh fig, bergamot, jasmine, and vanilla. The harmonious notes of plum leaves, pear, cyclamen, mingle with coconut to evoke sun-kissed vacations. Free from animal products, parabens, and phthalates, it’s a conscious creation for indulging in the sweet escape of tropical bliss. Apply on pulse points or body for an instant getaway. Spiced Florals Fragrance Gone are the predictable floral scents of yesteryear. These innovative perfume houses are adding a splash of spice and wood to their florals, infusing traditional notes with tantalizing spices. Just as studies found that pumpkin spice boosts mood, these fragrances will also uplift the soul. Twilly d’Hermes Eau Ginger by Hermes This fragrance intertwines the vibrancy of fruity notes with the invigorating zest of ginger, creating a dazzling creation woven with peony, candied ginger, and cedar. It’s a burst of freshness,…

articles.title: I Tried Micro-Infusion at Home. Here's My Honest Review.
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Microneedling's gentler cousin has come home. Here's what happened when I stamped 24K gold needles across my skin before a big event.
articles.body: Last updated June 2026 Micro-infusion is at-home microneedling with a serum chamber built in. You stamp tiny 0.5mm gold needles across clean skin, and serum floods the micro-channels as you go. I tried Qure's system before an event. It stung a little, calmed by morning and left my skin glowing for days. If you've missed the dermarolling and stamping movement that's taken the skincare world by storm, then where on earth have you been? The idea of rolling or stamping your skin with tiny needles to create rejuvenating micro trauma and help products better penetrate has become de rigueur in dermal circles. It's even filtered down to the masses with leading skincare brands launching their own home dermarollers alongside serums to encourage the practice at home. These tools come with their own set of caveats, however. The main concern being that, in the uneducated hand, the needles can cause much more damage than intended. According to many leading dermatologists, dermarollers can drag the skin and create uneven punctures. There's also a risk of infection if they're not done in sterile-enough conditions. What is micro-infusion? Micro-infusion is a form of at-home microneedling with a serum chamber built into the device. Instead of rolling, you stamp a head of tiny hollow needles across clean skin, and serum is delivered through the micro-channels as you go. Enter Qure: a Micro-Infusion system for home use that was inspired by clinical dermastamping procedures. The 3-month Micro-Infusion Facial System kit includes six single-use heads that have hollow 24K gold 0.5mm clinical-grade needles, making it a safer and more hygienic alternative to derma rolling. It also contains six individual use serums that you fill the heads up with, as you press the stamp into the skin, the serums are distributed into the skin. This helps active ingredients penetrate the upper layers of the skin through fresh micro-channels, which is where that immediate glow comes from. (And luckily I have a discount code for you! Use this link to purchase and it will apply a 10% discount for you.) Micro-infusion vs microneedling: what's the difference? So how is this any different to microneedling? Same idea, softer touch. Traditional microneedling and dermarolling drag tiny needles across the skin to create the micro-injuries that wake up collagen. Micro-infusion swaps the roller for a stamp. That means a controlled, even depth, and far less risk of tearing the skin. Australian dermatologist Dr. Davin Lim puts it beautifully. A little stamping device, its hollow needles finer than a single strand of hair, presses tailored serums into the upper layers of the skin. At an at-home depth of 0.5mm, the magic is in the delivery. You are flooding fresh micro-channels with active ingredients, and that is exactly why the glow arrives so fast. So think of at-home micro-infusion as your glow-and-delivery treatment. A beautiful weekly ritual, not a replacement for the real thing. How to use the Qure Micro-Infusion System Twist open the chamber of the device and fill until it's half full with one ampoule of serum. Then leave the device upside down for two to three minutes while the serum travels into the needles. This is the step most people rush — don't. If the serum hasn't primed into the needles, you'll be stamping dry. While the serum is priming, wash your face and hands thoroughly. This is a device with needles, so sterility matters. Clean skin, clean hands, clean device — no exceptions. Start from the centre of your face and work outwards, using a 50% overlap technique. This creates a controlled wound healing response in the skin which in…

articles.title: These Are the Essentials Your Skin Needs This Winter
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Sig shares her cold-weather must-haves.
articles.body: Winter is coming Jon Snow and, as usual, my skin is freaking out. As someone who adores the sultry months and the way my skin looks when it's sun-kissed and dewy, I always struggle to adjust to dry, chilly air. Every time I step outside, I can feel my face being sapped of moisture and I’m starting to get those weird flaky bits around my nose, a tell tale sign of barrier impairment. Not cute. But as the saying goes, when life hands you lemons, make lemonade. Or in this case, when winter hands you dry, irritated skin, switch up your skincare routine. And trust me, I’ve tried it all. So here are my tips for fixing a freaked-out barrier and keeping your skin protected against the elements. Clean Slate First things first, let’s talk about cleansing. I used to be a big fan of those gel or mousse cleansers that made my skin feel squeaky clean. But after a few too many winters of flaky, irritated skin, I’ve learned that gentle cream or oil is the way to go. I’m currently loving the QV Ceramides Cleanser. It’s cost effective super gentle and doesn’t strip my skin of its natural oils. Plus, it’s formulated with ceramides to help strengthen my skin’s natural barrier. It’s a win-win. On the days that I’m wearing more makeup I can’t go past a cleansing oil. Current favourite? Kiehl’s Midnight Recovery Cleansing Oil. This luxurious oil transforms into a milky emulsion, melting away even the toughest makeup while leaving skin feeling nourished and hydrated. The scent of lavender oil adds a relaxing touch to my night time skincare routine that has become quite addictive. And, while muslin cloths seem to be all the rage right now (often paired with cleansing oils and creams), when your skin is sensitised they can be a little rough. Enter Sante Enjo’s eco-friendly makeup remover pads that are a must-have for anyone looking to be kinder to their skin and the environment. Made of ultra-soft microfiber, these pads gently remove makeup with just water, without the need for harsh cleansers or abrasive muslin cloths. Unlike traditional cloths, Sante Enjo’s pads are gentle on skin and won’t cause irritation, making them perfect for use with cleansing oil. With the added bonus of being reusable and long-lasting, they are a smart and sustainable choice for any beauty routine. Shop The Look: QV Ceramides Cleanser Kiehl’s Midnight Recovery Cleansing Oil Sante Enjo Cleaning Cloth Serum Saviours When the weather begins to turn you may notice some of your more active serums are feeling a little bitey. It doesn’t mean you have to ditch the active ingredients completely. Just revise your routine to introduce buffered formulas (where the vitamin A or C is minimised through encapsulation), or consider Bakuchiol which is a gentler alternative to Vitamin A. If you’re suffering from dehydration, the first serum you should double down on is hyaluronic acid. Alpha-H Hyaluronic 8 Serum is a super hydrating serum that eight different types of hyaluronic acid that work together to hydrate and nourish. The lightweight texture makes it perfect for layering under other skincare products. I’ve also recently been enjoying Kora Organics’ Noni Night AHA Resurfacing Serum with Bakuchiol: AKA “beauty sleep in a bottle.” This powerful serum is packed with natural AHAs, BHA, and bakuchiol, that work together to resurface and refine your skin while you catch some zzz’s. And finally, Aesop’s Lucent Facial Concentrate is like “wake-up juice” for your face! This serum is like a bolt of lightening for your skin, packing a powerful punch of vitamin C…

articles.title: I’m 41, Here's What I Recommend for Skin
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: My current treatment plan in all its line-blitzing, dermal-plumping glory
articles.body: Having been a beauty editor for more than half my life, I’ve been lucky enough to sample a smorgasbord of skincare and treatments. As I hurtle into my forties, I’m constantly cherry-picking weapons for my skin arsenal and dialing in different experts to help me along the way. So, here is my current treatment plan, in all its line-blitzing, dermal-plumping glory. The Big Guns For injectables you need to find someone you trust and who has your best interests at heart. I’m a huge fan of Dr Joseph Hkeik All Saint Skin Clinic in Double Bay who, as skin whisperer to some of the country’s most illustrious personalities delivers a “has-she-or-hasn’t-she?” level of work. For me, he has recommended the following treatment plan. “I believe in a less is more approach,” says Joseph. “When you’re in the right hands, little touches in the right places are often all that is needed. Most importantly, we need to preserve your authentic beauty and character.” Injectables Joseph recommends the All Saints 3-point liquid facelift, which involves injecting a small amount of wrinkle relaxing injections where needed and then a very fine wash of filler to help stimulate collagen and elastin and give a little bit of volume to the cheeks, without creating that puffed up look that some fillers give. “It’s bespoke treatment that we modify to the individual,” says Joseph. “We will increase or decrease the amount of product that we place in different areas of the face, depending on what each part of the face needs. So, in some instances, I might just really create a higher cheekbone for some people. For some people I managed to create a bigger \[apple of the cheek\]. In this way I’m manipulating your face to change with the next three to six months to what I think is going to suit you best, for you. For a guy, I’ll do it differently. For an older woman, I do it differently to a younger girl in their 20s.” Another hugely popular ‘tweakment’ Joseph recommends? Profhilo, which is being billed as the New Botox. Unlike wrinkle relaxing or filler injections, however, it’s more of an injectable moisturizer that helps prompt your own collagen and elastin production. In doing so it smooths fine lines, plumps and hydrates and also gives insane amounts of glow. “Profhilo is a simple procedure. We put these five points on your face and it hydrates your skin, creating a nice scaffold for the cells so that they function better and can create collagen and elastin,” says Joseph. Lasers Creating a uniform skin tone is key when addressing the signs of aging. Joseph suggests a course of Picoway, a laser that uses short bursts of powerful lasers to target pigmentation, acne scars, fine lines and even to remove tattoos. Clients may see a lightening of the dark pigment patches and reportedly like it because it’s quick, and not as hot or painful as some of the other lasers – particularly with the numbing cream and cool jet they use at All Saints. There’s also virtually no downtime, just a bit of a sunburnt effect. Facials Apart from the lovely relaxation aspect, a results-driven facial is great at thoroughly cleaning your skin, giving a more effective exfoliation than you can achieve at home while the facial massage can sculpt and refresh the muscles in the face beautifully. One of my favourites, the Hydrafacial is a medical-grade treatment that involves a six-step process that combines cleansing, exfoliation, hydration, and nourishment, all while delivering essential antioxidants, peptides, and hyaluronic acid. The best part is seeing all…

articles.title: Facial Massages for Plumper Lips, Brighter Eyes, Smaller Nose and Slimmer Face
articles.author: Kristina Zhou
articles.excerpt: Most effective massages to sculpt the face
articles.body: Facial massages are not just a way to relax and de-stress; they can also help enhance your facial features. Although results will vary between individuals, facial yoga instructor, Masumi, says certain types of facial exercises can lift, tighten and contour the face, in the same way that exercises can help tone and sculpt our bodies. Other proponents such as facial massage expert, Anastacia, say the results from simple facial massages can be so significant, that people often accuse herself and even her clients of undergoing cosmetic surgery. Intrigued by the viral transformations across social media, Beauticate writer, Kristina, trialled a suite of different facial massages to see whether the hype was real. Whilst some massages offered short term benefits or no results at all, she discovered a handful of effective massage techniques that made a visible aesthetic difference. Read on for 6 tried-and-trusted massages that may help you achieve your personal beauty goals -- whether it be brighter eyes, a slimmer nose, plumper lips or reduction in facial puffiness and wrinkles. How long should each facial massage step take? The recommended duration for each individual step within the massages below is 30 seconds. For example: Complete step 1 in 30 seconds, then proceed to step 2 for 30 seconds and so on. Facial Massage for Smaller Nose 1) Use your knuckles to massage both sides of your nostrils, in a circular motion. 2) Place one knuckle on each side of your nostrils. Massage upwards in a zigzag motion until you reach the lower eyelids. Then massage downwards in a zigzag motion, until you reach the nasal base. 3) Completely cover both sides of your nose (use four fingers for each side). Then slide your fingers up and down vertically. 4) Use four fingers tips from your left hand to press against the entire right area of your nose. Hold this position for the duration of this instruction. Place four fingers from your other hand on the edges of the right side of your nose and proceed to massage towards your temple in an upward, gliding motion. 5) Press your nose together by deeply inhaling – think of it as squeezing your nose together by holding your breath in. Then exhale, and repeat the “inhale-exhale” motion. 6) Use your finger tips to press the sides of your nose together. At the same time, smile widely and then purse your lips together in an “air kiss” pose. 7) Use your knuckles to pinch your nose tip inwards. 8) Start from the sides of your nostrils and use your knuckles to slide upwards until you reach the inner corner of your eyebrows. Then glide your knuckles alongside the area slightly beneath the eyebrows and also just above the eyebrows. Facial massage to reduce double chin and puffiness 1) Open you mouth widely and smile. Then press your lips together in an air-kiss expression. 2) Open your mouth widely and smile, so that your mouth is shaped like an upside down triangle. Then proceed to press your lips together whilst you close your eyes. 3) Use your tongue to circle around your teeth in an anti-clockwise motion and then clockwise manner. 4) Massage your jaw area in a circular motion, whilst your mouth remains open. Facial massage for brighter eyes 1) Massage your eyebrows in a “pinching” motion from the inner corner of your eyebrows to the outer. 2) Use two fingers to massage your temple area in an upward circular motion. 3) Place your palms on the upper third of your head and lift your palm upwards, as though you are pulling your…

articles.title: All About Emface: A New Non-Invasive Beauty Treatment
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: The minimally invasive procedure promises to lift, contour and add volume without any needles.
articles.body: A new entrant in the world of non-invasive beauty treatments, Emface, is a facial technology developed by BTL (the team behind Emsculpt) that’s designed to help improve facial tone without injections. With its unique combination of radiofrequency and electrical stimulation, it’s gaining attention as a fresh option for those seeking subtle enhancement without needles. We quiz specialist plastic surgeon Dr. Liew, who has been using Emface in his Shape Clinic for some time for his thoughts: “The Emface technology combines electrical energy and radiofrequency to create an interesting synergy,” says Dr. Liew of Shape Clinic. “It’s been well received by patients looking for ways to support skin tone and structure without injectables.” He explains that Emface is particularly appealing to those who prefer a needle-free approach. It uses High-Intensity Facial Electrical Stimulation (HIFES) combined with radiofrequency to help stimulate collagen and improve facial muscle tone. The treatment involves adhesive applicators placed on key areas of the face during a 20-minute session. According to Dr. Liew, the combination of HIFES and radiofrequency may support collagen stimulation and help maintain muscle tone over time. So how does it feel? The sensation has been likened to Emsculpt—where the muscle contractions are noticeable but not usually painful. Some people describe a pulsing sensation or mild ache, especially near the jaw or teeth area, but most find it comfortable. The typical Emface protocol includes four sessions, each around 25 minutes. Improvements are said to become visible over time, with many clinics suggesting that the full effect is seen approximately 90 days after completion. Dr. Liew explains the differentiation from traditional fillers or Botox, pointing out that, Emface is positioned as a non-invasive option that supports facial volume and tone without injections. Emface does come with a notable caveat – the cost. With a price tag around $4,500 for a series of four sessions, it’s a premium investment. However, Dr. Liew attests to its patient satisfaction, with more than nine out of 10 patients expressing contentment, even among skeptics. To learn more or to find a clinic offering Emface, visit the official Emface website here or speak with a qualified practitioner. Story by Sigourney Cantelo.

articles.title: How to Nail the Clean Girl Beauty Trend
articles.author: Zoe Briggs
articles.excerpt: A gorgeous look on every gender, age and skin tone
articles.body: TikTok excels at repackaging trends that have existed for decades. ‘Coquette makeup’? That would be glamorous ‘60s Frenchwomen, all pouty pastel lips and dramatic winged liner. ‘Cold girl makeup’ is, more or less, a love letter to the long-understood flattering effects of pink blush. And ‘clean girl beauty’? It's the 2020s version of a timeless beauty adage: looking effortlessly fabulous. It’s about stripping back heavy layers of makeup to focus on healthy skin, while still looking polished and put together. Of course, the word ‘clean’ in beauty requires an acknowledgement of its problematic nature. Concepts of cleanliness have undeniably difficult historical, racist and sexist connotations. ‘Clean’ has also come to denote a whole world of unregulated ingredient ‘standards’ and largely unhelpful ‘free-from’ ingredient lists. Happily, though, the ‘clean girl beauty’ trend, for all that its title relies on a somewhat tricky word as well as limited concepts of age and gender, is really suggesting something far more desirable and accessible for any person who wants to partake – looking like the best everyday version of yourself. And to achieve that, it’s really about getting to know your own face. (For instance, do you have skin that needs more than a sheer wash of colour to look polished? Welcome to the club! And yes, this look can still be for you.) As Mecca’s Head of Artistry Jennifer Horsley says, “you might still use a lot of different products to achieve the ‘natural‘ look – it’s really about finding products that work for you and your skin.” Let us guide you to finding them. Prep with skincare Every makeup artist in existence will tell you that pulling off a beautiful makeup look always starts with getting your skin in the best shape possible. For clean girl beauty, the skin prep is about hydrating and brightening. Step 1 – Cleansing and masking Jennifer tells us, “I think having a normal routine keeps your skin in its best state, but if I want the skin to have an glow, I’ll reach for a mask”. Start with a gentle yet effective cleanser that will get rid of debris (last night’s skincare, sweat, grime – sleeping really is so attractive) without stripping your skin and making it dry or tight. Synergie Skin’s BioCleanse Gentle Milk Cleanser is silky and softening, and rinses off easily. If you prefer a refreshing gel option, Viviology Gentle Foaming Cleanser has a lovely zingy scent and is one of the only gel cleansers I have ever enjoyed using. Neither option will sting your eyes. Once skin is rinsed and patted dry, it’s masking time. Sodashi’s Brightening Marine Mineral Mask has a thick cream texture which at first you presume will act like a traditional clay mask. However, rather than drying, cracking and drawing out impurities, it works the opposite way; skin actually drinks all of the nourishing oils in, leaving it with a nice glow. Should you want a lighter texture, consider the Snow Fox Skincare multi-layered approach. I got the most refined results (that is, my skin looked clearer and less red) using the Ceramide & EGF Treatment Orb with the Cucumber Recovery Serum, followed by the cooling Arctic Breeze Rescue Mask. Step 2 – Toners and serums Fenty Skin’s Fat Water Pore-Refining Toner Serum is on my shortlist of most aptly and delightfully named skincare products ever created. Its texture is unique in the market – it’s not a lotion and it’s not a gel, but truly suspended somewhere in between. I found its cooling, comforting nature, not to mention the plumping and illuminating effects, delightful. It’s not technically…

articles.title: How to Bio-Hack Your Skin Routine
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Taking an inside-out/outside-in approach to skincare
articles.body: The Rise of Beauty Supplements In recent years, the beauty ingestible market has exploded. Like most biological processes, scientists have found a way to support our specific health & beauty needs with potent actives that work from the inside, out. Whether it’s healthy lustrous hair, diamond-hard nails, or candle-lit-skin you’re after, there’s a beauty supplement designed to support you on your journey. While some can be cautious to extol the benefits of supplements (preferring instead to focus on a nutrition-rich diet), experts have led promising studies into the science that sits behind these formulations – particularly if your diet is lacking (1). While this inside-out approach is gaining popularity, the ultimate beauty move is to combine the appropriate ingestibles with a potent outside-in skincare routine. Wellness company, Swisse, recognized the power of combining beauty supplements with skincare and have created a protocol of pairing their premium quality beauty supplements with their high-performance skincare products. Collagen and Hyaluronic Acid Explained Aptly coined a ‘glow duo’, Swisse Beauty Collagen + Hyaluronic Acid Booster supplement is designed to help enhance skin firmness & support healthy skin from within, while the Hyaluronic 2% Vitamin B5 Glow Booster Serum, instantly hydrates and plumps the skin from the outside. Collagen has been studied extensively and there is some evidence that it helps improve certain aspects of skin health, including elasticity (2). Hydrolysed collagen in particular has been found to be better absorbed by the body (3). Pairing Supplements with Topical Skincare The Swisse Beauty Collagen + Hyaluronic Acid Booster contains hydrolysed collagen to help improve skin elasticity and Vitamin C to support collagen production, plus our favourite skincare active – Hyaluronic Acid. Using collagen plus hyaluronic acid topically has long been a way to nourish and support skin health. By adding a pump of the Hyaluronic 2% Vitamin B5 Glow Booster Serum into your mornings and evenings, you’re doubling down on skin-plumping hyaluronic acid, as well as adding soothing and moisturising Vitamin B5, which plays an essential role in protecting the skin’s moisture barrier. This serum really contains an all-star cast of hydrating actives that will result in pillowy, dewy, smooth skin that looks fresh-from-a-facial. For daily multi-action wellness and beauty benefits, Swisse Beauty have launched a Multivitamin Beauty Complex that is designed to support different aspects of our health including healthy, glowing skin. Along with marine collagen and hyaluronic acid, the product contains a comprehensive blend of vitamins and minerals, including ashwagandha, which is traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine to help the body adapt to stress, turmeric which is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine to help relieve abdominal bloating and digestive discomfort, vitamin B3 to support energy production and help relieve tiredness, vitamin C to help support a healthy stress response, and biotin and silicon to support skin health, and strong hair and nails. Designed to be taken daily as part of an ideal beauty-from-within regime, the Beauty Multivitamin Beauty Complex is designed to provide additional support to help you look your best on the outside by feeling your best on the inside. The Inside-Out Beauty Approach Taking an inside-out/outside-in approach to skincare is a sneaky way to amplify beauty benefits and ensure your skin has ample nutrients to draw on. articles.title: Miracle Hair Treatments Compared: Epres vs. Olaplex – What's the Difference?
articles.author: Kristina Zhou
articles.excerpt: They're both formulated by the same scientist – but how does Epres compare to Olaplex?
articles.body: Olaplex caused a frenzy in the beauty and hair world with a slew of imitators that flooded the market. Now the founder of Olaplex is back with a brand new invention: Epres. Both Epres and Olaplex are bond repair treatments, meaning they repair broken bonds in our hair that cause our tresses to look and feel damaged. Although the products are formulated by the same scientist, how do they compare against each other? I have tried Olaplex before and loved how healthy and full of beauty my hair felt, so I was curious to see if Epres could live up to its standards or even surpass the quality of Olaplex. Read on to discover the differences and similarities between Epres and Olaplex, from the ingredients to the application method and results. What is the common thread between Epres and Olaplex? Epres is the brainchild of Dr Eric Pressly, a materials scientist who pioneered the bond-building technology behind Olaplex. Both Epres and Olaplex offer salon-exclusive formulas, but this article will only compare the respective brand’s at-home bond repair treatments. Epres (bond repair treatment starter kit) and Olaplex No 3 Hair Perfector are “pre-shampoo” hair treatments that target the root cause of hair damage: broken disulfide bonds. Hair is mostly composed of a protein called keratin, and according to Dr. Eric Pressly, disulfide bonds help connect the keratin in our hair—consider it the essential “glue” that holds our hair together. “When our hair is wet, these are the bonds that stop your hair from breaking,” Dr Eric Pressly says. Disulfide bonds can be damaged because of chemical treatments such as hair dying, excessive heat application, rough manual force applied to the hair, or environmental pollution. When these bonds are broken, this results in brittle, dehydrated, and damaged locks (think: unruly hair, split ends, and frizz). Both Epres and Olaplex are specifically designed to repair these internal broken bonds – meaning they focus on repairing damage to the hair structure. This is distinct from conditioners that work on moisturizing and sealing the surface layer of your hair, so it gives the cosmetic appearance of smoother and softer hair. Epres Olaplex Epres vs Olaplex: What are the key differences? Application Olaplex and Epres are pre-shampoo treatments that need to be left on the hair for a minimum of 10 minutes for the technology to take effect. However, there are differences in application methods. Olaplex should be applied on wet hair, whilst Epres can be applied on dry hair. Epres contains a bio diffusion technology that enables the treatment to continue repairing hair damage, even after it has been washed off — but it can also be left on overnight for maximum effectiveness. Olaplex can only be left on for a maximum of 90 minutes. With Olaplex, you simply deposit the product straight from the bottle and onto the hair – combing the product from the roots of your hair to the ends. On the other hand, Epres comes with an atomizer spray bottle and 2 x 15ml treatment vials. You pour one vial of the formula into the spray bottle, fill the bottle with water up until the line specified on the bottle, shake the formula, spray it onto dry hair, and comb the hair for even distribution. Epres (bond repair treatment starter kit) Olaplex No 3 Hair Perfector Ingredients Although both products work to link broken hair bonds, the ingredients that do the heavy lifting are very different. Epres Epres only contains 4 ingredients (all biodegradable and vegan) and is a waterless formula. This minimalistic formulation helps preserve the strength of the formula…

articles.title: New Year New Skin: 6 Quick Ways to a Glow Up
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Sigourney charts her new favourites from lasers to LED and beyond
articles.body: I know I’m not the only one who is making “Great Skin!” a resolution this year. For me, last year offered a host of challenges, not the least of which was my skin. After battling monthly hormonal breakouts, I burnt my face with hot oil while cooking. After a night in emergency and an extended date with the Burns Unit I put my skin into rehab with very basic moisturizers and regular LED treatments. Now that it’s mostly healed, I’m on a serious quest for a glow-up (as my son would say after watching Tik Tok.) And I'm not settling for just any ol' skincare routine. I’m delving into the world of high-tech treatments and skincare gadgets that promise to hydrate, refresh and renew the complexion and I’ll share all, so we can all herald in a great skin year together. 1\. The Deepest Clean Picture this: a facial that’s like a total spa day for your face. The Hydrafacial with the JLO Booster does it all – deep cleanse, exfoliation, hydration, and antioxidants galore. Plus, that JLO Booster gives you that ‘Jenny from the Block’ glow! No pain, just pampering, and you’ll walk out looking like you’ve had a month of beauty sleep. Monthly sessions can keep that glow on point. I’ve had a few of these and every time have been blown away by the levels of both radiance and hydration I experienced afterwards. I recently had the Hydrafacial JLO Booster at Max Media Lab‘s treatment suite with Dermal therapist Mala (reel coming soon!) and went to an event that evening. I was floored that my skin looked flawless, despite all the extractions and deep-cleaning I underwent. Mala used the new SYNDEO device which is the latest high tech machinery from Hydrafacial. Your therapist is able to program your usual settings so that you get the perfect treatment every time, no matter where in the world you are. The JLO Booster is just one of the Hydrafacial collaborations that are planned – can’t wait to see what the next will be. The treatment is a game-changer in the facial space and something that I will continue to rely on for an immaculate complexion. Hydrafacial with the JLO Booster 2\. Zap and Snap One surefire way to refresh the complexion is the Cynosure Picosure Pro Laser. It’s a high-tech zapper that targets all sorts of skin issues. You can kiss goodbye those annoying pigment spots and acne scars. It also boosts collagen and elastin production so over time your skin looks better too. It’s not painful, more like tiny snaps on the skin but you can get numbing cream if you like. Best part? Minimal downtime. You might look a bit flushed post-treatment, but it’s really no biggie. For serious results, plan a few sessions, usually a month apart. I’m already booking my next series of treatments for the months ahead. Cynosure Picosure Pro Laser 3\. Injectable Moisturiser Profhilo, often termed a ‘bio remodeller,’ consists of ultra-fine hyaluronic acid injected just beneath the surface of the skin. Once injected, it disperses and forms tiny moisture pockets. Unlike typical fillers that reshape features, Profhilo doesn’t alter the contours of cheeks or lips by filling in lines. Rather, it revs up our skin’s natural production of hyaluronic acid, which tends to decline with age, aiding in retaining that youthful radiance we all covet. I swear by the injectors at All Saint Clinic in Sydney’s Double Bay. Dr Hkeik and Dr Crimpston are genies when it comes to making you resemble a fetus. It’s a great alternative to Botox if you don’t…

articles.title: A Luxurious Culinary Escape to Lake Macquarie
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: The stunning restaurant that went viral for being “fine dining without the pretence”.
articles.body: As we pull into the postcard-pretty Trinity Point Marina on Lake Macquarie on a Friday evening, we’re not really sure what to expect. The family and I are here to experience the much-talked about 8 at Trinity Restaurant and have booked accommodation in the Marina complex just a few minutes walk from the restaurant. Of course, we’ve read the glowing Google reviews and seen the glitzy Gatsby-themed sizzle-reel that went viral on social, but we still can’t quite predict the visual and culinary feast for the senses that is about to unfold before us. Inside the Restaurant Nestled 80 minutes outside of Sydney, 8 at Trinity is more than just a restaurant; it’s a haven of indulgence. Boasting a grand dining room with soaring 6.5m ceilings, sun-drenched terraces that overlook the marina, and luxury resort vibes, the restaurant offers a blend of sophistication and approachability and sets the stage for an extraordinary dining experience. After checking into our three-bedroom townhouse, complete with lavish appointments and SMEG appliances, we decide to head to the restaurant for dinner despite having a lunch booking tomorrow. After all, there’s not much else in the area, and the menu is so extensive it would take us more than a weekend to work our way through it. Meeting Owner Natalie Johnson As we noted when we drove in, the sleepy suburb of Morisset Park is an unexpected spot for a world-class gastronomic playground and resort-style marina. Yet when we walk in, the 300 seat restaurant is already packed. We’re welcomed warmly by the passionate owner and manager Natalie Johnson, who settles us into our marble table on the deck, sorts the kids out with colouring-in packs and orders me the bougiest Margarita I’ve ever seen (complete with top shelf tequila and gold leafing). Once she’s helped us order just about everything on the menu, Natalie explains that the pop-up restaurant is only the initial piece in a grand $720 million transformation of the area. Remarkably, the restaurant will all be dismantled in a few years to make way for a planned luxury hotel and retail precinct of epic proportions. “Most people thought I was crazy,” she admits as she serves us a delicate Kingfish Ceviche that, adorned with flowers, is almost too pretty to eat. “The builders said, ‘good luck with your plans,” she says, laughing. Most people thought I was crazy. The builders said, good luck with your plans. Clad in a Balmain sweater and Vuitton trainers, it’s clear that Natalie has an eye for luxury. Her career trajectory has her perfectly poised for a project of this magnitude. She started working in property development with her father at 14 then took detours through interior design and beauty therapy before landing on hospitality and opening her first restaurant at 19. As she spreads print outs of the Trinity Point development plans before us it’s obvious that this is her passion project. The $720 Million Master Plan Natalie’s husband Keith Johnson owns Johnson Property Group and has already sold most of the land on the the 23-hectare development on the southern end of Lake Macquarie. The couple are intending to create a holistic luxury resort experience, their project will include two expansive 300-seat restaurants, a 220-room hotel, a wellness and day spa, multiple bars, a pool, and 218 waterfront apartments on the marina’s edge. But for now, it’s all about building the dream, starting with this restaurant. Natalie tells me proudly that they serve 1000 people a day- incredible given how remote the location is. A Visual and Culinary Feast As we work our way through…

articles.title: Peek Inside This Fashion Doyenne's Lush Palm Beach Villa
articles.author: Zoe Briggs
articles.excerpt: Designer Heidi Middleton shares her creative venture, Artclub.
articles.body: Australian fashion royalty Heidi Middleton is relishing a creatively-charged new chapter after a period of monumental changes, both personal and professional. Having started sass & bide with co-founder Sarah-Jane Clarke as an ad hoc project in the late ‘90s, the duo sold their remaining stake to Myer in 2014 (the total sale process netted them over $70 million). Heidi and her family then moved to a château in France, giving her the time, space and artistic freedom to revaluate what she wanted, which included returning to her first love, painting. Following her split from her husband in 2017, Heidi has returned to her European palazzo-style home in Sydney’s northern beaches, where she co-parents her two daughters. She welcomed us inside and discussed her matter-of-fact approach to what makes her feel and look her best, and what exactly it is about Artclub, a semi underground, fashion-but-not-as-we-know-it venture stemming from her creative incubation in France, that brings her the most joy. Heidi’s Pared-Down Skincare Routine ”I keep my beauty regime pared down. I find that it’s as much about exercise and sleep as it is about using good products. I don’t like anything too time consuming or fiddly. I start the day by washing my face with Chanel Mousse Visage followed by Chanel Hydra Beauty moisturiser. Then I massage Bio-Oil into the back of my hands. Heidi's Signature Eye Look For both day to day and a special night out, I like a natural look but with a strong eye. I get my signature eye look very quickly by running a short, fine line of kohl pencil along the inside of my eyes – it’s a tip that a friend from Hong Kong gave me years ago. I love YSL Touche Éclat Shimmer Stick in Copper and Chanel Duo Bronze et Lumire for that healthy glow. I like things fairly simple when it comes to my hair. I have it cut at Paloma salon and use Oribe products. After my shower each day, I run COMB Manuka Honey Infused Hair Oil through the ends of my hair. Heidi's Creative Journey to Artclub I have always been very creative. As a child, I wanted be an architect or a fashion designer. My mum really nurtured my brother and my creativity by doing craft workshops at home and helping us to make things out of discarded household packaging or things we would collect from our backyard. We would spend hours drawing and painting on holidays ­– that was one of my favourite things to do. After school I studied art, and then worked in advertising as a junior Art Director for several years, before moving across to fashion. Sarah-Jane and I moved to London in the mid-‘90s and starting making clothes and selling them at a market. The demand for what we were creating became so strong that we made the decision to launch sass & bide from Sydney and selling internationally. I now run a new art and fashion brand called Artclub, and in doing so have really flipped the old fashion business model on its head. Working in this new realm is something I love. The focus is on creativity in all different mediums, rather than building a big business or on doing anything too fast. The whole thing feels more free and is much gentler on people and the planet. I can’t imagine ever going back to that traditional business model! Heidi's Playful Personal Style My style has evolved over the years, but some of the elements that remain are my love of mixing strength with beauty. I enjoy balancing the…

articles.title: These Are Your Favourite Skincare Products
articles.author: Karina Wharton
articles.excerpt: We asked and you answered
articles.body: Here at Beauticate, we have always gone straight to in-the-know industry greats to provide you with the best beauty tips and trends from those who have tried it all and, in some cases, made a career of doing so. But, dear reader, this time you are the beauty guru.
