In association with Dr. Lancer.

articles.title: Self-Tan Tips from the Stars (to Make Your Bronze Way More Believable)
articles.author: Emily Algar
articles.excerpt: Learn to tan like an It Girl.
articles.body: A little bronze can hide a multitude of skin gripes, from skin tone imperfections to cellulite. It can even make you feel slimmer, and certainly more glowy. But while the sun feels good we all know it’s enemy number one for skin. In an effort to hone your faux-tanning efforts, we rounded up the best tanning tips from our most golden-hued interviewees - because, just like us, these women can often be found dipping into a bottle to get their glow on. Here are their secrets… @chloelecareux 1\. Cheyenne: Easy Does It @cheyennetozzi If you’re new to tanning or prefer a subtler option, gradual tanners are ideal. These moisturisers with a hint of DHA (the tanning ingredient) are almost impossible to stuff up as they allow you to build up to a desired colour. Cheyenne Tozzi loved Jergens Natural Glow Daily Moisturiser so much that she became the face of their brand. Lisa Messenger and Ashley Hart are also fans of the slowly-slowly approach, opting for St Tropez Gradual Tanner. 2\. Elle: Enlist The Help of a Professional Instagram@chloelecareux For all those summer parties, a spray tan can be one of the best decisions you’ll make. Elle Ferguson is so well-known for her flawless tan that she launched her very own line of self-tanning products, so now we can all emulate Elle’s signature glow. It’s reassuring to know that even faux tanning obsessives still rely on the experts – Elle says, “I go to Tan Temple with my own mousse and get them to put it through their spray gun.” 3\. Rosie: Preparation is Key @rosiehw If you’ve decided to take on the role of tanning yourself, preparing your skin is paramount. Make sure skin is exfoliated prior, and you’ve done any hair removal at least a day before. A great tip we grabbed from bronzed beauty Rosie Huntington-Whiteley is to “put a little bit of moisturiser on the elbows and knees and around the knuckle areas so the tan doesn’t grab or stain.” She swears by ModelCo Tan in a Can. 4\. Lara: Love Your Glove Instagram@laraworthington In the form of a tanning mitt, that is. Perennially bronze-limbed Lara Worthington knows that using a mitt to apply your tan can make the task a lot less daunting: “I start my tanning from head to toe and I always use a mitt, otherwise it just gets everywhere.” Use a velour glove that allows you to see exactly where the product is going and erase streaks as you go, without turning your palms orange. 5\. Erika: Contour Your Body Instagram@erikaheynatz In the same vein of using darker shades to contour your face, you can also use them when fake-tanning. Erika Heynatz loves this trick – and says she had it done with tanning guru Katrina Brown. “I had a great contoured tan once before a photoshoot at The Bronzing Boutique – it shaved off a few kilos and gave me a free six pack.” 6\. Match Your Makeup Instagram@lozcurtis One crucial step many forego when they have fake tanned is to match their makeup. Firstly, you’ll need to ensure your foundation matches your new colour. Bahar Etminan loves to apply JBronze Illuminator to bring some life to her face when she has fake tan on. Beauty vlogger extraordinaire Lauren Curtis is also a well-documented fake tan devotee (she uses Loving Tan Dark Mousse). She says that different shades of cosmetics can either enhance or wash out your skin tone. “Lipstick in a nude salmon pink looks great against tanned skin,” she says. Make the most of your burnished glow by introducing…

articles.title: 6 Products to Help Pollution-Proof Your Beauty Routine
articles.author: Marina Gainulina
articles.excerpt: And help protect your skin from premature ageing.
articles.body: Unless you’ve spent the better half of the past decade on an untouched, remote island, daiquiri in hand and blissfully unaware of our increasingly industrial world – in which case, we’re green with envy - no doubt you’ve heard about the corresponding rising levels of pollution. This is especially concerning for those of us who are, instead, livin’ la vida loca in the city. Unbeknownst to us, airborne dirt particles are busy at work, damaging the precious skin and hair barriers, breaking down collagen and ageing us. With Sydney and Melbourne currently congested by an unrelenting bushfire smoke haze - which scientists predict will last the whole summer - we’ve rounded up some hero pollution-proofing beauty products that we’ve tried and loved, and which now remain in heavy rotation. If you would like to contribue to the Australian bushfire relief efforts, please consider donating to the CFA, RFS and WIRES. Allies of Skin 1A All-Day Mask There are few things we love more at Beauticate HQ than stumbling upon the latest beauty innovations, and this is one such product. For those of us who love a mask but loathe the messy wash-off process sink side, you’ll love this world first leave-on mask​​. Working as a day treatment, this is my go-to when my skin is looking worse for wear. Use in place of moisturiser, underneath makeup, and let the powerful time-release formula work its magic in securing your skin’s defences against environmental pollutants, whilst simultaneously combating signs of stress and fatigue. Allies of Skin 1A All-Day Mask Biossance 100% Squalane Oil Biossance 100% Squalane oil If you haven’t heard of squalane oil, you’re not alone, but you are missing out. It mimics the lipid squalene (with an “e”), a moisturiser that is naturally produced by our skin cells, but less so with age. What secured this product a permanent shelfie spot (as well as being a trusty travel buddy) is the fact that this single-ingredient, lightweight oil is a hard multi-tasker – slather on your face, body and/or hair ends for weightless hydration and locked-in moisture. Skin Regimen Cleansing Cream Don’t underestimate the importance of the humble cleanser – it’s a crucial step in any skincare routine, and this non-drying cream is a fab option to do just that, and then some. It detoxifies the visage from nasties that accumulate on skin on the daily, effectively removing makeup, SPF, dust and excess sebum. Loaded with an exclusive mix of organic superfood extracts (think spinach, maqui berry and wild indigo), it’s gentle enough to do a thorough double cleanse with, which rebalances the skin without over stripping it – paramount when prepping for a clean slate on which to lather potent serums and the like. Skin Regimen Cleansing Cream Peter Thomas Roth Mix Mask & Hydrate Skincare Set Peter Thomas Roth Mix Mask & Hydrate Skincare Set Need a quick beauty fix, but can’t make it to your facialist? This latest set from PTR makes multi masking easy. Few products can deeply cleanse or moisturise the way a mask can, and with this set of five masks, plus a bonus 30% hyaluronic acid moisturiser, the hardest part is choosing which one you’ll slather on first. Our current fave to fend off the effects of pollution is the Irish Moor Mud mask, with volcanic ash and activated charcoal which draws out deep-set impurities, and minimises the look of pores. Whichever one you choose, your skin will be sure to thank you. Naturally Serious Cold-Pressed Peel Pads Cardinal skincare sin? Sleeping with your makeup on. Enter these pre-soaked pads, which have proved to…

articles.title: The Injectable-Free Lip Cheat That Fashion Influencer Pepa Mack Loves
articles.author: Zoe Briggs
articles.excerpt: Petra Mackova a.k.a. sleek fashion maven Pepamack shares her pared back, skin-focused approach to beauty.
articles.body: Petra Mackova is the woman behind Pepamack, the blog and Instagram ode to her sleek, minimal style that her more than 900,000 followers can’t get enough of. Here, she tells us about prioritising skincare well ahead of any makeup, and a bad experience with hair extensions that encouraged her to ditch them in favour of keeping things simple – an appropriate fit with the rest of her aesthetic. Pepa's Skin-First Daily Routine “My daily routine starts and ends with my skincare. I wash my face in the shower, only ever using a cream face wash because I have a dry complexion. I use tonic, followed by day cream and finish it with 40+ sunscreen. I have quite dry and delicate skin around my eyes, so I apply argan oil before my eye cream every day and night. I always prefer days without makeup, however if I wear anything it’s usually a very thin layer of foundation. I’m obsessed with a clean face. It’s the best feeling after coming home after a long day, to take a shower and wash your face. I follow it up with some beautifully rich moisturiser. My beauty look is minimal, always with a light brown lipstick. I like simple, easy to use products, keeping skin at the forefront. My favourite feature would have to be my eyebrows. When I do my eyebrow makeup, it completely changes my look. Sometimes I don’t wear other makeup, but I always do my eyebrows. For a night out, I love soft black kajal pencil. I put it on my top lid only and smudge it slightly so that the line is not too sharp. Also, I apply a double layer of mascara. @pepamack The White Pencil Lip Trick My top beauty tip is to use a white Burberry pencil to contour my lips. It’s tried and true, and always creates a great effect. I used to love doing makeup for all my girlfriends and think I learned my tricks there. When we went out on the weekends, there were bookings required and a line out the door! It was something that we loved doing together and was always a ritual on a night out. My mom doesn’t actually wear any makeup. She has the most beautiful skin! She would never judge me for wearing makeup or experimenting at a young age, but she was forever teaching me how important it is to really care for my skin (and to always remove makeup before bed). She is a big fan of natural herbal tonics and oils, which has influenced me to use them in my routines as well. Fine Hair and Minimal Styling I’m quite simple in my hair technique and not a big fan of styling products. My hair is very fine so I wash it almost every day. I use conditioner only occasionally, just because I prefer more volume, which I think you can only achieve when foregoing the conditioner. I don’t need to use any other products after that. My hair was also the source of my most embarrassing beauty moment. I once on a date, wearing clip in hair extensions. All was going well until my date touched my head and absolutely freaked out! Pepamack I still can’t believe my job every day is to do what I love. I have always been interested in fashion, styling and fashion photography, but there weren’t many options available to me when I was younger. It was something that I was continually working on as a hobby and was lucky enough to be able to progress that into my…

articles.title: The Desk Drawer Beauty Essentials You Need This New Year
articles.author: Tess Schlink
articles.excerpt: They make getting through the work day a lot more enjoyable.
articles.body: Because you still need a bit of TLC while you’re working hard. Whether you’re a student or your very own Girl Boss, these are the must-have products you need to get you through the day looking polished. They make getting through the work day a lot more enjoyable. Help At Hand If your job requires sitting at a computer typing the day away (ditto), it’s important to keep your hands in good nick and to thank them for all the hard work they do. And especially if your workplace blasts the air conditioning or heating 24/7, you’ve probably been a victim to dry and cracked skin – not ideal. A nourishing hand cream like The Body Shop's Hemp Hand Protector is just the ticket you need. THE BODY SHOP HEMP HAND PROTECTOR Great Hair Day Scünci Dent-Free Spirals Sometimes getting the job done requires pulling your hair out of your face and locking into focus mode. But if you’re like us and would rather die than ruin a great hair day with a standard hair tie, a fab alternative are Scünci Dent-Free Spirals – they don't leave those pesky dents in your strands, meaning the 'do you worked hard to achieve looks as good as when you first styled it. Pucker Up Lip balms in desk drawers are par for the course, so may we suggest something a little more original for your own stash? We're currently loving Lanolips Lanostick Lemonaid Scrubba Balm – a lip scrub and balm in one, that makes getting exfoliated and soft lips that much easier. The fact it's scented with citrus-y goodness is just another reason why we're obsessed. Lanolips Lanostick Lemonaid Scrubba Balm Get Hydrated BKR Water Bottle It's all well and good to have the best of intentions to hit your 2L of water a day target, but executing said goal can be a little tricky sometimes – so may we suggest a chic tool to keep you motivated? This water bottle from BKR is probably the most gorgeous one we've seen, and is eye-catching enough to remind you to keep your fluids up. We also rate that the rubber covering prevents cold water condensation from wetting other items at your desk or in your bag. Up The Volume Dry shampoo helps cure all manner of sins, doesn't it? From fixing limp, fourth-day locks, to adding much-needed volume to lank roots, it's a perennial saviour. We've always loved Batiste, but we're particularly partial to the tiny versions that fit so neatly into our desk drawer beauty edit. Perfect for whipping out for use when unexpected after-work drinks pop up. Batiste Dry Shampoo Set It Straight Hourglass Ambient Lighting Powder Much like oily hair, oily skin is never cute. If you find that your skin gets oily as your day goes by (as many skins, even drier types, tend to do even just a little), we recommend keeping a compact of translucent setting powder to matte down patches of shine. If you're nervous about things looking too cakey, opt for a very finely milled powder – the Ambient Lighting Powders from Hourglass are roundly adored by makeup artists worldwide. Story by Tess Schlink and Daniella Giancarli

articles.title: Celebrating Strong, Successful and Smart Women with Armani Beauty
articles.author: Tess Schlink
articles.excerpt: Introducing #FamigliaArmani
articles.body: At Beauticate, we're passionate about supporting clever, hardworking and stylish women (in fact, we've dedicated a whole section of the site to profiling them). So we recently teamed up with Armani Beauty, a brand that encapsulates these same values, to hold an intimate event at Sydney's Koda Cutters, where we launched the \ FamigliaArmani — a collective of said amazing women, in order to celebrate their success in the chicest way imaginable. An afternoon of blowdries courtesy of the Koda Cutters team, plus beauty consultations by the Armani MUAs, followed, where guests were introduced to the ideal products to match their non-stop lifestyles (you can understand why the effortlessly glowing Luminous Silk was a crowd favourite). Add some Pommery, delicious canapes from the clever Plated By Sava team, and architectural floral installations by Lisa Madigan (they were jaw-dropping), and it made for the perfect end to an amazing year. articles.title: These Are the Exact Products We Swear by to Travel in Style
articles.author: Beauticate Editorial
articles.excerpt: How we travel in style.
articles.body: For beauty lovers, part of the joy of heading on holiday is in choosing the products to bring: from the on-point in-flight skincare routine, to curating the perfect beachside makeup edit, it's a vital (and completely pleasurable) part of any trip. But it can be a fine line between being prepared for every possible scenario, and feeling like a packhorse swerving through the throngs of travellers at the airport (we’ve all been there). To avoid falling into this trap for any upcoming trips over Christmas (lucky you!), we’ve reflected on some recent trips and are sharing our tips and travel must-haves for a streamlined but functional holiday edit. Sigourney Cantelo, Editor and Founder I’ve been travelling a lot this past year but I probably put the most beauty-prep into my trip to Costa Rica and LA. For long-haul flights I always take a clear zip-around beauty bag. My new favourite is monogrammed from The Daily Edited. One side is jammed (I can barely zip it up) with minis – which change every trip I take. For Costa Rica it was mix of Ultraceuticals minis, Minenssey Flannel Flower Absolute, a baby Bioderma Sensibio, Biologique Recherche and Weleda Skin Food and It Cosmetics CC for touch-down. Style-wise I’ve spent years honing my transit attire as I hate wearing jeans and can’t be bothered to change. I wear Bassike pants on the plane (they’re basically trackies but more stylish) with Gucci slippers and a Mia Fratino cashmere cardigan. I love the Samsonite Cosmolite luggage as it’s super lightweight, and I’ve also just got the amazing Away Luggage cabin set. These specially designed bags (which you can stash your beauty bag and laptop in) fit perfectly over the handle of your roller so there’s no spillage and also no need to undo your whole roller bag to take out the laptop and beauty bits. The other thing I can’t travel without? My MacBook Air in Rose Gold. I am glued to it from the moment I set up in the lounge (glass of wine in hand) to the second I finally give in and watch a movie several hours into the flight. I go into hyper-productive mode when I travel, and always manage to smash out several stories and all my email correspondence when I have no WIFI to distract. Once I’ve done all my work I’ll reward myself with a nice gooey sleep mask like La Prairie one, which I get samples of from their counter as they don’t do it in travel size (it also smells like lavender), followed by a rom com and a glass of wine. Then I’ll pat in the excess, spritz a little Chanel Sublimage spray and tuck myself in for some shut-eye. It Cosmetics Your Skin But Better CC+ Cream Gucci Loafers Minenssey Flannel Flower Absolute Away Everywhere Bag MacBook Air in Rose Gold La Prairie Skin Caviar Luxe Sleep Mask Tess Schlink, Features Editor My most recent trip abroad was to visit my fiancé’s family in France and Switzerland, and a great deal of (some might say obsessive) thought went into packing. My in-flight beauty routine is always a highlight, adding a little interest to a tedious long-haul trip and keeping skin in good nick. I like to pack all my beauty bits into my Anya Hindmarch vanity, cleverly divided into ‘take off’ and ‘touch down’ sections to separate skincare and makeup upon arrival ( The Daily Edited also do a similar – and monogrammable – version). Exfoliation in transit is made easier with the portable Alpha Beta Universal Daily Peel pads – they come individually…

articles.title: Party Style Essentials – Sigourney's Edit
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Plus, a little bit of sparkle – just because.
articles.body: Is it just me or does the silly season just get sillier every year? (I just counted and I have SEVEN events in the next week!) Not only does this time of year require consistent attention to beauty maintenance and a rotating wardrobe of “fun and festive” pieces, you have to be ready to drop everything at a moment’s notice and tong your hair/craft a smoky eye all with one hand holding a margarita. Frankly, it’s all a bit stressful. In an effort to simplify the whole party-dressing process for you, I thought I’d round up a few of my favourite things (and phone numbers) that I have on high rotation when the proverbial glitter hits the fan. The Party Pieces For events I try to embrace colour or texture for a point of difference from my workday wardrobe. And of course, champagne – the ultimate party must-have The Beauty Groundwork When the calendar is filling up fast and you can foresee a string of social events, save yourself time and energy by scheduling in a few key beauty treatments beforehand. Case in point: lash extensions will save you many minutes in mascara or false lash application and removal. (I swear by Love Those Lashes ph: 1300 LASHES in Sydney’s Paddington for a glamorous yet natural-looking flutter). I have a full set of hybrid Russian Volume lashes. A good gel mani in glossy red will mean you don’t have to worry about chipped digits (I alternate between the luxurious Jocelyn Petroni (ph : 9363 3662) experience and a quick Sunday afternoon job at T-Luxe Beauty in Paddington (ph: 9332 3121). Sometimes you have to be a little high maintenance to be low maintenance. Magic makeup Add a little sparkle to your makeup kit with these fun festive buys. Yves Saint Laurent Tatouage Couture Chanel ÉCLAT LUNAIRE Oversize Illuminating Face Powder Clarins Water Lip Stain Tom Ford Shade and Illuminate Powder Duo Urban Decay Heavy Metal Eyeliner Tatcha Luminous Dewy Skin Mist Story by Sigourney Cantelo. Photography by Alice Mahran. Hair and makeup by Jess Diez. Shot at Manly Pavillion.

articles.title: Our Best Party-Proof Beauty Buys
articles.author: Kristina Zhou

articles.body: Who doesn't want luminous skin, great hair, and fab eye makeup? While these are all coveted year round, with the festive season around the corner, they certainly shoot up on our priority list. The Beauticate team reveal the products they're entrusting to put their best face forward during the Christmas and New Year period. From the ultimate secret to glossy skin, to the perfect multi-functional makeup palette, down to the skincare product that banishes clogged pores - these products will help you shine all festive season.
