articles.title: Laura Enever, Pro Surfer
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: The pro surfer chats her beauty routine and career goals.
articles.body: Warm, honest and with a calm wisdom way beyond her 23 years, Laura is a joy to talk to. She invited us into her family’s Northern Beaches home, impressed us with a superb cannonball into the backyard pool, and while we nibbled on her mum’s cookies she revealed how she combats the most skin-sapping, sun-burny, hair-frying conditions imaginable on a daily basis. Only days after our interview Laura won the Australian Open Surfing Title - proving she is just as focused and inspired as ever by her sport. Laura's Life as a Professional Surfer “My office is the ocean and it still changes every day… Some days it’s rainy and cold and a bit like, ‘ehhhh’ but you still get that same thrill. You get out there and sometimes it could be just one wave that could make the session horrible, but then you do just one thing, ride that one wave, and you’re like, ‘Oh that felt really cool.’ Being in the ocean, and going under the waves, it’s always so exciting. I’ve got so much energy and I’m a big adrenaline junky; I just love challenges so being able to work with the ocean is just unbelievable. The sun, particularly in Australia can be so harsh, so when I’m surfing or on the beach all day I always make sure I protect my skin. Laura Wears Wetsuit by Billabong Laura Swears by Moisturising Treatments to Save Her Strands Laura’s Hair Care for Sun and Salt It’s so funny because I go surfing in the sea salt… I come out, wash my hair, and the first thing I put back in it is sea salt. I love the feeling of the texture that you get from the ocean, but I also love to have clean hair as well. Leaving the sea salt in there after being in the water all day, can be damaging on the hair, so I come home, condition and use a little hair mask and put the sea salt back in. I also love volume in my hair so I’m always using the Batiste Plumping Powder, or Eleven I Want Volume, or Leave In Foam. When I was younger I learnt the hard way with my hair I learnt what damage the sun and ocean can do. My ends were just frizz, so it took a long time to come back from that… I just became very aware \[about using treatments regularly\]. Right now my favorite shampoo and conditioner is Eleven I want Body Volume. So I’ll use the shampoo and conditioner and then the treatment. Sometimes I use the I Want Body Three Minute Repair just as a conditioner as well. Eleven and Batiste Products Keep Her Hair Textured Laura Consciously Keeps Her Diet Healthy and Natural I actually live a very healthy lifestyle… I usually have an apple with peanut butter and coffee in the morning. Then after I come home from surfing, I’ll have a smoothie with protein powder, kale, spinach and maybe a little bit of banana. I was off and traveling for six months last year and I used to travel with my blender for the first couple of months. I had a little mini NutriBullet but then I had too much stuff, so I had to let it go. Fragrance, Diet and Healthy Living I use Old Spice deodorant… My dad wore it, so if I smell a guy with it on, I really like it. I put the Old Spice on, and my Tom Ford Black Orchid over top, creating my own smell!It’s funny, it’s actually been really…

articles.title: How to Do Undone, Beachy Hair
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Tousled beach waves are one of the season’s most in-demand hair looks. While you want them to look as if you just rolled out of
articles.body: Tousled beach waves are one of the season’s most in-demand hair looks. While you want them to look as if you just rolled out of the ocean, they do require a bit of nifty work with the GHD. We caught up with hair maestro Brad Ngata who demonstrates the process on the beautiful Tatyana. Here’s what you do… beauticate Loves…tatyana Gillam by Jake Terrey Step 1: Blowdry with Volume “Smooth the natural texture out of the hair to just get a nice, clean consistency,” says Brad. “I’ve just used a little bit of root volume spray, a mousse, for a little bit of grip into the hair and then we’re just smoothing it out. The trick to a smooth shiny blowdry is to direct the nozzle of the hair dryer down the shaft of the hair with a big round barrel brush.” Step 2: Create Waves with an Iron “Use either a straightening iron like I did here, twisting the hair back on itself,” says Brad. “or I’ve recently discovered Ego Professional Twist – a new tool to the market that has a series of bobbles along the length of the wand creating waves but even heat distribution. Take sections about 4 cm x 4cm and from the mid length wrap the hair away from the face run the iron or tong up and down the hair like a bungee jump this gives hair “movement” be sure over curl the ends , its OK if they are left straight. Do this pattern around the head till all the hair is styled. I like L’Oreal Professional plus a nifty setting lotion that locks in the movement while protecting from heat. Important to let the hair cool down completely this gives you a longer lasting curl/movement Step 3: Create Grit and Texture with Hair Powder “Sprinkle some L’Oreal Professionnel Texture Dust within the hair this will give you the Beach texture,” says Brad.” Use your fingers to massage it into the roots, creating volume and ‘oomph’. Step 4: Shake it Out Next you want to loosen the curls. “I like to use a large tooth comb or fingers to rake out the set and break the hair up giving a relaxed finish.” Says Brad. Shop the Look: ghd Ceramic Vented Radial Brush Ego Professional Twist Curler L’oreal Professional Texture Dust Story by Sigourney, photography by Jake Terrey, hair by Brad Ngata and Makeup by Desiree Wise.

articles.title: 50 Shades of Grey Eyeshadows
articles.author: Ashley Ropati
articles.excerpt: As the most loved up holiday of the year creeps up on us once again, there’s absolutely no need for Cupid’s bow when it comes
articles.body: As the most loved up holiday of the year creeps up on us once again, there’s absolutely no need for Cupid’s bow when it comes to finding the perfect date night eye palette. In a bid to pay homage to the recent release of 50 Shades of Grey, we’ve collated the smokiest and arguably sexiest shades you’ll ever lay eyes on, because nothing says ‘come hither’ quite like a sultry gunmetal lid. beauticate Loves Backstage Makeup Looks at Guy Laroche and Diane Von Furstenberg Behold the crème de la crème of palettes and paint pots to really get you in the mood. Chains, whips and leather optional, of course. Best Luxury Grey Eyeshadow Palettes Boasting four different textures of the same smoky shade, this glittering eye shadow Quattro deflects microscopic pigments for an iridescent effect that’ll last for hours. Givenchy Le Prisme Yeux Mono Eyeshadow in Black Oh la la, nothing says courtship like couture. This ready-to-wear five-colour combo encompasses the perfect shades of matte and satin grey, while blending seamlessly to the eyelid upon application. Yves Saint Laurent Couture Palette in Tuxedo Keep it smoldering with a dark and ashy eye. Highly pigmented for high intensity, build up for a moody hue to make the ultimate statement. Finish with a lashing of Eyes to Kill Mascara and you’re good to go. Be warned, not for the faint of heart. Giorgio Armani Eyes to Kill Solo in Black Light Cream and Stick Grey Formulas For those not wanting to dive in head first, take a subtler route to smoky. The famed Chubby stick for eyes provides a soft creamy finish and muted metallic colour. Simply smear and stare with the ease of use of cream-meets-mousse. A creamy hue of slate will speak volumes about the wearer and has never made the metallic smoky eye quite so attainable. Chanel Illusion D’ombre Eye Shadow in Mirifique Multi-Purpose Smoky Eye Kits The reigning queens of multi-purpose beauty, Benefit’s brow and eye duo make late night (or early morning, depending on your disposition) eyes easier than ever. Comprising of their famous brow zings, tiny tweezers and three complementary smokey shades; the walk of shame doesn’t look quite so shameful now, does it? Benefit Smokin’ Eyes Sexy Eye and Brow Make-over Kit How to Build a Smoky Grey Eye Arguably a must-have in any beauty guru’s kit, Naked Palettes will leave you spoilt for choice. If you’re after a deep gradient eye that’ll go the distance, cover the lid with Gunmetal grey and work the shade Creep into the outer crease of your lid and beneath the lower lash line for a smoke n’ smolder. Naked Eyeshadow Palette No.1 by Urban Decay Story by Ashley Ropati. Have you tried any of the above products? What did you think?

articles.title: Alice McCall, Fashion Designer
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Free spirited, feminine and fun, fashion designer Alice McCall welcomed us into her eclectic terrace to muse on the beauty secrets she has learned over ten years of design.
articles.body: Free spirited, feminine and fun, fashion designer Alice McCall’s personality perfectly matches her whimsical designs. Her eponymous label celebrates its 10th anniversary this year and has cemented itself in the style lexicon of trendsetters both here and overseas with the likes of Kendall Jenner and Margaret Zhang being spotted in the label. With her titian hair and bold, bohemian style, the mother-of-two has a natural approach to grooming, pairing a passionate yoga practice with coterie of tricks picked up during her travels. She recently welcomed us into her eclectic Eastern Suburbs terrace and, while corralling daughters Wilde Rose (7) and Hopi (2) into a few impromptu family portraits, mused on the beauty secrets she’s learned. Alice Wears Off-the-shoulder Dress from Her Own Label Alice's Fashion Career Beginnings I moved back to Australia in 2002… And I remember I was in Byron Bay over New Years, it was literally one of those times when I woke up one day and I was like, “I’ve got to go out on my own.” I got a whole collection together and by May 2003 I launched at Fashion Week in Australia. David Jones picked me up straight away, I was picked up by The Corner Store, we got about 30 stockists in Australia. It’s really landmark and it makes you think about how far you’ve come and where you’re going. I was a stylist for ten years in London, doing a combination of fashion, music and advertising. And I had a great time working with people like Destiny’s Child, Natalie Imbruglia and doing Nike campaigns, but I just knew I wanted to work for myself. Alice's Skincare and Fragrance Favourites I’m a Crème De La Mer girl I really love their moisturiser and I’ve used it for years. I’m quite dry skinned but it’s rich and I feel like it lasts all day. I’m quite frequently travelling and I always stock up when I’m at the airport. I love to go for facials too, I go and get a good old ‘face hoover’ microdermabrasion at Heber Davis in Broadway. I think to just have that ‘new skin’, it’s wonderful. In Her Makeup Bag - MAC, NARS and Rae Morris Brushes In Alice's Leopard Purse: Playful Sunnies and Cheek Stain Alice's Love of Rose and Scent Rose is good for the heart… So I love anything with rose essential oil. I use an Aveda rose oil on my face and for everything else I go to Mecca. That’s where I stock up. I get the Diptyque perfume, I wear Rose or Fig and I love the Diptyque candles. I’ve also got a wonderful new moisturiser I’ve started to use from Mecca with rose essence. I love Aesop as well, they use rose quite a bit. It’s divine, and Aesop do great oils. I like all natural products. I use a Clarins toner and cleanser, as I’m all about hydrating products. I’ve been going to Desmond and Molly Jones… For my colour and I touch it up myself. My hairdresser mixes this wonderful pink for me and then I’ll take it away. It’s so easy because you’re using it as a conditioning treatment at the same time. So you leave it in for half an hour and it conditions, so you get that real gloss. It’s a two in one with the colour and the condition, it’s perfect actually. Alice Captures Special Moments with Her Canon G15 Pom Pom Slippers from Mykonos and Colourful Makeup Alice's Makeup Tricks I think cheek stains are really good Benefit does good ones. A trick I leant was from a…

articles.title: The Best Beauty Tips and Hairstyles from Rom Coms
articles.author: Chrisanthi Kaliviotis
articles.excerpt: A cupid’s arrow away from the long-stemmed roses and fluffy teddy bears, we are celebrating Valentine’s Day sans le mush, with our favourite beauty moments
articles.body: A cupid’s arrow away from the long-stemmed roses and fluffy teddy bears, we are celebrating Valentine’s Day sans le mush, with our favourite beauty moments from Rom Coms throughout the decades. From the Queen of Romantic Comedies, Ms. Julia Roberts (who features in two of our favourites) to our own home-grown Rose (Byrne that is), we have plucked the best beauty and hair from the funny and oft romantically challenged darlings of the silver screen. Beauticate Loves Richard Gere and Julia Roberts in Pretty Woman (1990) Pick up the rose petals and charge the champagne to the ladies who made us laugh and cry; love (and laughter) is in the air. Notting Hill – Anna Scott Like Julia Roberts, Anna Scott is America’s Golden Girl, lighting up the big screen with a bouncy, blow-waved mane, a wallet boasting only big bucks (the million dollar variety) and most importantly that smile – far-reaching, sweeping, glistening and white. Follow the textbook looks by injecting some poof into your mane with a root booster, paint eyes in cocoa hues and most importantly (try) to recreate those lips, using a nude, lip-enhancing lip liner like ModelCo’s. She is after all, just a girl, standing in front of a boy, asking him to lover her. Sigh. Shop the Look: Modelco Lip Enhancer Illusion Lip Liner Crest 3d Whitestrips Vivid Lea Journo Pouf Root Booster Anna’s Perfect Gift: Aerin Parfum Rose De Grasse Love Actually – Juliet The beautifully ethereal and most eloquently spoken Juliet is just lovely; an English rose who bloomed in the hilarious romanticism that was Love Actually. Dabble in the beauty of this darling with a dewy and radiant complexion, a pretty shell-pink pout and of course, big yet fastidiously shaped brows. Juliet, you are perfect to us too. Shop the Look: Chanel Rouge Coco Hydrating Crème Lip Colour in Liaison Guerlain Eyebrow Kit in Universal Juliet’s Perfect Gift: Bella Freud Loving Candle When Harry Met Sally – Sally Albright Like Julia, Meg too, is the darling of romantic comedies; When Harry Met Sally has become Rom Com folklore, with the quirky and unceasingly cute Sally Albright becoming one of the most eminent characters in cinematic history. Simmer like Sally with flicked-out, slightly undone curls whilst paring down the garish 80s tones (bright blue eye shadow – eek!) and using a softer sky blue harmonised with a gentle blend of pink across cheek and lip. We’ll have what she’s having. Shop the Look: Cloud Nine the Wand Stila Eyes Are the Window Shadow Palette – Body Clarins Multi Blush Crème Blush in Candy Sally’s Perfect Gift: Sarah and Sebastian Love You the Moon and Back Gold Ring Pretty in Pink – Andie Walsh Long before the Delevingne’s or Ms. Miller, Andie Walsh in Pretty in Pink was the original ‘it’ girl of the 80s. Ringwald’s Andie became somewhat of a pin-up, a cult character whose fashion and beauty notes were mimicked for years to come, with the film a great influencer in modern popular culture. Flashback to Andie’s signature look with a red rinse, offset with pink-hued (naturally) beauty, flushed cheeks and a swipe of salmon on lips. You’ll be pretty in pink in no time. Shop the Look: De Lorenzo Fire Red Shampoo MAC Mineralize Rich Lipstick in Style Surge Andie’s Perfect Gift: Sophia Webster Nicole Pink Fur Heel How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days – Andie Anderson Kate Hudson’s Andie Anderson was equal parts charming as she was hilarious. The quirky and perennially glow-y Andie radiated, that lemon dress moment a most magical one which made us weak…

articles.title: The Sag Award's Beauty Trend: Origami Hair
articles.author: Ashley Ropati
articles.excerpt: Awards season comes with the usual red carpet winners. What we’ve learnt to expect aside from Meryl Streep’s predestined Oscar nod, usually reads as follows:
articles.body: The SAG Awards Japanese Beauty Trend \ \ \ Awards season comes with the usual red carpet winners. What we’ve learnt to expect aside from Meryl Streep’s predestined Oscar nod, usually reads as follows: the smokey eye, delicately-tonged hair, golden tans and the usual (yet admirable) run list of figure-hugging backless numbers. IMAGE: INSTAGRAM @SARAHHYLAND While the crowd pleasers are always commended, this year the SAG awards upped the anti in the beauty stakes with a notable nod to the orient. From sleek yet understated origami buns, blunt fan-like ponytails, sharp fringes and cherry blossom lips; these stars weren’t afraid to push the envelope or embrace the fold. Behold, our favorite Japanese-inspired beauty moments. Best Origami Hair Looks on the Red Carpet 1\. Felicity Jones’ origami bun Wearing an impossibly delicate shade of baby-shower blush, Felicity gave her look a little edge with a sharp fan chignon. As crisp as the folds in her tailored Balenciaga, nothing says ‘fierce’ quite like the fan bun. Be sure to invest in a heavy-duty heat spray to avoid breakage after straightening, like the cult classic L’Oreal Elnett Satin Heat Sprayto keep your look on point all night long. L’oreal Elnett Satin Heat Spray 2\. Sarah Hyland’s twist Many argued this twist deserved best bun of the night, Sarah Highland’s Japanese-me twist displays some serious artistry. Paired with a chic winged eye and sleek side part, the ode to the orient is clear with this one. To avoid fly-aways, carry a clutch-friendly comb like the Kent Pocket Styling Comb to sharpen up come nightfall. Kent Pocket Styling Comb Sharp Ponytails and Blunt Bangs 3\. Emma Stone’s sharp ponytail and ear cuff Emma Stone can do no wrong and this ponytail is all kinds of right. Boasting a blunt edge and killer red lip, the ear cuff is the icing on the cake. Pair a geometric ponytail with a little frosting like the Samantha Wills Earring Cuffs to add an element of femininity to an otherwise androgynous style. Samantha Wills Earring Cuffs 4. Rashida Jones’ Blunt Bangs No doubt Rashida Jones knows better than most that sporting a blunt fringe or bangs in the middle of summer is no easy feat. If a fringe is your style staple, you’ll be familiar with the usual ‘do’s and don’ts’, but to wear it blunt and ultimately go-geisha, blow dry your fringe with the Mason Pearson Pocket Boar Bristle and Nylon Brush to ensure your fringe stays full for hours on end. It’ll be your new best friend. Mason Pearson Pocket Boar Bristle and Nylon Brush How to Get the Textured Bob 5\. Rosamund Pike’s textured bob There is nothing ‘gone’ about this girl, or her killer bob for that matter. Pike’s short-n-sharp do proved its versatility this awards season, with this crumpled number a red-hot winner. A texturizer like Shu Uemura Art of Hair Texture Wave Dry Workable Spray provides an undone yet on-trend ripple effect. Shu Uemura Art of Hair Texture Wave Dry Workable Spray Story by Ashley Ropati. Layout by Nicola Donovan.

articles.title: New Beauty Buys: Illuminators and Highlighters
articles.author: Madeleine Boyd
articles.excerpt: From eye creams and moisturisers to primers and powders, we’ve got you covered. Shine bright like a diamond with these new beauties buys that promise
articles.body: In a bid to maximise our glow factor we've busy road testing the latest and greatest highlighters and illuminators (tough job, but someone has to do it!) From eye creams and moisturisers to primers and powders, these are the magic wands you need to own. Shine bright like a diamond with our pick of the eight most illuminating buys that promise to leave you with a lit-from-within glow. Best Illuminating Moisture Balms Bobbi Brown Extra Illuminating Moisture Balm Bobbi Brown Extra Illuminating Moisture Balm Bobbi calls it her “dream cream” and after giving it a try for ourselves, we totally get it. Pumped full of lychee extract and caffeine (even your skin craves a coffee fix sometimes), it can be used either as a moisturizer or like a primer layering it on top of your moisturizer and under makeup. Best for dry or combination skins. $95 Multi-Use Cream Highlighters Nars Multiple St Lucia NARS Multiple St Lucia If you’ve never tried a Nars Multiple, make a beeline for your nearest Mecca Cosmetica store and snap one up, stat. This all-in-one cream stick is great for highlighting, and Nars’ newest shade, St Lucia, in its pretty rose golden hue is perfect for illuminating eyes, cheeks and lips. $52 Glow-Enhancing Primers for Radiant Skin Shiseido Glow Enhancing Primer Shiseido Glow Enhancing Primer Shiseido’s new Glow Enhancing Primer hits shelves next month so be sure to put a note in your calendar. When applied under foundation, it creates a plump and hydrated base for a glowing, natural-looking complexion, minus the artificial shine. $54 \ Available 1 March 2015 Under-Eye Brightening Treatments Benefit Puff Off Benefit Puff Off Banish puffiness and brighten your eyes with Benefit’s new Puff Off under eye gel. We love the super cute iron-like, silver tip that not only makes the gel glide on easily, but also immediately cools skin upon contact. $44 La Prairie White Caviar Illuminating Moisturising Cream LA Prairie White Caviar Illuminating Moisturising Cream The ultimate indulgence. As the newest offering from La Prairie’s decadent White Caviar skincare collection, this moisturiser promises to give you a brighter, firmer, more even complexion by boosting hydration levels and targeting pigmentation. It will also look oh-so-pretty in your bathroom cabinet. 50mL / $575 \ Available March 2015 Illuminating Setting Powders Ellis Faas Glow Up Highlighting Powder If you want that fresh-faced glow, Ellis Faas Glow Up is the way to go. An illuminating pressed powder that comes in three shades, it’s perfect for smoothing imperfections and setting makeup. Ellis and her team have got the luminosity factor just right too (always a fine balance), so you won’t be left looking like a disco ball. $38 Overnight Skin Brightening Treatments Jurlique Purely White Skin Brightening Night Cream Jurlique Purely White Skin Brightening Night Cream A new and even better version of Jurlique’s Purely White Skin Brightening Night Cream will be released this month. Infused with kakadu plum, which is very rich in vitamin C, this night cream is great for those wanting to reduce the appearance of pigmentation to reveal a brighter and more even complexion. 50mL / $79 \ Available 16 February 2015 La Mer Awaken Eyes Illuminating Eye Gel LA Mer Awaken Eyes Illuminating Eye Gel Your eyes will love La Mer’s Awaken Eyes Illuminating Eye Gel. Made with mineralized algae, the lightweight formula cools, brightens and soothes even the most tired and puffy eyes. Beauty editor’s tip: keep it in the fridge to get that extra cooling effect upon application – perfect for the morning after a big night out. 15mL / $195 Story by Madeleine Boyd.

articles.title: Michelle Bridges, Personal Trainer & Author
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: With ten books to her name, a vitamin range, a fitness line and her 12 Week Body Transformation weight loss program worth at least $16
articles.body: With ten books to her name, a vitamin range, a fitness line and her 12 Week Body Transformation weight loss program worth at least $16 million a year, Michelle Bridges is building one heck of a health empire - one perfectly chiseled piece at a time. Since launching into the media stratosphere as a personal trainer on The Biggest Loser back in 2007, the energetic brunette has attracted legions of fans for her pragmatic approach to exercise - a kind of tough-love laced with tenderness, that has thousands following her every edict. We relished the opportunity to see inside Michelle’s glamorous inner city apartment and glimpse a different side of the trainer. She graciously let us rifle through her beauty cabinet and nose through her pantry (sorry, no surprises there), revealing a sensible approach to skincare and health. Michelle’s Fitness-First Beauty Philosophy I’m all about health and fitness My beauty regime starts with what I put into my body, as far as nutrients, and also what I do with my body, as far as exercise. That’s what it really stems from. I aim to train seven days a week, knowing the reality will be I’ll stick five. But if I aim for seven, that means I’ll grab time wherever I can. I don’t wear any makeup for training. Michelle’s Nighttime Skincare Routine My friends say, “She’s the queen of cream!” For night I cleanse and use the A+ and Ultra Brightening Face Cream and Eye Cream. The founder of Ultraceuticals, Dr. Geoffrey Heber and his wife, Deborah used to come to my Body Pump classes when I was teaching at Balmain Fitness! They also run Heber Davis Skin Clinic and I go there for a treatment called Pelleve. It just makes your face just glow and firms the skin. Heber Davis are amazing. The treatments there are results driven and very focused on skin care. Michelle's Favourite Fragrances Tom Ford Neroli Portofino is my all time favourite scent… I love it. I wear it all the time. A woman by the name of Alice Hampton sent it to me because she was working for Estee Lauder and Tom Ford at the time. I do wear different fragrances. But it’s the one I always go to. I am also a die hard for Aesop as the scent is always something so unique and fresh. I use the body wash and hand wash and always feel like it wakes me up in the morning! I’m a major fan of taking care of yourself. You only get one body – take care of it. Nurture it. It’s all about balance. I'm not a purist, I love to eat out. I don’t mind a wine or two. I train, I eat well. I make sure to take time out. I hang with my mates. I work hard. It’s all part of life and living. Michelle's Go-To Beauty Treatments For facials, I go to Jocelyn Petroni in Woollahra It’s not just a facial. It’s a spiritual experience! She is a total pro and clearly loves what she does. I have a mantra in my life – I'm only interested in working with people who are passionate about what they do. Jocelyn fits the bill to perfection. My massage therapist Georgie at Khoury Chiropractic in Potts Point is another definition of this. She is the best massage therapist I have ever had, and trust me, I had quite a few! My hairdresser is also passionate! Paloma from Oscar Oscar in Paddington. The products I use are fabulous as Im always having my hair blow dried with…

articles.title: Samantha Wills, Jewellery Designer
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: A gypsy at heart, jewellery designer Samantha Wills feeds her wanderlust by dividing her time between her offices in Sydney, New York, Tokyo and Seoul. The style-savvy
articles.body: A gypsy at heart, jewellery designer Samantha Wills feeds her wanderlust by dividing her time between her offices in Sydney, New York, Tokyo and Seoul. Gathering inspiration from her travels that filter into her designs, the style-savvy blonde has become one of Australia’s most sought-after fashion exports – the New York Times even called her “A Break Out Star”. Her warm and honest voice has attracted an impressive social media following who follow her every glamorous movement across the globe. While visiting her Tamarama home, Samantha opened the doors to her bohemian beach pad, dishing out her trademark anecdotes alongside some very nifty beauty tips. Samantha Spritzes Herself in Chanel Coco Mademoiselle Samantha's Jewellery Brand Story “I started designing jewellery as a hobby Selling my designs down at Bondi beach markets in Sydney. A friend had spot on a showroom wall at Australian Fashion Week, and I took the spot hoping to make back the $500 cost and wrote $17,000 worth of orders. I was 22 years old at the time and had no idea about anything – all I knew was that I wanted to create a brand, so that’s what I set out to do. I love the concept of branding and being creative, jewellery became the vehicle to achieve that. I also enjoy the social media side and personally engaging and interacting with followers of the brand – it is very rewarding and I am very grateful. My approach to beauty is about health Healthy hair, skin and how to accent your best features. I definitely have a more minimalist approach these days that also comes from being more comfortable with who you are. That’s why I love being in my thirties. In your twenties you are still figuring that all out – and applying far too much makeup in the process! My beauty look is natural beachy waves, sun kissed skin and minimal makeup. Rose Gold Accents Adorn Samantha's Vanity Samantha's Glowing Complexion is a Result of Her Dedicated Skincare Routine Samantha's Skincare Secrets I was told by a beautician to try… to use creams in the day as they sit on top of the skin and protect, and serums at night as they sink in. So I use an SK-II serum at night and different moisturisers through the day. I love SK-II cleanser and facial treatment essence and their facial mask once a week – it does make you look like Hannibal Lector, so I usually use it when my boyfriend is away! But what it lacks in social appeal, it makes up for in hydration. It’s like a miracle cloth! I alternate my moisturisers, but currently love the face moisturiser from GO-TO skin care and Chanel Le Blanc & La Nuit. I travel with them all the time. For a night out… I love Diorshow mascara and always apply to a curled lash. I use a bronzer over my moisturiser and then a slightly darker bronzer to contour cheeks. At the moment I love the Luma bronzer by Jess Hart and SunBeam by Benefit. I use an eyebrow mascara to fill in brows and apply a liquid liner to the top lid. I make sure to never wear too much foundation but work on contouring and brightness instead. I prep my skin as well with a SK-II treatment the day before and get a fresh manicure too. Samantha Has a Minimalist Approach to Her Beauty Routine - Sunkissed Skin and Barely-there Makeup. Shu Uemura and Kerastase Are Hair Staples for the Blonde. Samantha's Beachy Hair Routine I usually wash my hair every three days…

articles.title: How to Do Summer Braids and Plaits
articles.author: Ashley Ropati
articles.excerpt: From plaited halos to loose and ethereal braids, it needn’t all be bobby pins and super-strength hairspray.
articles.body: While tousled beach hair and salty strands are a long reigning summer staple, it’s high time to get your head in the game and switch things up. From plaited halos to loose and ethereal braids, it needn’t all be bobby pins and super-strength hairspray. IMAGE: INSTAGRAM @JOSEPHINESKRIVER Thanks to on-screen queens like JLaw’s Hunger Games character Katniss Everdeen, fresh and disheveled summery plaits are no longer strictly reserved for the playground and have never looked quite so effortless… 1\. the Halo Jennifer Lawrence All hail the halo! Jennifer Lawrence proves this ethereal go-to is just as on trend as ever – both on the screen and off. Keep it contemporary cool with a gritty yet lightweight texturizer like Eleven Sea Salt Texture Spray. Eleven Sea Salt Texture Spray 2\. The Deconstructed Braid Mara Hoffman The disheveled side plait sported backstage at Mara Hoffman SS15 is as easy as One, Two, Three. While it works all year round, this one reigns supreme on sweaty summer days. Towel dry and tease hair for a welcome beach-hair kink when undone. To revive sun-soaked hair, work a natural hair mask into your weekly routine throughout beach season. Living Proof Restore Hair Mask will deeply nourish even the most distressed tresses. The Fishtail Tory Burch While the fishtail certainly isn’t for the novice, once you’ve nailed this ‘do you’ll be set. Update an undone beach ensemble with the most polished of the braid family and finish with a sleek and luminous finishing spray like Kevin Murphy Shimmer Shine to defy the weather gods and that dreaded humidity. Kevin Murphy Shimmer Shine The Golden Girl Zoe Saldana From the catwalk to the red carpet, gold leaf is most definitely having a moment. Get crafty with a traditional braid by adding loose gold threaded accents to a polished plait or slip on a gold headpiece a la’ Zoe Saldana like the Rosantica Maria Gold-Dipped Pearl Headband for a little sparkle come starlight. Rosantica Maria Gold-dipped Pearl Headband The Rosette Braid Rodarte Channel your inner garden-party goddess with a simple yet striking rosette. There were roses by the dozen backstage at Rodarte, proving the half-up half-down do’ can hold its own in the high fashion stakes. Add lightweight pins like Lady Jayne Hair Pins to hold your bud in place and avoid heavy hairspray to keep it flowing and effortless. Lady Jayne Hair Pins Story by Ashley Ropati.

articles.title: The New Years Resolutions I’ve Kept so Far – Sigourney’s Edit
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Sigourney reflects on new years resolutions she's kept so far.
articles.body: There’s nothing like a fresh, clean calendar year to inspire fervent promises and lofty intentions. The problem with New Years resolutions is that often they’re so extreme that they’re hard to upkeep year round. I can’t tell you how many of my optimistic Januarys have given way to unused gym memberships, lapsed meal plans and dusty Pilates DVD’s… This year I tried to make resolutions that were realistic and so far (cross fingers), so good. Here are a few intentions that have been working well for me already. Now… if I can just keep it up all year. Hydration and Moisturising Goals 1\. I will… drink loads of water and moisturise more The most sublime-skinned Beauticates that I’ve interviewed have all sworn by bucket loads of hydration. Lindy Klim relies on coconut water and Lara Bingle swears by SK-II masks. So I’ve been drinking a lot more water (after much research switched from tap water to a four litre Berkey water filter from Aussie website Divine Water) and slathering on trowels of moisturiser. New favourites? The new moisturiser by the ladies at The Clinic – a Sydney institution famous for treating A-listers, TV personalities and beauty editors alike. The founders, Kate Scott and Lisa Sullivan, really know their stuff. So it made perfect sense that they decided to launch their own do-it-all melt-on-contact face cream that leaves skin feeling all juicy and springy. Another beautiful one I’ve found is Argentum La Potion Infinie – it’s a beautiful silky lotion that is 99.9% natural origins and goes on like a dream. It’s rare to find an all-natural anti-ager so this is great when I’m having a chemi-free “my body is a temple’” moment. Berkey Water Filter The Clinic Scott and Sullivan Moisturiser Argentum LA Potion Infinie Keeping Up With Beauty Appointments 2. I will… keep up my beauty appointments I know how lucky I am to be able to test out the best beauty treatments and call it work. But often I get bogged down in deadlines and let my beauty maintenance slip. This year I’m going to make (and keep!) standing appointments with the following superstar salons: Lash Extensions at Love Those Lashes – this is my time-saving beauty secret, AKA mummy’s little helper. On non-event days I can roll out of bed and skip the makeup because my lashes are always looking fierce. The express, supercharged facials brighten and plump skin and whiten teeth; Vinylux manis with Jocelyn Petroni – Joss is not only a superstar facialist, her digit work is so stellar she frequently gets called to do Miranda and Jenn’s nails for big shoots. Sun Protection and Daily Sunscreen 3\. I will…wear more hats and apply sunscreen EVERY day I love that there are so many gorgeous hats in fashion at the moment from the panama to the boater. I’m currently loving the Fallen Broken Street Straw Boater, (gorgeous with a simple white dress). Fallen Broken Street ‘the Bambi’ Wide Brim Straw Boater Ditching Screens Before Bedtime 4\. I will… ditch my phone at bedtime and wake up gently One thing I learnt at Gwinganna was the importance of winding down and switching off your devices before bed. Phones and laptops emit LED light, which is blue on the light spectrum – like sunrise. So looking at blue light before bed tells the brain that it’s time to wake up. It’s also seriously stimulating to work before bed (I blame late laptop sessions for all the insomnia I’ve suffered this year). Enough is enough! I’ve started to leave my phone charging in the other room at night…

articles.title: Your Australia Day Beauty Kit
articles.author: Chrisanthi Kaliviotis
articles.excerpt: Beauticate shows you what to back for you Australia Day Beauty Kit.
articles.body: Vegemite on toast. Snags on the barbie. A piping hot meat pie at the footy. The Australian colloquialisms stretch near and far on this great Southern land. But in terms of beauty, the Australians have stamped their might and prowess on a global scale. @jesinta franklin All-time classics such as the ‘Pav’ and the ‘Pie’ feature in the Aussie vernacular, but the beauty world too has its own inventory of Aussie favourites. With Australia Day on the sun-dipped horizon, we have packed our beauty bag for barbeques and beach days, full of products to placate the oft-harsh Australian climate. Call it beauty patriotism if you will; a ripper round up of the best Australian make up and skincare for rain, hail or shine. You beauty! Sensible Hatter Nerida Winter Rosie Since donning daggy Legionnaire’s hats (see: Australian primary school necessity), Australian’s have been quite the shady nation. Be it lolloping at Long Beach or floating around the lake on lazy afternoons, a hat is quite simply an Australia Day necessity. A big brim away from the floppy cricket hats, Nerida Winter is the darling of the millinery world, and we think her Rosie is just divine. Nerida Winter Rosie Miss Tinted The Base by Lara Bingle LB Cream If one were to think of the quintessential bronzed Aussie babe, Ms. Lara Bingle’s name would most definitely transpire. It’s no wonder then, the beachy Bingle launched an all-inclusive bronzing range with affordable pricing. The clever LB Cream does it all; bronzes, primes, moisturises, balances skin tone and masks imperfections (and most importantly will provide that ‘Bingle’ glow). The Base by Lara Bingle Lb Cream Face Filly J Bronze Face Flawless Tan For clandestine bar-hopping and heady rooftop jaunts in the sprawling Melbourne CBD, a bronzed face is a must. Good news: J Bronze have just improved their Flawless Tan for the Face, tweaking the formula to provide a slightly deeper tan. However, J Bronze disciples fear not; the same moisturising, brightening and anti-ageing properties are still there. Perfect timing too, a flawless faux glow will be perfect for that sunny rooftop tipple this Monday. J Bronze Face Flawless Tan Sunburn Saviour Sodashi After Sun Recovery Body Lotion After spending the day baking in Bondi, nothing quite appeases the heat of the Australian sun like this. Super soothing and deeply hydrating, this beautifully rich lotion instantly cools hot, unhappy skin and reduces peeling. The cult skincare brand is an all-natural, all-Australian all-star, using a combination of biochemistry, aromatherapy and Ayurvedic principles to produces chemical-free, holistic skincare. We’ll slather to that. Sodashi After Sun Recovery Body Lotion Surf-proof Lashes Napoleon Perdis Mesmer Eyes Mascara Waterproof A mascara to combat the surf, waterfalls, lakes and rivers, Napoleon’s Mesmer Eyes Waterproof mascara is also clump-proof and smudge-proof. The paraben-free formula also conditions lashes with vitamin E, Panthenol and bamboo, and who doesn’t want silky, soft but oh-so-sexy lashes to flutter at the boy at the BBQ. Mascara on, Mooloolaba here we come. Napoleon Perdis Mesmer Eyes Mascara Waterproof Facial Hydrator Ultraceuticals Ultra Rich Moisturising Cream A day riding around Rottnest Island or exploring the idyllic nooks of Wineglass Bay calls for some serious afterhours skin therapy. Slather on Ultraceuticals Ultra Rich Moisturiser Cream, formulated with ceramides and a cocktail of potent peptides to deeply nourish, repair and hydrate sad, thirsty skin. A home-grown hero (Australian made and owned), we trust them with our lives (or faces). Ultraceuticals Ultra Rich Moisturising Cream Shady Lady Pared Charlie & The Angels Sunglasses With all the coot cats in Sydney parading around in their Pared sunnies, it’s no wonder…

articles.title: Erika Heynatz, Actor
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Erika Heynatz is a self-confessed beauty junkie (years in front of a camera lens will do that to a girl). She’s also warm, funny and
articles.body: Erika Heynatz is a self-confessed beauty junkie - years in front of a camera lens will do that to a girl. She’s also warm, funny and has a flair for design. With an artist mother and a creative upbringing, Erika studied graphic design before crossing over to the world of performance art. Now, the model turned TV and theatre star has an extensive performance resume and an even longer list of beauty must-haves. After hosting the first two series of Australia's Next Top Model, Erika left to focus on her singing career. More recently she has been treading the boards and honing her stage makeup with roles in musicals Legally Blonde, The Rocky Horror Picture Show and, this year, Singin' in the Rain. She also joined Australian TV institution, Home and Away, playing controversial teacher, Charlotte at fictional Summer Bay High. We caught up with Erika in her colourful and stylish Northern Beaches abode and discovered an impressive array of covetable cosmetics. Erika Loves the Ritual of Hair, Makeup and Wardrobe When Preparing for a Role. Dress by Alice Mccall. Erika’s Creative Career Path I’ve always wanted a creative career I got into modeling in my final year of University. Modeling lead to commercials, which lead into television presenting & film acting, and finally into musical theatre. I love that my job gives me a chance to play different characters and the live performance element of it can be a real thrill, especially singing with others, that’s a really magic feeling. I really enjoy the ritual of preparing myself for a role; hair, makeup & wardrobe become such transformative tools. I studied graphic design I majored in illustration. My mum’s an artist, so from a really early age I was playing with paints, drawing and sketching. I’ve always been quite tactile and having moved into performing arts so much of getting into character for work is about creating – even as a fashion model – \[it’s about\] presenting a façade of sorts. Erika Approaches All Tasks with a Creative Flair. An Aveda Devotee, Favourites Include; Caribbean Body Cleanser, Volumising Clay Conditioner and Botanical Toning Mist. Erika’s Beauty Product Obsession I’m an absolute product whore. I love it… One of the benefits of working in the fashion and beauty industry is you get exposure to all of the latest stuff with makeup artists. A great primer is a must if I want the look to go the distance. Laura Mercier is fantastic. I would love to say that my look is simple & effortless but deep down I love to try new things and sometimes that means I’m slapping on five creams at night like a crazy woman just because I want to use it all at once! I am leaning more towards products with natural ingredients, fragrances & ethical production. There are some beautiful products now without all the chemicals that are just as effective. I’m a self-confessed tanorexic… I’m definitely a fake tan girl. I’ve been using Vani-T organic tan for years and it’s the best tan I’ve ever used, I tend to do my own at home these days. A lot of beauticians use it now because it’s one of the only organic tans. I had a great ‘contoured tan’ from Katrina Brown at the Bronzing Boutique once before a photoshoot that shaved off a few kilos and gave me a free 6 pack. Her Fridge is Laden with Friendly Faces and Happy Memories Skincare Favourites in Erika's Beauty Cupboard. Erika's Skincare Routine Cleansing is so important to me… I find that the chore of taking makeup off…

articles.title: Tan Tips from a Man. a (Hot) Guy Tells Us How It’s Done.
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Tan tips from a man – Blair James, co-founder of Bondi Sands gives us his best fake tan, self tan and spray tan tips.
articles.body: He spent the next six years honing his product, Bondi Sands, with business partner Shaun Wilson. The olive-tinged competitively-priced tanning range is now number one bestseller in Priceline) and is expanding rapidly internationally (check locations?). We sat down with the handsome Tan-treprenuer and were gobsmacked when he successfully managed to school us in the Art of the Bronze. Blair, who, at times would step in to do spray tans in his salon, revealed that he and his business partner regularly test the product on themselves – and have got it down to a fine art. And we have to say, he sports a very impressive tan. Here he shares his jewels of wisdom. Essential Skin Preparation Steps “The number one thing is to prepare the skin properly, if you don’t have your skin completely exfoliated it’s going to grab the dark skin and come out patchy,” says Blair. “You need to pick a product that suits your skin,” says Blair. “A lot of people want to go as dark as possible but if you have pale skin it can look unnatural. Try one coat of the lighter shade first, then darken the tan as you need.” Fair skins should opt for Self Tanning Foam Light/Medium and more olive girls can give Dark Foam a go. Perfecting Your Tan Application “When we used to do spray tans in the salon a lot of girls used to shower and come straight in, but if your skin is still holding moisture the product doesn’t actually take to the skin so make sure your skin is completely dry,” says Blair. We would add to that that it’s a good idea to open the bathroom door and wait for a bit while the steam escapes and your skin dries before starting your application. “Your skin needs to be clean and thoroughly washed but I don’t recommend putting moisturizer on before you apply the tan because it’s a barrier so it’s going to stop the tan from taking.” Moisturising to Extend Your Tan “As soon as you wash the tan off [after it’s developed], start moisturizing. That’s half the reason we brought out the gradual tanning milk. While you’re actually moisturizing the tan, you actually extend the life of the tan by adding the active ingredients to it. You can extend that tan by about two or three weeks.” We love that they also have an Everyday Gradual Tanning Milk with SPF 15 in it. “When you’re tanning your face use some moisturizer in your eyebrows and around your hairline to stop the tan from grabbing those areas or it can end up being very prominent when you wash the rest of it off – and no makeup is going to cover that!” adds Blair. Tanning Hard-to-Reach Areas Evenly “You can buy these back applicators but if you haven’t had a chance to buy one, you can get a piece of Glad wrap about 30& 215;30 cm, put the product in a little bit of Glad wrap, [ Apply some tanning lotion or foam down one side of the sheet then?] slide the cling wrap to each side, it will stick to your skin and you can actually drag it to spread evenly over your back.” “Mitts make applying foam much easier, “ says Blair, who swears by Bondi Sands Application Mitt and adds that there’s a bit of technique to the finishing touches. “Do your limbs first and leave knees, elbows, wrists, ankles and the backs of your hands until last – applying just the residue that’s left on the mitt to those areas,” says…

articles.title: Jacqueline Alwill, Nutritionist
articles.author: Lauren Rose Burke
articles.excerpt: Jacqueline Alwill, of Brown Paper Bag, opened up her lovely Bondi home (and pantry) to Beauticate, sharing her best health tips and beauty products.
articles.body: Very few women glow quite so convincingly as nutritionist and model Jacqueline Alwill. With a thriving whole foods catering business, Brown Paper Bag Nutrition and a busy schedule as a consulting nutritionist, this mum of one favours a simple beauty routine that lets her inner radiance shine. Jacqueline opened up her lovely Bondi home (and pantry) to Beauticate, sharing her best health tips, how to use food as medicine and the ways in which her mother and sisters inspired her love of beauty. JACQUELINE IN HER BONDI HOME Jacqueline's Shift to Nutrition Health is always something I wanted in my life I was working as a media strategist in Sydney, but lunch times I would be out running and training work colleagues, I’d bring healthy treats for others into work to share, was constantly reading nutrition books and articles. The more thought I put into it; the more I was drawn to making the shift from corporate life to retraining in nutrition and health. I decided that personal training would be a great way to support myself whilst I was studying Nutritional Medicine. I love giving people a chance to renew their health. People seem to think it takes a lot more time to be healthy. Time is our greatest gift, and our health our greatest asset – we just need to figure out the best way to make them a winning team. Jacqueline's Beauty Influences My two sisters epitomise beauty to me I’ve always looked up to them, and loved how they helped to sculpt my attitude to beauty along the way. Mum has always taken pride in presenting herself immaculately. Hair, skincare and simple but elegant make up. I remember as a child, tucking myself into my parents’ bed at night and watching her ritual of massaging her hands with Clarins Hand Cream. It was such a lesson in the gentle soothing nature of physical touch and caring for yourself, in the humblest of ways. THE NUTRITIONIST TAKES INSPIRATION FROM HER MOTHER AND SISTERS JACQUELINE FAVOURS NATURAL SKIN CARE PRODUCTS Jacqueline's Natural Skincare Routine Let your natural features shine I love simplicity and that’s my approach to beauty. In the mornings I like to use La Mav Hydra Calm Cleansing Crème, followed by Kiehls or La Mav Eye Gel and La Mav Hyaluronan Daily Mosisture Crème. I’ll moisturise my body with Aesop Rejuvenate Intensive Body Balm. Evenings I’ll cleanse with O Cosmedics or La Mav Cleansing Creme, followed by Dr Alkalitis Organic Night Creme and some Kiehl’s for eyes. I like to nourish my hands at bedtime with L’Occitane Hand and Nail cream, which my mum gave me. If there is anything that might be troubling me it would be my eyes, so I’ll always carry Kiehls Eye Cream with me, and Kosmea 24/7 Youth Boost to apply if I my skin feels dehydrated. I love natural, fresh looks They inspire me most. Helena Christensen inspires me. Her beauty is timeless and graceful. I love a dust of bronzer and curling my eyelashes a little to give things a lift. Other than that my make up is very modest. When I was fresh into motherhood, I kept my routine extremely basic; moisturise in the morning, cleanse and moisturise by night. Now that my little man is a touch older and we can chat as I am doing things I have given more time to my beauty regime. He’s pretty fascinated by it and asks all sorts of questions, ‘Mummy why do you put white paint on your face?’ When I do a mask. He loves gently applying my…

articles.title: Golden Globes Makeup Ideas and Hairstyles: What They Actually Used
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: The red carpet was laid, the diamonds polished and the whiff of hairspray was in the air; cue the Golden Globes. Tinsletown was alight with
articles.body: The red carpet was laid, the diamonds polished and the whiff of hairspray was in the air; cue the Golden Globes. Tinsletown was alight with the razzle and dazzle of the first awards show of the season, and the first ladies of both cinema and television definitely delivered in the beauty stakes. Beauticate Loves... Marilyn Monroe at the Golden Globe Awards In amongst the snapping and pap-ing, we got the scoop from the celebrity make up artists who painted the faces of Hollywood’s most famed dames, and shared the products they actually used. Pens at the ready; you’ll want to take notes. Cue the applause. 1\. Reese Witherspoon – Golden Girl America’s petite sweetheart opted for a smouldering, metallic-laden maquillage; with her make up artist Molly R. Stern creating a look that “shined brilliantly like the prize she is.” Shine she did; thanks to an array of products by Laura Mercier. Shop the Look: Laura Mercier Silk Crème Moisturizing Photo Edition Foundation in Cream Ivory Laura Mercier Crème Cheek Colour in Blaze Laura Mercier Baked Eye Colour in Black Karat Laura Mercier Crème Eye Liner in Noir Laura Mercier Full Blown Volume Supreme Mascara Laura Mercier Crème Smooth Lip Colour in Merlot 2\. Kate Beckinsdale – Complexion Perfection Ms. Beckinsdale’s Globe glamour was impeccable; the classic English belle channelled an earthy, gently bronzed look. She screamed sultry siren, all the while without looking ostentatious, owing to an entirely Chantecaille makeover. Shop the Look: Chantecaille Just Skin Chantecaille Future Skin Chantecaille Liquid Lumiere 3\. Keira Knightley – Barely Blushing The English Rose was true to her elegant and pretty style; a flushed complexion, bold brows and tea rose stained lips keynote to her Globe look. Her flawless beauty was care of Chanel, naturellement . Shop the Look: Chanel Les 4 Ombres Tissè Rivoli Chanel Jous Contraste Relfex Chanel Perfection Lumière Velvet Chanel Imitable Waterproof Mascara Chanel Hydra Beauty Nourishing Lip Balm Chanel Hydra Beauty Essence Mist 4\. Dakota Johnson – Smoke and Mirro The up and coming actress’ beauty was most definitely ‘it’ girl worthy; understated and earthy, not to distract from her sparkly and swanky gown. Like any cool cat, her smoky-eyed Globe guise came courtesy of Chanel. articles.title: Gwinganna Health Retreat Review
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Sigourney reviews her retreat to Gwinganna.
articles.body: The new year is the perfect time to hit ‘reset’ on your lifestyle choices and one of the most effective ways to do that is to head to a health retreat. It’s easier than fumbling along trying to make changes at home, as there are qualified experts to hold your hand the whole way through. It fully immerses you in the study of health and wellness and allows you to cherry-pick the therapies and activities that will assist you most in your journey. I first visited Gwinganna Lifestyle Retreat almost five years ago and found it to be a complete game-changer in the way I looked at health and wellbeing. After that trip, I started healthy habits that continue with me today. But last November, after an extremely taxing year, I was totally burnt-out. I knew I had to reprioritise things and start putting my health first, but I lacked the discipline to do it by myself. So, I enrolled in the four day Nourishing You workshop. here’s how it went… Story by Sigourney. Video and photography by Manuela Leigh. Sigourney wears pieces by Zimmermann and workout wear by Lululemon and Stella McCartney. Shop the Look: Zimmermann Essence Choker Swing Dress Zimmermann Trinity Scallop Top Zimmermann Confetti Scallop Flare Dress Adidas by Stella Mccartney Barricade Tank Adidas by Stella Mccartney Studio Tights Triangle Winnie Bikini in Miami Mint A special thank you to all the amazing staff and therapists who helped me on my journey: Sharon Kolkka, Donna Abbate, The Horse Whisperer Therapist Sue Spence, Integrated Massage Therapist Stephen Canning, Sound of Spirit Therapist Petrina Tonkin, Yoga and Meditation guru Andy Kidd, Naturopath Shannon McNeill.

articles.title: Supermodel Beach Beauty Secrets
articles.author: Sarina Zoe
articles.excerpt: Vibrant colours and laid-back feelings, warm sandy skin and cool water swims. We show you how to have a supermodel summer.
articles.body: As a certain literary genius once wrote, summer’s lease hath all too short a date. Vibrant colours and laid-back feelings, warm sandy skin and cool water swims inspire more than just Shakespearean sonnets. Yes, it’s the season of reverie and the season we romance about, so soak it up like Helena, Linda, Claudia and Kate and indulge in the temporal beauty of summer, supermodel style. @kacitansey “Sometime too hot the eye of heaven shines” Beauticate Loves Helena Christenson by Xavi Gordo for Elle Spain When the sun beats down and the pool seduces you in, do waterproof beauty the Helena way. Charcoal smoky eyes with protected skin that survives a swim? Eyeko and La Roche-Posay deliver. Shop the Look: Eyeko Me and My Shadow in Charcoal Agent Provocateur Dakotta Bikini Bra “And often is his gold complexion dimm’d” Beauticate Loves Linda Evangelista by Steven Meisel for Vogue Italia With a golden, olive-based St Tropez tan, your complexion will glow come summer rain or shine. Channel Linda’s laid-back summer with a headwrap (very Missoni SS15). No tying skills? No sweat. Louvelle have you covered. Shop the Look: St Tropez Dark Bronzing Mousse Eres Paradise Sky Bikini Top Louvelle Amelie Turban in Ruby “So long as men can breathe and eyes can see” Beauticate Loves Claudia Schiffer by Ellen Von Unwerth for Guess …We will lust after voluminous beach hair and a retro feline flick. Summer lounging never looked so good. Get Claudia’s separated texture and volume in a Bumble and bumble can, and elongated eyes with Maybelline’s gel precision formula. Shop the Look: Maybelline Lasting Drama Gel Liner Karla Coletto Gingham One Shoulder “But thy eternal summer shall not fade” Beauticate Loves Kate Moss by Mert & Marcus for Vogue UK For enduring summer skin, do sunkissed Kate with Stila’s Stay All Day matte Bronzer. Pair with a long-lasting velvet nude lip from Tom Ford. Offset matte summer beauty with a décolletage adorned in silver. Shop the Look: Stila Stay All Day Bronzer Tom Ford Lip Color in Blush Nude Stella and Dot Sutton Silver Necklace Story by Sarina Zoe. Layout by Amanda Chan.

articles.title: Bip Ling, Fashion Blogger
articles.author: Beauticate Editorial
articles.excerpt: Blogger, DJ, model and Brit-centric belle of the London fashion scene, Bip Ling has lured almost two million viewers to her Blog
articles.body: Blogger, DJ, model and Brit-centric belle of the London fashion scene, Bip Ling has lured almost two million viewers to her kooky blog. When she’s not starring in Louis Vuitton Campaigns or working the front row at fashion week she’s in her studio blogging GIFS: turning selfies into animated art. It isn’t any wonder- Bip’s practically art aristocracy, with two parents who are prominent in the art scene (Dad’s a fashion illustration gallery owner, Mum’s an artist/designer) and encourage her every artistic move. Bip’s quirky, expressive style doesn’t stop at fashion…she pushes the beauty boundaries too with an effortless approach to creative makeup. Bip's Approach to Makeup I love to experiment with makeup and play around with colours but I think looking natural is beautiful. I rarely wear foundation- just concealer. When makeup artist, Lisa Eldridge did my makeup she taught me that I don’t need foundation so I gave it up and haven’t used it since. I’m lucky to come from an Indian family with strong female role models – my mother and grandmother always encouraged me to focus on the important things – to be happy, be gracious, to smile…and have fun! Bip's Style Evolution I used to be a tomboy… who wore shorts and shirts all the time. Now I’m the complete opposite. It was after I took a foundation course at Central St Martin’s University of Arts that I started blogging about my friends and the outfits I wore. I had no idea what I wanted to do, I wanted to do everything! I always knew I would end up in a creative field because I love art and design. My blog started off as a sort of scrapbook and a way for me to express myself but I never intentionally set out for it to become what it has turned into. Now everyday is different and I spend my time going from modelling, DJing, blogging, vlogging and creating content for my YouTube channel. Now I would describe my style as ‘British Museum Chic’ and prefer wearing clothes from new designers Bip's Skincare Routine I like to look after my skin My mother always taught me to tone the skin before cleansing because it keeps skin pimple free. I always use Kiehl’s Midnight Recovery Concentrate before I sleep and I apply it whenever I fly because it’s really hydrating. During the day I use their Rose Arctica Youth Regenerating Cream. I’ve been obsessed with Kiehl’s since I started using it because my skin has been so much better since. All the products really work, without being oily or greasy. When I wash my face, I always rinse with cold water. In fact I am obsessed with cold rinsing in the shower and I even use it in the bath. It makes my skin feel tight and my hair glossy –it also makes my hair get less knotty during the day. Bip's Haircare Secrets When it comes to my hair… I’m quite low maintenance. I visit Paul Edmonds in London regularly for a hair treatment and blow dry. At home I use Kiehl’s shampoo and conditioner and rub Moroccan oil through it everyday except when I go in the sun….oil in the sun can be so damaging to hair but used daily it makes it feel like silk. Bip on Feeling Beautiful I feel at my most beautiful when… I’m fulfilled and that can depend on what I’m working on. A little spray tan from celebrity tanner, Jules Von Heptonstall at St Tropez helps too. I pick up tips from makeup artists here and there but actually…

articles.title: Madeleine Boyd, Beauty Editor
articles.author: Madeleine Boyd
articles.excerpt: Beauticate's Beauty editor Madeleine Boyd shares her beauty essentials and your ultimate shopping list for the new year
articles.body: Madeleine and I met five years ago when we were both working at Vogue. Although she was in the fashion department, she spent a good chunk of time in my office going through the beauty deliveries with me. After Vogue she tried her hand at PR working at evh across brands like Scanlan Theodore, Max Mara and Ladurée, but the call of the written word was too strong. She went freelance working on Broadsheet writing fashion profiles. When I set up Beauticate, Madeleine was one of the first people I called on and she slipped into the beauty editor role as if she’d been cut for it. Madeleine's Everyday Makeup Favourites I feel really lucky that I get to try beauty products …and call it work. I love that there is always something new and exciting to discover and I believe makeup is something you can really have fun with. When I was four I loved playing with lipstick. I’ll never forget that one time I used Mum’s favourite shade of pink to ‘decorate’ my chest of drawers. Not much has changed, though I do keep my lipsticks away from furniture. Despite being a beauty journalist I don’t actually spend much time doing my makeup in the morning. I prefer to keep it quite natural. My go-to foundations are ByTerry Sheer Expert Foundation and Chantecaille Future Skin – both are quite dewy and sheer coverage. I use ByTerry’s Touché Veloutee concealer – it’s really brightening, which is ideal for me as I can get quite dark under eye circles especially after a late night. I love blush and usually wear either Nars Deep Throat or Gilda, then dust on a bit of Nars Laguna Bronzer. Madeleine’s Eye Makeup Must-Haves I’ve always done my own eyebrows I’m such a perfectionist about them! I fill them in with an Hourglass Brow Pencil in soft brunette. I don’t feel ‘done’ unless I’ve penciled my brows. I also swear by Chantecaille Faux Cils Longest Lash Mascara. While it’s not cheap, I have a weakness for a lash serum mascara that gives long, voluminous lashes. Liquid eyeliner is probably one of the first beauty products I ever mastered. I’ve tried so many different black liquid eyeliners but I always go back to Rimmel Glam Eyes. It’s around $14 from the supermarket and the best thing going round. Eye shadow-wise, I’m a fan ofStila’s Kitten Eye Shadow (for day) and for nighttime or if I have an event, I look to Chanel or Bobbi Brown’s smoky eye shadow quads in browns and taupes. Madeleine's Skincare Ritual I can’t live without Eve Lom’s cleanser Which I use every night. It removes makeup, cleanses, gently exfoliates and has quite the cult following. It’s thick like a balm and you apply it to dry skin, then wipe it off with a damp muslin cloth. I love the ritual of it. I have really dry skin and this doesn’t strip, yet my skin always feels squeaky clean after I use it. After that I apply Ultraceuticals Red-Action Serum (it’s one of those products that you can actually see working). I follow this with Verso Super Eye Serum. Every few days I’ll use Dr Dennis Gross peel pads to exfoliate – they’re magic! I’ve got so many of my friends onto them. I also do an Aesop clay maskonce a week. I probably shouldn’t be admitting this… But when I was younger I used the solarium all the time. My attitude to tanning is so different now; I wear sunscreen everyday, even in winter. Every few months I have sessions of…

articles.title: Jess Hart, Model & Entrepreneur
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Jess Hart has certainly come a long way since winning the Dolly model contest back in 2000. The New York based, Australian beauty had only
articles.body: Jess Hart has certainly come a long way since winning the Dolly model contest back in 2000. The New York based, Australian beauty boasts an impressive CV, counting Victoria’s Secret Angel and Vogue Australia cover girl among her stellar career highlights. She recently jetted home to Sydney to unveil her new makeup brand, Luma Cosmetics, a project she has been quietly working away at over the past two years. Jess's Lip and Colour Secrets I hate that my lips are so red So I’m always looking for the right thing for them. The LUMA sheer lipstick in nude shimmer is a favourite because it takes out the red but doesn’t dry me out. I’ve always suffered from really dry lips, which is why I think they’re so red. When I was younger my mum would try to make me put lip balm on and I thought it was the most disgusting thing in the world. Now I’m always looking for good lip balms and anything I can get my hands on. I wear bronzer on my eyelids. As well as on my face. I think the copper tone really brings out the blue in my eyes. I swear by the LUMA Illuminating Highlighter. I found it really hard to find a good highlighter and ours took a long time to finally get it to where we wanted. Applying highlighter on the highs of your cheeks makes you look fresh whether you feel it or not, and putting it on your eyebrow bones can give you a bit of an oomph. Jess's Journey to Creating LUMA I love tinted moisturiser but it’s hard to find a good one. I think this is probably how the LUMA line came about. I was finding that most of the ones out there were too much like a moisturiser, didn’t have enough colour or were too shiny. I did have an amazing tinted moisturiser that I would use all the time (I probably brought it six times over) but when it was discontinued I was devastated, so I decided I had to make my own so I’ll never run out again. I was the biggest tomboy My sister [model Ashley Hart] and I didn’t really grow up with cosmetics. In recent years I’ve had a few key products that I loved and I thought, “Why don’t I just create my own ideal, basic kit?” – That’s what LUMA Cosmetics is. My brand always had to feel easy. It’s been a long time in the works and I’m very happy that we’re actually here because there were many times when we questioned whether we would pull it off. I just hope everyone loves it as much as I do. Jess's Skincare Routine I was very lucky with my skin growing up I still am. I feel bad for girls that have problematic skin because it would change my day, it would change my life, so I think I’m really lucky. I thought moisturising was a big step a few years ago when I started doing it and now it’s pretty much all I do. I’ll just wash my face with water and a wet face cloth then apply Embryolisse 24hr Miracle Crème Moisturiser. When I’m flying I really pack on the moisturiser and lather on a fair bit of Dr Haunschka hand cream. I have two little sprays I can’t travel without – Nu Skin Moisture Mist and SK-II Facial Treatment Essence. I discovered La Prairie’s Eye & Lip Portable Perfector when I was at the airport. I love it for those days when you’re not…

articles.title: New Year's Makeup Inspo from Iconic Party Girls
articles.author: Chrisanthi Kaliviotis
articles.excerpt: Beauticate shows you New Years Makeup Inspiration from Iconic Party Girls like Debbie Harry, Bianca Jagger, Jerry Hall, Edie Sedgewick and Gia Carangi.
articles.body: Parading in towering platforms, rich, rouge slicked lips, big, bouffant manes and of course plenty of sequins; the party princess’ of the 60s, 70s and 80s were the definition of high-octane glamour and flamboyant flair. It was all glitz and ritz for the disco damsels of old; those affected by the scene were always flawlessly presented, each with their own unique polish (and forever with a rocker, artist or heir on their arm). @badgalriri These were the women that defined partying for the girls that groove today. From the theatrical and edgy Edie, to the polished and modish Bianca, we’ve kicked on our dancing shoes and taken inspiration from the most iconic party girls. We have your New Year’s maquillage sorted – now fill the flutes with French bubbles and pass the Camembert and crackers – it’s time to ring in the New Year looking fabulous. 1\. Talitha Getty A truly bohemian beauty, Talitha was the personification of all that 1960s and 70s bohemia had to offer. Getty’s beauty was steeped in boho accents; a deeply bronzed complexion, a matte, nude lip and long, loose curls which fell in profusion. Such beauty resonated with a distinctly luxe-hippie style; comprising jewel-toned kaftans, white harem pants and thigh-high ivory boots (naturally). Tap into the glamorous gypsy spirit of Getty and go big with hair and slightly more minimal with makeup. The Look Vs Sassoon Big Hair Hot Rollers NARS Laguna Bronzer YSL Rouge Volupte Lipstick in Nude Beige Perfect for: Floating on a luxury boat around the harbour on New Year’s Day 2\. Jane Birkin Birkin’s look eschews ostentatious glamour and favours an unaffected and unadorned air. A look for ushering in the New Year (in favour of ringing), the pared-back yet peachy-keen beauty of Birkin is forever chic and à la mode. Long, spidery lashes (both top and bottom), a peach-hued lipstick and straightened, simple locks with her signature fringe make for French beauty at its best. Channel the English-Rose-turned-Parisian-Party-Princess this New Years and opt for a radiant complexion, giraffe-esque lashes and bangs which are tres dernier cri . The Look: GHD V Rose Gold Hair Styler MAC Opulash Optimum Black Mascara NARS Lipstick in Honolulu Honey Perfect for: New Year’s Day festivals (like Falls) where the cool cats play 3\. Gia Carangi The world’s first ‘Supermodel’, the brunette bombshell was a regular fixture on the legendary dance floor of 54. With her smouldering brown eyes, wasp-stung lips and voluminous, chocolate mane, Gia was the epitome of natural allure and charm. Recreate this sultry look with a brown hued palette for lids, strong eyes are keynote, as is big hair, with blown out, big waves defining in her guise. Pair with cool, ‘model-off-duty’ pieces and retro supermodel here we come. The Look Vs Sassoon 3q High Performance Hairdryer Clinique Superfine Liner for Brows Burberry Beauty Sheer Eyeshadow in Dark Sable Perfect for: Ringing in the New Year at a casual yet chic home ‘do 4\. Jerry Hall With fanciful frocks, luxe makeup and Rapunzel-esque locks, Jerry was right amongst the glitter and glomesh of the scene circa 1970 and 80. Draped on the arm of Mick, her Amazonian looks and garish glamour rendered Jerry lookalikes aplenty. Spread a little of the Hall stardust and glam it up – long, loose and lovely curls, a glossed-up pout and flush it out with blush; all necessary components of a rock star wife makeover. The Look Cloud Nine the Wand Illamasqua Cream Blush in Dixie Thierry Mugler ‘angel’ Eau De Parfum Perfect for: A glamorous New Year’s day affair 5\. Bianca Jagger The poster…

articles.title: Carlos Huber, Perfumer, Arquiste
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Carlos Huber has created a fragrance collection that encapsulates different moments in time, inspired from his architectural background specialising in historical preservation.
articles.body: Our first male profile for Beauticate leaves a trail of scents to enchant. Perfumer Carlos Huber has created Arquiste, a collection that encapsulates different moments in time, inspired by his architectural background specialising in historical preservation. He is a master at storytelling, and with a single spritz you’re taken to the Claridges Hotel in London drinking cocktails, or to a farm at sunrise, observing the crisp dew on a citron tree. The Mexican perfumer recently visited Sydney for the launch of his two new fragrances, L'Etrog Acque and The Architects Club. We caught up with him where he was staying with friends Jason and Adam (who own Becker Minty that stocks his range) to learn about his small batch perfumery, along with two new fragrances he created exclusively for J. Crew (available only in J Crew stores overseas). We also plied his travel grooming secrets from him. Suave and Stylish; Carlos Is Always Immaculately Presented Carlos's Path to Perfumery "I did a graduate degree in architecture at Columbia University… And through that I became a perfumer. The teachers at Columbia are very keen on saying that preservation is not necessarily a conservative career. There was a lot of question about interpreting history and how to take these historic sites and tell a story about them through something else. So I think that's what really sparked Arquiste, the idea that I could use scent and fragrance to tell stories and to evoke different historic moments." Carlos's Favourite Fragrances I've been a big fragrance aficionado; I've always been very keen on buying perfume. Chanel Sycomore is a favourite of mine. I think it's a wonderful one to wear. And the D'Orsay, it's a very old French house and they have a few perfumes. There's one called the Le Nomade, which is very pretty and it's a cologne. I tend to be very classic in what I wear on a day-to-day basis." A Dab of The Architects Club Lavish Stationery and Naturally, Perfume   In New York I meet Yann Vasnier… Who is the creator of Tom Ford's Santal Blush and Lavender Palm. I met him at a party and it turns out we had a friend in common who was a perfumer that lived in Mexico, where I was from. One day he introduced me to Rodrigo, one of the other perfumers and we clicked instantly. It turns out that he came from a family of perfumers so he had a very good training ground. Together we started to develop the concept of Arquiste." Carlos's J. Crew Collaboration J. Crew came about because… I participated in a campaign for them that used five regular guys and girls. They selected a perfumer, the founder of Tumblr and things like that. So J. Crew's Creative Director, Jenna Lyons, had wanted to do fragrance for a while so they called me and I said, "you know, we need to do two exclusive fragrances for you." Golden Accents on Both Fragrance and Furniture Cool Cobalt Sunnies Complement a Couple of Arquiste Fragrances   The J. Crew scents are called No. 31 and No. 57 And the story of them is inspired by Exhibition by 31 Women, the first all women exhibit in the US. This happened in Peggy Guggenheim's Gallery, which was on West 57th Street. So No. 57 is inspired from that gallery because it was all in oak and pine, and then we mixed it with a little bit of whisky and bourbon. And No. 31 is really inspired from the women themselves, so it's very floral and romantic - gardenia, violet, muguet. It's…

articles.title: How to Master the Art of Fragrance Combining
articles.author: Sigourney Cantelo
articles.excerpt: Sigourney masters the art of fragrance combining with Jo Malone.
articles.body: On the hunt for Christmas gifts I popped into the Jo Malone London store in Mosman. Being a steamy Sydney afternoon, I can’t resist the store’s luxe creamy-hued allure. It’s quiet so the store manager, Sarah Louise, invites me to have a hand & arm massage and to find my own signature scent (you can actually book in for this complimentary treatment by ringing the store). After offering me a glass of champagne (Mumm & Co – no less!), she asks me if I have a favourite Jo Malone London scent I don’t quite know where to begin... I’ve had a long-standing love affair with Jo Malone London. I first fell for Orange Blossom in my twenties – its innocent floral freshness is like slipping on a white cotton sundress – it always feels appropriate. I reach for this when I don’t know what else to wear. Later, the brand took me to London to interview their perfumer Christine Nagel, and I fell in love with her most famous concoction, English Pear & Freesia. It’s pure Sloane Street in a bottle: preppy, well-groomed but with luscious fruity overtones. The next year, I kept smelling Pomegranate Noir on all these stylish people at events, and I eventually gave in and got a bottle for myself. It didn’t disappoint. Finally, only last week I was sent the beautiful Christmas Cologne Collection to try and I discovered Blackberry & Bay – another juicy feast of a fragrance, mouth-watering and wet and totally refreshing in all this humidity. GRAPEFRUIT COLOGNE I give Sarah Louise a kind of abridged version of my perfume diatribe and to her credit, she doesn’t bat an eye. “Well you could actually combine a few of those and create your own signature scent,” she says, picking up the pomegranate noir and spraying it on a scent card. How Fragrance Combining Actually Works I’d heard of the brands technique of fragrance combining but, to be honest, I was always a bit skeptical. Surely it would be too much – layering all these scents? “My favourite combo at the moment is adding the Orange Blossom on top of the Pomegranate Noir to make it fresher,” she says, spritzing the floral scent over the top of the scent card and handing it to me. True to her word, it’s suddenly lifted. The layering of the two takes a dark, inky evening scent into playful territory. I could imagine wearing it to a Christmas party, it’s fun and frivolous but with the guts of spiced woods and pink pepper. “Jo Malone London fragrances are created very simply,” explains Sarah Louise. “There’s a lot of clarity in them, so compared to most other fragrances that have about 400 ingredients ours only have 100. Fragrance combining makes it more bespoke as well. You don’t have to do two fragrances, you can do a lotion and a cologne, or when you’re entertaining you can do “scent surround” by mixing room sprays and candles, so you can create a really unique space.” Layering Scent on Skin for Lasting Power We head over the table and Sarah Louise gives me a little felt bag for my rings, hands me my champagne and begins a totally luxurious hand massage with the new Wood Sage & Sea Salt Body Crème. She then spritzes Red Roses Cologneover the top, onto my forearms. “It adds a bit of warmth and floralness to the already woody and fresh Wood Sage & Sea Salt,” she explains as she presses it into my skin gently. ENGLISH PEAR & FREESIA COLOGNE “Don’t ever rub – when a…
